speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: Well, I think it's also very personal to our context and our upbringing. For us, Sriram and I came from a fairly middle class family in India, this city in India that most people here won't probably know.
keySentence: For us, Sriram and I came from a fairly middle class family in India.
text_ko: 음, 제겐 이건 저희 맥락과 성장 배경에 관한 아주 개인적인 얘기이기도 해요. 스리람과 저는 인도에서 비교적 중산층 가정에서 자랐는데, 저희가 자란 도시는 여기 계신 분들 대부분이 아마 잘 모를 거예요. 어렸을 때 저희는 컴퓨터를 정말 좋아했지만 오랫동안 컴퓨터를 접할 수 없었어요. 저희 둘 다 부모님이 돈을 모아 첫 컴퓨터를 사주셨는데, 그게 정말 쉬운 일이 아니었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得这跟我们自己的成长背景很有关系。我和Sriram都出生在印度的中产家庭，来自一个可能大家都没听说过的印度小城市。我们从小就特别喜欢电脑，但很长时间都碰不到电脑。我们俩的情况都一样，父母为了给我们买第一台电脑，攒了很久的钱，真的挺不容易的。
text_es: Bueno, creo que también es muy personal según nuestro contexto y cómo nos criaron. En nuestro caso, Sriram y yo venimos de una familia de clase media en la India, de una ciudad que probablemente la mayoría aquí no conoce. Crecimos con muchas ganas de tener computadoras pero no tuvimos acceso a una por muchísimo tiempo. En los dos casos, nuestros papás nos compraron nuestras primeras computadoras después de ahorrar dinero para eso, y fue algo muy difícil para ellos.
fullContext: Lenny asks Aarthi and Sriram about their techno-optimism movement and why it's important to them. Aarthi explains their personal background - growing up middle-class in India without easy access to computers, then eventually getting their first computers after their parents saved money. She's setting up the foundation for why technology has been so transformative in their lives and why they're advocates for tech's positive impact.

vocabulary.definition: The circumstances or setting surrounding an event, statement, or idea that help to clarify its meaning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding the context is crucial for making informed decisions, as it encompasses market conditions, cultural factors, and stakeholder perspectives.

insight.nuance: While context is often used to provide clarity, it can also imply that certain interpretations may vary based on different situational factors.

vocabulary.definition: The treatment and education received by a child from their parents or guardians, shaping their values and behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, understanding an employee's upbringing can provide insights into their work ethic, communication style, and approach to teamwork.

insight.nuance: Upbringing often carries a personal connotation, and discussing it in a professional setting may require sensitivity to avoid assumptions or stereotypes.

vocabulary.definition: A social class between the upper and working classes, typically characterized by moderate income, education, and occupation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market analysis, the middle class is often targeted for consumer goods and services, as their purchasing power can significantly influence economic trends.

insight.nuance: The term can vary by country and culture, so it is important to consider local economic conditions when discussing middle-class demographics.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to approach, enter, or make use of something, often referring to resources, information, or opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, access is crucial for ensuring that stakeholders can utilize data and tools necessary for effective decision-making and operations.

insight.nuance: While access generally implies availability, it can also suggest issues of equity and inclusion, particularly in discussions about digital divides or resource allocation.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: You're almost better off doing these small, niche, non-scalable things to go find these oddball set of people who are doing this, who are really interested in this one thing and kind of scale from there and grow from there.
keySentence: You're almost better off doing these small, niche, non-scalable things to go find these oddball set of people
text_ko: 오히려 작고 틈새적이고 확장 불가능한(non-scalable) 일들을 먼저 해보는 편이 더 나을 때가 많아요. 그런 식으로 이 한 가지에 정말 관심 있는, 조금 독특한 소수의 사람들을 찾아서 거기서부터 조금씩 스케일(scale)해 나가고 성장하면 돼요. 커뮤니티를 만들기 시작할 때 한 가지 중요한 건, 처음부터 엄청나게 규모를 키우려고 하지 말라는 거예요. 특정 문제에 열정을 가진 몇몇 사람들부터 모아 시작하는 게 훨씬 좋아요.
text_zh: 你最好是先做一些小众的、非标准化的事情，去找到那些真正对某个特定领域感兴趣的人，然后再从那里慢慢做大。我觉得在搭建社群的时候，千万别一上来就想着做成超大规模的社群。你得先找到几个对某个问题特别有热情、想要聚在一起交流的人开始做起。
text_es: Es casi mejor que te enfoques en cosas pequeñas, muy específicas, que no se puedan escalar masivamente para encontrar a esa gente medio rara que está metida en esto, que realmente le apasiona este tema en particular, y desde ahí empezar a crecer. Y creo que eso es algo clave cuando estás empezando a construir una comunidad: no trates de armar una súper comunidad escalable desde el inicio. Empieza con poca gente que esté apasionada por un problema específico y que quiera juntarse, ¿sabes?
fullContext: Aarthi continues her advice on community building. She advocates for deliberately doing 'non-scalable things' initially to find a core group of passionate users - what she calls an 'oddball set of people' who are deeply interested in a specific problem or topic. This is part of her broader framework that successful communities should start small and niche before attempting to scale, rather than trying to build massive communities from day one.

vocabulary.definition: A specialized segment of the market for a particular kind of product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying a niche allows companies to target specific customer needs that are not being met by mainstream providers, often leading to competitive advantages.

insight.nuance: While 'niche' can imply a limited audience, it often carries a positive connotation of exclusivity and specialization.

vocabulary.definition: The capability of a business or system to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance or losing revenue potential.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, scalability is crucial as it indicates the potential for growth and the ability to expand operations efficiently as demand increases.

insight.nuance: The term often implies not just growth, but growth that can be achieved without proportional increases in costs.

vocabulary.definition: In a purposeful and intentional manner, often implying careful consideration or planning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In strategic planning, actions taken deliberately are often seen as more calculated and aligned with long-term goals, rather than reactive or impulsive.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a level of thoughtfulness that can enhance credibility and trust in business decisions.

vocabulary.definition: A central or primary group of individuals who are essential to the functioning or success of an organization or project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In team dynamics, the core group often consists of key stakeholders or decision-makers whose collaboration is vital for achieving objectives.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the importance of this group in driving initiatives, and its members are often seen as leaders or influencers within the organization.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: Our first jobs were at Microsoft, we built developer tools and platforms. If you were in our shoes, you would feel the same way too. Tech has given us so much.
keySentence: Tech has given us so much.
text_ko: 저희 첫 직장은 마이크로소프트였고, 개발자 도구와 플랫폼(developer tools and platforms)을 만들었어요. 여러분이 우리 입장이라면 아마 같은 기분을 느끼실 거예요. 기술(tech)이 우리에게 정말 많은 것을 주었어요. 저희는 인도에서 출발해 여러 도시를 거쳐 여기까지 왔고, 시애틀에 살다가 지금은 베이 에어리어에 있죠. 저는 여기서 테크 회사들(tech companies)을 창업하기도 했어요. 그래서 다른 관점을 보는 건 좀 답답해요. 얼마나 많은 사람들의 삶과 커리어를 끌어올렸는지 뻔히 보이니까요. 저희가 직접 해온 일들이나 친구들이 만들어서 출시한 것들만 봐도 영향력이 엄청났어요.
text_zh: 我们的第一份工作都是在微软，做开发工具和平台。如果你站在我们的角度，你也会有同样的感受。科技给了我们太多太多。我们从印度一路走来，辗转多个城市，在西雅图住过，现在又到了湾区，我也创办过科技公司，所以看到另一种观点时确实有点憋屈，因为你能亲眼看到科技是怎么改变人们的生活、事业和人生轨迹的。不光是我们自己做的项目，还有朋友们开发和推出的产品，真的是带来了翻天覆地的变化。
text_es: Nuestros primeros trabajos fueron en Microsoft, desarrollamos herramientas y plataformas para programadores. Si estuvieras en nuestro lugar, sentirías lo mismo. La tecnología nos ha dado muchísimo. Y para nosotros, que vinimos desde la India, pasando por varias ciudades, vivimos en Seattle y después aquí, en el Área de la Bahía, he fundado empresas de tech, es un poco frustrante ver el otro punto de vista porque puedes ver cómo ha transformado vidas, carreras profesionales, pero también por todo lo que hemos podido desarrollar, lo que hemos visto que nuestros amigos desarrollan y lanzan al mercado, realmente ha marcado una diferencia enorme.
fullContext: Aarthi continues explaining why she and Sriram are techno-optimists. She describes their journey from India to working at Microsoft, then moving through Seattle to Silicon Valley where she started companies. She argues that technology has been transformative for their lives and careers, and expresses frustration with critics of tech because she's witnessed firsthand how technology uplifts people and creates opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Software applications or utilities that assist programmers in creating, debugging, and maintaining software applications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, developer tools are essential for enhancing productivity and efficiency in software development processes, often leading to faster product releases.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a focus on enhancing the developer's experience and capabilities, rather than just the end product.

vocabulary.definition: Frameworks or environments that enable the development and deployment of applications, often providing a set of tools and services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, platforms can refer to both software platforms, like operating systems, and business platforms, like marketplaces, that facilitate interactions between users and providers.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a foundational role in technology ecosystems, suggesting scalability and integration capabilities.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who believe that technology will lead to significant improvements in society and solve major global challenges.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, techno-optimists often advocate for investment in innovative technologies, believing they will drive growth and societal progress.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a positive connotation, but may also imply a naivety about the potential downsides of technology.

vocabulary.definition: The process of traveling from one place to another, often used metaphorically to describe a progression or development over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'journey' frequently refers to customer journeys or employee journeys, highlighting the experiences and interactions individuals have with a brand or organization.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a focus on the process and experiences rather than just the end goal, emphasizing growth and learning.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: you have to get out there and build your own brand... All of that is just up to you.
keySentence: All of that is just up to you.
text_ko: 제 경력의 대부분 동안은 '그게 당연하지, 그런 게 하는 일이야'라고 생각했어요. 그런데 점점 그것이 사실이 아니라는 걸 알게 됐어요. 좀 논란이 될 수도 있지만, 직접 나서서 자기만의 브랜드(brand)를 만들어야 해요. 자신이 무엇을 지향하는지, 핵심 가치가 무엇인지, 무엇을 믿는지, 무엇을 하고 싶은지, 앞으로 커리어가 어떻게 전개될지를 스스로 찾아 정해야 해요. 그 모든 건 결국 본인에게 달려 있어요.
text_zh: 我职业生涯的大部分时间都觉得，"对啊，这不是很正常吗，大家不都是这么做的嘛。"但后来我才意识到根本不是这回事儿。这话可能有点争议，但你必须得主动出击，打造自己的个人品牌(personal brand)。你得搞清楚自己代表什么，核心价值观是什么，信念是什么，想做什么，下一步的职业发展轨迹会是什么样。这些都得靠你自己。
text_es: Durante la mayor parte de mi carrera pensaba: "Claro, eso tiene sentido, es lo que uno hace normalmente." Pero me he dado cuenta de que eso simplemente no es cierto, y quizás sea una opinión polémica, pero tienes que salir ahí afuera y construir tu propia marca personal. Tienes que descubrir qué representas, cuáles son tus valores fundamentales, en qué crees, qué piensas que quieres hacer, cómo va a ser tu próxima trayectoria profesional. Todo eso depende únicamente de ti.
fullContext: Lenny asks about building personal brands and networks. Aarthi explains how she used to believe the common corporate advice to 'just put your head down and do good work' - that products would speak for themselves. However, she's come to realize this approach doesn't work in practice. She argues that professionals need to actively build their personal brand and figure out their own career direction rather than expecting companies to do it for them.

vocabulary.definition: To create and develop a unique identity or reputation for oneself or a business in the marketplace.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, building your own brand is crucial for establishing a distinct presence that attracts customers and differentiates from competitors, especially in personal branding and entrepreneurship.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a proactive approach to self-promotion and personal development, and is best used in contexts emphasizing individual initiative.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance or recommendations provided to businesses regarding their operations, strategy, or management practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: Corporate advice is commonly sought by companies to improve efficiency, navigate challenges, or make informed decisions, often provided by consultants or industry experts.

insight.nuance: This term carries a formal connotation and is typically used in professional settings; it may not be suitable for casual discussions.

vocabulary.definition: The perception and reputation that an individual cultivates about themselves, often through their online presence and professional interactions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and entrepreneurship, personal brands can significantly influence career opportunities, networking potential, and marketability.

insight.nuance: While personal brands are often seen as positive, they can also be viewed skeptically if perceived as overly self-promotional or inauthentic.

vocabulary.definition: A group of interconnected individuals or organizations that share information, resources, or support for mutual benefit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, networking is essential for building relationships, discovering opportunities, and fostering collaborations that can lead to growth and success.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both formal and informal connections; however, it is often associated with strategic relationship-building rather than casual acquaintances.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: And I think building a personal brand is looked down upon so much that people think of it as a dirty word. It's like, 'No, you can't do that.' 'Oh, look at this person who's branding themselves,' kind of thing.
keySentence: building a personal brand is looked down upon so much that people think of it as a dirty word.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 개인 브랜드(personal brand)를 만드는 걸 사람들이 너무 폄하해서 마치 부정적인 말, 꺼리는 말처럼 여기는 것 같아요. '아니야, 그건 하면 안 돼'라든가 '저 사람 자기 브랜딩(branding) 하는 것 봐라' 이런 식이죠. 근데 저는 오히려 그게 남들과 차별되는 지점이라고 봐요. 개인 브랜딩이란 못하는 걸 부풀리거나 자랑을 더 하려는 게 아니라, '나는 이걸 정말 잘해요. 이 주제로 얘기하고 싶고, 영상도 만들고 글도 쓰고 트윗도 하고 싶다'는 걸 강조하는 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得打造个人品牌(personal brand)被大家看得太负面了，好像成了什么见不得人的词儿。大家都会说"不行，你不能这么干"，"你看这人，又在包装自己"，就是这种感觉。但我觉得这其实就是让你从众人中脱颖而出的东西，也不是说要吹嘘自己不擅长的事儿，或者过度自我推销，而是要突出"我在这方面确实很厉害，我想聊这个话题，我想做视频讲这个，或者写文章，发推特什么的"。
text_es: Y creo que construir una marca personal está tan mal visto que la gente lo ve como algo sucio. Es como "No, eso no se puede hacer" o "Ay, mira a este que se está promocionando", ¿sabes? Pero yo más bien lo veo como lo que te diferencia de todos los demás, y no se trata tanto de decir algo en lo que no eres bueno o presumir de más, sino realmente de destacar: "Soy muy bueno en esto y quiero hablar de esto y quiero hacer videos al respecto o escribir sobre ello o tuitearlo."
fullContext: Aarthi continues her response about personal branding. She addresses the negative perception many people have of personal branding, noting that it's often seen as a 'dirty word' or something unprofessional. She reframes personal branding not as boastful self-promotion, but as authentically highlighting your genuine strengths and expertise through various content channels like videos, writing, or social media.

vocabulary.definition: A personal brand is the unique combination of skills, experiences, and personality that an individual presents to the world, particularly in a professional context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, a strong personal brand can enhance an individual's credibility, attract opportunities, and differentiate them from competitors.

insight.nuance: While a personal brand can be empowering, it may also carry a stigma if perceived as self-promotional or inauthentic.

vocabulary.definition: Negative perception refers to an unfavorable view or opinion that individuals or groups hold about a person, brand, or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, negative perceptions can significantly impact a company's reputation, customer loyalty, and overall success, often requiring strategic management to address.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a bias or misunderstanding that may not reflect the actual qualities of the subject in question.

vocabulary.definition: Branding is the process of creating a unique identity and image for a product, service, or individual in the minds of consumers, often through the use of names, symbols, and design.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, effective branding is crucial for establishing market presence, fostering customer loyalty, and differentiating offerings in competitive landscapes.

insight.nuance: Branding encompasses both visual elements and the emotional connections consumers have with a brand, making it a multifaceted concept.

vocabulary.definition: Professionalism refers to the conduct, aims, and qualities that characterize a professional individual, including competence, reliability, and ethical behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, professionalism is essential for fostering trust, maintaining workplace standards, and enhancing organizational reputation.

insight.nuance: While professionalism is generally viewed positively, excessive rigidity or formality may hinder creativity and personal expression in some environments.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: You do this, you do two coffees a week and literally just ask me two hours a week, everyone has two hours a week, it'll start compounding over overtime and time.
keySentence: Two hours a week can start compounding over overtime, expanding your network.
text_ko: 이렇게 해보세요. 일주일에 커피 약속을 두 번 잡고, 그냥 주당 두 시간만 저한테 물어보면 돼요. 누구에게나 일주일에 두 시간은 있잖아요. 그러면 시간이 지날수록 복리 효과(compounding)처럼 쌓이기 시작해요. 그리고 몇 년이 지나 같이 일했던 사람들과 계속 연락을 유지하면, 그 사람들이 다른 곳으로 옮기기도 하고, 5년, 6년이 지나면 20대 중반이나 후반에 시작했을 때 이미 여러 곳에 아는 사람이 수백 명이 돼요.
text_zh: 你就这么做，每周约两次咖啡聊天，就问我要两个小时，谁都能挤出两个小时吧，这样慢慢积累下去会有复利效应。然后随着时间推移，你跟以前的同事保持联系，这些人会跳槽到其他地方，五六年过去了，你从二十多岁开始做起，到时候就认识好几百号人，遍布各个地方。
text_es: Mira, haces esto, te tomas dos cafés a la semana conmigo y literalmente me dedicas dos horas a la semana - todo el mundo tiene dos horas a la semana - y esto se va acumulando con el tiempo. Y entonces, conforme pasan los años, mantienes el contacto con la gente con la que trabajabas, esta gente se va a otros lados, pasan cinco, seis años, empiezas a los 25 o casi 30 y ya conoces a cientos de personas por todas partes.
fullContext: Sriram is giving detailed advice on how to build a professional network. He's explaining a systematic approach where you consistently meet with two people per week for coffee - just investing two hours weekly. He emphasizes how this compounds over time, and as people move to different companies over the years, you build a network of hundreds of contacts across the industry. This is part of his broader framework for authentic relationship building.

vocabulary.definition: The process of accumulating interest or value over time, where the returns on an investment generate their own returns.
vocabulary.businessContext: In finance and investing, compounding is crucial as it illustrates how investments can grow exponentially over time, emphasizing the importance of starting early.

insight.nuance: Compounding often carries a positive connotation, suggesting growth and increasing returns, and is typically used in discussions about long-term financial strategies.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a methodical and organized approach to a process or task, often involving a set plan or framework.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and project management, a systematic approach ensures that tasks are completed efficiently and effectively, reducing errors and improving outcomes.

insight.nuance: While systematic implies thoroughness and reliability, it can also suggest rigidity; thus, it's important to balance systematic methods with flexibility when necessary.

vocabulary.definition: The act of allocating resources, usually money, with the expectation of generating an income or profit over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: Investing is a fundamental concept in finance, where individuals or companies put capital into assets, projects, or ventures to achieve financial growth or returns.

insight.nuance: Investing can imply a long-term commitment and carries risks; it is often discussed in contexts that emphasize strategic planning and risk management.

vocabulary.definition: A group or system of interconnected people or things, often used to facilitate communication and collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, networking is essential for building relationships, sharing information, and creating opportunities for collaboration and growth.

insight.nuance: While networking can have a positive connotation of support and opportunity, it can also imply opportunism; thus, the context in which it is used can greatly affect its perception.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: The other key part is expecting nothing in return.
keySentence: expecting nothing in return.
text_ko: 다른 핵심은 아무 대가도 바라지 않는 거예요. 그리고 보통 사람들은 상대 의도를 잘 알아봐요. '저는 일자리 때문에 만나고 싶어요'라든지 '네트워킹(networking)하러 왔어요'라고 하면 상대가 만나고 싶어하지 않아요. 그냥 가서 그 사람이 어떤 사람인지 진심으로 궁금해해 보세요. 그리고 도와줄 수 있는 게 있으면 도와주려고 해보세요. 어디서 시작하든 1년, 2년 안에 도움 받을 수 있는 수백 명의 사람들을 알게 돼서 깜짝 놀랄 거예요. 그래서 그게 정말 강력해요.
text_zh: 另一个关键点就是不要指望别人回报你什么。一般来说，大家都很会看人，如果你过去就是那种"嘿，我想认识你是因为我想找工作"或者"我是来networking的"，不管这意味着什么吧，人家根本不想见你。你就去真心地对他们这个人感兴趣，想办法帮助他们。你会发现很神奇，不管你从哪儿开始，一年两年内，你就能认识几百号人，需要的时候都能联系上，我觉得这个力量真的很强大。
text_es: La otra parte clave es no esperar nada a cambio. Y en general la gente es muy buena leyendo a otros, entonces si llegas con la actitud de "Oye, solo quiero conocerte porque quiero un trabajo" o "estoy aquí para hacer networking," como sea que le digas, no van a querer conocerte. Simplemente ve y ten mucha curiosidad genuina sobre quién son y trata de ayudarlos. Y te vas a sorprender - no importa dónde empieces, en un año, dos años, vas a conocer cientos de personas a las que puedes recurrir, así que creo que eso es súper poderoso.
fullContext: Sriram continues his networking advice, emphasizing the importance of authentic relationship building. He warns against transactional approaches where you're obviously seeking something (like a job), noting that people can easily detect these motives. Instead, he advocates for genuine curiosity about others and a willingness to help them. He promises that this authentic approach will build a valuable network you can eventually 'tap into' for opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Genuine and true to its origin; not false or copied.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being authentic often refers to a brand's ability to convey its true values and mission, fostering trust and loyalty among customers.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting integrity and transparency, and is often used in discussions about branding and corporate culture.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the conduct of business or transactions, often emphasizing a focus on exchanges rather than relationships.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, a transactional approach may prioritize short-term gains and efficiency over long-term partnerships and customer loyalty.

insight.nuance: While sometimes necessary, a purely transactional mindset can lead to superficial interactions and may not foster lasting business relationships.

vocabulary.definition: The process of establishing and nurturing connections with individuals or organizations to foster trust and collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, relationship building is crucial for networking, customer retention, and creating partnerships that can lead to mutual benefits and growth.

insight.nuance: This term implies a long-term commitment to developing connections, contrasting with more transactional interactions that focus solely on immediate outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: The act of giving or offering something without anticipating any compensation or reciprocation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, this mindset can enhance goodwill and foster a positive corporate culture, as it emphasizes altruism and community engagement.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a selfless approach to interactions, which can be beneficial in building trust but may also be misinterpreted as a lack of ambition in competitive environments.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: That is terrible feedback and to totally ignore that... The things that work well for me and a lot of others is putting yourself out there.
keySentence: Ignore terrible feedback about brand building; putting yourself out there is crucial.
text_ko: 아르티와 저는 커리어의 각기 다른 시점에서 회사에서 '스리람(Sriram)이나 아르티는 브랜드 구축(brand build)을 너무 많이 한다'라는 피드백을 받은 적이 있어요. 저는 그게 정말 형편없는 피드백이라는 걸 배웠고, 그런 얘기를 들으면 그냥 완전히 무시하라고 배웠어요. 저와 많은 사람들에게 잘 통하는 건 자신을 적극적으로 드러내는 것(putting yourself out there)인데, 그 방법은 뭐든 될 수 있어요.
text_zh: 我和Aarthi在职业生涯的不同阶段都收到过这样的反馈，说什么"Sriram和Aarthi太爱搞个人品牌了"之类的。我现在明白了，这种反馈简直就是废话，完全不用理会。如果有人听到类似的话，直接忽略就行了。对我和很多人来说，真正有用的就是要敢于表现自己，这可以是任何形式。
text_es: Tanto Aarthi como yo, en diferentes momentos de nuestras carreras, hemos recibido comentarios en el trabajo del tipo "Ay, es que Sriram y Aarthi se enfocan demasiado en construir su marca personal, y todo eso." He aprendido que ese tipo de feedback es pésimo y hay que ignorarlo completamente, y si alguien escucha algo así, que lo ignore totalmente. Lo que me funciona bien a mí y a muchos otros es darse a conocer (putting yourself out there), y eso puede ser cualquier cosa.
fullContext: Sriram is discussing personal branding and shares that both he and Aarthi have received negative feedback at work for building their personal brands too much. He strongly advises people to ignore this type of feedback, calling it 'terrible feedback.' He argues that 'putting yourself out there' through various forms of content creation and personal branding is actually beneficial for career success, contrary to what some managers might say.

vocabulary.definition: Information or criticism about a person's performance or behavior, often used to improve future actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, feedback is crucial for employee development, product improvement, and customer satisfaction, often gathered through surveys, reviews, or performance evaluations.

insight.nuance: While feedback can be constructive, it may also carry negative connotations if perceived as harsh or unhelpful; thus, it is important to deliver it thoughtfully.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of individuals marketing themselves and their careers as brands, emphasizing unique skills and values.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, personal branding is essential for professionals to differentiate themselves in competitive job markets and to build a strong online presence.

insight.nuance: Personal branding can sometimes be viewed as self-promotional or superficial if not grounded in authenticity and genuine value.

vocabulary.definition: The act of exposing oneself to new experiences, opportunities, or risks, particularly in social or professional contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and business networking, putting yourself out there is vital for building connections, seeking partnerships, and promoting one's ideas or products.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a level of vulnerability and courage, and may not be suitable in contexts where caution is warranted.

vocabulary.definition: To deliberately pay no attention to something or someone, often to dismiss or overlook it.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, ignoring feedback or market signals can lead to missed opportunities or failures, making it a critical action to avoid.

insight.nuance: While ignoring can sometimes be strategic, it often carries a negative connotation, suggesting negligence or lack of awareness.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: You'd be amazed how often somebody just have a random great Twitter thread with no followers and somebody super interesting will email them and that leads to amazing things happening, it encourages serendipity.
keySentence: Encourages serendipity, leading to amazing things happening from random connections.
text_ko: 생각보다 자주 팔로워(followers)가 거의 없는 사람이 우연히 멋진 트위터(Twitter) 쓰레드(thread)를 올리면, 굉장히 흥미로운 사람이 그 사람에게 이메일을 보내고 그게 놀라운 일로 이어지곤 해요. 그게 우연한 행운(serendipity)을 만들어줘요. 그래서 지난 몇 년을 돌이켜보면, '이걸 하지 마'라고 했던 사람들 말은 좀 덜 들을 걸 그랬고, '이걸 더 해'라고 했던 사람들 말은 더 들었어야 했어요.
text_zh: 你会惊讶地发现，经常有人发了个很棒的推特串(Twitter thread)，明明没什么粉丝，结果就有超有意思的人给他们发邮件，然后就促成了很多amazing的事情，这就是在创造偶然的机会嘛。所以这些年下来，我真希望当初少听那些劝我别这么做的人的话，多听听那些鼓励我更多去做的人。
text_es: Te sorprendería la cantidad de veces que alguien simplemente publica un hilo genial en Twitter sin tener seguidores y de repente una persona súper interesante le manda un email, y eso termina generando cosas increíbles. Es como que facilita esas casualidades afortunadas. Así que después de todos estos años, ojalá hubiera hecho menos caso a la gente que me decía que no debería hacer esto y hubiera escuchado más a los que me decían que tenía que hacerlo más seguido.
fullContext: Sriram continues explaining the benefits of creating content and building a personal brand online. He describes how putting yourself out there acts like a 'Bat-Signal' that attracts interesting opportunities and people. He gives an example of how even someone with no followers can create great content that gets noticed by influential people, leading to unexpected opportunities. This is part of his argument for why people should ignore advice against personal branding.

vocabulary.definition: The occurrence of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, serendipity often refers to unexpected opportunities that arise, such as networking connections or innovative ideas that emerge from casual interactions.

insight.nuance: While serendipity implies a fortunate accident, it is often used to highlight the importance of being open to new experiences and ideas.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of marketing oneself and one's career as a brand, emphasizing unique qualities and values.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, a strong personal brand can enhance professional reputation, attract job opportunities, and foster networking relationships.

insight.nuance: Personal branding is often associated with social media presence and public perception, making it crucial for professionals in competitive fields.

vocabulary.definition: The process of generating material, such as text, images, or videos, for digital platforms to engage an audience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the digital marketing landscape, content creation is vital for building brand awareness, driving traffic, and fostering customer engagement.

insight.nuance: Content creation can range from casual social media posts to highly polished marketing campaigns, depending on the target audience and business goals.

vocabulary.definition: To draw or pull towards oneself or itself; to engage interest or attention.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, attracting customers or clients is essential for growth, often achieved through effective marketing strategies and value propositions.

insight.nuance: While 'attracts' implies a positive draw, it is important to ensure that the methods used to attract do not compromise brand integrity.

speaker: Aarthi Ramamurthy
text: Find the niche, start really small and find the niche. I think oftentimes I've seen other startup founders and I invest and advise in a lot of early stage companies.
keySentence: Find the niche, start really small and find the niche.
text_ko: 틈새 시장을 찾아야 해요. 정말 작게 시작해서 그 틈새를 공략해요. 저는 다른 스타트업 창업자들을 자주 보는데, 초기 단계 회사들에 많이 투자하고 조언해요. 와이컴비네이터(Y Combinator)를 거쳐서 가능한 한 자주 YC에 가서 사람들을 도와주고요. 그런데 종종 창업자들이 와서 "이 커뮤니티를 위한 제품을 만들고, 이걸로 세계에서 가장 큰 커뮤니티를 만들겠다"라고 말해요. 거의 처음부터 지나치게 확장된 버전으로 시작하다 보니 스스로 실패를 불러오더라고요.
text_zh: 要找到细分市场，从特别小的地方开始，先找准这个细分领域。我经常看到其他创业者——我投资和指导了很多早期公司，我自己也是从Y Combinator出来的，所以经常回YC帮忙——但我常常看到有人创业或者创始人过来就说，"我要做个产品服务这个群体，我要围绕这个东西打造全世界最大的社区"，一上来就想做得特别大，结果往往把自己给坑了。
text_es: Encuentra tu nicho, empieza súper pequeño y encuentra ese nicho. Creo que muchas veces he visto a otros fundadores de startups - y yo invierto y asesoro en muchas empresas que están empezando - pasé por Y Combinator, entonces regreso a YC siempre que puedo para echar una mano. Pero muchas veces veo gente que está arrancando empresas o fundadores que llegan y dicen, 'Voy a crear este producto que va a servir a esta comunidad. Voy a construir la comunidad más grande del mundo de este tipo de cosa,' y casi empiezan con esta versión súper escalada y ahí mismo se están preparando para el fracaso.
fullContext: Lenny asks Aarthi about the key things to get right when building a new community. Aarthi, drawing from her experience building community products at Facebook and Clubhouse, plus her work as an investor and advisor to early-stage companies, emphasizes starting small and finding a specific niche. She criticizes founders who try to build massive, scaled communities from the beginning, arguing this approach sets them up for failure rather than finding focused product-market fit first.

vocabulary.definition: A niche refers to a specialized segment of the market for a particular kind of product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying a niche allows companies to target specific customer needs and differentiate themselves from competitors.

insight.nuance: While 'niche' often implies a smaller market, it can also suggest a unique opportunity for growth and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: A startup is a newly established business, typically in the early stages of development, focused on bringing a unique product or service to market.
vocabulary.businessContext: Startups often seek funding and mentorship to scale their operations and validate their business models in competitive environments.

insight.nuance: The term 'startup' can carry a connotation of innovation and disruption, often associated with technology-driven ventures.

vocabulary.definition: Early stage refers to the initial phase of a company's development, where it is typically focused on product development, market research, and initial customer acquisition.
vocabulary.businessContext: Investors often look for early stage companies as opportunities for high growth potential, albeit with higher risk.

insight.nuance: The term 'early stage' implies that the company is still refining its business model and may not yet be profitable.

vocabulary.definition: To advise means to offer recommendations or guidance to someone regarding a particular course of action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, advising can involve providing strategic insights, mentorship, or operational guidance to startups and entrepreneurs.

insight.nuance: The term 'advise' suggests a level of expertise and authority, often implying that the advisor has relevant experience or knowledge.

speaker: Ada Chen Rekhi
text: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
keySentence: It's bad not because it's not well-intentioned, but because it's not contextual.
text_ko: 그게 나쁜 이유는 잘못된 의도 때문이 아니라, 상황에 맞지 않기 때문이에요. 그래서 누군가가 당신에게 직장을 그만두고 꿈을 쫓으라고 하거나, 아니면 조금 더 버티면서 경험을 쌓으라고 할 때, 어떤 조언을 실제로 받아들여야 할까요? 이건 정말 당신의 상황, 고민하고 있는 것, 가지고 있는 기술과 경험에 따라 달라져요. 그리고 호기심 루프(curiosity loop)는 조언을 어떻게 상황에 맞게 만들 수 있을지를 생각하는 좋은 방법이에요.
text_zh: 这并不是因为建议出发点不善良而糟糕，而是因为缺乏具体情境。因此，当有人告诉你辞掉工作去追求梦想，或者让你耐心坚持，积累经验再去创办你一直想创办的公司时，你究竟该听取哪种建议呢？很多时候，这取决于你的具体情况、你正在考虑的事项、你实际拥有的技能和经验。而“好奇循环”（curiosity loops）正是一种思考如何使建议具有情境性的方式。
text_es: Y no está mal porque no sea bien intencionado, sino que está mal porque no es contextual. Así que cuando alguien te dice que dejes tu trabajo y persigas tus sueños, o te aconseja que te mantengas firme y trabajes duro para adquirir experiencia antes de lanzarte a crear la empresa que siempre has querido iniciar, ¿cuál de esos consejos realmente sigues? Mucho depende de tu situación, de lo que estás considerando, de las habilidades y la experiencia que realmente tienes, y los bucles de curiosidad (curiosity loops) son una forma de pensar en cómo hacer que tu consejo sea contextual.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ada to explain curiosity loops after she used this method to gather structured feedback for their podcast conversation. A curiosity loop is when you ask the same question to multiple people (around 10-15) to gather diverse perspectives rather than relying on one person's opinion. Ada explains that most advice fails not because of bad intentions, but because it lacks context for your specific situation - what worked for one person may not apply to your circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: Having good intentions or motives, often with the aim of helping others or improving a situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a well-intentioned initiative may refer to a project or policy designed to benefit employees or customers, even if the execution is flawed.

insight.nuance: While well-intentioned actions are often viewed positively, they may be criticized if they lead to unintended negative consequences.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the circumstances or setting in which something occurs, providing necessary background for understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, contextual information is crucial for decision-making, as it helps leaders understand market dynamics and consumer behavior.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the importance of situational awareness and can imply that actions or strategies should be tailored to specific environments.

vocabulary.definition: Feedback that is organized and delivered in a systematic manner, often following a specific framework or criteria.
vocabulary.businessContext: Structured feedback is commonly used in performance reviews and project assessments to ensure clarity and objectivity in evaluations.

insight.nuance: This type of feedback is often preferred in professional settings as it promotes constructive criticism and actionable insights.

vocabulary.definition: A concept referring to the cycle of inquiry and exploration that leads to deeper understanding and engagement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, curiosity loops are often leveraged in product development and marketing strategies to foster user engagement and innovation.

insight.nuance: The term suggests an ongoing process of questioning and discovery, which can be particularly effective in dynamic and rapidly changing industries.

speaker: Ada Chen Rekhi
text: One thing was really telling, no one out of everyone we asked said 18. So that really dragged my partner up. And then the other thing that was really interesting was that we learned a little bit about executive function and the research around it.
keySentence: No one said 18, which really dragged my partner up.
text_ko: 한 가지 정말 흥미로운 점은 우리가 물어본 사람들 중에 아무도 18이라고 답하지 않았다는 거예요. 그래서 그게 제 파트너에게 큰 영향을 줬어요. 그리고 또 하나 재미있었던 건, 우리는 실행 기능(executive function)과 그에 대한 연구에 대해 조금 배웠다는 거예요. 실행 기능은 결정을 내리고 계획을 세우고 사려 깊게 행동하는 능력인데, 이게 30세에 최고조에 이르고 그 이후로는 점점 떨어진다고 하더라고요.
text_zh: 有一点非常明显，我们问的所有人中没有一个人提到18岁。这让我的合伙人感到很震惊。另外一个有趣的发现是，我们了解到了一些关于执行功能（executive function）及其相关研究的信息。执行功能是指你做决策、制定计划和深思熟虑的能力，这种能力在30岁时达到巅峰，之后就开始下降。
text_es: Una cosa que fue muy reveladora fue que nadie de todos a quienes preguntamos mencionó 18. Eso realmente sorprendió a mi socio. Y lo otro que fue muy interesante es que aprendimos un poco sobre la función ejecutiva y la investigación relacionada. La función ejecutiva, que es tu capacidad para tomar decisiones y hacer planes de manera reflexiva, alcanza su punto máximo a los 30 años, y a partir de ahí comienza a decaer.
fullContext: Ada gives a personal example of using curiosity loops for non-work decisions. She and her partner were debating when their daughter should inherit their estate if something happened to both parents - he wanted 18 years old, she wanted 25. They asked trusted friends and family for input, discovering unanimous feedback against 18 and learning about executive function research that informed their final decision.

vocabulary.definition: Executive function refers to a set of cognitive processes that enable individuals to plan, focus attention, remember instructions, and juggle multiple tasks successfully.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, strong executive function is crucial for effective leadership, project management, and strategic decision-making, as it allows individuals to prioritize tasks and manage resources efficiently.

insight.nuance: While often associated with cognitive abilities, executive function can also imply emotional regulation and adaptability in dynamic business environments.

vocabulary.definition: Research is the systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, research is essential for market analysis, product development, and understanding consumer behavior, guiding strategic decisions and innovations.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both qualitative and quantitative methods, and while it often denotes formal studies, it can also refer to informal inquiries or explorations.

vocabulary.definition: Curiosity loops are cycles of inquiry and exploration that stimulate a person's desire to learn more about a subject or problem, often leading to deeper understanding and engagement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, curiosity loops can drive innovation and creativity, as they encourage teams to explore new ideas and solutions through iterative questioning and experimentation.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a positive feedback mechanism in learning, and it is often used in contexts where engagement and discovery are prioritized over rote learning.

vocabulary.definition: Interesting describes something that arouses curiosity or holds attention due to its unique or engaging qualities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, identifying interesting trends or insights can lead to innovative strategies and opportunities for growth, making it a key term in presentations and brainstorming sessions.

insight.nuance: While 'interesting' is generally positive, it can sometimes imply a lack of depth or seriousness, so it is important to use it in contexts where genuine engagement is evident.

speaker: Ada Chen Rekhi
text: When I reflect back on what works across my early career, it really comes down in a nutshell to this career concept of explore and exploit.
keySentence: Explore and exploit defines my early career experience in a nutshell.
text_ko: 내 경력을 돌아보면, 결국에는 '탐색(explore)과 활용(exploit)'이라는 경력 개념으로 요약할 수 있어요. 탐색하는 모드에 있을 때는 여러 가지 미지의 것들을 경험해보면서 내가 좋아하는지 테스트하는 단계고, 활용하는 모드에 들어가면 정말 가치 있고 깊이 있는 것을 찾은 상태예요.
text_zh: 回顾我早期职业生涯中有效的经验，归根结底可以总结为“探索与利用”（explore and exploit）的职业理念。你要么处于探索者的状态，面对许多未知的事物，测试自己是否喜欢；要么处于利用的状态，发现了一些真正丰富且深刻的机会。
text_es: Cuando reflexiono sobre lo que ha funcionado en mi carrera temprana, se reduce a este concepto profesional de explorar y explotar. Estás en un modo de explorador, donde hay muchas incógnitas y estás probando para ver si te gusta, o estás en modo de explotación, donde realmente has encontrado algo que es muy valioso y profundo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ada about her advice for early career professionals, noting her rapid career progression from entry-level at Microsoft to SVP of marketing at SurveyMonkey in seven years. Ada explains her framework of 'explore and exploit' - early in your career you should explore different roles and industries to find what you enjoy, then once you find something valuable, exploit it by going deep and building expertise in that area.

vocabulary.definition: To think deeply or carefully about something, often in order to gain insight or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, reflecting can involve analyzing past decisions, strategies, or performance to inform future actions and improve outcomes.

insight.nuance: While reflecting can imply a thoughtful consideration, it may also suggest a need for introspection, which is sometimes viewed as less action-oriented.

vocabulary.definition: A dual strategy where 'explore' refers to searching for new opportunities and 'exploit' refers to maximizing existing resources or capabilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and innovation, this phrase emphasizes the balance between seeking new markets or ideas and capitalizing on current strengths to drive growth.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a strategic approach that requires careful management of resources and risk, often used in discussions about innovation and market strategy.

vocabulary.definition: An overarching idea or framework that guides an individual's professional development and career choices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a career concept can help employees align their personal goals with organizational objectives, fostering engagement and growth.

insight.nuance: This term can imply a broader vision for one's career path, which may include aspirations, values, and the strategic planning necessary to achieve them.

vocabulary.definition: A swift advancement or development in a particular area, often referring to career growth or skill acquisition.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, rapid progression is often sought after in high-performing employees, indicating their potential for leadership roles and increased responsibilities.

insight.nuance: While rapid progression is generally viewed positively, it can also raise concerns about sustainability and the depth of experience gained in a short time.

speaker: Ada Chen Rekhi
text: It's really easy to be a victim of inertia. It's really easy for all of us to be the frog where there are little things that make us uncomfortable, and we sit with them or we think, 'Gosh, it'll get better.
keySentence: It's easy to be a victim of inertia and think it'll get better.
text_ko: 관성의 희생자가 되는 건 정말 쉽죠. 우리 모두가 불편한 작은 것들에 대해 그냥 앉아 있거나 '아, 다음 매니저가 더 나아질 거야. 나는 항상 한 번의 대화나 승진만 있으면 다음 단계에 도달할 수 있어.'라고 생각하는 개구리가 되기 쉬워요. 하지만 주변을 잘 살펴봐야 해요. 물의 온도가 어떤 방향으로 가고 있는지 인식하는 게 중요해요.
text_zh: 很容易成为惯性的受害者。我们每个人都可能像那只青蛙一样，面对一些让我们不舒服的小事，却选择忍耐，心里想着“哦，这会好起来的，下一个经理会更好。我总是离下一步的对话或晋升只有一步之遥。”但你真的需要关注周围的环境，留意水温的变化方向。
text_es: Es muy fácil caer en la inercia. Todos podemos ser como la rana que se siente incómoda con pequeñas cosas, y nos quedamos ahí pensando: "Bueno, esto mejorará. El próximo gerente será mejor. Siempre estoy a una conversación o a una promoción de dar el siguiente paso." Pero realmente debes estar consciente de tu entorno. Debes estar atento a hacia dónde se está moviendo la temperatura del agua.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ada how to know when to stick with a difficult job that might lead somewhere versus when to leave. Ada uses the metaphor of a frog being slowly boiled alive - if you put a frog in boiling water it jumps out, but if you gradually increase the temperature it doesn't notice until it's too late. She explains this applies to career situations where people become victims of inertia, always thinking things will improve with the next manager or promotion.

vocabulary.definition: Inertia refers to a tendency to remain unchanged or to resist motion or action. It can also denote a lack of progress or activity in a situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, inertia can manifest as resistance to change within an organization, leading to stagnation and missed opportunities for innovation or improvement.

insight.nuance: While inertia often has a negative connotation in a business context, it can also imply stability in certain situations where change may not be necessary.

vocabulary.definition: Uncomfortable describes a state of physical or emotional discomfort, often resulting from challenging or distressing situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, feeling uncomfortable can arise during difficult conversations, performance reviews, or when confronting issues that require change, which can hinder productivity and morale.

insight.nuance: While discomfort is often viewed negatively, it can also be a catalyst for growth and improvement when approached constructively.

vocabulary.definition: A metaphor is a figure of speech that makes a comparison between two unrelated things by stating that one is the other, thereby highlighting similarities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, metaphors are often used to simplify complex ideas, making them more relatable and easier for stakeholders to understand.

insight.nuance: Metaphors can enhance storytelling and persuasion in business, but overuse or inappropriate metaphors may lead to confusion or misinterpretation.

vocabulary.definition: Difficult describes something that is hard to accomplish, deal with, or understand, often requiring significant effort or skill.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, difficult tasks may include navigating complex projects, resolving conflicts, or implementing change management strategies.

insight.nuance: While 'difficult' generally has a negative connotation, it can also imply a challenge that, when overcome, leads to growth and achievement.

speaker: Ada Chen Rekhi
text: I think that's a terrible trap that we should all try to avoid as we navigate our career paths and find the thing that's most optimal for us.
keySentence: Avoid the terrible trap while navigating our career paths for meaningfulness and alignment.
text_ko: 우리는 경력 경로를 탐색하면서 피해야 할 끔찍한 함정이라고 생각해요. 우리에게 가장 최적화된 것을 찾는 과정에서 말이죠. 보통은 경력 성공의 조합이지만, 우리가 하는 일에서 의미와 가치와의 일치도 중요하잖아요.
text_zh: 我认为这是一个我们都应该尽量避免的陷阱，在我们职业发展和寻找最适合自己的方向时，通常需要平衡职业成功、工作意义以及与我们价值观的契合。
text_es: Creo que es una trampa terrible que todos debemos intentar evitar mientras navegamos por nuestras trayectorias profesionales y encontramos lo que es más óptimo para nosotros. Lo cual, por lo general, es una combinación de éxito profesional, pero también de significado y alineación en el trabajo que realizamos con nuestros valores.
fullContext: Ada is discussing the importance of not getting trapped in a career path driven solely by external expectations or lifestyle requirements. She emphasizes that waking up late in your career feeling unhappy with your work, but unable to change due to financial obligations or others' expectations, is a terrible outcome. She advocates for finding work that balances career success with personal meaningfulness and alignment with your core values.

vocabulary.definition: To plan and direct the course of something, often involving careful consideration of various factors and obstacles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'navigate' often refers to the process of steering through complex market conditions, organizational challenges, or career paths to achieve desired outcomes.

insight.nuance: While 'navigate' implies skill and strategy, it can also suggest the presence of difficulties that require careful maneuvering.

vocabulary.definition: The most favorable or desirable condition, especially in terms of efficiency or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, achieving 'optimal' results means maximizing productivity and minimizing waste, often through data-driven decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term 'optimal' suggests a balance between various competing factors, and is often used in discussions about resource allocation and strategic planning.

vocabulary.definition: A situation or condition that restricts freedom of action or leads to negative consequences, often unexpectedly.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a 'trap' may refer to pitfalls such as overcommitment to a failing project or falling into a cycle of unproductive habits that hinder growth.

insight.nuance: The word 'trap' carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of awareness or foresight that leads to undesirable outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: Beliefs or assumptions about what will happen in the future, often forming the basis for planning and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, managing 'expectations' is crucial for aligning team goals, client relationships, and stakeholder communications to ensure satisfaction and success.

insight.nuance: While 'expectations' can be positive, they can also lead to disappointment if not met, making it important to communicate them clearly and realistically.

speaker: Ada Chen Rekhi
text: My hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
keySentence: for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
text_ko: 내 생각에는 대다수의 사람들에게 코치가 꼭 필요하지는 않은 것 같아요. 보통 사람들이 코치를 생각할 때는 뭔가 막히거나 해결하고 싶은 문제가 있다는 신호거든요. 그래서 저는 그들에게 "코칭을 통해 어떤 목표를 이루고 싶으세요?"라고 물어봐요.
text_zh: 我的看法是，对于绝大多数人来说，他们可能并不需要教练（coach）。我常常会问那些考虑请教练的人，因为这通常表明他们感到困惑或有问题需要解决，我会问他们：“你在教练方面的目标是什么？”
text_es: Mi opinión es que para la gran mayoría de las personas, probablemente no necesitan un coach. Y lo que a menudo les pregunto es que si están considerando contratar a un coach, lo cual generalmente indica que se sienten estancados o tienen un problema que intentan resolver, les pregunto: '¿Cuáles son tus objetivos en relación al coaching?'
fullContext: Lenny asks Ada about when people should consider getting an executive coach, given her work as a coach to founders. Surprisingly, Ada argues that most people don't actually need a coach and should first explore alternatives like mentorship through curiosity loops, taking courses, or building supportive communities. She challenges people to clearly define their coaching goals and consider if there are better ways to achieve those same outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: A hot take is a quickly formed opinion or reaction to a current event or topic, often characterized by its provocative or controversial nature.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, a hot take can refer to an immediate, often bold opinion on market trends or company strategies that may not be fully substantiated.

insight.nuance: While hot takes can stimulate discussion, they may also lack depth and should be used cautiously to avoid misrepresentation of complex issues.

vocabulary.definition: The majority refers to more than half of a particular group or population, often used to indicate a dominant or prevailing opinion or trend.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market research, understanding the majority's preferences can guide product development and marketing strategies.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a sense of authority or consensus, but it may overlook minority perspectives that are equally important.

vocabulary.definition: To consider means to think carefully about something, especially in making a decision or forming an opinion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, leaders must consider various factors such as market conditions, stakeholder interests, and potential risks before making strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: While 'consider' suggests a thoughtful approach, it can also imply indecision if used excessively; thus, it should be balanced with action.

vocabulary.definition: An executive coach is a professional who provides guidance and support to business leaders and executives to enhance their leadership skills and performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: Executive coaching is often utilized in corporate environments to develop high-potential employees, improve team dynamics, and foster organizational growth.

insight.nuance: While executive coaching can be highly beneficial, it may also carry a stigma of being only for those in crisis, so it is important to frame it positively as a development tool.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: Onboarding is the only part of your product experience that a hundred percent of people are ever going to touch. Good luck getting a hundred percent feature adoption of anything else in your product, right?
keySentence: Onboarding is the only part of your product experience that a hundred percent of people are ever going to touch.
text_ko: 온보딩(onboarding)은 여러분의 제품 경험 중에서 모든 사람들이 반드시 경험하게 되는 유일한 부분이에요. 다른 어떤 기능도 100% 사용자가 다 사용할 거라고 기대하기는 힘들죠. 하지만 온보딩은 제품을 사용하기 위해 반드시 거쳐야 하는 과정이에요. 그리고 이건 여러분이 시장에서 약속한 것을 실현할 수 있는 첫 번째 기회이기도 해요.
text_zh: 用户引导是您产品体验中唯一一个百分之百的用户都会接触到的部分。想要实现其他功能的百分之百采用率几乎是不可能的，对吧？但是用户引导是用户使用产品之前必须经历的过程。这也是您作为公司在市场上兑现承诺的第一次机会。
text_es: La incorporación (onboarding) es la única parte de la experiencia de tu producto que el cien por ciento de las personas va a experimentar. Buena suerte logrando que el cien por ciento adopte cualquier otra función en tu producto, ¿verdad? Pero la incorporación es el proceso que todos deben atravesar para poder utilizar el producto. También es la primera oportunidad que tienes como empresa para cumplir con la promesa que hiciste en el mercado.
fullContext: Lenny asks Adam about onboarding as a growth lever and what gets him excited about investing in onboarding optimization. Adam explains why onboarding is such a critical part of the product experience that companies should prioritize. He emphasizes that onboarding is unique because it's the only feature with 100% user adoption, and it's the first chance to deliver on your brand promise to customers.

vocabulary.definition: Onboarding refers to the process of integrating new users or employees into a system or organization, ensuring they understand how to use the product or their role effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, onboarding is crucial for user retention and satisfaction, as it sets the foundation for a positive experience with the product or company.

insight.nuance: Onboarding can imply a structured process, and it is often emphasized in customer success strategies to enhance user engagement.

vocabulary.definition: Feature adoption is the process by which users begin to utilize and integrate new features of a product into their regular usage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, tracking feature adoption is essential for understanding user engagement and the overall success of product updates or new releases.

insight.nuance: Feature adoption can vary widely among users, and low adoption rates may indicate usability issues or a lack of awareness.

vocabulary.definition: A growth lever is a strategy or tactic that can be employed to drive significant growth in a business, often through scalable actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, identifying and utilizing growth levers is critical for achieving rapid expansion and maximizing return on investment.

insight.nuance: The term suggests that certain actions can produce disproportionately large results, making it important to prioritize high-impact strategies.

vocabulary.definition: Optimization is the process of making something as effective or functional as possible, often through adjustments and improvements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, optimization is frequently applied to processes, products, and marketing strategies to enhance performance and efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a continuous process of improvement rather than a one-time fix, highlighting the need for ongoing evaluation.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: I like to think of your brand is the promise that you're making and your product experience is your delivery of that promise.
keySentence: your brand is the promise that you're making and your product experience is your delivery of that promise.
text_ko: 당신의 브랜드는 약속이라고 생각해요. 그리고 제품 경험은 그 약속을 실현하는 방식이죠. 이 두 가지는 항상 맞물려 있어야 해요. 그렇지 않으면 고객의 기대와 실제 경험이 다르게 되어 실망하는 경우가 생길 수 있어요. 고객이 처음으로 느끼는 감정이 정말 기대되거나 실망스러울 수 있으니까, 이 부분을 잘 챙겨야 해요. 실수하지 마세요.
text_zh: 我认为你的品牌是你所做的承诺，而你的产品体验则是对这个承诺的兑现。这两者必须紧密相连，否则就会导致期望不匹配，进而让客户感到失望。因此，这是客户第一次真正感受到兴奋或失望的机会，所以一定要把握好这个环节。
text_es: Me gusta pensar en tu marca como la promesa que estás haciendo, y la experiencia de tu producto como la entrega de esa promesa. Ambas deben estar alineadas, de lo contrario, tendrás expectativas desajustadas y clientes realmente decepcionados. Esta es la primera oportunidad que tiene un cliente para sentirse realmente emocionado o muy decepcionado con lo que pensaba que iba a recibir. Así que no lo estropees.
fullContext: Adam continues explaining why onboarding is such a crucial growth lever for companies. He describes the relationship between brand promises and product delivery, emphasizing that these must be perfectly aligned. Adam warns that onboarding is the critical moment where customers first experience whether the product matches their expectations from marketing and sales efforts.

vocabulary.definition: A brand promise is a statement that communicates the value and experience a customer can expect from a brand's products or services. It serves as a commitment to deliver specific benefits and quality to consumers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in marketing and branding, the brand promise is essential for building customer trust and loyalty, as it sets expectations for the customer experience.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of reliability and integrity; it should be used when discussing the foundational commitments of a brand.

vocabulary.definition: Product experience refers to the overall interaction a customer has with a product, encompassing usability, design, and emotional response. It is a critical factor in customer satisfaction and retention.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, optimizing the product experience is vital for user engagement and can differentiate a product in a competitive market.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the holistic view of user interaction; it should be used when discussing aspects beyond just functionality, including aesthetics and emotional impact.

vocabulary.definition: Delivery in a business context refers to the process of providing a product or service to the customer, including logistics, timing, and quality of service. It is a critical aspect of fulfilling customer expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, effective delivery mechanisms can enhance customer satisfaction and operational efficiency, directly impacting sales and reputation.

insight.nuance: The term can imply not just physical delivery but also the timely and effective provision of services; it should be used when discussing logistics or service fulfillment.

vocabulary.definition: A crucial growth lever is a strategic factor or action that can significantly influence a company's growth trajectory. Identifying and utilizing these levers is essential for scaling a business effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, recognizing crucial growth levers can guide investment decisions and operational focus, helping to prioritize initiatives that will yield the highest impact.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests importance and urgency; it should be used when discussing strategic initiatives that are vital for achieving growth objectives.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: The goal of the competency model is not to find a unicorn human being that is an 11 out of 10 on every one of these things, because frankly, that person doesn't exist.
keySentence: the goal of the competency model is not to find a unicorn human being that is an 11 out of 10 on every one of these things
text_ko: 역량 모델의 목표는 모든 항목에서 10점 만점에 11점을 주는 유니콘 같은 사람을 찾는 게 아니에요. 솔직히 그런 사람은 존재하지 않거든요. 저도 이 스킬들에서 10점 만점에 11점은 아니지만, 여러 회사에서 성장 임원으로 일해왔어요. 제 일을 꽤 잘한다고 생각해요. 목표는 잘 균형 잡힌 팀을 만드는 거예요. 그래서 팀의 스킬을 다양하게 채용하고 포트폴리오에 빈틈이 없도록 하는 게 중요해요.
text_zh: 能力模型的目标并不是寻找一个在所有方面都能达到满分11分的“独角兽”人才，因为坦白说，这样的人并不存在。我在这些技能上也不是满分11分，但我在许多公司担任过增长高管，并且认为自己在这份工作上表现相当不错。目标是建立一个全面发展的团队，以便在招聘时能够平衡团队的技能，确保你的团队中没有技能空缺。
text_es: El objetivo del modelo de competencias no es encontrar un ser humano unicornio que sea un 11 de 10 en cada una de estas áreas, porque, francamente, esa persona no existe. Yo no soy un 11 de 10 en estas habilidades y he sido un ejecutivo de crecimiento en muchas empresas. Me considero bastante bueno en mi trabajo. El objetivo es crear un equipo equilibrado para que estés contratando y balanceando habilidades en tu equipo y así no tengas ninguna brecha en tu portafolio.
fullContext: Lenny asks Adam about the components of his growth competency model for hiring growth professionals. Adam explains that the model isn't about finding perfect candidates who excel at everything, but rather about building balanced teams. He emphasizes that even experienced growth executives like himself aren't perfect at all skills, and the key is ensuring your team collectively covers all necessary competencies without gaps.

vocabulary.definition: A competency model is a framework that outlines the skills, knowledge, and behaviors required for effective performance in a specific role or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, competency models are used for recruitment, training, and performance evaluation to ensure alignment between employee capabilities and organizational goals.

insight.nuance: While competency models aim to identify essential traits for success, they should not be viewed as rigid checklists but rather as flexible guidelines that can adapt to individual strengths.

vocabulary.definition: Components are individual parts or elements that make up a larger system or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding the components of a project or product is crucial for effective planning, execution, and analysis of performance.

insight.nuance: The term 'components' often implies a modular approach, suggesting that each part can be independently assessed or modified without affecting the whole.

vocabulary.definition: To excel means to perform exceptionally well or to surpass others in a particular area or skill.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, employees are often encouraged to excel in their roles to drive innovation, productivity, and overall organizational success.

insight.nuance: While 'excel' conveys a positive connotation of high achievement, it can also imply pressure to consistently perform at a high level, which may lead to stress.

vocabulary.definition: Candidates are individuals being considered for a position, role, or opportunity, often after a selection process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In recruitment, candidates are evaluated based on their qualifications and fit for the organization, with the goal of identifying the best match for the role.

insight.nuance: The term 'candidates' can sometimes carry a competitive connotation, suggesting that individuals are vying against each other for limited opportunities.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: One of the challenges of hiring a senior person is that they're all off writing newsletters and making podcast. Not that we know anybody who does that or anything, but... So I don't want to right now go back and work at a company again.
keySentence: One of the challenges of hiring a senior person is that they're all off writing newsletters and making podcast.
text_ko: 고위직 사람을 채용하는 데 어려운 점 중 하나는 그들이 모두 뉴스레터를 쓰고 팟캐스트를 만드는 데 바쁘다는 거예요. 그런 사람을 아는 건 아니지만... 지금은 다시 회사에서 일하고 싶지 않아요. 제가 하고 있는 일이 너무 재밌어서요. 그래서 저를 구하는 게 쉽지 않을 거예요, 맞죠? 하지만 처음 이걸 시도할 때는 저 같은 사람을 원하지 않을 것 같기도 해요.
text_zh: 招聘高级人才的一个挑战是，他们往往忙于撰写通讯和制作播客。并不是说我们认识这样的人，但……所以我现在不想回到公司工作。我很享受我现在的工作，因此很难找到我，对吧？但我觉得在你第一次进行这样的尝试时，你也不太需要我。
text_es: Uno de los desafíos de contratar a una persona senior es que todos están ocupados escribiendo boletines y haciendo podcasts. No es que conozcamos a alguien que haga eso, pero... Así que no quiero volver a trabajar en una empresa en este momento. Estoy disfrutando lo que hago y por eso es difícil que me consigan, ¿verdad? Pero también creo que no me querrían, especialmente si están haciendo esto por primera vez.
fullContext: Lenny asks whether founders should focus on finding up-and-coming growth talent versus senior executives. Adam humorously points out that many senior growth professionals have moved into advisory roles or content creation, making them unavailable for full-time positions. He suggests that founders shouldn't necessarily want the most senior person anyway when building their first growth function.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulties or obstacles that require effort to overcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, challenges often refer to issues that companies face in achieving their goals, such as market competition, resource limitations, or operational inefficiencies.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a need for strategic thinking and problem-solving skills to navigate complex situations.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals with senior management responsibilities within an organization, often involved in strategic decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: Executives play a crucial role in shaping company direction, managing resources, and leading teams to achieve organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of authority and leadership, often associated with high-level positions such as CEO, CFO, or COO.

vocabulary.definition: Providing guidance or recommendations, often based on expertise or experience in a particular field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, advisory roles can include consultants or boards that offer strategic insights to help organizations make informed decisions.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a supportive role rather than a directive one, emphasizing collaboration and expertise.

vocabulary.definition: The process of increasing in size, value, or importance over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, growth is often measured in terms of revenue, market share, or customer base expansion, and is a primary goal for many organizations.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both positive development and the challenges that come with scaling, such as resource allocation and market adaptation.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: So if you're going to hire a junior person, the key is, how do you help them learn? And I think if you don't know what you're doing as the founder or the leader, it's hard.
keySentence: the key is, how do you help them learn?
text_ko: 주니어 직원을 채용할 거라면, 가장 중요한 건 그들이 어떻게 배우도록 도와줄 수 있을까 하는 거예요. 만약 창립자나 리더로서 내가 뭘 하고 있는지 모른다면, 그들을 도와주기가 힘들어요. 그러니까 저 같은 외부 전문가나 교육, 멘토링, 코칭에 투자할 준비가 되어 있어야 해요. 그렇지 않으면, 의욕 넘치고 열정적인 그 사람이 벽을 뚫고 나가게 될 텐데, 그건 좋지만, 사실 그 벽 옆에 문이 있었던 걸 놓치게 될 거예요. 결국 바닥에 많은 벽돌만 남게 될 거예요.
text_zh: 如果你打算招聘一位初级员工，关键在于如何帮助他们学习。我认为，如果作为创始人或领导者你自己都不清楚该怎么做，那就很困难。你无法亲自帮助他们。因此，你必须愿意投资于像我这样的顾问、外部教育、指导和教练。否则，结果就是那些充满干劲、渴望和热情的人会不断撞墙，这固然很好，但他们可能会忽视旁边就有一扇门，而最终你会发现地上满是砖头。
text_es: Si vas a contratar a una persona junior, la clave es cómo ayudarles a aprender. Y creo que si no sabes lo que estás haciendo como fundador o líder, es complicado. No podrás ayudarles tú mismo. Por lo tanto, debes estar dispuesto a invertir en asesores como yo, educación externa, mentoría, coaching; de lo contrario, lo que sucederá es que esa persona muy motivada, hambrienta y entusiasta va a chocar contra muchas paredes, lo cual está bien, excepto que van a pasar por alto el hecho de que la puerta estaba justo al lado de la pared por la que acaban de pasar y terminarás con muchos ladrillos en el suelo.
fullContext: Adam continues discussing the strategy of hiring junior growth talent instead of senior executives. He explains that while hiring junior people can work well, founders need to invest in proper support systems like advisors, education, and mentorship. Adam uses a vivid metaphor to illustrate how enthusiastic but inexperienced people can waste effort on the wrong approaches when they lack proper guidance.

vocabulary.definition: To allocate resources, usually money, with the expectation of generating a profit or achieving a beneficial return in the future.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'invest in' often refers to funding startups, projects, or initiatives that are anticipated to yield financial returns or strategic advantages.

insight.nuance: While 'invest in' typically implies a financial commitment, it can also refer to investing time or effort in developing skills or relationships.

vocabulary.definition: To provide assistance or resources to help someone or something succeed or function effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'support' can refer to providing financial backing, mentorship, or operational resources to employees, projects, or initiatives.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of encouragement and active involvement, rather than passive assistance.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, often involving the allocation of resources and prioritization of goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'strategy' refers to the comprehensive plan that guides a company’s decisions and actions to achieve competitive advantage and market positioning.

insight.nuance: The term implies a thoughtful and systematic approach, distinguishing it from mere tactics or short-term actions.

vocabulary.definition: An individual who establishes or originates a business or organization, often taking on a significant role in its early development and direction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, 'founder' refers to the person or people who create the company, often responsible for its vision, culture, and initial operations.

insight.nuance: The term carries a sense of authority and responsibility, often implying a deep personal investment in the success of the venture.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: I actually think if you're doing it right, sometimes conversion should actually decrease a little bit.
keySentence: sometimes conversion should actually decrease a little bit.
text_ko: 사실 제가 생각하기에, 제대로 하고 있다면 가끔 전환율이 조금 떨어지는 게 맞는 것 같아요. 그래서 성공적으로 끝까지 가는 사람이 줄어들 수도 있는데, 그게 괜찮다고 생각해요. 왜냐하면 그런 사람들 중 많은 이들이 아마도 당신의 제품에 적합하지 않은 사람들이었을 테니까요. 그러면 그들은 고객으로서도 잘 참여하지 않았을 거고, 아마 이탈(churn)했을 가능성이 높아요.
text_zh: 我认为如果你做得对，有时候转化率（conversion）实际上应该稍微下降。这可能意味着成功完成购买的人数会减少，但我认为这没关系，因为很多人可能并不适合你的产品，这意味着他们不会成为活跃客户，最终可能会流失（churn）。
text_es: En realidad, creo que si lo estás haciendo bien, a veces la tasa de conversión (conversion rate) debería disminuir un poco. Puede que tengas menos personas que lleguen hasta el final con éxito, pero creo que eso está bien, porque muchas de esas personas probablemente no eran las adecuadas para tu producto, lo que significa que no habrían sido clientes comprometidos (engaged customers) y probablemente habrían abandonado (churned).
fullContext: Lenny asks Adam how to think about onboarding as a conversion opportunity versus retention opportunity. Adam explains a counterintuitive principle: good onboarding optimization might actually reduce conversion rates slightly. He argues this is beneficial because it filters out unqualified users who would likely churn anyway, resulting in higher quality users who are more likely to retain and succeed with the product.

vocabulary.definition: The process of changing or transforming something into a different state or form, often referring to turning prospects into customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, conversion typically refers to the percentage of visitors to a website who complete a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a newsletter.

insight.nuance: While a high conversion rate is generally desirable, it can sometimes indicate a lack of quality engagement if achieved through aggressive tactics.

vocabulary.definition: The action of making the best or most effective use of a resource or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, optimization often involves improving processes, systems, or marketing strategies to maximize efficiency and profitability.

insight.nuance: Optimization can sometimes lead to diminishing returns, where further improvements yield minimal benefits, so it's important to balance efforts with outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: Contrary to what one would intuitively expect or believe; not aligning with common sense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, counterintuitive strategies may lead to unexpected results, such as investing in customer service to reduce costs in the long run.

insight.nuance: Using 'counterintuitive' can imply a level of complexity or sophistication in thinking, making it suitable for discussions that challenge conventional wisdom.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to keep or hold onto something, particularly in the context of customers or employees.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, retention refers to the strategies and practices aimed at keeping customers engaged and loyal over time, which is crucial for long-term success.

insight.nuance: While retention is often viewed positively, it can also imply a need for improvement in customer satisfaction or employee engagement if retention rates are low.

speaker: Adam Fishman
text: When you're interviewing at a company, you are actually investing an even more scarce resource. You're investing your time. There is no way to get more time. We're all on a finite clock. You can always get more money.
keySentence: Interviewing is investing an even more scarce resource: your time, which is fleeting.
text_ko: 회사를 인터뷰할 때, 사실 더 귀한 자원에 투자하고 있는 거예요. 바로 시간이에요. 시간은 절대 늘릴 수 없잖아요. 우리 모두 한정된 시간 안에 살고 있어요. 돈은 언제든지 더 벌 수 있지만, 잘못된 투자 결정을 내리면 '아, 여기서 손해봤네.' 하고 넘어갈 수 있어요. 파산하지 않는 한, 파산해도 다시 일어설 수 있는 방법이 있죠. 하지만 시간은 정말 빠르게 지나가요.
text_zh: 在面试公司时，实际上你是在投资一种更加稀缺的资源，那就是时间。时间是无法再生的，我们每个人的时间都是有限的。你可以随时赚到更多的钱。如果做出了错误的投资决策，没关系，“我们在这里亏了。”只要你没有破产。即使破产了，你也可以东山再起。但时间是转瞬即逝的。
text_es: Cuando estás en una entrevista en una empresa, en realidad estás invirtiendo un recurso aún más escaso. Estás invirtiendo tu tiempo. No hay forma de recuperar el tiempo. Todos estamos en un reloj finito. Siempre puedes conseguir más dinero. Si tomas una mala decisión de inversión, 'Está bien, perdimos ahí.' Siempre y cuando no te hayas arruinado. Incluso si lo hiciste, puedes salir de la bancarrota. Hay cosas que puedes hacer, pero el tiempo es efímero.
fullContext: Lenny asks for tips on evaluating whether people at a company are a good fit before joining. Adam draws an analogy between job hunting and investing, explaining that candidates should do as much diligence as investors do when evaluating companies. He emphasizes that when you join a company, you're investing your most precious resource - time - which unlike money, can never be recovered once lost.
