vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding different audiences is critical for tailoring marketing strategies and ensuring effective communication in business operations.

insight.nuance: The term can imply various segments, such as demographics or psychographics, and should be used to highlight the diversity of consumer needs and preferences.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: Because these models are so effective at this point, you want to start to tune them to certain types of outcomes. All of a sudden, these are these living organisms that just get better with the more interactions that happen.
keySentence: Tune models to certain types of outcomes for better interactions.
text_ko: 이 모델(models)들이 이제 워낙 효과적이어서, 특정한 결과에 맞게 튜닝(tuning)하기 시작해야 해요. 어느 순간부터 이건 상호작용이 늘어날수록 더 좋아지는 살아있는 유기체처럼 됐어요. 생각하고, 살아있고, 학습하는 모든 회사 제품들에겐 이게 새로운 지적재산(IP)이 될 거라고 생각해요.
text_zh: 现在这些模型已经非常厉害了，你就想开始调教它们，让它们产生特定的结果。突然间，这些东西就像活的生物一样，互动得越多就越聪明。我觉得这就是每个公司的新知识产权(IP)——能思考、能存活、能学习的产品。
text_es: Como estos modelos son tan efectivos ya en este punto, quieres empezar a ajustarlos para ciertos tipos de resultados. De repente, se convierten en estos organismos vivos que mejoran mientras más interacciones tengan. Creo que esta es la nueva propiedad intelectual (IP) de todas las empresas: productos que piensan, viven y aprenden.
fullContext: Lenny asks Asha about her concept of moving from "product as artifact to product as organism." Asha explains how AI models have evolved beyond static software products that are shipped once and occasionally updated. Instead, modern AI products continuously improve through user interactions and feedback loops, creating what she calls "living organisms" that adapt and learn over time.

vocabulary.definition: To adjust or modify something to achieve a desired effect or performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'tuning' often refers to optimizing algorithms, models, or processes to enhance their effectiveness or efficiency in achieving specific goals.

insight.nuance: While 'tune' suggests a careful and precise adjustment, it can imply a level of experimentation and iteration, which may not always be suitable for all contexts.

vocabulary.definition: The results or consequences of a particular action, process, or decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'outcomes' are often used to measure the success or impact of strategies, initiatives, or projects, guiding future decisions.

insight.nuance: The term 'outcomes' can carry a positive or negative connotation depending on the context, emphasizing the importance of measuring effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: The act of communicating or engaging with others, often resulting in a reciprocal exchange.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'interactions' can refer to customer engagements, team collaborations, or stakeholder communications that influence relationships and outcomes.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a dynamic and ongoing process, highlighting the importance of relationship-building in business environments.

vocabulary.definition: To develop gradually, often in response to changing conditions or environments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, 'evolved' describes how products, services, or strategies adapt over time to meet market demands or technological advancements.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a positive progression and improvement, often associated with innovation and growth, making it suitable for discussions about development and change.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: We're approaching this world in which the marginal cost of the good output is approaching zero. We're going to see exponential demand for productivity and outputs. The way that you scale to that is with agents.
keySentence: Marginal cost of good output is approaching zero, changing the org chart.
text_ko: 우리는 산출물의 한계비용(marginal cost)이 거의 0에 가까워지는 세상으로 접어들고 있어요. 생산성(productivity)과 산출물(outputs)에 대한 수요가 기하급수적으로 늘어날 거예요. 그걸 확장(scale)하는 방법은 에이전트(agents)를 활용하는 거고요. 그런 변화가 일어나면 조직도(org chart)가 곧 실제 일(work chart)이 되기 시작해요. 그래서 계층 구조가 그렇게 많이 필요하지 않게 돼요.
text_zh: 我们正在进入一个边际成本(marginal cost)接近零的时代。生产力和产出的需求会呈指数级增长。要应对这种规模，就得靠智能代理(agents)。当这一切发生时，组织架构图基本上就变成了工作流程图。你根本不需要那么多层级了。
text_es: Nos estamos acercando a un mundo donde el costo marginal de producir buenos resultados se está volviendo casi cero. Vamos a ver una demanda exponencial de productividad y resultados. La forma de escalar a ese nivel es con agentes. Cuando todo eso pase, el organigrama empieza a convertirse en el diagrama de trabajo. Simplemente ya no necesitas tantos niveles jerárquicos.
fullContext: Lenny asks Asha about her prediction that we're just starting to scratch the surface of what an agentic society looks like. Asha explains her vision of the future where AI agents dramatically reduce the cost of producing quality work outputs, leading to exponential demand for productivity. She predicts this will fundamentally change organizational structures from traditional hierarchies to task-based work assignments.

vocabulary.definition: Marginal cost refers to the additional cost incurred to produce one more unit of a good or service. It is a crucial concept in economics that helps businesses determine pricing and production levels.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, understanding marginal cost is essential for making informed decisions about scaling production and pricing strategies to maximize profitability.

insight.nuance: While marginal cost is often considered in the context of production, it can also apply to service industries where incremental service delivery costs are analyzed.

vocabulary.definition: Exponential describes a rapid increase or growth pattern where the rate of change becomes more significant as time progresses, often represented mathematically as a constant raised to a variable exponent.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, exponential growth is frequently observed in user adoption rates, revenue generation, and data accumulation, leading companies to strategize for scalability and resource allocation.

insight.nuance: The term 'exponential' can imply not just rapid growth but also the potential for unsustainable practices if not managed correctly.

vocabulary.definition: Scale refers to the ability of a business to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance or losing revenue potential, often achieved through efficient processes and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, scaling is critical as it allows companies to expand their operations and reach larger markets while maintaining or reducing costs, often leveraging technology and automation.

insight.nuance: While scaling can indicate growth, it is important to differentiate between scaling sustainably and simply growing without a solid foundation, which can lead to operational challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Productivity measures the efficiency of production, typically expressed as the ratio of outputs produced to inputs used, indicating how effectively resources are utilized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, enhancing productivity is a key objective, as it directly impacts profitability and competitiveness, often driven by technological advancements and process improvements.

insight.nuance: While high productivity is generally positive, it should be balanced with employee well-being and sustainability to avoid burnout and ethical concerns.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: I think everybody is using some sort of co-pilot or sort of AI in their day-to-day workflows like job one, so everyone's not afraid of it, understands how we can raise the ceiling and lower the floor for all sorts of skills and tasks.
keySentence: Job one is using AI to raise the ceiling and lower the floor.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 거의 모든 사람이 일상 업무에서 코파일럿(co-pilot)이나 인공지능(AI) 같은 걸 이미 쓰고 있어요. 그래서 다들 이제 두려워하지 않고, 이런 도구로 여러 기술과 업무의 최고 성과는 끌어올리고 최소 수행 수준(진입 장벽)은 낮출 수 있다는 걸 이해하고 있어요.
text_zh: 我觉得现在大家在日常工作中都会用到一些副驾驶(co-pilot)或者AI工具，这已经是基本操作了，所以大家都不怕这些技术，也明白怎么用它们来提升上限、降低门槛，让各种技能和任务都变得更容易上手。
text_es: Creo que todo el mundo ya está usando algún tipo de copiloto o IA en su trabajo del día a día como prioridad número uno, entonces ya nadie le tiene miedo, entiende cómo podemos subir el techo y bajar el piso para todo tipo de habilidades y tareas.
fullContext: Lenny asks what patterns distinguish companies that successfully build AI products from those that struggle. Asha outlines the first step successful companies take: ensuring all employees become AI fluent by using AI tools in their daily work. This removes fear and helps everyone understand AI's potential to enhance capabilities across different skill levels and tasks.

vocabulary.definition: To increase the upper limit or potential of something, often referring to capabilities or performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, raising the ceiling can refer to enhancing productivity, innovation, or the overall performance of a team or organization through improved tools or strategies.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a positive enhancement, suggesting growth and improvement rather than merely meeting existing standards.

vocabulary.definition: To decrease the minimum standard or baseline level of performance or capability.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, lowering the floor can mean making tasks more accessible or achievable for a wider range of employees, often through training or simplified processes.

insight.nuance: This phrase can carry a connotation of making things easier or more inclusive, but may also imply a reduction in quality or standards if not managed carefully.

vocabulary.definition: A sequence of processes or tasks that are carried out to achieve a specific outcome or complete a project.
vocabulary.businessContext: Workflows are critical in business for streamlining operations, ensuring efficiency, and facilitating collaboration among team members.

insight.nuance: While workflows can be formalized and documented, they can also be informal and adaptable, depending on the team's needs and the nature of the tasks.

vocabulary.definition: The abilities or expertise that individuals possess, enabling them to perform tasks effectively and efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, skills are essential for employee performance, and organizations often invest in training and development to enhance their workforce's capabilities.

insight.nuance: The term can refer to both hard skills (technical abilities) and soft skills (interpersonal abilities), and its usage may vary depending on the context of the discussion.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: I really believe in the concept of the full stack builder. You're seeing it with a bunch of the AI native companies that are coming up. I'm even seeing it in enterprises that have been around for 50 years starting to operate in that way.
keySentence: I really believe in the concept of the full stack builder.
text_ko: 저는 풀 스택 빌더(full stack builder)라는 개념을 정말 믿어요. 요즘 생겨나는 AI 네이티브(AI native) 기업들에서 그 모습이 보이고 있고, 50년 넘은 기업들조차 그렇게 운영하기 시작하는 걸 보고 있어요. 그런 접근이 속도와 처리량(velocity and throughput)을 높여주고, 전체 루프(loop)를 만들어 실제로 그걸 더 빠르게 내재화(metabolize)하고 과정을 훨씬 빨리 돌릴 수 있게 해줘요.
text_zh: 我特别认同全栈建设者(full stack builder)这个理念。你看现在很多AI原生公司都是这么做的，连那些有五十年历史的老企业都开始这样运作了。我觉得这样能让你的执行速度更快，产出更高，而且能形成一个完整的闭环，让你消化吸收、迭代优化的速度大大提升。
text_es: Yo creo mucho en el concepto del desarrollador full stack (full stack builder). Lo estás viendo con un montón de estas empresas nativas de IA que están surgiendo. Incluso lo estoy viendo en empresas que llevan 50 años operando y están empezando a trabajar de esa manera. Y creo que eso te da velocidad y productividad, y luego te da todo el ciclo completo para realmente procesar y avanzar mucho más rápido.
fullContext: Lenny asks about patterns in successful AI companies, and Asha discusses how traditional organizational structures are changing. She explains that the traditional product development process involves too many layers and touchpoints to keep up with rapidly evolving AI technology. The solution is "full stack builders" - individuals who can work across multiple disciplines rather than being confined to narrow functional roles.

vocabulary.definition: A general idea or understanding of something, often serving as a foundation for further development or discussion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a concept can refer to a new product idea, a business model, or an innovative approach that guides strategic planning and execution.

insight.nuance: While 'concept' is often used in brainstorming and early-stage discussions, it may imply a lack of concrete details or implementation plans.

vocabulary.definition: Large organizations or businesses engaged in commercial activities, often characterized by complex structures and a focus on profit generation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, enterprises can refer to both established companies and startups that operate on a larger scale, often involving multiple departments and diverse product lines.

insight.nuance: The term 'enterprise' conveys a sense of ambition and scale, and is often associated with formal business structures rather than informal or small-scale operations.

vocabulary.definition: The system that outlines how certain activities are directed in order to achieve an organization's goals, including roles, responsibilities, and communication pathways.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, understanding organizational structures is crucial for effective management, as they determine how resources are allocated and how teams collaborate.

insight.nuance: While 'organizational structures' can refer to traditional hierarchies, it may also encompass more modern, agile frameworks that promote flexibility and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating, designing, and bringing a new product to market, encompassing all stages from initial idea to final launch.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, product development is critical for innovation and competitiveness, often involving iterative testing and feedback loops to refine offerings.

insight.nuance: The term 'product development' implies a systematic approach, and is often associated with methodologies like Agile or Lean, which emphasize rapid iteration and customer feedback.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: We think about it as what season are we in? Season one might've been prototyping of AI and then it was all around models and reasoning models, and now it's the advent of agents.
keySentence: We are witnessing the advent of agents in AI development.
text_ko: 우리는 지금 어떤 시즌에 있나 생각해요. 첫 시즌은 인공지능(AI) 프로토타이핑(prototyping) 단계였고, 그다음에는 모델(models)과 추론 모델(reasoning models)이 중심이었어요. 지금은 에이전트(agents)가 본격적으로 등장한 시기예요.
text_zh: 我们是这么想的，现在我们处在哪个阶段？第一阶段可能是AI原型开发，然后就是各种模型和推理模型(reasoning models)的阶段，现在我们迎来了智能代理(agents)的时代。
text_es: Lo vemos como ¿en qué temporada estamos? La primera temporada pudo haber sido el prototipado de la IA, después todo giró en torno a los modelos y modelos de razonamiento, y ahora estamos en la llegada de los agentes.
fullContext: Lenny asks how anyone can plan roadmaps when the AI landscape changes so rapidly with new model releases. Asha explains Microsoft's approach to strategic planning in the fast-moving AI space. Instead of traditional fixed timeframes, they think in "seasons" - periods defined by major technological or market shifts that can last anywhere from three months to a year.

vocabulary.definition: Prototyping is the process of creating an early model or sample of a product to test its functionality and design before full-scale production. It allows for iterative development and refinement based on user feedback.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, prototyping is crucial for startups to validate ideas, minimize risks, and ensure that the final product meets market needs. It often involves creating wireframes, mockups, or functional models.

insight.nuance: While 'prototyping' suggests a preliminary phase, it carries a connotation of innovation and experimentation, making it ideal for discussions about product development.

vocabulary.definition: Strategic planning is the process of defining an organization's direction and making decisions on allocating resources to pursue this strategy. It involves setting long-term goals and determining the actions needed to achieve them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, strategic planning is essential for aligning resources and efforts towards common objectives, often involving market analysis and competitive positioning.

insight.nuance: The term 'strategic planning' implies a comprehensive and forward-thinking approach, distinguishing it from more tactical or operational planning processes.

vocabulary.definition: In a business context, 'landscape' refers to the overall environment or market conditions in which a company operates, including competitors, trends, and regulatory factors. It encompasses both the internal and external factors that impact business strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the competitive landscape is vital for businesses to identify opportunities and threats, guiding strategic decisions and positioning.

insight.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of breadth and complexity, making it suitable for discussions about market dynamics and industry analysis.

vocabulary.definition: Advent refers to the arrival or beginning of an important event, innovation, or period, often signifying a transformative change. It is commonly used to denote the onset of new technologies or trends.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the advent of new technologies or methodologies can signify shifts in market dynamics, prompting companies to adapt their strategies to remain competitive.

insight.nuance: The word 'advent' carries a positive connotation, often associated with progress and opportunity, making it ideal for discussions about innovation.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: I've learned that optimism is a renewable resource.
keySentence: optimism is a renewable resource.
text_ko: 저는 낙관주의가 재생 가능한 자원이라는 걸 배웠어요. 이 회사는 지난 50년 동안 성공하지 못할 이유가 수도 없이 많았는데도, AI 시대(AI era)에 초기에 성공을 거두기도 했고 여러 도전과 또 다른 성과를 겪으면서 분야가 너무 빠르게 변하는 상황에서도, 그가 에너지를 만들어내고 자신의 낙관주의로 모두의 사명(mission)에 대한 헌신을 다시 불러일으키는 능력은 정말 놀라워요.
text_zh: 我发现乐观主义其实是可以不断更新的资源。这家公司50年来遇到过各种各样本来可能让它失败的理由，但它还是挺过来了。哪怕在AI时代早期取得成功，后来又遇到挑战，然后又有其他成功，整个行业发展得这么快，我觉得他那种能够激发团队活力，用自己的乐观精神重新点燃大家对使命投入的能力，真的是太厉害了。
text_es: He aprendido que el optimismo es un recurso renovable. Esta empresa durante 50 años ha tenido todas las razones del mundo para no triunfar y aun así lo ha logrado, incluso cuando tuvo éxito temprano en la era de la IA y desafíos y otros logros, y el sector está evolucionando tan rápido que creo que su capacidad para generar energía y usar su optimismo para renovar la dedicación de todos hacia la misión es increíble.
fullContext: Lenny asks what Asha has learned from working closely with Satya Nadella, Microsoft's CEO. Asha shares her key observation about his leadership style, particularly how he maintains and spreads optimism throughout the organization. She emphasizes how Satya uses optimism as a tool to continuously re-energize teams and maintain commitment to the company's mission, even during challenging periods.

vocabulary.definition: A mental attitude characterized by hope and confidence in positive outcomes or the belief that good things will happen.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, optimism can drive innovation and motivate teams, fostering a culture that embraces challenges and seeks growth opportunities.

insight.nuance: While optimism is generally positive, excessive optimism can lead to unrealistic expectations and poor decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to resources that are naturally replenished over time, such as solar or wind energy, and are sustainable for long-term use.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, particularly in tech and startups, renewable resources are increasingly prioritized for sustainable practices and corporate social responsibility initiatives.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation associated with sustainability, but it can also imply limitations in scalability or availability depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: A source of supply or support that can be drawn upon when needed, including materials, finances, human capital, or information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, effective resource management is crucial for maximizing productivity and ensuring the efficient allocation of assets to achieve strategic goals.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both tangible and intangible assets, and its use can vary based on context, such as human resources versus financial resources.

speaker: Asha Sharma
role: Chief Vice President of Product, Microsoft
text: I believe we will see just as much money spent on post-training as we will on pre-training and in the future, more on post-training.
keySentence: Post-training will see as much investment as pre-training, focusing on fine-tune and optimize.
text_ko: 저는 사전 학습(pre-training)만큼 사후 학습(post-training)에 돈이 들어갈 거라고 봐요. 앞으로는 오히려 사후 학습에 더 많이 투자할 것 같아요. 네이선 램버트(Nathan Lambert)의 연구를 잠깐 얘기했는데, 그 연구는 모델이 파라미터(parameters) 300억 개쯤 되면 파인튜닝(fine-tuning)과 최적화(optimize)가 더 합리적이라고 결론 내렸어요. 설문조사에 따르면 개발자의 약 50%가 지금 파인튜닝을 하고 있다고 하더라고요.
text_zh: 我觉得未来在后训练(post-training)上花的钱会跟预训练(pre-training)一样多，甚至后面可能后训练花得更多。我们之前聊过Nathan Lambert的那个研究，他的结论是模型一旦到了300亿参数，做微调(fine-tune)和优化就更划算了。调研显示现在有50%的开发者都在搞微调。
text_es: Creo que vamos a ver tanto dinero invertido en el post-entrenamiento como en el pre-entrenamiento, y en el futuro, incluso más en el post-entrenamiento. Hablamos un poco del estudio de Nathan Lambert donde concluyó que cuando un modelo llega a los 30 mil millones de parámetros, tiene más sentido hacer fine-tuning y optimizar. Y según las encuestas, el 50% de los desarrolladores ya están haciendo fine-tuning.
fullContext: Asha shares her prediction about a major shift in AI development investment priorities. Pre-training involves the initial creation of foundation models with massive compute requirements, while post-training involves customizing existing models through techniques like fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. She argues that economic and practical factors are driving companies to focus more resources on adapting existing powerful models rather than building new ones from scratch.

vocabulary.definition: Investment priorities refer to the specific areas or projects that an organization chooses to focus its financial resources on, based on strategic goals and potential returns. These priorities guide decision-making regarding where to allocate capital for maximum impact.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, investment priorities help determine which initiatives will receive funding, influencing growth strategies and operational effectiveness.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a strategic approach, suggesting that not all opportunities are equally valuable; it is important to communicate these priorities clearly to stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: Post-training refers to the period and activities that occur after an individual has completed a training program, often involving the application of learned skills and ongoing support. This phase is critical for reinforcing knowledge and ensuring effective implementation in the workplace.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate training and development, post-training initiatives such as follow-up sessions, assessments, and mentorship programs are essential for maximizing the return on investment in employee education.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a proactive approach to learning, emphasizing the importance of continuous improvement and support rather than viewing training as a one-time event.

vocabulary.definition: Pre-training refers to the phase before an individual undergoes a training program, which may include preparatory activities, assessments of existing skills, and setting learning objectives. This stage is crucial for tailoring the training experience to meet specific needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In organizational contexts, pre-training assessments help identify skill gaps and align training content with the strategic goals of the company, ensuring that resources are effectively utilized.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a foundational approach, suggesting that adequate preparation can significantly enhance the effectiveness of the subsequent training.

vocabulary.definition: Shift refers to a change or movement from one state, position, or condition to another, often indicating a significant transition in strategy, focus, or operations. In a business context, shifts can occur in market trends, consumer behavior, or organizational priorities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, a shift may signify a pivot in business strategy or a response to emerging market demands, necessitating adaptability and innovation.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a sense of urgency or necessity, often implying that the change is important for survival or growth, and is typically used in discussions about strategic planning.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: From 2010 to 2020, we had the golden years of deterministic matching where it was very easy to run an ad and understand with precision who installed the app.
keySentence: we had the golden years of deterministic matching where it was very easy to run an ad and understand with precision who installed the app.
text_ko: 2010년부터 2020년까지는 결정론적 매칭(deterministic matching)의 황금기였어요. 광고를 내면 누가 앱을 설치했는지 아주 정확히 파악하기가 쉬웠죠. 이름은 몰라도 그 사람의 광고 식별자(IDFA)를 알고, 그걸 개인 식별 정보(PII, personally identifiable information)와 연결할 수 있었어요. 이제는 그게 안 돼요. 그래서 광고 네트워크(ad networks)들이 더 복잡하고 정교해지면서 흥미로워지고 있는데, 마케터들이 실제로 돈을 어떻게 쓰는지 이해하기는 훨씬 더 어려워졌어요.
text_zh: 从2010年到2020年，那是确定性匹配(deterministic matching)的黄金时代，跑个广告就能很精准地知道是谁下载了你的应用。虽然你可能不知道用户的真实姓名，但你能拿到他们的IDFA，然后把这个跟个人身份信息(PII)关联起来。现在这套玩法行不通了。这就意味着，广告网络(ad networks)变得越来越复杂、越来越高端，与此同时，营销人员却更难搞清楚自己的钱到底花到哪儿去了。
text_es: Desde el 2010 hasta el 2020, tuvimos la época dorada del deterministic matching, donde era súper fácil lanzar un anuncio y entender con precisión exacta quién se descargó la app. Tal vez no sabías su nombre, pero sí sabías su IDFA y podías conectar eso con su información personal. Ya no se puede hacer eso. Entonces, lo que significa es que estas redes publicitarias se están volviendo más complejas, sofisticadas e interesantes, justo al mismo tiempo que se les hace más difícil a los marketers entender realmente en qué se están gastando el dinero.
fullContext: Austin is opening the podcast by explaining the dramatic shift in mobile app attribution that has fundamentally changed marketing technology. IDFA (Identifier for Advertisers) was Apple's unique identifier that allowed precise tracking of users from ads to app installs. PII stands for Personally Identifiable Information. Austin explains how the elimination of deterministic matching (precise, definitive tracking) has created a paradox where ad networks are becoming more sophisticated while marketers have less visibility into their spending effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a predictable outcome based on specific inputs or conditions, leaving no room for randomness or uncertainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, deterministic models are often used in data analytics and advertising to ensure that outcomes can be reliably forecasted based on known variables.

insight.nuance: While 'deterministic' implies certainty, it may not account for external factors that could influence outcomes, making it less applicable in highly variable environments.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being exact, accurate, and clearly defined, often measured in terms of consistency and reliability.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of advertising and data analysis, precision is crucial for targeting the right audience and measuring the effectiveness of campaigns.

insight.nuance: Precision implies a high degree of accuracy, but it may not always guarantee relevance or effectiveness in broader strategic contexts.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic or foundational manner; relating to the essential nature or underlying principles of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'fundamentally' is often used to emphasize core values, principles, or changes that affect the overall strategy or operations.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a deep-rooted significance, so it should be used when discussing core issues rather than superficial aspects.

vocabulary.definition: The process of identifying and assigning credit or responsibility for an outcome or result to a specific cause or source.
vocabulary.businessContext: Attribution is vital in marketing to determine which channels or strategies are most effective in driving customer actions, such as purchases or app installations.

insight.nuance: Attribution can be complex, as it often involves analyzing multiple factors, and should be used carefully to avoid oversimplifying the impact of various influences.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: Marketing technology is like this very amorphous, cross-functional discipline that lives at the crossroads of product and growth and engineering and marketing. It brings together processes and systems from a wide range of disciplines.
keySentence: Marketing technology exists at the crossroads of product, growth, engineering, and marketing.
text_ko: 마케팅 테크(marketing technology)는 굉장히 모호하고 크로스펑셔널(cross-functional)한 분야로, 제품(product)과 그로스(growth), 엔지니어링, 마케팅이 만나는 교차점에 있어요. 다양한 영역의 프로세스와 시스템을 한데 모으는 역할을 하고요. 제 생각엔 마케팅 테크를 이해하는 가장 좋은 방식은, 그 역할과 초점이 시스템이나 서드파티(third-party) 혹은 퍼스트파티(first-party) 플랫폼에 있는 제품 매니저(product manager)라고 보는 거예요.
text_zh: 营销技术(marketing technology)这个东西其实挺模糊的，它是个跨部门的领域，处在产品、增长、工程和营销的交叉点上。它把各个不同领域的流程和系统都整合在一起。我觉得理解营销技术最好的方式就是，把它想象成一个产品经理，只不过这个产品经理专门负责系统平台，不管是第三方的还是自家的平台。
text_es: La tecnología de marketing es como una disciplina muy fluida y transversal que está justo en el cruce entre producto, crecimiento, ingeniería y marketing. Junta procesos y sistemas de un montón de áreas diferentes. Y yo creo que realmente la forma de pensar en la tecnología de marketing es como un product manager cuyo rol específico y enfoque es el sistema o la plataforma, ya sea de terceros o propia.
fullContext: Lenny asks Austin to define what MarTech (Marketing Technology) is and what someone in MarTech does. Austin is explaining that MarTech is an interdisciplinary field that sits between multiple departments - product, growth, engineering, and marketing. He describes it as managing both third-party tools (external platforms like analytics or email tools) and first-party solutions (custom-built internal systems), similar to how a product manager approaches their role.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a team or process that involves members from multiple functional areas or departments within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, cross-functional teams are often formed to leverage diverse expertise and perspectives to solve complex problems or drive projects that require collaboration across various departments.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes collaboration and integration, and is often used in contexts where silos between departments are being broken down.

vocabulary.definition: Involving two or more academic, professional, or technical disciplines in a collaborative manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup environment, interdisciplinary approaches are essential for innovation, as they combine knowledge and methods from various fields to create comprehensive solutions.

insight.nuance: This term often suggests a deeper integration of knowledge and methodologies than simply cross-functional, and is typically used in academic or research contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, processes are critical for ensuring efficiency, consistency, and quality in operations, often documented and optimized for better performance.

insight.nuance: While 'processes' can refer to any sequence of actions, in a business context it often implies a formalized and repeatable method.

vocabulary.definition: A set of interconnected components or elements that work together to achieve a common goal or function.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, systems are used to integrate various processes and technologies, facilitating communication and data flow across an organization.

insight.nuance: The term 'systems' often implies a level of complexity and interdependence, and is typically used when discussing structured frameworks or models.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: And everybody thinks that marketing technology is just the third party tools, but actually it's designing, architecting and building that stuff on top of your third party tools. That's how you actually have a lot of velocity is thinking about not just build versus buy.
keySentence: Velocity comes from building on top of third party tools, not just buying them.
text_ko: 사람들은 마케팅 기술(marketing technology)이 그냥 서드파티 툴(third-party tools)이라고만 생각하지만, 사실은 그 위에 무엇을 설계(designing)하고, 아키텍처(architecting)를 잡아서 실제로 구현(building)하는 일이에요. 속도(velocity)를 내려면 단순히 '구축 대 구매(build vs buy)'만 고민할 게 아니라, 지금은 '구축도 하고 구매도 하는(build and buy)' 접근이 필요해요. 툴을 사서 90%는 해결하고, 나머지 10%를 직접 만들어서 멋진 기능을 얹는 식이에요.
text_zh: 大家都觉得营销技术(marketing technology)就是那些第三方工具，但其实真正的核心是在这些第三方工具基础上去设计、架构和开发东西。要想真正提高效率，不能只想着是自己开发还是直接买，现在得两手抓——既要买也要开发。你买个工具能解决90%的问题，然后在上面开发点酷炫的功能把剩下10%搞定。
text_es: Y todo el mundo piensa que la tecnología de marketing son solo las herramientas de terceros, pero en realidad se trata de diseñar, estructurar y construir cosas encima de esas herramientas que ya tienes. Así es como realmente logras mucha velocidad (velocity): no se trata solo de pensar en construir versus comprar. Ahora es construir y comprar a la vez. O sea, compras la herramienta para llegar al 90% del camino y luego construyes la parte genial encima con ese otro 10%.
fullContext: Austin is explaining the slice of work that a MarTech person would take from a growth team when companies reach the point of needing dedicated MarTech support. He's describing how MarTech involves both purchasing third-party tools and building custom solutions on top of them. The "build versus buy" decision framework traditionally meant choosing one or the other, but Austin advocates for "build and buy" - purchasing tools for the foundation and building custom features on top.

vocabulary.definition: The process of designing and planning the structure and components of a system or project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, architecting involves creating a blueprint for software, systems, or infrastructure that aligns with organizational goals and user needs.

insight.nuance: While often used in technical contexts, architecting can also imply a strategic approach to problem-solving and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: The speed at which a project or process is completed, often measured in terms of output over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, velocity refers to the rapid development and deployment of products or features, which is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: Velocity can carry a positive connotation of efficiency and agility, but excessive focus on speed may compromise quality.

vocabulary.definition: A strategic decision-making process that evaluates whether to create a solution in-house (build) or purchase an existing solution from an external provider (buy).
vocabulary.businessContext: This concept is critical in technology and business strategy, as it influences resource allocation, cost management, and time to market.

insight.nuance: The choice between build versus buy often reflects a company's capabilities, priorities, and long-term vision, with each option carrying its own risks and benefits.

vocabulary.definition: Devoted to a particular task, purpose, or service, often implying a strong commitment and focus.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, dedicated teams or resources are often assigned to specific projects or functions to ensure optimal performance and accountability.

insight.nuance: While 'dedicated' conveys a sense of commitment, it may also imply exclusivity, which can be viewed positively or negatively depending on the context.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: I think all marketing technologists at some level are ICs. I think it's a great job personally, because I get to be an IC and a manager.
keySentence: I think it's a great job personally, because I get to be an IC and a manager.
text_ko: 저는 모든 마케팅 테크놀로지스트(marketing technologists)가 어느 정도는 다들 IC(Individual Contributor)라고 생각해요. 개인적으로 이 일은 정말 좋은 직무예요 — IC이면서 매니저를 겸할 수 있어서요. 그 역할에서는 IC로서 직접 기여해야 해요. 퍼스트파티(first-party)와 서드파티(third-party) 시스템 전반에 대해 가장 선임된 기술 전문가거든요. 그래서 서드파티 도구(third-party tools)가 어떻게 작동하는지 정말 잘 알아야 하고, 직접 해보지 않으면 그걸 알 수 없어요.
text_zh: 我觉得所有的营销技术专家(marketing technologist)某种程度上都是个人贡献者(IC)。我个人认为这是个很棒的工作，因为我既能做IC又能做管理。你必须得是个IC，因为你要成为所有第一方和第三方系统最资深的技术专家。所以你得真正了解第三方工具是怎么运作的，不亲自动手你是搞不明白的。
text_es: Creo que todos los tecnólogos de marketing a cierto nivel son contribuidores individuales (ICs). Personalmente pienso que es un trabajo genial, porque puedo ser IC y gerente a la vez. Tienes que ser IC en el sentido de que eres el experto técnico más senior en todos los sistemas propios y de terceros. Entonces, tienes que saber muy bien cómo funcionan las herramientas de terceros y eso no lo aprendes sin meter las manos en la masa tú mismo.
fullContext: Lenny asks whether MarTech people do the work themselves or build teams with engineers. Austin explains that MarTech professionals are Individual Contributors (ICs) who must maintain hands-on technical expertise. Unlike traditional management roles where you might delegate technical work, MarTech requires you to be the senior technical expert on both internal systems (first party) and external tools (third party), which means staying involved in the actual implementation work.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who contribute to a project or organization through their specialized skills and expertise, rather than through managerial roles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, individual contributors are often responsible for executing specific tasks, such as coding, design, or analysis, without direct oversight of others.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the value of specialized skills and can imply a level of autonomy and responsibility in one's work.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals who specialize in the application of technology to solve problems or create products, often possessing a deep understanding of technical systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and product development, technologists play a crucial role in integrating technology with business strategies to enhance efficiency and innovation.

insight.nuance: The term often connotes a blend of technical expertise and practical application, distinguishing these professionals from purely theoretical scientists.

vocabulary.definition: To keep something in a specified state or condition through regular upkeep and management.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, maintaining systems, processes, or relationships is essential for ensuring operational efficiency and long-term success.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a proactive approach to preservation, rather than merely preventing decline or failure.

vocabulary.definition: An individual responsible for overseeing and coordinating the work of others, ensuring that organizational goals are met efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate settings, managers play a critical role in guiding teams, allocating resources, and making strategic decisions to drive performance.

insight.nuance: The term can suggest a level of authority and responsibility, but may also imply a need for interpersonal skills and adaptability in leadership styles.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: I almost view them like a true quarterback every [inaudible] says people are quarterbacks. But really marketing technology because it lives between so many departments, it plays that role of having to call plays and pull on different departments.
keySentence: Marketing technology calls plays and pulls on different departments like a quarterback.
text_ko: 저는 사실 그걸 진짜 쿼터백(quarterback)처럼 보는 편이에요. 사람들이 다들 쿼터백이라고 말하긴 하는데, 마케팅 테크놀로지(marketing technology)는 여러 부서 사이에 걸쳐 있어서 전술을 지시하고 다양한 부서를 끌어모아 조율하는 역할을 해요.
text_zh: 我觉得他们就像真正的四分卫(quarterback)一样，虽然每个人都说自己是四分卫。但营销技术因为要跟这么多部门打交道，确实起到了那种统筹协调的作用，需要制定策略，还要调动各个部门的资源。
text_es: Yo casi los veo como un verdadero mariscal de campo (quarterback), porque todo el mundo dice que la gente son mariscales de campo. Pero realmente la tecnología de marketing, como está entre tantos departamentos, juega ese papel de tener que dirigir las jugadas y coordinar con diferentes áreas.
fullContext: Austin continues explaining the cross-functional nature of MarTech roles. He's describing how MarTech professionals need to coordinate across multiple departments - they might need to work with the head of revenue operations to change something in Salesforce, talk to the VP of product for platform changes, or rely on the data team for resources. The quarterback analogy emphasizes how they orchestrate plays across different functional areas rather than having direct authority over team members.

vocabulary.definition: Involving multiple departments or areas of expertise within an organization to achieve a common goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, cross-functional teams are often formed to leverage diverse skills and perspectives, enhancing collaboration and innovation across different functions.

insight.nuance: This term implies a collaborative approach that breaks down silos, but it may also suggest complexity in communication and decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: To organize and harmonize activities or efforts among different parties to ensure effective collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, coordinating tasks among teams or departments is crucial for project management and achieving strategic objectives.

insight.nuance: While it suggests a level of organization, it can also imply the need for negotiation and compromise among various stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: Distinct divisions within an organization, each responsible for specific functions or areas of expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: Departments such as marketing, finance, and human resources play critical roles in the overall operation and strategy of a business.

insight.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of specialization, but it can also highlight potential barriers to communication and collaboration between units.

vocabulary.definition: The function or position that an individual or entity occupies within a specific context or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, clearly defined roles help delineate responsibilities and expectations, facilitating effective teamwork and accountability.

insight.nuance: While it denotes a specific function, 'role' can also imply a degree of flexibility, as individuals may take on multiple roles depending on the situation.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: I tend to take a little bit of a different approach than most, which is like I think you should always be thinking about the future.
keySentence: I think you should always be thinking about the future.
text_ko: 저는 보통 사람들과 조금 다르게 접근해요. 항상 미래를 생각해야 한다고 보는 편인데, 그렇다고 해서 미래에 지나치게 치우친 설계 선택으로 제품-시장 적합도(product-market fit)를 놓치거나 잘못된 제품 결정을 내려도 된다는 건 아니에요. 다만 도구를 고르고 도입해서 구현할 때는 '아무것도 안 바꾸면 1년 뒤에 어떻게 될까?'를 항상 염두에 둬야 해요.
text_zh: 我的做法跟大多数人不太一样，我觉得应该时刻想着未来。当然这不是说你要过度迎合未来，搞得连产品市场契合度(product market fit)都找不到，或者做出一堆糟糕的产品决策。但是当你在搭建工具、选择工具、落地实施的时候，你得想想，如果我一年内什么都不改，会发生什么？
text_es: Mi enfoque suele ser un poco diferente al de la mayoría. Yo creo que siempre hay que estar pensando en el futuro. Eso no significa que tengas que tomar decisiones de diseño que se enfoquen tanto en el futuro que termines perdiendo el product market fit o tomando malas decisiones de producto. Pero cuando configuras herramientas, las eliges y las implementas, tienes que preguntarte: ¿qué va a pasar dentro de un año si no cambio nada?
fullContext: Austin is explaining his philosophy for how growth managers should think about MarTech decisions beyond just immediate needs. He's addressing the balance between short-term execution and long-term planning. "Over index towards the future" means focusing too heavily on future needs at the expense of current priorities like achieving product-market fit. Austin advocates for making tool decisions that consider future scalability without sacrificing present objectives.

vocabulary.definition: A method or way of doing something, particularly in problem-solving or decision-making contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an approach can refer to a strategic methodology employed to achieve objectives or tackle challenges, such as a customer-centric approach or a data-driven approach.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a personal or unique perspective, suggesting that different individuals or organizations may have varied methods for addressing similar issues.

vocabulary.definition: The act of carrying out or putting into effect a plan, order, or course of action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, execution refers to the implementation of strategies and plans, where effective execution is crucial for achieving desired outcomes and objectives.

insight.nuance: The term often emphasizes the importance of precision and efficiency, indicating that successful execution can differentiate between a good plan and a successful outcome.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a time frame that extends far into the future, typically involving strategies or plans that require sustained effort and investment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, long-term strategies are essential for sustainable growth and involve considerations such as market trends, customer loyalty, and resource allocation over extended periods.

insight.nuance: The term often connotes a commitment to enduring goals rather than short-term gains, highlighting the importance of foresight in planning.

vocabulary.definition: Occurring or done at once; instant or urgent in nature, often requiring prompt attention or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, immediate actions may be necessary in crisis management or when responding to urgent market changes, highlighting the need for quick decision-making.

insight.nuance: While the term suggests urgency, it can also imply a lack of depth in planning, as immediate actions may not always consider long-term consequences.

speaker: Austin Hay
text: I think the most superhuman user acquisition people out there are engineers and they don't need a marketing technologist because they set up the tool themself. They know how the paid campaign runs and they just do it all.
keySentence: Superhuman user acquisition people are engineers who set up tools themselves.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 가장 대단한 사용자 확보(user acquisition) 담당자들은 엔지니어들이에요. 마케팅 테크놀로지스트(marketing technologist)가 따로 필요 없어요 — 도구를 스스로 세팅해 버리니까요. 유료 캠페인(paid campaign)이 어떻게 돌아가는지 알고, 그냥 전부 다 해버려요. 보통 이런 사람들은 작은 스타트업에서 만나는데, 공동창업자(co-founder)가 엔지니어에게 “페이스북 광고(Facebook ads) 어떻게 되는지 알아봐”라고 그냥 시키는 그런 곳이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得最牛的用户获取(user acquisition)高手其实都是工程师，他们根本不需要什么营销技术专家，因为工具都是自己搭建的。付费推广(paid campaign)怎么跑他们门儿清，什么都能自己搞定。你通常能在小创业公司见到这种大神，就是联合创始人跟工程师说一句："嘿，你去研究研究Facebook广告怎么玩。"
text_es: Creo que la gente más extraordinaria en adquisición de usuarios son los ingenieros, y no necesitan un tecnólogo de marketing porque ellos mismos configuran las herramientas. Saben cómo funcionan las campañas pagadas y simplemente lo hacen todo. Y normalmente encuentras a estos genios en startups pequeñas donde el cofundador le dice al ingeniero: "Oye, averigua cómo funcionan los anuncios de Facebook."
fullContext: Lenny asks about the relationship between MarTech people and paid growth specialists. Austin explains that the most effective user acquisition professionals are those with engineering backgrounds who can handle both the technical setup and campaign management themselves. However, he notes this is rare and typically occurs at small startups where engineers are forced to learn marketing out of necessity when founders tell them to "figure out" advertising platforms.

vocabulary.definition: User acquisition refers to the process of gaining new users or customers for a product or service, often through various marketing strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, user acquisition is critical for growth, as it directly impacts a company's customer base and revenue potential.

insight.nuance: While user acquisition focuses on attracting new users, it is important to balance this with user retention strategies to ensure long-term success.

vocabulary.definition: A marketing technologist is a professional who combines marketing expertise with technical skills to implement and optimize marketing technologies and strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, marketing technologists play a crucial role in leveraging data and tools to enhance marketing effectiveness and drive user engagement.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a blend of creativity and analytical skills, making it distinct from traditional marketing roles that may not require technical proficiency.

vocabulary.definition: A paid campaign is a marketing strategy that involves paying for advertisements to promote a product or service across various platforms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, paid campaigns are commonly used to quickly reach target audiences, generate leads, and drive conversions, often complementing organic marketing efforts.

insight.nuance: Paid campaigns can vary in scale and duration, and their effectiveness often depends on careful targeting and budget management.

vocabulary.definition: Effective refers to the ability to produce a desired or intended result, particularly in achieving specific goals or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, effective strategies and practices are essential for maximizing productivity, profitability, and overall success.

insight.nuance: While something may be effective, it is important to consider efficiency as well, which relates to how resources are utilized in achieving those results.

speaker: Ayo Omojola
text: My perspective is that, and I think this is a, people don't like this kind of answer. But the thing Cash App did right was like 10 things, not one.
keySentence: the thing Cash App did right was like 10 things, not one.
text_ko: 제 관점엔, 사람들이 이런 답을 별로 좋아하진 않아요. 그런데 Cash App이 잘한 건 한 가지가 아니라 열 가지쯤 됐어요. 인재 밀도(talent density)가 압도적이었고, 집중력도 대단했고, 사기 방지(fraud)에 매우 강했고, Brian·Dustin·Jesse·Dangi가 조직을 짜는 방식과 잭(Jack)의 지원 덕분에 스퀘어(Square)의 다른 부분과는 사실상 완전히 분리돼 있었어요. 영웅 고객(hero customer)이 소비자였기 때문에, 실제로 모든 트레이드오프(trade-offs)에서 항상 소비자의 필요를 최우선으로 뒀어요.
text_zh: 我的看法是，虽然可能大家不太爱听这种答案，但Cash App之所以成功，不是因为一个因素，而是有十来个方面都做得特别到位。比如说人才密度(talent density)极高，专注度超强，风控做得特别厉害，还有Brian、Dustin、Jesse、Dangi他们几个人在Jack的支持下，把这块业务和Square其他部分完全隔离开来运营。最关键的是，他们把消费者当作核心用户，不是商家，所以基本上所有的决策权衡都是消费者需求优先。
text_es: Mi punto de vista es que, y creo que esto es algo que a la gente no le gusta escuchar como respuesta. Pero lo que Cash App hizo bien no fue una sola cosa, sino como 10 cosas. Fueron como 10 cosas que realmente estaban a nivel de excelencia, como una densidad de talento impresionante, un enfoque increíble, muy sólidos en temas de fraude, mucho de la forma en que Brian, y Dustin, y Jesse, y Dangi trataron de organizar todo... Ya sabes, con el apoyo de Jack, estaba realmente aislado del resto de Square, el cliente héroe era el consumidor, no los comerciantes, entonces literalmente en el 100% de las decisiones las necesidades del consumidor iban primero.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ayo what Cash App did most right to launch successfully in the consumer space and scale to 50+ million monthly actives. Ayo explains that people often want to identify one key factor for success, but Cash App's achievement came from excelling at multiple dimensions simultaneously. He emphasizes that they maintained insane talent density, laser focus, fraud expertise, and most importantly, they were completely firewalled from Square's merchant business so consumer needs always came first in every trade-off decision.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of considering something; a point of view.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, perspective is crucial for understanding different viewpoints and making informed decisions, especially in team settings or strategy development.

insight.nuance: While 'perspective' can imply a subjective viewpoint, it is often valued in collaborative environments for fostering diverse ideas.

vocabulary.definition: To initiate or introduce a new product, service, or project into the market.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, launching a product involves strategic planning, marketing, and execution to ensure successful entry into the competitive landscape.

insight.nuance: The term 'launch' often conveys a sense of excitement and anticipation, making it suitable for marketing contexts, but should be used with caution to avoid overpromising.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that achieves a desired outcome or goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term is frequently used to measure the effectiveness of strategies, projects, or initiatives against predefined objectives.

insight.nuance: While 'successfully' indicates a positive result, it is important to specify the criteria for success to avoid ambiguity.

vocabulary.definition: To increase or expand in size, capacity, or scope, particularly in a business context.
vocabulary.businessContext: Scaling is a critical concept in startups, referring to the ability to grow operations and revenue without a corresponding increase in costs, often achieved through technology or efficient processes.

insight.nuance: The term 'scale' carries a positive connotation of growth and potential, but it should be used carefully to ensure that it reflects sustainable practices rather than mere expansion.

speaker: Ayo Omojola
text: Being different is not enough, because it's very easy to build a thing that's different from what exists today, because you just have to look at what exists today and build something else.
keySentence: Being different is not enough, because it's very easy to build a thing that's different from what exists today.
text_ko: 다르다고 되는 건 아니에요. 오늘 있는 것들과 그냥 다르게 만드는 건 너무 쉬워서, 지금 있는 걸 보고 ‘그거랑은 다른 걸 만들자’ 하면 되니까요. 더 나은 것도 충분하지 않아요. ‘이걸 더 좋게 만들어서 그냥 더 비싸게 팔면 되지’라고 말하는 건 역시 쉬운 일이니까요. 중요한 건 지금 있는 것들보다 나은데, 그 ‘나음’이 최종 사용자(end user)에게 실제로 의미가 있어야 한다는 거예요. 우리에게 오랫동안 기준이 됐던 건, 누군가가 “왜 Venmo에 베팅하냐?”고 물으면 제가 “지금 당장 내가 쓸 수 있는 1달러를 나한테 보내봐”라고 했을 때, 그걸 보낼 수 있는 앱이 딱 하나뿐이었어요.
text_zh: 光是不一样还不够，因为做个跟现在市面上不同的东西太容易了，你只要看看现在有什么，然后做点别的就行了。光是更好也不够，因为谁都可以说"嘿，我要把这个做得更好，然后多收你点钱"。关键是要比现有的产品好，而且这个"好"得对终端用户有意义。对我们来说，很长时间里，当有人问"你们为什么看好Venmo？"我就会说，"你试试给我转一块钱，让我现在就能用"，当时只有一个app能做到这点。
text_es: Ser diferente no es suficiente, porque es súper fácil crear algo que sea diferente a lo que ya existe - nada más tienes que ver qué hay ahora y hacer otra cosa. Ser mejor tampoco basta, porque también es fácil decir "Oye, voy a mejorar esto y te voy a cobrar más por ello." Tiene que ser mejor que lo que existe hoy, pero de una manera que realmente le importe al usuario final. Para nosotros, por mucho tiempo, cuando alguien nos decía "¿Por qué están apostando por Venmo?", yo les contestaba "A ver, mándame un dólar que pueda usar ahorita mismo" - y solo había una app con la que lo podías hacer.
fullContext: Ayo is explaining Cash App's differentiation strategy and what made it successful against competitors like Venmo. He's describing how the team focused on being both different AND better in ways that truly mattered to users. Cash App's key differentiator was instant money transfer - when you received money, you could use it immediately rather than waiting for processing. This gave them a clear, demonstrable advantage that users could experience firsthand when comparing apps.

vocabulary.definition: The process of distinguishing a product or offering from others to make it more attractive to a specific target market.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, differentiation is crucial for creating a unique value proposition that sets a company apart from its competitors, particularly in crowded markets.

insight.nuance: While differentiation often implies uniqueness, it should also convey added value to the customer; merely being different without clear benefits may not be effective.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, often involving the allocation of resources and setting of priorities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, strategy refers to the comprehensive plan that guides an organization in achieving its goals, including market positioning, competitive advantage, and resource management.

insight.nuance: The term 'strategy' implies a thoughtful, deliberate approach rather than a reactive or ad-hoc method; it is often associated with long-term vision and planning.

vocabulary.definition: Other businesses or entities that offer similar products or services and vie for the same market share or customer base.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding competitors is essential for businesses to identify market trends, assess their own positioning, and develop strategies to gain a competitive edge.

insight.nuance: The term 'competitors' can carry a connotation of rivalry, but it can also imply opportunities for collaboration or learning from others in the industry.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity, often measured by specific outcomes such as profit, market share, or customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, success is typically evaluated through performance metrics, including financial results, growth rates, and brand recognition, reflecting the effectiveness of strategies and operations.

insight.nuance: While 'successful' generally implies positive outcomes, it can also suggest a relative measure, as what is considered successful can vary greatly between industries and individual goals.

speaker: Ayo Omojola
text: I think when you are in a large organization, trying to do a actually new thing, I think small teams are better than big ones, period.
keySentence: Small teams are better than big ones in a startup within a startup.
text_ko: 제가 보기엔 큰 조직 안에서 진짜 새로운 걸 하려면 소규모 팀이 대규모 팀보다 무조건 더 좋아요. 그리고 팀들이 마일스톤(milestones)을 지키고 실제로 가치(value)를 만들어내는 것에 대해 철저히, 진지하게 고민하게끔 해야 해요. 사람들이 '스타트업 안의 스타트업(startup within a startup)은 다 가짜다'고 하는데, 제가 그걸 가짜라고 보는 이유는 진짜 스타트업은 같이 일하는 사람들의 급여를 실제로 걱정하게 되지만 회사 안에 있으면 그런 걱정을 안 하게 되거든요.
text_zh: 我觉得在大公司里想搞点真正创新的东西，小团队绝对比大团队好使，这没什么好争的。而且得逼着这些团队特别用心地去达成里程碑，真正创造价值，因为经常有人说什么"公司内部的创业团队啊，都是假的"。我觉得之所以假，是因为真正的创业公司你得操心给员工发工资的事儿，但在大公司内部你根本不用担心这个。
text_es: Creo que cuando estás en una organización grande, tratando de hacer algo realmente nuevo, los equipos pequeños funcionan mejor que los grandes, punto. Y hay que obligar a los equipos a ser súper conscientes de cumplir objetivos y realmente agregar valor, porque existe esa cosa que dice la gente de "oye, la startup dentro de la startup, todo es falso." Y creo que es falso porque cuando eres una startup de verdad te preocupas por pagarle a la gente que trabaja contigo, y cuando estás dentro de una empresa grande simplemente no te preocupas por eso.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ayo what Square/Block did right as a product company that he brings to his current role. Ayo explains his philosophy about building new products within large organizations. He argues that small teams are more effective because they maintain the existential pressure that real startups face. In true startups, founders worry about meeting payroll, but internal teams don't have that same urgency, which can lead to resource bloat without corresponding results.

vocabulary.definition: A large organization refers to a business or entity that employs a significant number of people and typically operates on a national or global scale.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, large organizations often have complex structures, extensive resources, and established processes, which can impact their ability to innovate quickly.

insight.nuance: While large organizations may have more resources, they can also face bureaucratic challenges that hinder agility and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Small teams are groups of individuals, typically consisting of fewer than ten members, who collaborate closely to achieve specific goals or projects.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, small teams are often favored for their ability to communicate effectively, adapt quickly, and foster innovation.

insight.nuance: The term 'small teams' conveys a sense of agility and intimacy, suggesting that collaboration is more effective in smaller groups.

vocabulary.definition: Building new products refers to the process of designing, developing, and launching innovative goods or services that meet market needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech companies, building new products is crucial for staying competitive and addressing evolving customer demands.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies a proactive approach to innovation, often associated with risk-taking and creativity in business.

vocabulary.definition: A product company is a business that primarily focuses on creating and selling tangible goods or software solutions, as opposed to providing services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, product companies are often characterized by their emphasis on user experience and continuous improvement of their offerings.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a focus on the lifecycle of a product, from conception to market delivery, highlighting the importance of innovation and customer feedback.

speaker: Ayo Omojola
text: When you're hiring you pick the people, but they pick when. So you're actually like, there's these people...
keySentence: you pick the people, but they pick when.
text_ko: 채용할 때는 우리가 사람을 고르지만, 그들이 언제 올지는 결국 그들이 정해요. 사실 팀에 합류하기까지 처음 만난 순간부터 실제로 합류할 때까지 몇 달이 걸리는 사람이 정말 많아요. 어떤 사람은 거의 1년 반이나 걸렸어요. 그래서 저는 그걸 이렇게 실무적으로 풀어요. 계속 사람들을 만나고, 같이 일하고 싶은 사람을 만나면 '안녕하세요' 하고 다가가서 '제가 어떻게 하면 당신 삶에 가치를 더해서 언젠가 함께 일할 사람으로 저를 생각해주실 수 있을까요? 그러면 기회가 왔을 때 진짜 열려 계시지, 줌(Zoom)에서 한 번 만난 사람으로만 남지 않잖아요'라고 말해요.
text_zh: 招人的时候是这样的，你可以挑人，但什么时候加入是他们说了算。所以实际上就是，有很多团队成员，从我第一次见到他们，到他们真正加入团队，中间隔了好几个月。有一个人差不多等了一年半才来。所以我的做法就是，我会一直去认识各种人，然后就想着，如果遇到想合作的人，我就会想"我怎么能给你的生活带来价值，让你觉得我是个值得合作的人，这样以后有机会一起工作的时候，你会愿意考虑，而不是把我当成只是在Zoom上见过一面的路人甲。"
text_es: Cuando contratas, tú eliges a las personas, pero ellas eligen cuándo. O sea, realmente es como... hay muchísima gente en el equipo donde el tiempo entre que los conocí por primera vez y cuando se unieron al equipo fue de meses. Hubo una persona que tardó como año y medio, casi. Entonces la forma en que yo operacionalizo eso es que estoy conociendo gente todo el tiempo, y simplemente es como, "Oye," o sea, si conozco a alguien con quien quiero trabajar, le digo, "Oye, ¿cómo puedo aportarte valor a tu vida para que me consideres alguien con quien te gustaría trabajar algún día? Para que cuando llegue el momento y haya una oportunidad de trabajar juntos, realmente estés abierto a ello, en lugar de ser simplemente un tipo que conociste una vez por Zoom."
fullContext: Lenny asks Ayo about his hiring and team-building philosophies beyond his preference for hiring founders. Ayo explains his long-term approach to talent acquisition - recognizing that while he can choose who to pursue, candidates control the timing of when they're ready to join. He invests in relationships by actively helping people achieve their current goals, positioning himself as someone they'd want to work with when the right opportunity arises, rather than just another recruiter who reached out once.

vocabulary.definition: The process of identifying, attracting, and hiring skilled individuals to meet organizational needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, talent acquisition is a strategic function that focuses on building a strong workforce to drive company growth and innovation.

insight.nuance: While often used interchangeably with recruitment, talent acquisition implies a more proactive and long-term strategy for workforce planning.

vocabulary.definition: A strategy that emphasizes sustained growth and development over an extended period rather than focusing on immediate results.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, a long-term approach is crucial for strategic planning, investment decisions, and building lasting relationships with clients and employees.

insight.nuance: This term often connotes patience and foresight, contrasting with short-term tactics that prioritize quick wins.

vocabulary.definition: Activities and exercises designed to enhance social relations and define roles within teams to improve collaboration and performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, team-building is essential for fostering a cohesive work culture and enhancing productivity among team members.

insight.nuance: While team-building can be seen as a fun or informal activity, it is fundamentally about improving team dynamics and effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: To employ someone for a job or position within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, hiring is a critical process that involves selecting candidates who align with the company's goals and culture.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a formal process but may also be used informally in discussions about staffing needs.

speaker: Ayo Omojola
text: My biggest thing, and I say this all the time, is that everybody wants something. And most of the time it's not something you have to give, or you can connect them to.
keySentence: everybody wants something.
text_ko: 내가 항상 말하는 가장 중요한 점은, 모든 사람이 뭔가를 원한다는 거예요. 그리고 대부분의 경우 그게 당신이 줄 수 있는 것이거나 연결해줄 수 있는 것이 아닐 때가 많아요. 하지만 만약 당신이 줄 수 있는 것이거나 연결해줄 수 있는 것이라면, 그걸 안 해주는 건 정말 잘못된 거예요. 상상해보세요, 누군가와 대화하고 있는데 그 사람이 당신이 원하는 걸 알고 있고, 그걸 줄 비용이 전혀 없는데도 그냥 안 해주는 거예요. 그게 얼마나 미친 짓인가요?
text_zh: 我最常说的一个观点就是，每个人都有需求对吧。大部分时候呢，可能不是你能提供的，或者你也帮不上忙。但是，如果真的是你能给的，或者你能牵个线搭个桥的，那不帮忙就真的说不过去了。你想想啊，就好比你跟别人聊天，对方明明知道你想要什么，他也有这个资源，给你也不费什么事儿，结果他就是不给你。这不是挺奇葩的吗？
text_es: Mi punto principal, y lo digo siempre, es que todo el mundo quiere algo. Y la mayoría de las veces no es algo que tú tengas para ofrecer, o que puedas conectarlos con alguien que lo tenga. Pero, si resulta que sí es algo que tú puedes dar, o puedes conectarlos, es una locura no hacerlo, en serio. Es como, imagínate que estás hablando con alguien, y esa persona, sabiendo que tú quieres algo, lo tiene, no le cuesta nada dártelo, y simplemente no lo hace. ¿Qué tan absurdo es eso?
fullContext: Ayo continues explaining his networking and relationship-building philosophy. He describes his core belief that everyone wants something, and when you can help provide what someone needs at little cost to yourself, it's morally wrong not to help them. He uses this principle to build long-term professional relationships by actively connecting people to opportunities, introductions, or resources they need, which eventually comes back to benefit him through stronger networks and goodwill.

vocabulary.definition: To join or link together; to establish a relationship or communication between entities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'connect' often refers to establishing relationships with clients, partners, or networks that can facilitate collaboration and opportunities.

insight.nuance: While 'connect' can imply a simple link, in a business context it often carries the connotation of building meaningful and strategic relationships.

vocabulary.definition: The act of interacting with others to exchange information and develop professional or social contacts.
vocabulary.businessContext: Networking is a crucial activity in business for creating opportunities, sharing knowledge, and building relationships that can lead to partnerships or job opportunities.

insight.nuance: Networking can sometimes have a transactional connotation, implying that relationships are built primarily for mutual benefit rather than genuine connection.

vocabulary.definition: The process of establishing and nurturing connections with individuals or organizations over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, relationship-building is essential for fostering trust and loyalty among clients, partners, and employees, which can lead to long-term success.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of ongoing interaction and investment in relationships, rather than a one-time engagement.

vocabulary.definition: To supply or make available something that is needed or desired.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'provide' often refers to delivering products, services, or information to customers or stakeholders to meet their needs.

insight.nuance: The term 'provide' suggests a proactive role in fulfilling needs, and it is often used in contexts where reliability and support are emphasized.

speaker: Ayo Omojola
text: It's not that you have to do everything yourself, it's that the person who you trust in the execution role, they have to become the expert. They have to be like, they can't stop until they hit the end. And, I don't know.
keySentence: The execution role must be in command of all the details and can't stop until they hit the end.
text_ko: 제가 다 직접 해야 하는 건 아니에요. 중요한 건 실행 담당자(execution role)를 믿는다면 그 사람이 전문가가 돼야 한다는 거예요. 그 사람은 끝을 볼 때까지 멈출 수 없어야 해요. 음… 야심 있는 사람들이 큰 목표에 도전하는 곳에서는 실행을 맡은 사람이 모든 디테일을 완전히 파악하고 있지 못하면 엄청난 가치가 사라져요. 그래서 현실은, 야심찬 일을 하려면 사람들과 함께 일해야 하고 저 혼자 다 할 수는 없다는 거예요. 진짜 교훈은 '내가 다 해야 한다'가 아니라 '누군가는 해야 한다'는 거예요.
text_zh: 不是说你得什么事儿都自己干，而是你信任的那个负责执行的人，他必须得成为这方面的专家。他得有那种不达目的不罢休的劲头。我觉得吧，在那些有野心的人想干大事的地方，如果负责执行的人对各种细节都不够了解，掌控不了全局，那真的会损失很多价值。所以现实就是，要想干成大事，你肯定得和别人合作，我也知道我不可能什么都自己来。真正的道理是，不是非得我来，但总得有人能扛起这个责任。
text_es: No es que tengas que hacer todo tú solo, sino que la persona en quien confías para la ejecución tiene que convertirse en el experto. Tiene que estar en modo de "no paro hasta llegar al final". Y no sé... Creo que en todos estos lugares donde gente ambiciosa y fuerte está intentando cosas grandes, se pierde muchísimo valor cuando la persona a cargo de la ejecución no domina realmente todos los detalles, y está como que... Entonces pienso que la realidad es que para hacer cosas ambiciosas tienes que trabajar con gente, no puedo hacerlo todo yo solo y lo sé. La verdadera lección ahí es que no es que yo tenga que hacerlo, simplemente alguien lo tiene que hacer.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ayo to clarify his philosophy about 'going deep' on problems after hearing his story about personally visiting card manufacturing facilities for the Cash Card. Ayo explains that he doesn't believe leaders must personally do everything, but rather that someone in the execution role must become the true expert and own all the details. He argues that in ambitious projects, massive value is lost when executors aren't in complete command of the specifics, and leaders must ensure someone on the team has that deep expertise.

vocabulary.definition: A specific position or responsibility within a team or organization focused on implementing strategies and completing tasks effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, the execution role is critical for ensuring that plans are translated into actionable steps and that projects are delivered on time and within scope.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of accountability and skill in executing plans, distinguishing it from more strategic or planning-focused roles.

vocabulary.definition: A person who possesses extensive knowledge or skill in a particular area or field, often recognized by peers as a leader or authority.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, having an expert on a team can significantly enhance decision-making, innovation, and problem-solving capabilities.

insight.nuance: While 'expert' implies a high level of proficiency, it can also suggest a degree of specialization that may not be applicable in broader contexts.

vocabulary.definition: To reach the conclusion or final stage of a process, project, or task.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and execution, 'hitting the end' signifies the successful completion of objectives and deliverables, often marked by a review or evaluation phase.

insight.nuance: This phrase can imply a sense of urgency or determination to finish, which may not always align with thoroughness or quality.

vocabulary.definition: To explore a subject or issue in great detail, often involving thorough analysis and understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'going deep' can refer to the need for in-depth research or analysis to inform strategic decisions and ensure comprehensive understanding.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a commitment to thoroughness and depth, which can be beneficial but may also lead to analysis paralysis if not balanced with timely action.

speaker: Bangaly Kaba
text: I found this framework travels with me. It's got these five components to it, vision, skills, incentives, resources, action plan, and you need all of those to have change.
keySentence: This framework travels with me; you need the right levers to achieve change.
text_ko: 저와 늘 함께하는 프레임워크(framework)이에요. 다섯 가지 요소로 구성돼 있는데, 비전(vision), 역량(skills), 인센티브(incentives), 자원(resources), 실행 계획(action plan)이에요. 변화를 만들려면 이 모든 요소가 필요해요. 그리고 각 요소 안에서 어떤 지렛대(levers)를 당겨야 할지, 어떤 부분이 빠져 있는지 찾아내야 해요.
text_zh: 我发现这个框架(framework)特别实用，走到哪都能用。它有五个要素：愿景、技能、激励机制、资源，还有行动计划。想要推动变革，这五样缺一不可。然后在每个板块里，你得琢磨哪些是关键抓手，哪些地方还有缺口。
text_es: He descubierto que este marco de trabajo me acompaña a donde vaya. Tiene cinco componentes: visión, habilidades, incentivos, recursos, y plan de acción, y necesitas todos esos elementos para lograr el cambio. Y luego, dentro de cada una de esas áreas, tienes que identificar cuáles son las palancas correctas que debes activar. ¿Qué es lo que te está faltando?
fullContext: Lenny introduces Bangaly as someone who has had a lot of impact on different cultures at various tech companies. Bangaly explains his framework for managing complex change, which he uses when joining new teams or trying to transform organizational culture. The framework consists of five essential components that must all be present for successful change: vision, skills, incentives, resources, and action plan. When any component is missing, it leads to different problems like confusion, anxiety, or false starts.

vocabulary.definition: A structured system or set of guidelines that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a complex issue.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a framework often refers to a conceptual structure that guides the development of projects, strategies, or policies.

insight.nuance: While 'framework' suggests a supportive structure, it can imply rigidity; thus, it may not be suitable in contexts requiring flexibility or creativity.

vocabulary.definition: Individual parts or elements that make up a larger system or framework.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, components can refer to various elements of a project, such as resources, tools, or team roles that contribute to achieving objectives.

insight.nuance: The term 'components' emphasizes the importance of each part in contributing to the overall effectiveness, making it less suitable when discussing singular, isolated elements.

vocabulary.definition: Motivational factors or rewards designed to encourage specific behaviors or actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: Incentives are commonly used in business to drive employee performance, customer loyalty, or stakeholder engagement through bonuses, discounts, or recognition programs.

insight.nuance: While 'incentives' typically carry a positive connotation of motivation, they can also imply manipulation if perceived as coercive or overly aggressive.

vocabulary.definition: A detailed strategy outlining specific steps, resources, and timelines required to achieve a particular goal or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an action plan serves as a roadmap for teams to follow, ensuring accountability and clarity in executing projects or initiatives.

insight.nuance: The term 'action plan' suggests a proactive approach; however, it may not be suitable in discussions where flexibility or adaptability is paramount.

speaker: Bangaly Kaba
text: What I call the anti-pattern of what we want to do. Someone says, "Hey, you know what? This would be great to build." And you go pull data to go justify why that would be great to build. Call that identify, justify, execute.
keySentence: identify, justify, execute.
text_ko: 제가 말하는 '우리가 하려는 일의 안티패턴(anti-pattern)'이 있어요. 누군가 '야, 이거 만들면 좋겠다' 그러면 곧바로 그걸 만들면 좋다는 걸 증명하려고 데이터를 끌어와 정당화(justify)해요. 그걸 identify, justify, execute(identify, justify, execute)라고 부르죠. 그런데 먼저 근본 원리(first principles)부터 출발해서 진짜 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지 제대로 이해(understand)해야 해요. 그래서 순서는 이해(understand), 식별(identify), 실행(execute)이에요.
text_zh: 我把这叫做我们要做的事情的反面典型。有人说："嘿，你知道吗？做这个东西肯定很棒。" 然后你就去找数据来证明为什么做这个东西很棒。我把这叫做识别、论证、执行。但实际上你得先从根本原理真正搞明白到底是怎么回事。所以应该是理解、识别、执行。
text_es: A esto le llamo el anti-patrón de lo que queremos hacer. Alguien dice, "Oye, ¿sabes qué? Esto estaría genial construirlo." Y vas y buscas datos para justificar por qué sería genial construirlo. A eso le llamo identificar, justificar, ejecutar. Pero primero tienes que entender realmente desde los principios básicos qué está pasando en realidad. O sea, entender, identificar, ejecutar.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Bangaly's concept of 'understand work' - spending intentional time understanding problems before building solutions. Bangaly explains that most teams fall into a dangerous pattern he calls 'identify, justify, execute' where they identify something to build, then find data to justify it, then spend enormous time building it only to see flat metrics. He advocates for 'understand, identify, execute' instead, where teams must first deeply understand the problem space from first principles before identifying solutions.
