vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, addressing quality issues is critical for maintaining customer satisfaction and compliance with industry standards, often leading to additional testing or revisions.

insight.nuance: The term carries a negative connotation, suggesting a failure to meet expected standards, and is often used in discussions about product improvements and customer feedback.

vocabulary.definition: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are measurable values that demonstrate how effectively an organization is achieving its key business objectives. They are used to evaluate success at reaching targets.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, KPIs are essential for tracking progress, making informed decisions, and aligning team efforts with strategic goals.

insight.nuance: The term is often used in a formal context, and while it indicates measurable success, it can also imply a focus on quantitative metrics over qualitative aspects.

speaker: Geoff Charles
text: Behind Ramp's velocity is a lot less the culture that I try to amplify, but a lot more the quality of the engineering and design talent candidly. And so I'm just standing really on their shoulders here.
keySentence: Behind Ramp's velocity is a lot less the culture that I try to amplify, but a lot more the quality of the engineering and design talent candidly.
text_ko: Ramp의 속도 뒤에는 제가 강조하려는 문화보다 솔직히 말해서 엔지니어링과 디자인 인재의 품질이 훨씬 더 중요해요. 그래서 저는 그들의 어깨 위에 서 있는 거죠. 첫 번째 조언은 위에서부터 R&D에 대한 투자가 1급 시민으로 이루어지도록 해야 한다는 거예요. 즉, 좋은 인재를 채용하고, 엔지니어링과 기술 브랜드에 집중하며, 그곳에서 일하고 싶어 하는 사람들을 끌어들이는 것이죠. 그들이 권한을 부여받고 싶어 하니까요.
text_zh: Ramp能发展这么快，说实话主要不是因为我推动的企业文化，更多的是因为我们工程和设计团队的质量真的很高。我其实就是站在他们肩膀上而已。所以我的第一个建议就是，从上到下一定要把研发(R&D)当成头等大事来投资，该花的钱不能省，要招最好的人，要好好打造你的工程和技术品牌，要让那些真正想发挥才能的人愿意来你这里工作。
text_es: Detrás de la velocidad de Ramp hay mucho menos de la cultura que trato de impulsar, y mucho más de la calidad del talento en ingeniería y diseño, para ser honesto. Yo simplemente me apoyo en sus hombros aquí. Entonces mi primer consejo es asegurarte de que desde arriba haya una inversión en I+D como ciudadano de primera clase - que pagues bien en el mercado premium, que contrates a los mejores, que te enfoques en tu marca de ingeniería y tecnología, que traigas gente que quiera trabajar ahí porque quieren sentirse empoderados.
fullContext: Lenny mentions that after their post about Ramp's approach, many CEOs started pressuring their PMs to move faster like Ramp, and asks for advice for PMs facing this pressure. Geoff clarifies that Ramp's velocity comes primarily from having exceptional engineering and design talent rather than just culture. He emphasizes that leaders must first invest in R&D as a priority, pay competitive rates, hire top talent, and build a strong engineering brand that attracts people who want to be empowered.

vocabulary.definition: Velocity refers to the speed of something in a given direction, often used to describe the rate of progress or change in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, velocity often pertains to the speed at which a team can deliver products or services, particularly in agile methodologies where rapid iteration is crucial.

insight.nuance: While velocity generally implies speed, in a business context, it also encompasses the effectiveness and efficiency of processes, making it more than just a measure of time.

vocabulary.definition: To amplify means to increase the volume, intensity, or significance of something, often by adding more resources or support.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, amplifying can refer to enhancing a brand's message, increasing market reach, or boosting team morale through strategic initiatives.

insight.nuance: Amplify carries a connotation of not just increasing quantity but also enhancing quality or impact, making it suitable for contexts where improvement is desired.

vocabulary.definition: Engineering is the application of scientific and mathematical principles to design, build, and analyze structures, systems, and processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, engineering is crucial for developing software and hardware products, where skilled engineers translate ideas into functional solutions.

insight.nuance: While engineering typically refers to technical disciplines, it can also imply problem-solving and innovation, making it relevant in various business discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Candidly means speaking in an honest and straightforward manner, without any pretense or deceit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, being candid can foster transparency and trust, especially during feedback sessions or discussions about challenges and opportunities.

insight.nuance: Candidly implies a level of openness that may sometimes be uncomfortable, but is often necessary for genuine dialogue and problem-solving.

speaker: Geoff Charles
text: I think the debate around working hard and burnout misses a key point, which is all about how much impact and how good you feel about the work that you're doing.
keySentence: The debate around burnout misses a key point about impact and moving the needle.
text_ko: 열심히 일하는 것과 번아웃에 대한 논의는 중요한 한 가지를 놓치고 있는 것 같아요. 그건 바로 당신이 하는 일이 얼마나 임팩트(impact)가 있는지, 그리고 그 일에 대해 얼마나 만족감이나 보람을 느끼는지예요. 제 경우 번아웃을 느꼈을 때는 사실 진행 속도(velocity)가 가장 낮았을 때였어요. 많은 노력을 들이고 있다고 느꼈는데도 정작 일이 앞으로 나아가지 않을 때였죠.
text_zh: 我觉得大家在讨论努力工作和职业倦怠的时候，漏掉了一个关键点，就是你的工作到底能产生多大影响，以及你对自己做的事情感觉怎么样。对我来说，我感到倦怠的时候，其实恰恰是我工作效率最低的时候。那时候我感觉自己明明很努力，但做的那些事情根本没什么进展。
text_es: Creo que todo el debate sobre trabajar duro y el agotamiento se pierde un punto clave, que tiene que ver con el impacto que generas y qué tan bien te sientes con el trabajo que estás haciendo. Y para mí, cuando me sentí quemado, en realidad fue justo cuando tenía menos velocidad. Pero era cuando sentía que le estaba metiendo un montón de esfuerzo a cosas que realmente no estaban avanzando.
fullContext: Lenny asks about burnout concerns given Ramp's intense focus on velocity and constant shipping. Geoff argues that the typical debate about working hard versus burnout misses a crucial point - burnout is more about lack of impact and meaningful progress than about working long hours. He shares that his personal experience with burnout occurred during periods of low velocity when he felt he was putting effort into work that wasn't actually moving the needle or creating meaningful outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that something has on a situation or person.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'impact' often refers to the measurable outcomes of a project or initiative, such as increased revenue or improved customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: While 'impact' can imply a positive effect, it can also refer to negative consequences, so context is important when using the term.

vocabulary.definition: A state of physical, emotional, and mental exhaustion caused by prolonged stress or overwork.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, burnout can lead to decreased productivity, increased absenteeism, and higher turnover rates, making it a critical issue for management.

insight.nuance: Burnout is often associated with chronic stress and can be more severe than simple fatigue, indicating a need for systemic changes rather than individual solutions.

vocabulary.definition: Extremely important or essential, especially in determining the outcome of a situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, identifying crucial factors can help prioritize resources and efforts to achieve success.

insight.nuance: While 'crucial' implies high importance, it can also suggest a sense of urgency, making it more impactful than simply 'important.'

vocabulary.definition: The speed at which something moves or operates, often used to describe the rate of progress in a given context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In agile project management, 'velocity' refers to the amount of work completed in a given timeframe, helping teams measure their efficiency and predict future performance.

insight.nuance: While 'velocity' typically denotes speed, it can also imply a focus on the quality of progress, distinguishing it from mere rapidity.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: The tendency when you're in the chasm is, "I just need more customers. I should take any customer I could find," because we need revenue. It's like taking a match and running it back and forth under a log.
keySentence: Taking any customer in the chasm won't ignite your business.
text_ko: 캐즘(chasm)에 빠져 있으면 흔히 "그냥 고객만 더 있으면 돼요. 찾을 수 있는 고객이면 누구든 받아야 해요"라고 생각해요. 매출이 필요하니까요. 그런데 그건 성냥을 들고 통나무 밑을 왔다 갔다 문지르는 것과 같아요. 통나무에 불이 붙지 않아요. 그럼 어떻게 불을 붙이나요? 작은 땔감(kindling)과 구겨 둔 종이 조금을 넣고 성냥을 한 곳에 대고 가만히 붙여서 불이 붙을 때까지 기다려야 해요.
text_zh: 当你处在鸿沟期(chasm)的时候，往往会想"我就是需要更多客户，只要能找到客户我都要"，因为我们需要收入嘛。但这就像拿根火柴在木头下面来回划，是点不着火的。那怎么生火呢？你得先放点引火物，比如揉成团的纸，然后把火柴固定在一个地方，一直烧到火真正燃起来。
text_es: La tendencia cuando estás en el abismo es pensar "necesito más clientes, debería aceptar cualquier cliente que encuentre" porque necesitamos ingresos. Es como tomar un fósforo y pasarlo de un lado a otro debajo de un tronco. No va a prender el tronco. Entonces, ¿cómo prendes un fuego? Bueno, lo prendes poniendo un poco de leña seca, papelitos arrugados, y mantienes el fósforo en un solo lugar hasta que el fuego comience.
fullContext: Lenny asks Geoffrey about the importance of starting very focused with your initial target audience. Geoffrey explains why companies should resist the urge to go after any customer when trying to cross the chasm - the gap between early adopters and mainstream pragmatic customers. He uses a bonfire analogy to illustrate that scattered efforts won't create sustainable momentum, just as moving a match around won't light a log.

vocabulary.definition: A specific group of consumers identified as the intended recipient of a marketing message or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, understanding the target audience is crucial for tailoring strategies that effectively reach and engage potential customers.

insight.nuance: The term implies a focused approach rather than a broad one, suggesting that not all consumers are equally valuable or relevant to a particular product or service.

vocabulary.definition: To consciously refrain from acting on a strong impulse or desire.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, resisting the urge often relates to avoiding impulsive decisions that may lead to negative consequences, such as overextending resources or compromising quality.

insight.nuance: This phrase carries a sense of self-control and discipline, often used in discussions about strategic decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: The total income generated from the sale of goods or services before any expenses are deducted.
vocabulary.businessContext: Revenue is a critical metric for businesses, as it reflects the effectiveness of sales strategies and overall market demand for products or services.

insight.nuance: While revenue indicates financial performance, it does not account for profitability, making it important to consider alongside expenses and net income.

vocabulary.definition: An inclination or predisposition to behave in a certain way or to favor a particular outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, recognizing tendencies can help organizations anticipate market trends and consumer behavior, guiding strategic planning and decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a pattern that may not be absolute but is observed frequently, indicating a need for careful consideration rather than a definitive rule.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: The Crossing the Chasm model is, "Can you create a viable repeatable business?" And in order to do that, you need to have an ecosystem of partners work with you in order to consolidate your position.
keySentence: you need to have an ecosystem of partners work with you in order to consolidate your position.
text_ko: 크로싱 더 채즘(Crossing the Chasm) 모델은 '지속 가능하고 반복 가능한 비즈니스를 만들 수 있느냐?'를 묻는 모델이에요. 그렇게 하려면 파트너로 구성된 생태계(partner ecosystem)가 함께 움직여 회사의 입지를 공고히 해줘야 해요. 그런데 왜 아무도 모르는 스타트업과 그런 파트너 생태계가 굳이 협력하겠어요? 답은 그 스타트업이 특정 시장 세그먼트(market segment)에서 1위로 자리잡아야 한다는 거예요.
text_zh: 跨越鸿沟(Crossing the Chasm)模型其实就是在问，"你能不能打造一个可持续、可复制的生意？"要做到这一点，你得有一个生态圈，让各种合作伙伴愿意跟你一起干，这样才能巩固你的地位。但问题来了，凭什么这些生态伙伴要跟一个没人听过的小创业公司合作呢？答案很简单——除非你已经在某个细分市场里做到了老大的位置。
text_es: El modelo de Crossing the Chasm se trata de "¿Puedes crear un negocio viable y repetible?" Y para lograr eso, necesitas tener todo un ecosistema de socios que trabajen contigo para consolidar tu posición. Bueno, pero ¿por qué un ecosistema va a querer trabajar con una startup que nadie conoce? La respuesta sería si ya hubieras consolidado un segmento de mercado donde fueras el número uno.
fullContext: Lenny asks why it's important to start focused with your initial target audience rather than going wide. Geoffrey explains the Crossing the Chasm framework - the challenge of moving from early visionary customers to mainstream pragmatic buyers. He emphasizes that ecosystems only form around market leaders, so startups must dominate a narrow segment first to attract partners and build sustainable competitive advantage.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of working successfully or feasibly; able to be sustained or continued.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a viable idea or model refers to one that can generate profit and sustain operations over time, making it essential for startups to assess viability before launching.

insight.nuance: While 'viable' suggests practicality, it may imply that something is merely functional rather than innovative or exceptional.

vocabulary.definition: Able to be done or performed again in the same manner; consistent in results.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business processes or models, repeatability is crucial for scaling operations and ensuring that successful strategies can be applied consistently across different scenarios.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting reliability, but can imply a lack of creativity if overemphasized.

vocabulary.definition: A complex network or interconnected system of entities, including businesses, partners, and customers, that interact and depend on each other.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an ecosystem refers to the collaborative environment in which companies operate, emphasizing partnerships and interdependencies that drive innovation and growth.

insight.nuance: The term often suggests a dynamic and evolving environment, which can be both beneficial and challenging for businesses navigating competition and collaboration.

vocabulary.definition: To combine or bring together multiple elements into a single, more effective or coherent whole.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, consolidation often refers to merging companies or streamlining operations to enhance efficiency and market position.

insight.nuance: While consolidation can imply strength and stability, it may also suggest a reduction in diversity or competition within the market.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: Before the chasm, the customers you work with are people who say, "We believe what you believe." So in other words, they're on the same side.
keySentence: We believe what you believe.
text_ko: 캐즘(chasm) 이전에 함께 일하는 고객들은 "당신이 믿는 걸 우리도 믿어요"라고 말하는 사람들이에요. 다시 말해 같은 편이죠. 캐즘(chasm) 이후에는 "그건 잘 모르겠지만, 당신이 가진 건 필요해요"라고 말해요. 즉 "당신이 믿는 걸 우리도 믿어요"라고 팔던 비전가들(visionaries)에게 파는 방식에서, "당신이 가진 게 필요해요"라고 팔아야 하는 실용주의자들(pragmatists)에게 파는 방식으로 바뀌는 거예요.
text_zh: 在跨越鸿沟之前，你服务的客户会说"我们跟你想的一样"。换句话说，他们跟你是一伙的。跨越鸿沟之后，他们会说"这个我还不太确定，但是我们需要你这个东西"。所以就是从"我们跟你想的一样"——这是你跟那些有远见的人做生意的方式，转变到"我们需要你这个东西"——这是你跟那些务实派做生意的方式。
text_es: Antes del abismo, los clientes con los que trabajas son personas que te dicen: "Creemos en lo mismo que tú". O sea, están de tu lado. Después del abismo, te dicen: "No estoy tan seguro de eso, pero necesitamos lo que tienes". Entonces es pasar de "Creemos en lo mismo que tú", que es como le vendes a los visionarios, a "Necesitamos lo que tienes", que es como le vendes a los pragmáticos.
fullContext: Lenny explains the root of Crossing the Chasm - that pragmatists wait for references and social proof while visionaries want to use the future first. Geoffrey clarifies the fundamental shift in customer motivation across the technology adoption lifecycle. Early customers (visionaries) are excited about your vision and want to partner with you, while later customers (pragmatists) are primarily concerned with solving their practical business problems.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who are practical and focused on results rather than theories or ideals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, pragmatists are often decision-makers who prioritize actionable solutions and measurable outcomes over abstract concepts.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting a realistic approach, and is often used in contrast to idealists.

vocabulary.definition: The psychological phenomenon where individuals look to the behavior and opinions of others to guide their own actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and sales, social proof is leveraged through testimonials, reviews, and case studies to build trust and influence potential customers.

insight.nuance: While generally positive, over-reliance on social proof can lead to groupthink or herd behavior, which may not always be beneficial.

vocabulary.definition: A significant change in the underlying principles or structure of a system or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business strategy, a fundamental shift may refer to a major pivot in operations, market focus, or technology that alters the trajectory of a company.

insight.nuance: This term implies a deep and often disruptive change, and should be used when the change is not merely incremental but transformative.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who have a clear, imaginative, and often innovative perspective on the future, capable of inspiring others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and entrepreneurship, visionaries are crucial for driving innovation and setting long-term goals that can motivate teams and attract investors.

insight.nuance: While often admired, the term can also imply a disconnect from practical realities, so it should be used carefully to avoid suggesting impracticality.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: The key formula, and this is the formula... If there's one sort of takeaway from founders listening at this point, you want to have a target segment that is big enough to matter, small enough to lead and a good fit with your crown jewels.
keySentence: Target a segment that is big enough to matter and small enough to lead.
text_ko: 핵심 공식이에요. 정말로, 공식은 이렇습니다. 지금 이걸 듣고 있는 창업자분들께 한 가지 꼭 기억하실 점이 있다면, 타깃 세그먼트(target segment)는 충분히 중요할 만큼 커야 하고, 여러분이 주도할 수 있을 만큼 작아야 하며, 여러분의 핵심 자산(crown jewels)과 잘 맞아야 해요. 그게 공식이에요.
text_zh: 关键的公式就是这样的...如果创始人们要从这里带走一个核心观点的话，就是你要找到一个目标细分市场(target segment)，这个市场要足够大、有意义，但又要足够小、你能做到头部，而且还要跟你的核心优势特别匹配。这就是公式。
text_es: La fórmula clave, y esta es la fórmula... Si hay algo que los fundadores que nos escuchan se tienen que llevar de aquí, es que necesitan un segmento objetivo que sea lo suficientemente grande como para que valga la pena, lo suficientemente pequeño como para poder dominarlo, y que encaje bien con sus joyas de la corona (crown jewels). Esa es la fórmula.
fullContext: Lenny asks for advice on how startup founders should decide if their initial target audience is too wide and how to narrow it down effectively. Geoffrey provides his core formula for selecting the right beachhead market when crossing the chasm. He explains that founders need to balance market size with their ability to dominate that segment, while ensuring their unique capabilities match the market's needs.

vocabulary.definition: A specific group of consumers identified as the intended audience for a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, defining a target segment helps companies tailor their strategies and offerings to meet the needs of a particular demographic or market niche.

insight.nuance: The term implies a strategic focus on a specific audience rather than a broad market, emphasizing the importance of precision in marketing efforts.

vocabulary.definition: The most valuable assets or resources of a company, often critical to its competitive advantage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, identifying crown jewels helps organizations prioritize their most important products, services, or intellectual properties that drive success.

insight.nuance: The phrase carries a connotation of exclusivity and high value, often used to highlight what sets a company apart from its competitors.

vocabulary.definition: To reduce the number of options or possibilities to a more manageable or specific selection.
vocabulary.businessContext: In decision-making processes, businesses often narrow down choices to focus on the most viable options, enhancing efficiency and clarity.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a process of elimination and refinement, often used in strategic planning or problem-solving discussions.

vocabulary.definition: The degree to which a product, service, or strategy aligns with the needs and preferences of a target audience or market.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, assessing fit is crucial for ensuring that offerings resonate with customers and meet market demands, influencing product development and marketing strategies.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a qualitative assessment, suggesting that a good fit enhances customer satisfaction and loyalty.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: You're looking for the 10th one. The 10th one is one who says, "I'm so tired of the status quo. I'm looking for people that are visionary like me.
keySentence: I'm so tired of the status quo. I'm looking for people that are visionary like me.
text_ko: 당신이 찾는 건 바로 열 번째 사람이에요. 그 사람은 이렇게 말해요. "저는 현상 유지(status quo)에 너무 지쳤어요. 저처럼 비전 있는 사람들을 찾고 있어요. 동료들하고 얘기하는 것보다 당신과 얘기하는 게 더 좋아요. 당신은 달라서 저도 달라지고 싶거든요. 세계 시장에서 한 발 앞서 도약(leapfrog)하고 싶어요. 반면 어떤 사람들은 그냥 에스컬레이터에 올라탄 채 가만히 있으려 해요."
text_zh: 你要找的是第十个人。第十个人会说："我真的受够了现状了。我在找和我一样有远见的人。我更愿意跟你聊天，而不是跟我那些同行聊，因为你不一样，我也想变得不一样。我想实现跨越式发展，而那些人只想待在舒适圈里原地踏步。"
text_es: Buscas al décimo. El décimo es el que te dice: "Ya estoy harto del status quo. Busco gente visionaria como yo. Me gusta más hablar contigo que con mis colegas porque eres diferente y yo quiero ser diferente. Quiero saltar por encima del mundo, y esta gente solo quiere quedarse en la escalera mecánica."
fullContext: Lenny asks about the common advice to avoid working with big companies because they'll push you around and force custom development. Geoffrey explains how to identify the right type of executive sponsor at large companies. He describes the persona-based approach to finding visionary leaders who are frustrated with the status quo and willing to take risks on new technology, rather than typical company people who follow standard processes.

vocabulary.definition: The existing state or condition of affairs, particularly in a social, political, or business context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, challenging the status quo often involves innovating or implementing changes to improve efficiency or competitiveness.

insight.nuance: While the term can imply a sense of complacency, it can also denote stability that some may wish to preserve.

vocabulary.definition: A person who is able to envision the future, often with innovative ideas and a clear sense of direction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, visionary leaders are crucial for driving innovation and inspiring teams to pursue ambitious goals.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting creativity and foresight, but can imply impracticality if ideas are not grounded in reality.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or establish the identity of something or someone; to determine the characteristics or qualities of.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying key market trends or customer needs is essential for strategic planning and decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a thorough analysis or understanding, but may also suggest a more superficial recognition in less formal contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A person with senior managerial responsibilities in an organization, often involved in strategic decision-making and leadership.
vocabulary.businessContext: Executives play a critical role in setting the vision and direction of a company, as well as managing resources and operations.

insight.nuance: The term often conveys authority and high-level responsibility, but can also imply detachment from day-to-day operations.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: All you really care about is cashflow positive. I just want to be able to keep doing what I'm doing. So you don't care about the actual GAAP accounting at all.
keySentence: All you really care about is cashflow positive.
text_ko: 정말 신경 쓰는 건 현금 흐름이 흑자라는 것(cashflow positive)뿐이에요. 그냥 지금 하던 걸 계속할 수 있으면 돼요. 그러니까 실제 GAAP 회계(GAAP accounting)에는 전혀 신경 안 써요.
text_zh: 你真正在乎的就是现金流为正。我只是想能继续做我现在做的事儿。所以你根本不care那些GAAP会计准则(GAAP accounting)。
text_es: Lo único que realmente te importa es tener flujo de caja positivo. Yo solo quiero poder seguir haciendo lo que estoy haciendo. O sea que no te importa para nada la contabilidad GAAP real.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Geoffrey's insight that you know you've crossed the chasm when you can survive without more venture funding, specifically wondering about the profit element. Geoffrey clarifies that crossing the chasm is about achieving operational sustainability rather than formal profitability. The goal is to reach a point where the company can continue operating and growing without requiring additional external funding, focusing on cash flow rather than accounting profits.

vocabulary.definition: A financial state where a company's incoming cash exceeds its outgoing cash, resulting in a net positive cash flow.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being cashflow positive is crucial for sustainability, as it indicates that a company can cover its expenses and invest in growth without relying on external financing.

insight.nuance: The term is often used to emphasize operational efficiency and financial health, particularly in startups where profitability may not yet be achieved.

vocabulary.definition: Capital provided by investors to startup companies and small businesses with perceived long-term growth potential, typically in exchange for equity.
vocabulary.businessContext: Venture funding is a critical source of financing for startups in the technology sector, enabling them to scale operations and innovate without immediate profitability.

insight.nuance: While venture funding can accelerate growth, it often comes with high expectations for returns and can lead to loss of control for founders.

vocabulary.definition: The portion of a company's revenue that contributes to its overall profit, after accounting for costs and expenses.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business analysis, understanding the profit element helps companies identify which products or services are most profitable and inform strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in discussions about pricing strategies and cost management, highlighting the importance of maximizing profitability.

vocabulary.definition: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) are a set of rules and standards used in the United States for financial reporting and accounting practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: GAAP accounting ensures consistency and transparency in financial statements, which is essential for investors and stakeholders to assess a company's financial health.

insight.nuance: While GAAP is crucial for compliance and credibility, some businesses, particularly startups, may prioritize cash flow over strict adherence to GAAP in their early stages.

speaker: Geoffrey Moore
text: In the bowling alley, it's never about you. And that is so hard for a series of entrepreneurs because they want to give a demo, they want to tell the story, they want to share their vision. The answer is, "We don't care.
keySentence: In the bowling alley, it's never about you; it's about the customer's needs.
text_ko: 볼링장에서는 절대 당신에 대한 것이 아니에요. 이게 많은 기업가들에게 정말 힘든 부분인데, 그들은 데모를 보여주고 싶어하고, 이야기를 나누고 싶어하고, 자신의 비전을 공유하고 싶어하거든요. 하지만 대답은 이거예요, "우리는 관심 없어요. 당신의 이야기를 듣고 싶지 않아요. 데모도 싫고, 당신이 누구인지도 모르겠고, 관심도 없어요. 지금 나는 어려운 상황이에요. 우리는 나에 대해 이야기해야 해요. 당신에 대해 이야기하고 싶지 않아요."
text_zh: 在保龄球馆里，永远不是以你为中心的。这对很多创业者来说特别难接受，因为他们就想做产品演示(demo)，想讲自己的故事，想分享自己的愿景。但现实是："我们不在乎这些。我们不想听你的故事。我们讨厌看演示，我也不知道你是谁，也不关心。我现在有麻烦，咱们得聊聊我的问题。我们不想聊你的事儿。"
text_es: Mira, en el mundo de las ventas, nunca se trata de ti. Y esto les cuesta horrores a muchos emprendedores porque quieren hacer su presentación, quieren contar su historia, quieren compartir su visión. Pero la realidad es: "Nos da igual. No queremos escuchar tu rollo. Odiamos las demos, no sé quién eres y me importa un bledo. Yo tengo problemas. Necesitamos hablar de mí. No queremos hablar de ti."
fullContext: Lenny clarifies that compelling reason to buy refers to the customer's pain point, not the company's sales pitch. Geoffrey explains the fundamental shift in sales approach needed for the bowling alley phase (crossing the chasm). He emphasizes that pragmatic customers experiencing serious business problems don't want product demos or company vision - they want solutions to their specific challenges and need consultative conversations focused on their situation.

vocabulary.definition: Evoking interest, attention, or admiration in a powerfully irresistible way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a compelling argument or presentation can significantly influence decision-making and persuade stakeholders to take action.

insight.nuance: While 'compelling' suggests strong appeal, it is often used in contexts where emotional engagement is crucial, such as marketing or storytelling.

vocabulary.definition: Forming a necessary base or core; of central importance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, understanding fundamental principles is essential for effective strategy development and operational success.

insight.nuance: The term 'fundamental' implies a foundational aspect that is critical to the functioning or understanding of a system or concept.

vocabulary.definition: A specific problem or issue that customers experience, which creates a need for a solution.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying pain points is crucial for businesses as it allows them to tailor their products or services to meet customer needs effectively.

insight.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of urgency and importance, highlighting areas where customers feel dissatisfaction or frustration.

vocabulary.definition: A presentation or speech designed to persuade an audience to purchase a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: A well-crafted sales pitch is vital in business, as it can make the difference between closing a deal and losing a potential customer.

insight.nuance: While 'sales pitch' is generally understood, it can carry a negative connotation if perceived as overly aggressive or insincere.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: The problem with funnels and pirate metrics and the favorites that I love to pick on are MQLs and SQLs is that nobody knows what those mean. It puts every customer in the same sort of buckets.
keySentence: MQLs and SQLs put customers in the same sort of buckets.
text_ko: 퍼널(funnels)이나 파이럿 메트릭스(pirate metrics), 제가 자주 지적하는 MQLs(마케팅 적격 리드)와 SQLs(영업 적격 리드)의 문제는 아무도 그게 정확히 무엇을 뜻하는지 모른다는 거예요. 그런 접근법은 모든 고객을 똑같은 몇 개의 '버킷'에 넣어버리고, 모든 고객과 모든 제품이 같다고 가정하게 만들어요. 결과적으로 기업(비즈니스)을 중심에 놓고 고객을 중심에 두지 않게 되죠.
text_zh: 漏斗模型和海盗指标(pirate metrics)这些东西的问题，还有我最爱吐槽的MQL和SQL，就是根本没人搞得清楚这些到底是什么意思。这套方法把所有客户都往同一个框里装，默认所有客户、所有产品都一个样。结果呢，企业就以自己为中心在做生意，而不是以客户为中心。
text_es: El problema con los embudos y las métricas pirata y mis favoritos que me encanta criticar, que son los MQLs y SQLs, es que nadie sabe realmente qué significan. Meten a todos los clientes en las mismas cajitas. Asumen que todos los clientes y todos los productos son iguales. Ponen a las empresas, o mejor dicho, hacen que las empresas se pongan en el centro del negocio en lugar de poner a los clientes en el centro.
fullContext: Lenny asks Georgiana why she calls her consultancy 'Forget The Funnel.' Georgiana explains her fundamental criticism of traditional marketing funnels and metrics like MQLs (Marketing Qualified Leads) and SQLs (Sales Qualified Leads). She argues these frameworks are outdated because they treat all customers the same way and focus on what's valuable to the business rather than what's valuable to customers.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a foundation or basis; essential and primary in nature.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'fundamental' often refers to core principles or elements that are crucial for the success of a strategy or operation, such as fundamental market trends or fundamental financial metrics.

insight.nuance: While 'fundamental' implies importance, it can also suggest a basic level of understanding, so it should be used when emphasizing essential concepts rather than superficial ones.

vocabulary.definition: Quantitative measures used to assess, compare, and track performance or progress.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, metrics are critical for evaluating the effectiveness of strategies, products, or campaigns, such as conversion rates or customer acquisition costs.

insight.nuance: The term 'metrics' often carries a connotation of data-driven decision-making, so it is best used in contexts that emphasize analytical approaches rather than qualitative assessments.

vocabulary.definition: Having the necessary skills, knowledge, or experience to perform a specific task or role.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'qualified' often describes candidates for a position or leads in a sales funnel, indicating that they meet certain criteria for further consideration.

insight.nuance: While 'qualified' suggests suitability, it can also imply a level of exclusivity, so it should be used carefully to avoid appearing elitist or dismissive of other candidates.

vocabulary.definition: Categories or groups used to organize or classify items, data, or individuals based on shared characteristics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'buckets' are often used to segment customers, leads, or data points for analysis or targeted strategies, such as customer demographics or sales stages.

insight.nuance: The term 'buckets' can imply a simplistic or overly broad categorization, so it is best used when discussing clear groupings rather than nuanced distinctions.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: Generally, the lowest hanging fruit outcome is realigning around better positioning and messaging.
keySentence: Lowest hanging fruit is better positioning and messaging.
text_ko: 일반적으로 가장 쉬운 성과는 포지셔닝(positioning)과 메시징(messaging)을 더 잘 맞추는 거예요. 그리고 사람들이 당신을 알기도 전에—제가 아까 말한 그 맥락에서—'세상에, 이건 바뀌어야 해. 진짜 불편해'라고 느끼게 하는 더 공감되는 포지셔닝과 메시징을 찾아내는 거예요. 그걸 그 순간에 연결해서, 그들이 신경 쓰는 것과 제품의 가치, 그리고 그들이 원하는 결과(desired outcome)까지 엮어주는 거죠.
text_zh: 一般来说，最容易拿到的成果就是重新调整定位和信息传达。找到更有共鸣的定位和信息，能够切中我之前说的那个场景——就是在用户发现你之前，让他们产生那种"天哪，这个必须得改，太糟糕了"的想法，然后把这个跟他们真正关心的东西、你产品的价值点，还有他们想要达到的结果都串联起来。
text_es: Por lo general, lo más fácil de conseguir es reajustar el posicionamiento y la comunicación para que funcionen mejor. Se trata de encontrar un posicionamiento y mensajes que realmente conecten con ese contexto del que hablaba antes - antes de que la gente siquiera sepa que existes, captar ese momento cuando piensan "Dios mío, esto tiene que cambiar, esto es un desastre", y conectar eso con lo que realmente les importa, lo que tiene valor de tu producto, y también con el resultado que buscan.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the impact Georgiana has seen working with companies through her process. Georgiana explains that the most immediate and common win from her customer research work is improving a company's positioning and messaging. She emphasizes the importance of connecting with customers' pre-discovery context - understanding their frustrations and problems before they even know your product exists.

vocabulary.definition: The easiest or most accessible tasks or opportunities that can yield quick results or benefits.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying the lowest hanging fruit allows teams to prioritize initiatives that require minimal effort for maximum impact, often in sales or project management.

insight.nuance: This phrase carries a connotation of seeking quick wins and may imply a lack of ambition if overused in strategic discussions.

vocabulary.definition: The process of adjusting or changing the direction, focus, or strategy of an organization or project to better meet objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: Realigning is often necessary in response to market changes or internal assessments, ensuring that resources and efforts are optimally directed towards achieving business goals.

insight.nuance: While realigning suggests a proactive approach to improvement, it can also imply that previous strategies were ineffective or misaligned.

vocabulary.definition: The strategic process of establishing a brand or product in the minds of consumers relative to competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective positioning helps businesses differentiate themselves in the marketplace, influencing marketing strategies and customer perceptions.

insight.nuance: Positioning often involves nuanced understanding of target audiences and competitive landscapes, making it a critical aspect of marketing strategy.

vocabulary.definition: The way in which a company communicates its value proposition, brand identity, and key messages to its target audience.
vocabulary.businessContext: Clear and effective messaging is crucial for marketing and public relations, as it shapes customer understanding and engagement with the brand.

insight.nuance: Messaging should be tailored to resonate with specific audiences, and inconsistency can lead to brand dilution or misunderstanding.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: So we end up seeing a messy middle there because there's no natural handoff. So pretty well, every company that we've worked with has had an opportunity to improve, especially product onboarding and product activation.
keySentence: Companies see a messy middle due to no natural handoff.
text_ko: 그래서 자연스러운 핸드오프(handoff)가 없으면 중간 부분이 뒤엉켜 보이게 돼요. 우리가 함께 일해 본 거의 모든 회사는 개선할 여지가 있었고, 특히 제품 온보딩(product onboarding)과 제품 활성화(product activation) 쪽에서요.
text_zh: 所以我们看到中间这一段就比较乱，因为没有一个自然的交接过程。基本上我们合作过的每家公司都有提升空间，特别是在产品引导(product onboarding)和产品激活(product activation)这块。
text_es: Entonces terminamos viendo un lío en el medio porque no hay una transición natural. Así que prácticamente todas las empresas con las que hemos trabajado han tenido oportunidad de mejorar, especialmente en la incorporación de usuarios (product onboarding) y la activación del producto (product activation).
fullContext: Georgiana discusses why product onboarding is often neglected at companies. She explains that it falls into a gray area where it's unclear whether marketing or product teams should own it, especially for freemium products. This lack of clear ownership creates what she calls a 'messy middle' where the customer experience suffers, but also represents a major opportunity for improvement.

vocabulary.definition: A favorable set of circumstances that allows for the possibility of achieving a desired outcome or benefit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an opportunity often refers to a chance for growth, market expansion, or the introduction of a new product that can lead to increased revenue.

insight.nuance: While 'opportunity' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply risk if not approached carefully.

vocabulary.definition: The process of integrating a new employee or customer into an organization or system, ensuring they understand the necessary tools and culture.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, effective onboarding is crucial for user retention and employee productivity, as it helps familiarize them with products or company policies.

insight.nuance: Onboarding can sometimes be viewed as a mere formality, but a well-executed onboarding process can significantly enhance engagement and satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: The process of enabling a user to start utilizing a product or service, often involving initial setup or configuration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, activation is a key metric that reflects how effectively users are engaged with a product after initial sign-up, impacting overall user retention.

insight.nuance: Activation implies a transition from mere registration to active use, and its success can indicate the product's value to the user.

vocabulary.definition: Failing to give proper attention or care to something, resulting in deterioration or lack of development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, neglected areas may refer to underperforming products, customer segments, or processes that have not received adequate focus or resources.

insight.nuance: The term 'neglected' often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of responsibility or foresight.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: So what we did was, we identified SparkToro's best customers. Now, what I mean by best customers is those that get a ton of value from your product as of exist today, pay obviously. They're happy. They're low maintenance.
keySentence: Best customers get a ton of value and are low maintenance.
text_ko: 그래서 저희가 한 건 SparkToro의 이상적인 고객을 찾아낸 거예요. 여기서 말하는 이상적인 고객이란, 지금 있는 제품에서 큰 가치를 얻고 있고(당연히 비용을 내요), 만족도가 높아서 손이 많이 가지 않으며, 무엇보다도 비교적 최근에 가입해서 제품 사용 전의 불편함을 아직 기억하는 고객들이에요.
text_zh: 所以我们当时做的就是，找出了SparkToro最优质的那些客户。我说的最优质客户是什么意思呢，就是那些从你现有产品中获得巨大价值的，当然了，付费也很爽快的。他们很满意，也不怎么折腾你。还有很重要的一点，他们注册使用你产品的时间还不算太久，所以还记得用你产品之前是什么样子的。
text_es: Entonces lo que hicimos fue identificar a los mejores clientes de SparkToro. Y cuando digo mejores clientes me refiero a aquellos que realmente sacan muchísimo provecho de tu producto tal como está ahora, que obviamente pagan. Están contentos. No dan lata. Y muy importante, se registraron hace poco tiempo, lo suficientemente reciente como para que todavía se acuerden de cómo era su vida antes.
fullContext: Georgiana explains her methodology for customer research using SparkToro as an example. She defines 'best customers' not just as high-paying customers, but as those who get significant value, are satisfied, require minimal support, and crucially - signed up recently enough (3-6 months) to accurately remember their pre-product experience. This recency is key to getting reliable data about customer motivations.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or establish the identity of something or someone.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying key customers or market trends is crucial for strategic planning and resource allocation.

insight.nuance: While 'identify' is often used in a straightforward sense, it can imply a deeper analysis or understanding in a business context.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something, often measured in terms of financial return or customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, understanding the value that a product or service provides to customers is essential for driving sales and enhancing customer loyalty.

insight.nuance: The term 'value' can encompass both tangible and intangible benefits, and it is often discussed in terms of perceived versus actual value.

vocabulary.definition: The process of preserving or keeping something in good condition, often involving regular checks and repairs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and startups, maintenance refers to the ongoing support and updates required to ensure software or systems function effectively over time.

insight.nuance: While 'maintenance' typically suggests routine care, it can also imply a need for proactive measures to prevent issues before they arise.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic, theoretical analysis of the methods applied to a field of study or practice.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, a clear methodology is essential for project management, ensuring that processes are followed to achieve consistent results.

insight.nuance: The term 'methodology' often carries an implication of rigor and structure, making it suitable for formal discussions about processes and strategies.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: The whole pain killer versus vitamin thing, you always want to be selling a pain killer. So who has an urgent problem that needs solving, not something that they might have a problem with six months down the line?
keySentence: Sell a pain killer, not a problem six months down the line.
text_ko: ‘페인킬러(pain killer)이냐 비타민(vitamin)이냐’ 하는 얘기에서는 항상 페인킬러를 팔아야 해요. 즉, 6개월 뒤에나 문제가 될 수도 있는 게 아니라 지금 당장 해결이 필요한 긴급한 문제가 있는 사람을 찾아야 해요.
text_zh: 止痛药和维生素的区别，你肯定要卖止痛药啊。就是说，谁现在就有急需解决的痛点，而不是那种可能六个月后才会遇到的问题，对吧？
text_es: Esa cosa del analgésico versus la vitamina, siempre hay que vender el analgésico. O sea, ¿quién tiene un problema urgente que necesita resolver ya mismo, y no algo con lo que tal vez tenga problemas dentro de seis meses?
fullContext: Georgiana describes the criteria for prioritizing which customer segment to focus on when multiple options exist. She references the classic business concept of 'painkiller vs vitamin' - meaning you want to target customers who have an urgent, pressing problem that needs immediate solving, rather than a nice-to-have improvement they might consider in the future.

vocabulary.definition: The act of arranging or dealing with tasks or issues in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, prioritizing is crucial for effective project management and resource allocation, ensuring that the most critical tasks are addressed first.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a strategic approach to decision-making, where not all tasks are treated equally.

vocabulary.definition: A pressing issue that requires immediate attention and resolution to prevent negative consequences.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying urgent problems is essential for businesses to maintain operational efficiency and customer satisfaction, often driving quick decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a sense of immediacy and importance, distinguishing it from less critical issues.

vocabulary.definition: A distinct group of consumers within a broader market, characterized by shared needs, preferences, or behaviors.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding customer segments allows businesses to tailor their marketing strategies and product offerings to meet the specific demands of different groups.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of targeted marketing and personalization in business strategies.

vocabulary.definition: A product or service that addresses a significant problem or need, providing immediate relief or solution to customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and innovation, a 'pain killer' is often preferred over a 'vitamin' product, as it directly solves urgent customer problems and drives sales.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of urgency and necessity, implying that the solution is essential rather than optional.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: We often talk about it and describe it as the story of how I met and fell in love with your product.
keySentence: the story of how I met and fell in love with your product.
text_ko: 우리는 이걸 종종 '여러분의 제품을 만나서 사랑에 빠진 이야기'라고 얘기해요. 세상 밖을 돌아다니다 우연히 그 제품을 발견하고, '와, 이거 진짜 우리 문제를 해결해줄 수도 있겠네. 이거다!' 하고 깨닫게 되는 다큐 같은 이야기예요. 사람들이 거기서 충분한 가치를 느껴서 계속 완전한 가치 실현(full value realization)까지 나아가고, 가치-대-가치 성장(value-to-value growth)을 이어가도록 설득하게 만드는 거예요.
text_zh: 我们经常说这就像是一个故事——我怎么遇到并且爱上了你们的产品。就好比拍纪录片一样，在外面转悠，突然发现了这个东西，然后意识到"哇塞，这玩意儿真的能帮我们解决问题啊，就是它了！"先让他们尝到甜头，觉得有价值，愿意继续用下去，最后实现产品的全部价值，形成价值增长的良性循环。
text_es: Siempre hablamos de esto y lo describimos como la historia de cómo conocí y me enamoré de tu producto. Es como un documental de estar ahí afuera en el mundo real, encontrarlo, y darte cuenta de que "¡Órale, esto sí podría resolver un problema para nosotros. Esto podría ser lo que buscamos." Conseguir el valor suficiente para convencerlos de seguir adelante hasta llegar a la realización completa del valor (full value realization), y continuar con ese crecimiento valor tras valor.
fullContext: Georgiana explains how she conceptualizes customer journey mapping. Instead of traditional business funnels, she frames it as a love story or documentary that follows the customer's emotional journey from discovering a problem exists, through finding and evaluating the product, to getting value and growing their usage over time.

vocabulary.definition: To form a concept or idea of something in the mind.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'conceptualizes' often refers to the process of developing innovative ideas or strategies that can be translated into actionable plans or products.

insight.nuance: This term implies a level of creativity and abstraction, making it suitable for discussions around brainstorming and ideation but less so for concrete execution.

vocabulary.definition: A visual representation of the process a customer goes through to achieve a goal with a company, from initial awareness to post-purchase evaluation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, customer journey mapping is used to identify pain points and opportunities for improving customer experience and engagement throughout the buying process.

insight.nuance: This term carries a strategic connotation, suggesting a comprehensive analysis of customer interactions, and is best used in contexts focused on user experience and service design.

vocabulary.definition: The series of emotional experiences a customer undergoes while interacting with a product or brand.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, understanding the emotional journey helps businesses create more resonant messages and foster deeper connections with their audience.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the psychological aspects of customer experience, making it particularly relevant in discussions about brand loyalty and customer satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: A model that outlines the stages a customer goes through from awareness to purchase, typically represented as a funnel shape to illustrate the decreasing number of prospects at each stage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales and marketing, traditional business funnels are used to strategize customer acquisition and retention efforts, helping businesses understand where to focus their resources.

insight.nuance: While this term is widely recognized, it may imply a linear approach to customer engagement, which can be limiting in today's more dynamic and multi-channel environments.

speaker: Georgiana Laudi
text: You want to reflect them back to them. That is what is going to show them that you understand the problem that they have and that your product has exactly what it is that they need.
keySentence: Reflect them back to them to show understanding of their problem.
text_ko: 그들이 말한 걸 그대로 되돌려줘야 해요. 그래야 그들이 가진 문제를 이해하고 있다는 걸 보여주고, 제품이 바로 그들이 필요로 하는 걸 정확히 갖추고 있다는 것도 알릴 수 있어요.
text_zh: 你要把他们的话反映回去给他们听。这样才能让他们知道你真的理解他们遇到的问题，而且你的产品正好能解决他们的需求。
text_es: Tienes que reflejarles sus propias palabras. Así es como les vas a demostrar que realmente entiendes su problema y que tu producto tiene exactamente lo que necesitan.
fullContext: Lenny asks for messaging tips once you understand your customer journey. Georgiana emphasizes the importance of using customer research and voice-of-customer data to inform messaging. Her key insight is that effective messaging should mirror customers' own language back to them, demonstrating deep understanding of their problems and showing that your product provides the exact solution they need.

vocabulary.definition: To show or demonstrate something, often by mirroring or echoing back information or feelings.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, reflecting can involve restating a client's concerns or needs to show understanding and build rapport.

insight.nuance: While reflecting can indicate empathy and active listening, overuse may come across as insincere or mechanical.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something, often through analysis or empathy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding is crucial for identifying client needs and tailoring solutions effectively.

insight.nuance: Understanding implies a deeper level of comprehension than simply knowing; it often involves emotional intelligence.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity to gain an accurate and deep understanding of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: Insights are valuable in business as they inform strategic decisions and help identify market trends or customer behaviors.

insight.nuance: Insights often imply a level of analysis that leads to actionable conclusions, distinguishing them from mere observations.

vocabulary.definition: To provide someone with knowledge or information about a particular subject.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, informing stakeholders or team members is essential for effective communication and decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: Informing is typically straightforward, but it can also imply a responsibility to ensure the information is accurate and relevant.

speaker: Gergely Orosz
text: In my best year at Uber, I made about 320 or $330,000 in total compensation. And when I quit my job, I was actually thinking, am I crazy? Because I am leaving... Especially in Europe, this is a lot of money.
keySentence: Especially in Europe, this is a lot of money.
text_ko: 우버에서 가장 잘 벌었던 해에 총보수(total compensation)가 대략 32만~33만 달러였어요. 회사를 그만둘 때는 솔직히 '내가 미친 건가?'라는 생각도 했어요. 떠나는 거였으니까요... 특히 유럽에선 정말 큰돈이잖아요. 그런데 지금은 우버 때보다 보수(compensation)를 더 받고 있어요. 차이라면 지금 제 수입은 뉴스레터(newsletter)가 성장하는 한 계속 늘어나서 이론적으로 상한선이 없다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 我在Uber最好的那年，总收入大概是32万到33万美金。当时辞职的时候，我真的在想，我是不是疯了？因为我要放弃这份工作...特别是在欧洲，这可是一大笔钱啊。但是现在我的收入已经超过了在Uber的时候。区别就在于，现在我的收入...怎么说呢，只要我的邮件订阅(newsletter)一直在增长，我的收入就会一直涨，理论上没有天花板。
text_es: En mi mejor año en Uber, gané como 320 o 330 mil dólares en compensación total. Y cuando renuncié, de verdad pensé: ¿estaré loco? Porque estaba dejando... Sobre todo en Europa, esa es muchísima plata. Pero ahora estoy ganando más de lo que ganaba en Uber. Y la diferencia es que ahora mi compensación... Bueno, mis ingresos siguen subiendo mientras el newsletter siga creciendo, así que no hay un tope teórico en esto.
fullContext: Lenny asks Gergely to compare his income from running a paid newsletter versus his previous high-paying tech job at Uber. Gergely explains that he left a very lucrative position in Europe (around $330,000 annually) to pursue newsletter writing full-time, initially expecting to make much less money. He shares how his current newsletter income has surprisingly exceeded his Uber compensation, with the key difference being that newsletter earnings can theoretically grow indefinitely as long as subscriber numbers increase, unlike fixed corporate salaries.

vocabulary.definition: Compensation refers to the total monetary and non-monetary rewards provided to an employee in exchange for their work, including salary, bonuses, and benefits.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, compensation packages are critical for attracting and retaining talent, often tailored to industry standards and individual performance.

insight.nuance: While 'compensation' generally implies financial remuneration, it can also encompass non-monetary benefits like stock options or flexible working conditions.

vocabulary.definition: Lucrative describes an opportunity or venture that is highly profitable or financially rewarding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, a lucrative business model is often sought after as it indicates potential for significant revenue generation and investor interest.

insight.nuance: The term 'lucrative' often carries a positive connotation, suggesting not just profitability but also sustainability and growth potential.

vocabulary.definition: High-paying refers to jobs or positions that offer salaries significantly above the average market rate for similar roles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In competitive industries like tech, high-paying roles are essential for attracting skilled professionals and can be a key factor in employee satisfaction and retention.

insight.nuance: While 'high-paying' is generally viewed positively, it can also imply high expectations or demands placed on the employee.

vocabulary.definition: Especially is an adverb used to indicate that something is particularly significant or noteworthy in a specific context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, 'especially' is often used to highlight key points or exceptional cases that warrant attention or consideration.

insight.nuance: The use of 'especially' can add emphasis and urgency to a statement, but overuse may dilute its impact.

speaker: Gergely Orosz
text: So I was working on parallel things at the same time, and I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially.
keySentence: I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 여러 일을 동시에 병행하고 있었고, 마감(deadline)에 자주 쫓겨 거의 간신히 마무리하곤 했어요. 처음에는 그렇게 될 줄 몰랐어요. 첫 몇 달은 스트레스를 좀 많이 받았던 것 같아요. 그래도 다행인 건 일정을 비워둬서 누구랑도 얘기하지 않고 이 일에만 집중하기로 했다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 所以我当时同时在做好几个项目，经常赶deadline，基本上都是卡着点儿完成，这跟我最初的预期完全不一样。头几个月压力确实挺大的，不过好在我把日程全清空了，跟谁都不见，就专心做这一件事。
text_es: Entonces estaba trabajando en varias cosas a la vez, y siempre andaba corriendo contra el tiempo, apenas lograba terminar, lo cual no era para nada lo que esperaba al principio. Los primeros meses sí me sentí bastante estresado, pero bueno, lo bueno es que liberé mi agenda completamente, o sea dije "no voy a hablar con nadie, solo me voy a enfocar en esto."
fullContext: Lenny asks about what daily life is like running a newsletter full-time, since people might think writing one post per week sounds easy. Gergely explains that creating quality newsletter content actually takes much more time than expected - requiring research, writing, feedback, and editing phases that can span an entire week. He describes how the first few months were surprisingly stressful as he learned to manage multiple projects simultaneously while working against weekly publishing deadlines.

vocabulary.definition: Existing or occurring at the same time; similar in nature or function.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and project management, 'parallel' often refers to tasks or projects that are executed simultaneously to optimize time and resources.

insight.nuance: While 'parallel' suggests simultaneous action, it can also imply a need for coordination to ensure that overlapping tasks do not interfere with one another.

vocabulary.definition: A specific date or time by which a task or project must be completed.
vocabulary.businessContext: Deadlines are critical in business settings as they help manage time effectively, ensuring that projects are delivered on schedule and resources are allocated efficiently.

insight.nuance: While deadlines can create urgency and focus, they may also lead to stress if they are perceived as unrealistic or overly tight.

vocabulary.definition: Anticipating or looking forward to a particular outcome or event.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'expecting' often relates to forecasts, projections, or assumptions about future performance or market conditions.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a level of uncertainty; it is often used when outcomes are not guaranteed but are hoped for based on available data.

vocabulary.definition: The standard of something as measured against other things of a similar kind; the degree of excellence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, quality is paramount as it affects customer satisfaction, brand reputation, and overall competitiveness in the market.

insight.nuance: Quality can be subjective and context-dependent, often requiring careful consideration of customer expectations and industry standards.

speaker: Gergely Orosz
text: Without that, when you're on your own, when you're entrepreneur, I was a great... I think I was a really diligent employee. I always tried to get my work done, show up on time, I tried to meet all expectations.
keySentence: when you're on your own, when you're entrepreneur
text_ko: 그게 없으니까, 혼자일 때나 창업가로 일할 때는요... 저는 정말 성실한 직원이었어요. 항상 일을 끝내려고 했고, 제시간에 출근했고, 모든 기대를 맞추려고 노력했어요. 그런데 혼자 일하기 시작하니까 그런 것들이 싹 사라지더라고요. 거의 15년 동안 잘하려고 애쓴 모범 직원이었는데, 막상 혼자 일하니까 하루를 그냥 낭비하는 제 자신에게 화가 났어요.
text_zh: 没有这个的话，当你自己创业的时候，我以前是个很棒的...我觉得我真的是个特别勤奋的员工。我总是努力把工作做完，按时上班，尽量达到所有要求。但我发现，当我开始为自己工作的时候，这些习惯就全没了。做了将近15年的明星员工，真的很想把事情做好，结果我发现自己在为没有...就是在浪费时间而生自己的气。
text_es: Sin eso, cuando trabajas por tu cuenta, cuando eres emprendedor... yo era un... creo que era un empleado muy responsable. Siempre trataba de terminar mi trabajo, llegar puntual, cumplir con todas las expectativas. Pero lo que me di cuenta es que cuando empecé a trabajar para mí mismo, se me fue todo por la borda. Casi 15 años de ser ese empleado estrella que de verdad quería destacar, y me encontré molesto conmigo mismo por no... simplemente por desperdiciar el día.
fullContext: Gergely and Lenny are discussing the challenges of self-directed work and staying productive without external structure. Gergely shares a surprising discovery about the transition from corporate employment to entrepreneurship - despite being an extremely disciplined and high-performing employee for 15 years, he found himself struggling with productivity and time management when working independently. This illustrates a common challenge entrepreneurs face when they lose the external accountability and structure that corporate environments provide.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort; showing careful and persistent work or effort.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being diligent is crucial for meeting deadlines, maintaining quality standards, and achieving project goals.

insight.nuance: While 'diligent' conveys a positive work ethic, it can imply a level of meticulousness that may not always be necessary in fast-paced environments.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of managing one's own learning or work without needing external guidance or supervision.
vocabulary.businessContext: Self-directed individuals are highly valued in startups and tech companies where autonomy and initiative are essential for innovation and problem-solving.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a proactive attitude, but it may also imply a lack of collaboration if taken to an extreme.

vocabulary.definition: The measure of how efficiently and effectively resources are utilized to produce goods or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, productivity is often analyzed to improve operational efficiency, enhance profitability, and assess employee performance.

insight.nuance: While high productivity is generally viewed positively, it can sometimes lead to burnout if not balanced with employee well-being.

vocabulary.definition: Beliefs or assumptions about what will happen in the future, often related to performance or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: Setting clear expectations is vital in business to ensure alignment among team members and to measure success against defined goals.

insight.nuance: Expectations can vary widely among individuals and cultures, so it's important to communicate them clearly to avoid misunderstandings.

speaker: Gergely Orosz
text: I use Twitter for a lot of research. And unfortunately what that means is when I start to write something, it can really pull my attention, because I have Twitter open and then I get a message from someone.
keySentence: it can really pull my attention, because I have Twitter open and then I get a message from someone.
text_ko: 저는 트위터(Twitter)를 리서치할 때 많이 사용해요. 안타깝게도 그게 의미하는 건, 뭔가 글을 쓰기 시작하면 트위터를 켜둔 상태에서 누가 메시지를 보내면 금방 집중이 흐트러진다는 거예요. 약간 슬랙(Slack) 같기도 한데, 오히려 더 나쁠 수 있어요. 제게 트위터는 사람들의 관심을 환기시키고 인식을 높이는 데도 정말 유용하거든요.
text_zh: 我经常用推特做研究。但问题是，一旦我开始写东西的时候，注意力就特别容易被分散，因为推特一直开着，然后就有人给我发消息。这跟Slack有点像，但我觉得推特可能更糟糕，因为对我来说，推特还有个很重要的作用就是帮我提升知名度、扩大影响力。
text_es: Uso Twitter para hacer mucha investigación. Y desafortunadamente lo que pasa es que cuando me pongo a escribir algo, me distrae muchísimo, porque tengo Twitter abierto y de repente me llega un mensaje de alguien. Es un poco como Slack, pero yo diría que puede ser peor, porque además Twitter para mí también es muy útil para generar que la gente se entere de las cosas, para crear awareness.
fullContext: Lenny asks Gergely about productivity challenges and how to stay focused while working independently. Gergely describes a specific dilemma many content creators face - Twitter serves a dual purpose as both a research tool and a marketing platform for his newsletter business, making it difficult to avoid distractions. Unlike typical workplace distractions, social media platforms create a complex situation where the distraction source is also legitimately part of the work, making it harder to simply block or avoid.

vocabulary.definition: Productivity refers to the efficiency with which goods and services are produced, often measured as the output per unit of input over a specific period.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, productivity is a key performance indicator that helps organizations assess the effectiveness of their processes and workforce.

insight.nuance: While productivity often has a positive connotation, it can imply pressure to perform, which may lead to burnout if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: Focus is the concentration of attention or effort on a particular task or objective, minimizing distractions to enhance performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech, maintaining focus is crucial for teams to achieve their goals and meet deadlines amidst numerous competing priorities.

insight.nuance: Focus can imply a deliberate choice to prioritize certain tasks over others, and it is often associated with clarity and determination.

vocabulary.definition: Attention is the cognitive process of selectively concentrating on one aspect of the environment while ignoring other stimuli.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding how to capture and maintain customer attention is vital for marketing strategies and product development.

insight.nuance: Attention can suggest a temporary engagement with a task or subject, and it is often seen as a limited resource that must be managed carefully.

vocabulary.definition: Independently means acting or functioning without reliance on others, often implying self-sufficiency and autonomy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a startup environment, employees are often encouraged to work independently to foster innovation and quick decision-making.

insight.nuance: While independence is generally viewed positively, it can sometimes lead to isolation if collaboration is not balanced with individual work.

speaker: Gergely Orosz
text: And I was asking myself, all right, and then what? And I was like, after I've bought everything that I don't need, I probably want to share what I know with people, do YouTube videos and write books.
keySentence: I asked myself, 'and then what?' after buying everything I don't need.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 '좋아, 그다음엔?' 하고 제 자신에게 물었어요. 그리고 '필요 없는 걸 다 사고 나면 아마 아는 걸 사람들과 나누고, 유튜브 영상도 만들고 책도 쓰게 될 거예요'라고 생각했어요. 그러다가 '잠깐만, 이걸 하려면 한 10년은 해야겠더라고요' 하고 생각했어요. 그만큼 장기적으로 계획해야 하니까요.
text_zh: 然后我就在想，好吧，接下来呢？我想着，等我把那些用不着的东西都买完了，我可能就想跟大家分享一下我知道的东西，做做YouTube视频，写写书什么的。然后我又想，等等，这样的话我得花个十年时间去搞这个，因为你得提前规划这么长时间才行。
text_es: Y me estaba preguntando, bueno, ¿y después qué? Y pensé, después de comprarme todo lo que no necesito, probablemente voy a querer compartir lo que sé con la gente, hacer videos de YouTube y escribir libros. Y me dije, espera un momento. Me iría a hacer esto como por diez años, porque eso es lo que necesitas planificar para hacerlo bien.
fullContext: Gergely explains his thought process when deciding between starting a traditional venture-funded startup versus pursuing newsletter writing. He was calculating the potential financial outcomes of building a unicorn startup, realizing that even after achieving massive success (like a billion-dollar valuation), his ultimate goal would be to share knowledge through content creation - exactly what he could do immediately. This realization led him to question why he should spend a decade building a company just to end up doing what he was already interested in doing.

vocabulary.definition: The mental sequence of ideas and reasoning that leads to a conclusion or decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding an individual's thought process can help in decision-making, problem-solving, and strategic planning.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a deeper level of analysis and reflection, making it suitable for discussions about critical thinking.

vocabulary.definition: The results or consequences of financial activities, often measured in terms of profit, loss, or return on investment.
vocabulary.businessContext: Evaluating financial outcomes is crucial for assessing the success of business strategies and investments.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes measurable results, making it more suitable for formal financial analysis rather than casual discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a business or project that has received financial backing from venture capitalists or investment firms.
vocabulary.businessContext: Venture-funded startups often have access to significant resources for growth and innovation, but they also face pressure to deliver rapid returns.

insight.nuance: This term carries a connotation of high risk and high reward, making it relevant in discussions about startup culture and investment.

vocabulary.definition: To determine a numerical value or amount through mathematical processes or logical reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, calculating costs, revenues, and projections is essential for budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.

insight.nuance: While often associated with numerical computation, this term can also imply careful consideration and analysis in decision-making.

speaker: Gergely Orosz
text: So there was years of work, and I wish I could tell you how to build a successful newsletter, but the best advice I have is still what Jeff Atwood does, except I have less conviction.
keySentence: there was years of work
text_ko: 그건 수년간의 작업이었어요. 성공적인 뉴스레터(newsletter)를 어떻게 만드는지 확실히 알려드리고 싶지만, 제가 드릴 수 있는 가장 좋은 조언은 제프 앳우드(Jeff Atwood)가 하는 방식이에요. 다만 저는 그만큼 확신은 없어요. 그래도 글쓰기를 시작해서 꾸준히 하면 두 가지가 일어나요. 우선 스스로를 위해 글을 쓰게 되고, 계속해서 실력이 늘면서 확실히 더 나은 글쓴이가 돼요.
text_zh: 所以这是好几年的功夫，我真希望能告诉你怎么做出一个成功的newsletter，但我能给的最好建议还是学Jeff Atwood那套，只不过我没他那么有把握。不过如果你开始写，而且坚持定期写的话，会有两个效果。首先，你为自己而写，不断改进，你的文笔肯定会越来越好。这个是肯定的。
text_es: Fueron años de trabajo, y me encantaría poder decirte cómo crear un newsletter exitoso, pero el mejor consejo que tengo sigue siendo lo que hace Jeff Atwood, aunque yo lo tengo menos claro. Pero si empiezas a escribir y lo haces con regularidad, van a pasar dos cosas. Primero, vas a escribir para ti mismo y vas a ir mejorando, vas a ser mejor escritor. Eso te lo aseguro.
fullContext: Lenny asks how Gergely got his first thousand newsletter subscribers, expecting tactical advice. Gergely explains that his 'overnight success' was actually built on six years of consistent blogging and building an audience. He references advice from Jeff Atwood (Stack Overflow founder) about becoming internet-famous through consistent writing - publish regularly for an extended period. Gergely emphasizes that while he can't guarantee newsletter success, consistent writing practice will definitely improve your skills as a writer.

vocabulary.definition: Acting or done in the same way over time, especially to be fair or accurate.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, consistency is crucial for building trust with customers and ensuring reliable performance in products or services.

insight.nuance: While consistency is generally positive, over-reliance on it can lead to stagnation or lack of innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity and accomplishment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, a successful venture often refers to one that meets its financial goals, scales effectively, and satisfies customer needs.

insight.nuance: The term can vary in meaning based on individual goals; what is deemed successful for one entity may not be for another.

vocabulary.definition: A firmly held belief or opinion, often accompanied by a strong sense of certainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, conviction can drive decision-making and influence others, particularly in leadership roles or during negotiations.

insight.nuance: While conviction can inspire confidence, excessive conviction without flexibility may lead to poor decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance or recommendations concerning prudent future action, typically offered by someone knowledgeable.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, advice is often sought from mentors, consultants, or industry experts to inform strategic decisions and improve operations.

insight.nuance: Advice can be subjective and may vary in relevance depending on the context and the advisor's experience.

speaker: Gibson Biddle
text: The A/B test we set up, we said, okay, everybody says they want this, in focus groups and qualitative and surveys. Well, let's A/B test and see what we really learn. So, the AB test was called the Perfect New Release Test.
keySentence: let's A/B test and see what we really learn.
text_ko: 우리가 세운 A/B 테스트(A/B test)는, 포커스 그룹(focus groups)이나 정성(qualitative) 인터뷰랑 설문(surveys)에서 다들 이걸 원한다고 하길래, '그럼 A/B 테스트로 실제로 뭘 배우는지 보자' 하고 한 거예요. 그래서 그 A/B 테스트는 퍼펙트 뉴 릴리스 테스트(Perfect New Release Test)라고 불렀어요. 2005년쯤 고객이 대략 백만 명 정도 있다고 가정해 보세요. 테스트 셀(test cell)에는 1만 명이 들어가고, 그분들은 신작 DVD를 다음 날 우편으로 받아요. 멋지죠? 반면 대조군(control)은 평소대로 받고, 평균적으로 아마 2주쯤 늦게 받는다고 합시다.
text_zh: 我们设置的A/B测试是这样的，我们说，好吧，所有人在焦点小组、定性研究和调研中都说他们想要这个功能。那我们就做个A/B测试，看看到底能学到什么。这个AB测试叫做"完美新片发布测试"。想象一下，2005年左右我们大概有一百万用户。一万个人在测试组里。他们第二天就能收到新上架的DVD邮件。很棒，对吧？而对照组呢，就是正常时间收到。比如说，平均可能要两周后才收到。
text_es: La prueba A/B que montamos, dijimos, bueno, todo el mundo dice que quiere esto en los focus groups y en las encuestas cualitativas. Pues hagamos una prueba A/B a ver qué aprendemos en realidad. Entonces, la prueba A/B se llamaba Perfect New Release Test. Imagínate que tenemos como un millón de clientes por el 2005. 10,000 personas están en el grupo de prueba. Les llega su DVD nuevo al día siguiente por correo. Genial, ¿no? Y el grupo de control lo recibe cuando sea. Digamos, en promedio como dos semanas después.
fullContext: Lenny asks Gibson about how Netflix balanced delight versus margin when making product decisions. Gibson explains how Netflix tested customer requests for faster access to new DVD releases. The Perfect New Release Test was an A/B test where 10,000 customers received their new release DVDs the next day, while the control group waited the usual two weeks. This test was designed to validate whether what customers said they wanted in surveys and focus groups would actually impact their behavior and retention when delivered.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the quality or characteristics of something rather than its quantity. It often involves descriptive data that can be observed but not measured.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, qualitative research is used to gain insights into customer behaviors, preferences, and motivations through methods like interviews and focus groups.

insight.nuance: Qualitative data is often seen as more subjective and exploratory, making it suitable for understanding complex issues but not for making definitive statistical conclusions.

vocabulary.definition: A method of comparing two versions of a webpage, product, or marketing strategy to determine which one performs better based on user response.
vocabulary.businessContext: A/B testing is widely used in digital marketing and product development to optimize user experience and increase conversion rates by analyzing real-time data.

insight.nuance: While A/B testing is valuable for making data-driven decisions, it requires careful planning and sufficient sample sizes to ensure reliable results.

vocabulary.definition: A state of equilibrium or equal distribution of weight, resources, or attention among various elements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, achieving balance often refers to managing competing priorities such as cost versus quality, or work-life balance for employees.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a delicate trade-off, suggesting that too much focus on one area may lead to neglect in another.

vocabulary.definition: Inquiries or demands made by customers regarding products, services, or support, often reflecting their needs or preferences.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding and addressing customer requests is crucial for businesses to enhance customer satisfaction and loyalty, often leading to product improvements or new offerings.

insight.nuance: While customer requests can provide valuable insights, they should be evaluated critically to avoid overreacting to individual demands that may not represent the broader customer base.

speaker: Gibson Biddle
text: Amazon would use a 10X, right? And so, sort of a wash there. You'd probably lean forward and do it. We actually worked hard to try to isolate what that word of mouth factor was. It was really frustrating.
keySentence: We actually worked hard to try to isolate what that word of mouth factor was.
text_ko: 아마존이라면 10배(10X)를 썼을 거예요, 그렇죠? 그래서 그 부분은 어느 정도 상쇄됐어요. 아마 당신은 좀 더 적극적으로 밀어붙였을 거예요. 사실 우리는 그 '입소문 효과(word-of-mouth factor)'가 정확히 뭔지 분리해서 규명하려고 정말 애썼어요. 정말 답답했어요. 그리고 실제로 배리 맥카시는 최고재무책임자(CFO)였는데, 그는 2배(2X)를 쓰자는 아이디어에 매우 분개했어요. 그건 더 나은 제품을 만들기 위해 더 많이 투자해야 한다는 뜻이니까요.
text_zh: 亚马逊肯定会用10倍系数，对吧？所以这样算下来基本持平。你可能还是会倾向于去做这件事。我们当时真的很努力想把口碑效应(word of mouth factor)这个因素单独分离出来，结果搞得特别头疼。然后现实情况是，Barry McCarthy是我们的CFO，一听到要用2倍系数他就炸毛了，因为这意味着你要在产品上砸更多钱。
text_es: Amazon usaría un 10X, ¿verdad? Entonces, digamos que ahí se equilibra la cosa. Probablemente te inclinarías por hacerlo. De hecho trabajamos duro para tratar de aislar ese factor de boca a boca (word of mouth). Era súper frustrante. Y entonces, la realidad era que Barry McCarthy era el CFO. Se puso como loco con la idea de usar un 2X, porque significa que vas a invertir más en crear un mejor producto.
fullContext: Gibson is discussing Netflix's Perfect New Release Test results and how they calculated the business value of retaining customers.
