insight.nuance: This term can imply a strong commitment to product excellence, but may also suggest a disconnect from market demands if customer feedback is not adequately integrated.

vocabulary.definition: Sales and marketing encompass the strategies and activities involved in promoting and selling products or services to customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, sales and marketing are critical functions that work together to drive revenue, with marketing generating leads and sales converting those leads into customers.

insight.nuance: While often used interchangeably, sales and marketing can represent distinct functions, with marketing focusing on brand awareness and customer engagement, while sales is more directly concerned with transactions.

speaker: Marc Benioff
text: My friend, Michael Bell, is probably the best entrepreneur I know. He says, 'There is no linear success.' So what that means is that stock chart that you just referred to, there's no up-and-to-the-right perfect chart where it's just one line.
keySentence: There is no linear success; no perfect up-and-to-the-right chart.
text_ko: 제 친구 마이클 벨은 아마 제가 아는 최고의 기업가예요. 그는 "성공에는 선형적(linear success)인 경로가 없다"고 말해요. 그러니까 방금 말씀하신 그 주식 차트(stock chart)는 한 줄로 쭉 이어져서 계속 우상향(up-and-to-the-right)만 하는 완벽한 그래프는 없다는 뜻이에요.
text_zh: 我朋友迈克尔·贝尔，应该是我认识的最厉害的创业者了。他总说，"成功这事儿没有直线型的。" 意思就是你刚才提到的那个股票图表，不可能是一条完美的从左下到右上的直线，现实中根本没有这种一帆风顺的曲线。
text_es: Mi amigo Michael Bell es probablemente el mejor emprendedor que conozco. Él siempre dice: "No existe el éxito lineal". O sea, esa gráfica bursátil de la que acabas de hablar, no hay ninguna curva perfecta que vaya siempre para arriba y a la derecha, como una sola línea recta.
fullContext: Marc shares a difficult period from two years ago when Salesforce had to lay off 10% of their workforce after overhiring during the pandemic. He reflects on this failure and the broader lesson that entrepreneurship involves constant ups and downs. He quotes entrepreneur Michael Bell's wisdom that no company, not even Apple, experiences perfectly smooth growth - there will always be setbacks, economic changes, and unexpected challenges.

vocabulary.definition: An entrepreneur is an individual who initiates and manages a business venture, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, entrepreneurs are often seen as innovators who drive economic growth by creating new products or services.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of creativity and risk-taking, often associated with startups rather than established businesses.

vocabulary.definition: Linear success refers to a straightforward, predictable trajectory of progress or achievement, often visualized as a continuous upward trend.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the concept of linear success is often challenged, as many ventures experience fluctuations and setbacks that deviate from a straight path.

insight.nuance: This term can imply unrealistic expectations, as it overlooks the complexities and non-linear nature of most entrepreneurial journeys.

vocabulary.definition: A broader lesson refers to a general principle or insight that can be derived from a specific experience or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, identifying broader lessons can help teams apply insights from past experiences to future strategies and decision-making.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a deeper understanding that transcends the immediate context, encouraging reflection and learning.

vocabulary.definition: Overhiring is the practice of recruiting more employees than necessary for a company's current operational needs, often leading to inefficiencies and increased costs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, overhiring can occur during periods of rapid growth, but it may result in layoffs or restructuring when market conditions change.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting poor planning or misjudgment in workforce management.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: There is something called the shiny object trap, and I'm always telling people, 'Hey, don't do AI for the sake of doing AI.' Make sure there is a problem there.
keySentence: Don't do AI for the sake of doing AI.
text_ko: 샤이니 오브젝트 트랩(shiny object trap)이라는 게 있는데요, 저는 항상 사람들에게 "그냥 한다고 해서 AI를 도입하지 마세요"라고 말해요. 실제로 해결해야 할 문제가 있는지, 그리고 똑똑하게 해결해야 할 페인 포인트(pain point)가 있는지 꼭 확인하세요. 그 문제와 아주 높은 수준의 해결책(high-level solution)이 무엇인지 파악한 다음에는, 실제로 어떻게 구현할지 찾아보고 시도해 보세요.
text_zh: 有个东西叫"闪亮物体陷阱"(shiny object trap)，我总是跟大家说，"嘿，别为了做AI而做AI。"你得确保那里真的有问题存在，确保有个痛点需要用巧妙的方式来解决。一旦你搞清楚问题是什么，以及大方向的解决方案是什么，然后再去琢磨具体怎么落地实施。
text_es: Existe algo que se llama la trampa del objeto brillante (shiny object trap), y siempre les digo a las empresas: "Oigan, no hagan IA solo por hacer IA." Asegúrense de que realmente haya un problema ahí. Asegúrense de que exista un punto de dolor (pain point) que necesite resolverse de manera inteligente. Una vez que hayan identificado cuál es ese problema y cuál es esa solución a muy alto nivel, entonces sí, acérquense y traten de encontrar cómo implementarla realmente.
fullContext: Lenny asks Marily about when AI might not be a good approach to solving problems, given that many AI investments end up being low ROI and taking months to show results. The 'shiny object trap' refers to the tendency to pursue trendy technologies without clear purpose. Marily emphasizes that product managers should always start by identifying genuine user problems and pain points before considering AI solutions, rather than implementing AI technology just because it's exciting or fashionable.

vocabulary.definition: ROI, or Return on Investment, is a financial metric used to evaluate the profitability of an investment relative to its cost.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, ROI is crucial for assessing the effectiveness of investments in projects, marketing campaigns, or new technologies, helping stakeholders make informed decisions.

insight.nuance: While ROI is a widely used metric, it can sometimes oversimplify complex investment outcomes and may not capture long-term benefits.

vocabulary.definition: Investments refer to the allocation of resources, typically money, into assets or projects with the expectation of generating a return or profit over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and businesses, investments can take various forms, including capital funding, equity stakes, or purchasing equipment, all aimed at fostering growth and innovation.

insight.nuance: The term 'investment' often implies a long-term commitment, and the risk associated with it can vary significantly depending on the type of asset or project.

vocabulary.definition: An approach is a method or strategy employed to address a particular issue or achieve a specific goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, an approach can refer to the way a company tackles challenges, such as adopting agile methodologies or implementing customer-centric strategies.

insight.nuance: The term often suggests a systematic or thoughtful method, and it can vary widely depending on the context and objectives at hand.

vocabulary.definition: A problem is a situation or issue that presents a challenge or obstacle that requires a solution or resolution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, identifying and solving problems is essential for innovation and operational efficiency, often driving the development of new products or services.

insight.nuance: The term 'problem' can carry a negative connotation, but in a business context, it may also signify an opportunity for improvement or growth.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: I believe that all product managers will be AI product managers in the future. And this is because we see all products needing to have a personalized experience, a recommender system that is actually good.
keySentence: All products will need a personalized experience and a good recommender system.
text_ko: 앞으로 모든 프로덕트 매니저들이 AI 프로덕트 매니저(AI product managers)가 될 거라고 생각해요. 그 이유는 모든 제품이 개인화된 경험(personalized experience)을 제공해야 하고, 정말 잘 작동하는 추천 시스템(recommender system)이 필요해지는 걸 보았기 때문이에요. 제 말은 넷플릭스 같은 서비스를 볼 때 그게 없으면 영화를 보기 힘들어요. 'White Lotus'나 'Stranger Things'를 본 뒤에는 비슷한 걸 보고 싶을 텐데, 로맨스물이 추천되는 걸 원하지 않잖아요.
text_zh: 我觉得以后所有的产品经理都会变成AI产品经理。为什么这么说呢？因为现在所有产品都需要个性化体验，需要一个真正好用的推荐系统(recommender system)。就拿看Netflix来说吧，现在你想看个电影都离不开推荐算法。比如你刚看完《白莲花度假村》或者《怪奇物语》，肯定想看点类似的内容对吧？这时候系统要是给你推荐爱情片，你肯定不乐意啊。
text_es: Creo que todos los product managers van a ser product managers de IA en el futuro. Y esto es porque vemos que todos los productos necesitan tener una experiencia personalizada, un sistema de recomendaciones que realmente funcione bien. O sea, no puedes ver Netflix, ni siquiera puedes ver una película sin necesitar eso. Después de que veas White Lotus o Stranger Things, vas a querer ver algo parecido. No vas a querer que te sugieran o recomienden algo romántico.
fullContext: Lenny asks Marily what she means when she says AI will be the default in the future. Marily explains her vision that every product manager will eventually become an AI product manager because all modern products require personalization, recommendations, and automation to meet user expectations. She uses Netflix's recommendation system as an example of how AI has become essential for delivering relevant, personalized experiences that users now expect as standard.

vocabulary.definition: A tailored interaction or engagement with a product or service that meets the specific needs and preferences of an individual user.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, creating a personalized experience is crucial for enhancing customer satisfaction and loyalty, often achieved through data analysis and user feedback.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a sense of customization and individual attention, making it more appealing in marketing contexts; however, it should be used carefully to avoid implying excessive surveillance or data misuse.

vocabulary.definition: An algorithmic framework that analyzes user data to suggest products, services, or content that align with the user's preferences and behaviors.
vocabulary.businessContext: Recommender systems are widely used in e-commerce and digital platforms to enhance user engagement and increase sales by providing personalized suggestions.

insight.nuance: While effective, the term can imply a reliance on algorithms that may not always accurately reflect user desires, so it should be used with an understanding of its limitations.

vocabulary.definition: The pre-set option or configuration that is automatically selected unless the user specifies an alternative choice.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and software development, defaults are critical for user experience design, as they guide users toward the most common or recommended settings.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a negative connotation when it implies a lack of user choice or customization, so it should be used with care in contexts emphasizing user agency.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and feature definition of a product, ensuring it meets market needs and aligns with business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, product managers play a pivotal role in cross-functional teams, collaborating with engineering, marketing, and design to deliver successful products.

insight.nuance: The role can vary significantly across organizations, and the term may imply varying levels of authority and responsibility, so it is important to clarify the specific context when using it.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: Don't do it for your MVP. It makes zero sense. Do not waste time of data scientists that can train models using powerful machines that are going take weeks to train.
keySentence: Don't do it for your MVP. It makes zero sense.
text_ko: MVP를 위해 그렇게 하지 마세요. 전혀 의미가 없어요. 강력한 머신을 이용해 모델을 훈련할 수 있는 데이터 과학자들의 시간을 낭비하지 마세요. 훈련하는 데 몇 주가 걸릴 수 있거든요. 만약 MVP가 있고, 단순히 아이디어나 기능에 대한 동의를 얻고 싶다면, 그냥 Figma 프로토타입 같은 걸 만들어서 몇몇 사용자에게 보여주면 돼요. AI가 할 것처럼 보이게 살짝 꾸며서 보여주는 거죠.
text_zh: MVP阶段千万别这么干，完全没意义。别浪费数据科学家的时间让他们用高配机器训练模型，那种训练一跑就是好几周。因为如果你只是做MVP，就是想让大家认可一个想法或者功能，以后可能会用到AI，那就直接造假呗，做个Figma原型出来给用户看看，把AI要做的事情模拟一下就行了。
text_es: No lo hagas para tu MVP. No tiene ningún sentido. No desperdicies el tiempo de los científicos de datos que pueden entrenar modelos usando máquinas potentes que van a tardar semanas en entrenar. Esto es porque si tienes un MVP y solo quieres conseguir apoyo para una idea o funcionalidad que tal vez use IA en el futuro, simúlalo, crea un prototipito en Figma y simplemente muéstraselo a algunos usuarios, solo simula lo que va a hacer la IA.
fullContext: Lenny asks about signs that AI may not be a good approach to solving problems. Marily strongly advises against using AI for minimum viable products (MVPs). An MVP is the simplest version of a product used to test market demand and gather early feedback. Instead of spending weeks training expensive models for unproven concepts, she recommends creating mock-ups in design tools like Figma to simulate AI functionality and validate user interest before investing in actual AI development.

vocabulary.definition: A minimum viable product (MVP) is a version of a new product that includes only the essential features necessary to satisfy early adopters and gather feedback for future development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startup environments, an MVP is crucial for testing hypotheses about product-market fit without incurring excessive costs or time, allowing for iterative improvements based on user feedback.

insight.nuance: While an MVP should be functional, it should not be confused with a fully developed product; it is a strategic approach to validate ideas quickly.

vocabulary.definition: Data scientists are professionals who use statistical analysis, machine learning, and programming skills to extract insights and knowledge from structured and unstructured data.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, data scientists play a pivotal role in decision-making processes by analyzing data trends, building predictive models, and informing product development strategies.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a blend of skills in mathematics, computer science, and domain expertise, distinguishing them from traditional analysts.

vocabulary.definition: To train models refers to the process of using algorithms to learn from data, enabling the model to make predictions or decisions based on new, unseen data.
vocabulary.businessContext: In machine learning and artificial intelligence, training models is a critical step that allows businesses to automate processes, improve customer experiences, and derive actionable insights from data.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the iterative nature of refining models through continuous learning and adjustment based on performance metrics.

vocabulary.definition: Powerful machines refer to high-performance computing systems that have advanced processing capabilities, enabling them to handle complex computations and large datasets efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In data science and machine learning, powerful machines are essential for training sophisticated models that require significant computational resources, often reducing the time needed for processing.

insight.nuance: The term suggests not only speed but also the capacity to manage extensive data and perform intricate calculations, which is critical in competitive tech environments.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: So I have a three-year-old girl and I'm teaching her about life and everything. So I was recently teaching her about the animals and you explain things to her once or twice, what a mammal is or rhino and so on.
keySentence: I'm teaching her about life and everything.
text_ko: 제가 세 살 된 딸이 있어요. 그 아이한테 삶과 이런저런 걸 가르치고 있는데요, 얼마 전엔 동물에 대해 알려주고 있었어요. 포유류가 뭔지, 코뿔소가 어떤 동물인지 한두 번 설명해 주면 되는데요, 같은 정보를 반복해서 알려주다 보면 결국 아이의 뇌를 훈련시키게 돼요. 예를 들어 '코뿔소는 이렇게 생겼고, 코끼리는 이렇게 생겼어' 하고 자꾸 보여주면, 나중에 길에서 동물을 보면 '아, 아까 말한 코뿔소랑 비슷하네' 하고 알아보게 되는 거예요. 이게 바로 모델(model)이에요.
text_zh: 我有个三岁的女儿，平时教她认识这个世界的各种东西。最近在教她认动物，你跟她解释一两遍什么是哺乳动物啊、犀牛长什么样啊这些。但是你得不断重复同样的信息，这样才能训练孩子的大脑。你会说"来，犀牛长这样，大象长那样"，重复多了以后，你孩子在街上看到动物就能认出来，会说"哎呀，这就是我们说的那个犀牛！"这就是模型(model)的工作原理。
text_es: Mira, tengo una niña de tres años y le estoy enseñando sobre la vida y todo eso. Hace poco le estaba enseñando sobre los animales y le explicas las cosas una o dos veces, qué es un mamífero o un rinoceronte y todo eso. Pero terminas entrenando el cerebro de tu hijo repitiendo la misma información una y otra vez. Entonces le dices: "Mira, así se ve un rinoceronte, así se ve un elefante", y una vez que has hecho esto suficientes veces, entonces tu hijo ve un animal en la calle y puede reconocerlo y decir: "Ah sí, eso es como el rinoceronte del que estábamos hablando". Esto es exactamente lo que es un modelo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Marily to explain what a model is for non-technical people. Marily uses the analogy of teaching her three-year-old daughter to recognize animals. Just as a child learns to identify animals by seeing many examples repeatedly, an AI model learns patterns from training data. The model becomes like a trained brain that can take new inputs (like images) and recognize what they contain based on the patterns it learned during training.

vocabulary.definition: To make something clear or easy to understand by describing it in detail.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, explaining concepts or processes is crucial for effective communication, especially during presentations or training sessions.

insight.nuance: While 'explain' is straightforward, it often implies a need for clarity and simplicity, making it less suitable for complex or technical discussions without further elaboration.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or establish the identity of someone or something, often by pointing out specific characteristics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, identifying key stakeholders or market trends is essential for strategic planning and decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term 'identify' suggests a process of discovery or analysis, making it particularly relevant in contexts where detailed assessment is required.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison between two things, typically for the purpose of explanation or clarification.
vocabulary.businessContext: Analogy is often used in business presentations to simplify complex ideas by relating them to familiar concepts, enhancing audience understanding.

insight.nuance: While analogies can be powerful tools for communication, they should be used carefully to avoid oversimplification or misinterpretation.

vocabulary.definition: To acknowledge the existence, validity, or legality of something or someone.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, recognizing achievements or contributions of employees is vital for morale and motivation, as well as for establishing credibility in negotiations.

insight.nuance: The term 'recognize' carries a connotation of validation and respect, making it particularly impactful in interpersonal communications.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: I'd like to see people being less overwhelmed, less intimidated, less afraid to start learning how to code, how to train a little model on their own.
keySentence: less afraid to start learning how to code, how to train a little model on their own.
text_ko: 사람들이 코딩(coding)을 배우기 시작할 때 덜 압도당하고, 덜 위축되고, 덜 두려워했으면 해요. 자신이 직접 작은 모델을 훈련시키는 법(train a little model on their own)도 마찬가지예요. 설령 ChatGPT(ChatGPT)나 이런 노코드 애플리케이션(no-code applications)이 우리 대신 해줄 수 있다 해도, 스스로 어떻게 작동하는지 아는 건 다른 접근 방식과 다른 사고방식, 그리고 자신감을 줘요.
text_zh: 我希望大家不要被编程吓到，不要觉得压力山大，也别害怕开始学写代码，或者自己训练个小模型什么的。虽然ChatGPT或者那些无代码(no-code)工具可能都能帮我们搞定这些事儿，但你自己会了就不一样了，思维方式会变，做事的信心也会不同，因为你知道这些东西到底是怎么运作的。
text_es: Me gustaría ver que la gente se sienta menos abrumada, menos intimidada, que tenga menos miedo de empezar a aprender a programar o a entrenar un pequeño modelo por su cuenta. Esto es porque aunque ChatGPT o estas aplicaciones sin código (no-code) puedan hacerlo por nosotros, te da un enfoque diferente, una mentalidad distinta, otra confianza al saber cómo funcionan las cosas por dentro.
fullContext: Lenny asks whether there are areas PMs should invest in skill-wise as AI becomes more prevalent. Marily encourages product managers to overcome their fear of learning to code and train basic models themselves. She compares this to learning piano fundamentals - even if tools can automate tasks, understanding the underlying mechanics gives you better intuition, confidence, and strategic thinking when making product decisions involving AI technology.

vocabulary.definition: Experiencing an excessive amount of stress or difficulty, often leading to a feeling of being unable to cope. It can also refer to being inundated with tasks or information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, employees may feel overwhelmed by tight deadlines, complex projects, or high expectations, which can affect productivity and morale.

insight.nuance: While 'overwhelmed' often has a negative connotation, it can also indicate a high level of engagement or responsibility in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling frightened or apprehensive, often due to perceived inferiority or the presence of authority. It can also imply a lack of confidence in one's abilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, employees may feel intimidated by senior management or complex tasks, which can hinder their willingness to contribute ideas or take initiative.

insight.nuance: The term 'intimidated' carries a strong emotional weight and is best used when discussing feelings of fear or anxiety in professional interactions.

vocabulary.definition: To allocate resources, such as time or money, into a project, venture, or asset with the expectation of generating a return or achieving growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, 'investing in' can refer to funding new technologies, hiring talent, or developing products to enhance competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies a long-term commitment and expectation of future benefits, and should be used when discussing strategic decisions rather than short-term expenditures.

vocabulary.definition: Widespread or commonly occurring; often used to describe trends, practices, or phenomena that are widely accepted or adopted.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market analysis, identifying prevalent trends can help businesses adapt their strategies to meet consumer demands and stay competitive.

insight.nuance: While 'prevalent' indicates commonality, it does not necessarily imply quality or effectiveness, so caution should be taken when using it to describe practices or ideas.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: What I feel people should understand is what it takes to manage an AI product. Of course people are very familiar with the stages of product development in general, but AI product development is different.
keySentence: AI product development is different.
text_ko: 제가 사람들이 알았으면 하는 건 AI 제품(AI product)을 관리하려면 어떤 일이 필요한지예요. 물론 일반적인 제품 개발(product development) 단계는 익숙하실 텐데, AI 제품 개발은 달라요. 앞서 말했듯이 때로는 제품 자체를 관리하는 게 아니라 문제를 관리하게 되고, 그 문제가 스마트한 솔루션(smart solution)으로 의미 있게 답할 수 있는지 범위를 정하는(스코핑(scoping)) 작업을 하게 돼요.
text_zh: 我觉得大家应该明白的是，管理AI产品到底需要什么。当然了，大家对一般的产品开发流程都很熟悉，但AI产品开发就不一样了。就像我之前说的，有时候你其实是在管理问题本身，而不是管理产品，你要搞清楚这个问题是不是真的需要用智能化的方案来解决。
text_es: Lo que creo que la gente debería entender es lo que implica gestionar un producto de IA. Claro, todos conocemos bien las etapas del desarrollo de productos en general, pero el desarrollo de productos de IA es otra cosa. Como mencioné antes, a veces en realidad estás gestionando el problema y no el producto, y estás tratando de definir si hay un problema que tenga sentido resolver con una solución inteligente.
fullContext: Lenny asks what PMs should do to become strong AI product managers. Marily explains that AI product management requires different skills than traditional product management. Unlike regular products where you manage features and roadmaps, AI product management often involves 'managing the problem' - determining whether a problem even exists that warrants an AI solution, and whether that problem can be effectively solved with available data and technology.

vocabulary.definition: To oversee and coordinate the activities of a team or project to achieve specific objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, managing often involves resource allocation, decision-making, and ensuring that team members work effectively towards common goals.

insight.nuance: While 'manage' implies control, it also suggests a collaborative approach, as effective management often requires engaging and motivating team members.

vocabulary.definition: The process of designing, creating, and bringing a new product to market, encompassing idea generation, design, testing, and launch.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product development is critical for innovation and involves cross-functional teams working together to meet market needs.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a structured approach, but can also encompass agile methodologies that allow for rapid iteration and adaptation based on feedback.

vocabulary.definition: The abilities and expertise that individuals possess, which enable them to perform tasks effectively and efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, skills are essential for job performance and can include both hard skills, like technical knowledge, and soft skills, like communication and teamwork.

insight.nuance: The term 'skills' often implies a level of proficiency that can be developed through training and experience, distinguishing it from mere knowledge.

vocabulary.definition: Not the same as another or each other; distinct in nature or quality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, particularly in innovation and product development, 'different' often refers to unique features or approaches that set a product apart from competitors.

insight.nuance: While 'different' is a neutral term, it can carry positive connotations when highlighting innovation or differentiation, but may also imply a lack of familiarity or acceptance.

speaker: Marily Nika
text: You may have been working on all of these incredible research and ideas... but then when you actually train the model, the results... may not be optimal... You need to be able to encourage the teams throughout this process.
keySentence: You need to be able to encourage the teams throughout this process.
text_ko: 멋진 연구와 아이디어, 여러 가설들(hypotheses)을 쌓아왔을 수 있어요. 그런데 실제로 모델을 학습시켜볼 때(train the model)는 기대만큼 성과가 안 나거나, 원래 의도했던 질문이나 가설에 답하지 못하는 경우가 있어요. 이게 첫 번째로 짚어야 할 점이에요. 그리고 이 과정 전체에서 팀을 계속 격려해야 해요. 당신은 배의 선장 같은 위치라서 팀의 치어리더 역할(cheerleading)을 하면서 모두가 멈추지 않고 계속 나아가도록 챙겨야 해요.
text_zh: 你可能已经做了很多很棒的研究，有很多想法和假设，但是等你真正开始训练模型的时候，得出来的结果可能不太理想，可能根本回答不了你原本想解决的问题，或者验证不了你的假设。这是第一点。在这整个过程中，你得给团队打气加油，因为你就像船长一样，你得当啦啦队长，确保大家都能坚持下去。
text_es: Puede que hayas estado trabajando en todas estas investigaciones increíbles, ideas e hipótesis, pero luego cuando realmente entrenas el modelo, los resultados que obtienes pueden no ser los óptimos, pueden no estar respondiendo las preguntas o la hipótesis que tenías en mente. Entonces ese es el punto número uno. Tienes que poder motivar a los equipos durante todo este proceso porque eres como el capitán del barco, tienes que ser el que anime al equipo, asegurándote de que todos sigan adelante.
fullContext: Lenny asks what else Marily wants to share from her course about AI product management. Marily discusses the key challenges of being an AI PM, particularly dealing with uncertainty when research doesn't produce expected results. Unlike traditional product development with predictable outcomes, AI projects often fail to meet initial hypotheses even after months of work. She emphasizes that AI PMs must act as team motivators and leaders during these uncertain periods.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the most favorable or efficient condition or outcome in a given situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, achieving optimal results is crucial for maximizing efficiency, productivity, and profitability, particularly in project management and product development.

insight.nuance: While 'optimal' suggests the best possible outcome, it can imply that there may be trade-offs involved in reaching that state.

vocabulary.definition: To give support, confidence, or hope to someone, often to motivate them to take action or pursue a goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In team dynamics, encouraging employees fosters a positive work environment and can lead to increased innovation and collaboration.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation and is often used in contexts where motivation and support are needed, but it may not imply direct intervention or assistance.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end or result.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, processes are essential for ensuring consistency, efficiency, and quality in operations, from product development to customer service.

insight.nuance: While 'process' generally refers to a structured approach, it can also imply complexity and may require careful management to avoid inefficiencies.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulties or obstacles that require a solution or effort to overcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, challenges can arise in various forms, such as market competition, resource limitations, or technological changes, and addressing them is vital for growth and sustainability.

insight.nuance: The term 'challenges' often carries a connotation of opportunity for growth and improvement, rather than just negative obstacles.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: There is no question that a lot of companies overhired during the pandemic. I go into some companies and honestly I can't believe all the ridiculous roles that they have, agile coaches and product owners and product ops and business analysts.
keySentence: Many companies overhired during the pandemic, creating ridiculous roles.
text_ko: 팬데믹 때 많은 회사가 채용을 과하게 한 건 분명해요. 몇몇 회사에 가 보면 솔직히 애자일 코치(agile coach), 프로덕트 오너(product owner), 프로덕트 운영(product ops), 비즈니스 애널리스트(business analyst) 같은 어처구니없는 직책들이 있는 걸 보고는 믿을 수가 없어요.
text_zh: 毫无疑问，疫情期间很多公司确实招人招得太猛了。我去一些公司看，说实话真是被他们那些莫名其妙的岗位给震惊了，什么敏捷教练(agile coach)啊、产品负责人(product owner)啊、产品运营(product ops)啊、业务分析师(business analyst)啊，一大堆。
text_es: No hay duda de que muchas empresas contrataron de más durante la pandemia. Entro a algunas empresas y la verdad no me puedo creer todos los puestos absurdos que tienen: coaches ágiles, product owners, product ops, analistas de negocio...
fullContext: Lenny asks about the spiciness in Marty's recent writing, leading to a discussion about factors causing chaos in the product community. Marty explains that companies not only overhired during the pandemic but also lowered hiring standards, creating numerous unnecessary roles. He argues that many companies have created positions that don't add meaningful value compared to how the best product companies operate with leaner, more focused teams.

vocabulary.definition: The term 'overhired' refers to the practice of employing more staff than necessary, often resulting in excess labor costs and inefficiencies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, particularly during rapid growth phases like the pandemic, companies may overhire to meet increased demand, leading to a bloated workforce when demand stabilizes.

insight.nuance: While overhiring can indicate optimism about growth, it often carries a negative connotation related to poor workforce planning.

vocabulary.definition: Agile refers to a flexible and iterative approach to project management and product development that emphasizes collaboration, customer feedback, and rapid delivery.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, agile methodologies are commonly adopted to enhance responsiveness to market changes and improve team collaboration.

insight.nuance: While agile is often viewed positively for its adaptability, it can also imply a lack of structure if not implemented properly.

vocabulary.definition: Roles refer to the specific functions or positions that individuals hold within an organization, often defining their responsibilities and contributions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, clearly defined roles are crucial for organizational structure, ensuring that tasks are allocated efficiently and that accountability is maintained.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a hierarchy or specialization, and may carry a connotation of rigidity in traditional corporate environments.

vocabulary.definition: Chaos refers to a state of complete disorder and confusion, often resulting from a lack of organization or control.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business contexts, chaos can arise during periods of rapid change or crisis, impacting decision-making and operational efficiency.

insight.nuance: While chaos can sometimes lead to innovation and creativity, it generally has a negative connotation associated with instability and unpredictability.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: People don't buy the problem, they buy your solution. Obviously they don't buy it if it's not solving something they care about, but there are many products that are solving what they care about.
keySentence: People don't buy the problem, they buy your solution.
text_ko: 사람들은 문제 자체를 사는 게 아니라, 그 문제를 해결해 주는 여러분의 솔루션(solution)을 사요. 물론 그들이 중요하게 여기는 문제를 해결하지 못하면 사지 않아요. 그런데 그들이 신경 쓰는 문제를 해결해 주는 제품(product)은 많아요. 진짜 질문은, 다른 경쟁자보다 더 잘 해결해서 사람들이 여러분의 솔루션(solution)을 선택하게 만들 수 있느냐는 거예요. 그걸 위해 시간을 투자해야 해요.
text_zh: 客户买的不是问题本身，而是你的解决方案。当然了，如果你解决的不是他们关心的事情，那肯定不会买单。但是市面上解决同样问题的产品一大堆。真正的关键是，你能不能比其他人做得更好，让客户选择你？这就需要你花时间好好琢磨了。
text_es: La gente no compra el problema, compra tu solución. Obvio que no la van a comprar si no está resolviendo algo que les importa, pero hay muchos productos que sí resuelven lo que les importa. La pregunta de verdad es: ¿lo resuelves mejor que todos los demás para que te elijan a ti? Y ahí es donde tienes que invertir tiempo.
fullContext: Lenny is asking about product discovery and how teams should spend their time between understanding problems versus creating solutions. Marty is explaining why product teams should focus most of their discovery time on solution development rather than problem validation. He argues that while problems are important, customers ultimately purchase solutions, and the key differentiator is building a better solution than competitors.

vocabulary.definition: A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation. In business, it often refers to a product or service that addresses a specific need or challenge.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a solution is typically presented as a product or service that resolves a customer's pain point, thereby creating value and driving sales.

insight.nuance: While 'solution' implies a positive outcome, it can sometimes carry the connotation of overselling or simplifying complex issues.

vocabulary.definition: To find an answer to a problem or to deal effectively with a challenge. It involves the application of critical thinking and analysis.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'solve' often refers to the process of addressing customer needs or operational challenges through innovative strategies or products.

insight.nuance: The term suggests an active, dynamic process and is often used in contexts where creativity and resourcefulness are required.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to comprehend or grasp the meaning of something, often involving insight into complex issues or relationships. It is essential for effective communication and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding is crucial for identifying customer needs, market trends, and internal dynamics, which informs strategy and operations.

insight.nuance: While 'understanding' implies a depth of knowledge, it can also suggest empathy and awareness, particularly in interpersonal or customer relations.

vocabulary.definition: The center of interest or activity; the act of concentrating attention on a particular task or objective. It is essential for achieving goals efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business environments, maintaining focus is critical for prioritizing tasks, aligning team efforts, and driving projects to successful completion.

insight.nuance: While 'focus' suggests clarity and direction, it can also imply the risk of neglecting other important areas if overemphasized.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: They're dramatically overpaid for the value they provide. Because it's a project management role. It is a lot easier to deliver output than it is to deliver outcomes.
keySentence: They are dramatically overpaid for delivering output rather than outcomes.
text_ko: 그들은 제공하는 가치에 비해 보수를 지나치게 많이 받고 있어요. 그건 프로젝트 관리 역할(project management role)이기 때문이에요. 산출물(output)을 내는 건 결과(outcome)를 만들어내는 것보다 훨씬 쉬워요.
text_zh: 他们拿的薪水跟他们创造的价值完全不成正比，拿得太多了。因为这就是个项目管理(project management)的活儿嘛。你要说交付成果(output)，那简单，但要真正实现效果(outcomes)，那就难多了。
text_es: Están súper sobrepagados para el valor que realmente aportan. Porque es un puesto de gestión de proyectos. Es mucho más fácil entregar productos que entregar resultados de verdad.
fullContext: Lenny describes Marty's concept of 'product management theater' - people who aren't real product managers but hold the title. Marty explains that many people calling themselves product managers are actually doing project management work, focusing on shipping features rather than solving problems. He emphasizes the critical difference between delivering output (shipping features) versus delivering outcomes (solving customer and business problems).

vocabulary.definition: The process of planning, executing, and overseeing a project to achieve specific goals within a defined timeline and budget.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, project management is crucial for coordinating resources, managing risks, and ensuring that project deliverables meet stakeholder expectations.

insight.nuance: While often associated with administrative tasks, effective project management requires strategic thinking and leadership skills to navigate complex challenges.

vocabulary.definition: To achieve and present the intended results or impacts of a project or initiative, often measured against predefined objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, delivering outcomes is essential for demonstrating value to stakeholders and ensuring that projects align with strategic goals.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the importance of results over mere completion of tasks, highlighting a focus on effectiveness rather than just efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something, often assessed in terms of its benefits relative to its costs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, value is a critical concept that influences decision-making, pricing strategies, and customer satisfaction, as organizations strive to maximize the benefits they provide to clients.

insight.nuance: Value can be subjective, varying between different stakeholders based on their perspectives and needs, making it essential to understand the audience when discussing it.

vocabulary.definition: The tangible products, results, or services produced as a result of a process or activity, often quantifiable in nature.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, output is frequently measured to assess productivity and efficiency, serving as a key performance indicator for teams and projects.

insight.nuance: While output is important, it is often seen as a less comprehensive measure of success compared to outcomes, which consider the broader impact of the work done.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: It's frustrating because I really thought by the year 2022, we would not have such a chasm between how good companies work and the rest. There's such strong incentives, just the profit motive alone. Why don't more companies want to work like the best?
keySentence: The chasm between good companies and the rest is perplexing.
text_ko: 정말 2022년쯤이면 잘하는 회사들이 일하는 방식과 다른 회사들 사이에 이런 큰 격차가 없을 줄 알았어요. 유인이 충분히 강한데, 이윤 동기(profit motive)만 봐도 그렇고요. 그래서 왜 더 많은 회사들이 최고 수준처럼 일하려고 하지 않는지 정말 이해가 안 돼요.
text_zh: 这真的很让人郁闷，我原本以为到了2022年，优秀公司和普通公司之间不会有这么大的差距。动力其实很强啊，光是利润驱动就够了。为什么更多公司不愿意学习那些最好的公司呢？我觉得这事儿真的很费解。
text_es: Es frustrante porque realmente pensé que para el año 2022, no tendríamos semejante abismo entre cómo funcionan las empresas que lo hacen bien y el resto. Hay incentivos muy fuertes, solo el motivo de ganancia ya es suficiente. ¿Por qué no quieren más empresas trabajar como las mejores? Eso me resulta desconcertante.
fullContext: Lenny asks Marty about his recent philosophical approach to writing about product management and the misconceptions he's been observing. Marty explains his frustration with the persistent gap between high-performing product companies and the majority of companies. Despite clear financial incentives and proven success models, most companies continue using outdated product development approaches rather than adopting the practices of leading tech companies.

vocabulary.definition: Causing feelings of annoyance or disappointment due to inability to achieve something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, frustration often arises when expectations are not met, such as delays in project timelines or unmet performance targets.

insight.nuance: While it conveys a sense of dissatisfaction, it can also imply a need for improvement or change.

vocabulary.definition: Factors or rewards that motivate individuals or organizations to act in a certain way.
vocabulary.businessContext: Incentives are commonly used in business to drive employee performance, customer loyalty, or sales growth, often taking the form of bonuses, commissions, or discounts.

insight.nuance: Incentives can be both monetary and non-monetary, and their effectiveness can vary based on individual motivations.

vocabulary.definition: The desire to achieve financial gain as a primary objective of business activities.
vocabulary.businessContext: The profit motive drives companies to innovate, reduce costs, and improve efficiency, often influencing strategic decisions and market competition.

insight.nuance: While the profit motive is a fundamental aspect of capitalism, it can sometimes lead to ethical dilemmas or short-term thinking.

vocabulary.definition: A continuous and significant difference or disparity between two entities or groups over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a persistent gap may refer to ongoing disparities in performance, technology adoption, or market access between leading companies and their competitors.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a need for urgent action to address the underlying issues causing the disparity.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: Too many people in our industry view themselves as a victim of their company, like they're stuck in a feature team and there's nothing they can do about it other than quit. I think that's not true. There is so much they can do.
keySentence: Many view themselves as a victim, feeling stuck in a feature team.
text_ko: 우리 업계에서는 스스로를 회사의 피해자라고 보는 분들이 너무 많아요. 마치 기능팀(feature team)에 갇혀서 그걸 벗어날 방법은 그만두는 것뿐이라고 생각하죠. 저는 그게 사실이 아니라고 봐요. 할 수 있는 일이 정말 많아요.
text_zh: 我们这个行业里太多人都觉得自己是公司的受害者，好像被困在功能团队(feature team)里就没办法了，除了辞职别无选择。我觉得这想法不对，其实他们能做的事情多着呢。
text_es: Mucha gente en nuestra industria se ve como víctima de su empresa, como si estuviera atrapada en un equipo de desarrollo y no pudiera hacer nada más que renunciar. Yo creo que eso no es cierto. Hay muchísimo que pueden hacer.
fullContext: Lenny asks what motivated Marty to write his third book, TRANSFORMED. Marty explains that many product professionals feel trapped in organizations that operate as 'feature teams' - teams given roadmaps of features to build rather than problems to solve. Instead of viewing themselves as powerless victims, Marty argues these individuals have much more agency than they realize to transform their companies and elevate their own roles.

vocabulary.definition: A feature team is a cross-functional group of professionals who collaborate to deliver a specific feature or product increment within a larger project or system.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, feature teams are often employed in Agile methodologies to enhance productivity and ensure that all aspects of a feature, from design to testing, are addressed collaboratively.

insight.nuance: While feature teams can foster innovation and speed, they may also lead to silos if not managed properly, as team members may become overly focused on their specific feature rather than the overall product vision.

vocabulary.definition: Being trapped in organizations refers to the feeling of being stuck in a company or role with limited opportunities for growth or change.
vocabulary.businessContext: This phrase is often used in discussions about employee engagement and retention, highlighting the importance of fostering a culture that empowers employees to seek development and innovation.

insight.nuance: The term carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of agency or autonomy, and is typically used to describe dissatisfaction among employees who feel constrained by organizational structures.

vocabulary.definition: A roadmap is a strategic plan that outlines the vision, direction, and milestones for a project or product over a specified period.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, roadmaps are essential for aligning teams, setting priorities, and communicating the timeline and goals for product development or organizational initiatives.

insight.nuance: While roadmaps provide a clear direction, they should remain flexible to adapt to changing market conditions or feedback, and are often revised as projects evolve.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: In a feature team, basically you are handed a typical roadmap. Almost everybody, even though I wish this wasn't the case, almost everybody to have the same thing, that it's a prioritized list of features and projects.
keySentence: A prioritized list of features guides typical roadmap decisions.
text_ko: 기능 팀(feature team)에서는 보통 전형적인 로드맵을 넘겨받아요. 솔직히 이게 아니었으면 좋겠지만, 거의 다들 똑같아요 — 우선순위가 매겨진 기능과 프로젝트 목록(features and projects)을요. 그래서 이해관계자들이 보통 분기마다 모여서, "우리 쪽 비즈니스를 운영하려면 이 기능들이 필요하다"고 말해요.
text_zh: 在功能团队(feature team)里，基本上就是给你一个典型的路线图(roadmap)。几乎所有人，虽然我希望情况不是这样，但几乎所有人拿到的都是同一个东西——就是一个按优先级排列的功能和项目清单。一般是一些利益相关方(stakeholders)聚在一起，通常是每个季度一次，然后他们会说："你看，要想把我们这块业务搞好，我们需要这些功能。"
text_es: En un equipo de funcionalidades (feature team), básicamente te entregan una hoja de ruta típica. Casi todo el mundo, aunque ojalá no fuera así, casi todo el mundo tiene lo mismo: una lista priorizada de funcionalidades y proyectos. Entonces se juntan algunos stakeholders, normalmente cada trimestre, y dicen: "Mira, para manejar nuestra parte del negocio, necesitamos estas funcionalidades."
fullContext: Lenny asks Marty to help listeners identify whether they work on a feature team (feature factory) or a real product team. Marty explains the characteristics of feature teams, where teams are given predetermined solutions in the form of roadmaps rather than problems to solve. He describes how stakeholders typically create quarterly lists of required features, essentially asking teams to build pre-defined solutions rather than empowering them to discover the best approaches.

vocabulary.definition: Ranked or arranged in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, prioritization is crucial for resource allocation and project management, ensuring that the most critical tasks are addressed first.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a strategic decision-making process, and it is important to use it when discussing the importance of tasks rather than just listing them.

vocabulary.definition: A strategic plan that outlines goals, milestones, and the steps necessary to achieve them over a specific timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, a roadmap serves as a guiding document for product development, aligning teams on objectives and timelines.

insight.nuance: While it suggests a clear path forward, it can also imply flexibility, as roadmaps may need to adapt to changing circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: Distinctive attributes or functionalities of a product or service that provide value to users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development, features are critical for differentiating offerings in the market and meeting customer needs.

insight.nuance: The term can sometimes be used interchangeably with 'benefits,' but it specifically refers to the characteristics rather than the advantages they provide.

vocabulary.definition: Temporary endeavors undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result, characterized by specific objectives and constraints.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, projects are essential for driving innovation and achieving strategic goals, often requiring careful planning and execution.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the temporary nature and specific goals of the work, distinguishing it from ongoing operations or processes.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: We are looking for the commonality and mostly we're looking to help a company, whether it's a startup or a large company to have the best possible chance of success. That's the goal for us. It's a different goal.
keySentence: We are looking for the commonality to give companies the best possible chance of success.
text_ko: 우리는 공통점을 찾고, 무엇보다 스타트업이든 대기업이든 회사가 성공할 가능성을 최대한 높일 수 있도록 돕는 데 집중하고 있어요. 그게 우리의 목표예요. 좀 다른 목표예요.
text_zh: 我们主要是在找共同点，更重要的是，我们想帮助公司——不管是初创公司(startup)还是大企业——让他们有最大的成功机会。这就是我们的目标，跟别人不太一样。
text_es: Buscamos los puntos en común y sobre todo queremos ayudar a una empresa, ya sea una startup o una compañía grande, a que tenga las mejores posibilidades de éxito. Ese es nuestro objetivo. Es un enfoque distinto.
fullContext: Marty contrasts his approach with Lenny's podcast style. While Lenny seeks to showcase diverse perspectives and unique practices across different companies, Marty explains that his Silicon Valley Product Group focuses on identifying common principles and practices consistently used by the best product companies. Their heuristic requires seeing techniques used successfully by multiple proven companies before they evangelize them.

vocabulary.definition: Commonality refers to the shared characteristics or features among different entities or groups.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying commonality can help organizations understand market trends, customer preferences, and potential collaboration opportunities.

insight.nuance: While commonality emphasizes similarities, it is important to recognize unique aspects that may differentiate entities in competitive contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A startup is a newly established business, often in the early stages of development, focused on bringing a unique product or service to market.
vocabulary.businessContext: Startups are typically characterized by innovation, scalability, and a high potential for growth, often seeking venture capital to fund their operations.

insight.nuance: The term 'startup' often connotes a sense of agility and disruption, distinguishing it from more traditional, established businesses.

vocabulary.definition: Success is the achievement of desired goals or outcomes, often measured by specific metrics such as profitability, market share, or customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, success can be defined differently depending on the organization's objectives, ranging from financial performance to social impact.

insight.nuance: Success can be subjective and may vary across different stakeholders, making it essential to clarify what success means in specific contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A goal is a specific aim or desired result that an individual or organization strives to achieve within a defined timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, setting clear goals is crucial for strategic planning, performance measurement, and aligning team efforts towards common objectives.

insight.nuance: While goals can be short-term or long-term, it is important to ensure they are SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) for effective implementation.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: But on an empowered product team, where you're trying to come up with a solution that solves the problem you've been assigned, that's much harder because that means we have to discover a solution that's valuable, usable, feasible, viable.
keySentence: An empowered product team discovers valuable, usable, feasible, and viable solutions.
text_ko: 하지만 권한이 주어진 프로덕트 팀(empowered product team)에서는 배정된 문제를 실제로 해결할 수 있는 해법을 찾아내야 해서 훨씬 더 어려워요. 우리가 찾아야 하는 해법은 가치(valuable)가 있고, 사용성(usable)이 뛰어나고, 실현 가능성(feasible)이 있으며, 사업성(viable)도 갖춰야 하거든요. 엔지니어들은 확실히 실현 가능성(feasible)을 책임지고, 디자이너는 사용성(usable)을 책임지지만, 가치(valuable)와 사업성(viable) — 이 두 가지가 가장 어려운 과제들 중 하나예요 — 을 책임지는 건 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)예요.
text_zh: 但是在一个有自主权的产品团队里，你要想出解决方案来搞定分配给你的问题，这就难多了，因为这意味着我们得找到一个既有价值、又好用、还能实现、也能盈利的解决方案。虽然工程师肯定负责"能不能实现"这块，设计师肯定负责"好不好用"这块，但是"有没有价值"和"能不能盈利"——这两个最难搞的事情，就是产品经理的活儿了。
text_es: Pero en un equipo de producto empoderado (empowered), donde estás tratando de encontrar una solución que resuelva el problema que te asignaron, eso es mucho más difícil porque significa que tenemos que descubrir una solución que sea valiosa, usable, factible y viable. Ahora, mientras que los ingenieros definitivamente se encargan de lo factible, y el diseñador se encarga de lo usable, lo valioso y lo viable, que son dos de las cosas más difíciles de lograr, eso le toca al product manager.
fullContext: Continuing his explanation of the differences between feature teams and empowered product teams, Marty describes how empowered product teams work. Instead of building predetermined features, these teams are given problems to solve and must discover solutions that meet four key criteria. He explains how responsibilities are divided: engineers handle feasibility, designers handle usability, while product managers tackle the challenging areas of value and viability.

vocabulary.definition: Having the authority or power to make decisions and take actions independently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, an empowered team is one that is trusted to innovate and solve problems without excessive oversight, fostering creativity and accountability.

insight.nuance: While 'empowered' conveys a sense of autonomy, it also implies a responsibility to deliver results, making it important to use in contexts where both authority and accountability are present.

vocabulary.definition: A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech, a solution often refers to a product or service designed to address specific customer pain points or operational challenges.

insight.nuance: The term 'solution' can imply a comprehensive approach to a problem, so it is best used when discussing strategies or offerings that provide clear benefits.

vocabulary.definition: Having worth, significance, or usefulness; providing benefits that justify its cost or investment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a valuable product or service is one that meets customer needs effectively, leading to customer satisfaction and loyalty, as well as potential profitability.

insight.nuance: While 'valuable' is often used to describe tangible assets, it can also refer to intangible qualities such as insights or relationships, making it versatile in usage.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of working successfully; feasible or practical in a given context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup discussions, a viable solution is one that can be realistically implemented and sustained, considering factors like market demand, resources, and scalability.

insight.nuance: The term 'viable' often carries a connotation of long-term sustainability, so it is best used when assessing the practicality of a proposal or idea over time.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: I do. In fact, I've got some very uncomfortable things to talk about, which I know the more intelligent part of me is like, "Don't bring that up." But also the other side of me is like, "But people need to hear it."
keySentence: I have uncomfortable things to talk about that people need to hear.
text_ko: 네, 있어요. 사실 꽤 불편한 얘기들이 있어요. 머리로는 '그 얘기 꺼내지 마'라고 하는데, 다른 한쪽은 '그래도 사람들이 들어야 해'라고 해요.
text_zh: 有啊。其实我有些挺敏感的话题想聊，我理智的那一面告诉我"别提这事儿"，但另一面又觉得"大家确实需要听听这些"。
text_es: Claro que sí. De hecho, tengo que hablar de algunas cosas bastante incómodas, y sé que la parte más inteligente de mí me dice "No saques ese tema." Pero por otro lado también pienso "La gente necesita escuchar esto."
fullContext: Lenny asks about Marty's recent 'spiciness' in writing, suggesting he's telling people things they don't want to hear but need to hear. Marty confirms this is conscious - he's deliberately dialing up his rhetoric around uncomfortable truths in the product management industry. He acknowledges internal conflict between staying diplomatic versus sharing harsh realities that could help people and companies improve.

vocabulary.definition: Experiencing physical or emotional discomfort; causing unease or awkwardness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'uncomfortable' often refers to topics that may provoke tension or disagreement, yet are necessary for growth and transparency.

insight.nuance: While it typically has a negative connotation, discussing uncomfortable topics can be crucial for progress and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Possessing a high level of understanding, knowledge, or mental capacity; able to think critically and solve problems effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, 'intelligent' often describes employees or strategies that demonstrate analytical thinking and innovative solutions.

insight.nuance: While generally positive, labeling someone as 'intelligent' can imply a comparison to others, which may not always be appropriate.

vocabulary.definition: In a purposeful or intentional manner; done with careful consideration or planning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, actions taken 'deliberately' indicate strategic decision-making, often reflecting a calculated approach to risk and opportunity.

insight.nuance: This term can imply a sense of control or forethought, but it may also suggest a lack of spontaneity or flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: To increase or intensify something; to enhance or amplify a particular aspect or quality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and marketing, 'dialing up' often refers to boosting efforts in areas such as customer engagement, advertising, or product features to achieve better results.

insight.nuance: While it conveys a proactive approach, overusing this phrase can imply excessive or aggressive tactics that may not align with a company's values.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: Nothing I talk about, and honestly being very clear, nothing I've written about in Inspired, nothing I've written about in Empowered was invented by us. All we do is share the practices we see being used in the best teams.
keySentence: The heuristic is to recommend practices used by the best teams.
text_ko: 솔직히 말하면요, 제가 이야기하는 것들—그리고 분명히 해두자면 제가 Inspired나 Empowered에 쓴 내용들 중 어느 것도 우리가 발명한 게 아니에요. 우리가 하는 건 최고의 팀들이 실제로 쓰는 관행들만 공유하는 거예요. 그래서 판단 기준(heuristic)은 꽤 간단해요. 여러 우수한 팀들이 쓰고 있으면, '좋아요, 그럼 추천을 시작해보죠' 하는 식이에요.
text_zh: 说实话，我讲的这些东西，还有我在《启示录》和《赋能》里写的那些，都不是我们发明的。我们就是把那些顶尖团队在用的方法分享出来而已。判断标准其实很简单——如果好几个顶级团队都在用某个做法，我们就会想"行，那咱们就开始推荐这个方法吧。"
text_es: Nada de lo que hablo, y siendo muy honesto, nada de lo que he escrito en Inspired, nada de lo que he escrito en Empowered lo inventamos nosotros. Lo único que hacemos es compartir las prácticas que vemos que usan los mejores equipos. Así que la regla es bastante sencilla. Si varios de los mejores equipos lo están usando, decimos: "Bueno, empecemos a recomendarlo."
fullContext: Lenny asks whether the high-performing product practices Marty describes actually exist at real companies, as some people doubt these methods are used anywhere. Marty explains his methodology for developing recommendations - he doesn't invent practices but rather observes and shares what the best product teams are already doing. He describes his approach of only recommending practices that are proven effective at multiple top-performing companies.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by exceptional efficiency and effectiveness in achieving goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, 'high-performing' often describes teams or individuals who consistently exceed performance benchmarks and contribute significantly to organizational success.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a positive connotation and is typically used to highlight excellence, but should be applied carefully to avoid unrealistic expectations.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic, theoretical analysis of the methods applied to a field of study or practice.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'methodology' refers to structured approaches used to manage projects, conduct research, or implement processes, such as Agile or Lean methodologies.

insight.nuance: While often used interchangeably with 'methods,' 'methodology' implies a broader framework and should be used when discussing the rationale behind chosen methods.

vocabulary.definition: Established methods or techniques that are regularly employed in a specific field or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, 'practices' often refer to best practices that enhance efficiency, productivity, and quality of work.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a level of standardization and is often used in discussions about continuous improvement; however, it may imply rigidity if not contextualized with innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Groups of individuals organized to work collaboratively towards a common goal or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, 'teams' are fundamental units that drive projects and initiatives, often characterized by diverse skills and roles.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes collaboration and shared responsibility, but should be used carefully to distinguish between formal teams and informal groups.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: And then the one that I really probably shouldn't bring up just because it's become a religious topic almost. I know it's a super sensitive topic for people, but the reality is with remote employees, both velocity and innovation have taken a real hit.
keySentence: Remote employees have taken a real hit in both velocity and innovation.
text_ko: 솔직히 이 얘기는 거의 종교 논쟁 수준이라서 꺼내지 않는 게 나을 수도 있는데요. 사람들한테 정말 민감한 주제인 건 알고요. 그런데 현실은 원격 근무자의 경우 속도(velocity)와 혁신(innovation) 둘 다 실질적으로 큰 타격을 받았어요.
text_zh: 还有一个我本来不太想提的话题，因为这几乎成了一个很敏感的宗教话题了。我知道大家对这个都很敏感，但现实就是远程办公的员工，无论是工作效率还是创新能力，确实都受到了不小的冲击。
text_es: Y luego está el tema que probablemente no debería ni mencionar porque se ha vuelto casi como una religión. Sé que es un tema súper delicado para la gente, pero la realidad es que con los empleados remotos, tanto la velocidad como la innovación han sufrido un golpe bastante duro.
fullContext: Marty discusses macro factors creating challenges in the product management field, including overhiring during the pandemic, rising cost of funds, and potential AI disruption. He addresses what he calls a 'religious topic' - the impact of remote work on product development. Despite knowing it's sensitive, he shares his observation that companies with remote teams struggle with both development speed and innovation compared to co-located teams.

vocabulary.definition: Velocity refers to the speed at which something moves or operates, often in a business context relating to the rate of progress or output.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, velocity is frequently used to measure the pace of project completion, product development, or sales cycles, indicating how quickly a team can deliver results.

insight.nuance: While velocity suggests speed, it can also imply efficiency; using it in discussions about performance may highlight the need for balance between speed and quality.

vocabulary.definition: Innovation is the process of creating new ideas, products, or methods that improve existing solutions or address unmet needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, innovation is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage, driving growth, and responding to changing market demands.

insight.nuance: Innovation can carry a positive connotation of progress and advancement, but it may also imply risk and uncertainty, particularly when discussing disruptive changes.

vocabulary.definition: Sensitive describes a state of being easily affected or responsive to external factors, often relating to emotions or reactions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, a sensitive topic may refer to issues that require careful handling due to their potential impact on employee morale or public perception.

insight.nuance: Using 'sensitive' can imply a need for caution and empathy; it is advisable to approach sensitive topics with tact to avoid conflict or misunderstanding.

vocabulary.definition: Macro factors are large-scale influences that affect an organization or industry, including economic, political, social, and technological elements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In strategic planning, understanding macro factors is essential for assessing risks and opportunities that can impact long-term business success.

insight.nuance: While macro factors provide a broad perspective, they can sometimes overshadow specific, actionable insights; it's important to balance macro analysis with micro-level considerations.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: And his argument was because as a company gets bigger, product historically became less important. The people in a company that would be celebrated were marketing people, sales people, finance people. If a company stops innovating, these are the engines for growth.
keySentence: Sales and marketing are engines for growth when companies stop innovating.
text_ko: 그의 주장은, 회사가 커질수록 역사적으로 프로덕트(product)의 중요성이 낮아졌다는 거였어요. 회사에서 칭찬받는 사람들은 마케팅(marketing), 영업(sales), 재무(finance) 같은 사람들이죠. 그리고 회사가 혁신을 멈추면 이 사람들이 성장(growth)의 엔진이라고 여겨지는데, 사실은 성장을 만들어낸다기보다 비용 절감(cost-cutting)으로 조직을 굴리는 쪽이에요.
text_zh: 他的观点是，公司规模越大，产品就越不重要了。公司里受到重视的都是做市场的、跑销售的、搞财务的人。如果一个公司不再创新了，那增长就只能靠这些了——销售、市场营销，财务虽然不能带来增长，但至少能控制成本。
text_es: Y su argumento era que mientras más grande se vuelve una empresa, históricamente el producto va perdiendo importancia. La gente que celebraban en la compañía eran los de marketing, los de ventas, los de finanzas. Si una empresa deja de innovar, estos son los motores de crecimiento. Ventas, marketing, o bueno, con finanzas no es crecimiento, sino recortar costos.
fullContext: Lenny asks about insights from Steve Jobs's lost interview documentary. Marty explains Jobs's theory about why companies lose their product innovation edge as they grow. According to Jobs, as companies get larger and stop innovating, the focus shifts from product development to other functions like sales, marketing, and finance, which become the primary drivers of business results. These non-product functions then gain more influence and recognition within the company.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating new ideas, products, or methods that improve efficiency or effectiveness. It often involves the application of creative thinking to solve problems or meet market demands.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, innovation is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and driving growth, often leading to the development of new products or services that meet evolving consumer needs.

insight.nuance: While 'innovation' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply risk and uncertainty, especially when it involves significant changes to existing processes or products.

vocabulary.definition: Key drivers or mechanisms that propel a business or economy forward, often through increased productivity, sales, or market expansion. These engines can include innovation, effective marketing, and strong sales strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startup and corporate environments, identifying and leveraging engines for growth is essential for scaling operations and achieving long-term success.

insight.nuance: The phrase suggests a proactive approach to growth, emphasizing the need for dynamic strategies rather than passive reliance on existing success.

vocabulary.definition: Widely recognized and praised for achievements or contributions, often in a public or formal context. It implies a level of admiration and respect from peers or the industry.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, celebrated individuals or teams are often highlighted in company communications and marketing materials, serving as examples of excellence and success that can inspire others.

insight.nuance: While 'celebrated' carries a positive connotation, it can also imply that the focus is on recognition rather than substantive contributions, particularly in hierarchical organizations.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to events or trends that have occurred in the past and have shaped the current state of affairs. It often implies a consideration of how past actions influence present circumstances.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business analysis, understanding historical trends is vital for making informed decisions, forecasting future performance, and recognizing patterns that can impact strategy.

insight.nuance: The term can suggest a critical examination of past practices, which may be necessary for learning and improvement, but it should be used carefully to avoid implying that past failures dictate future outcomes.

speaker: Marty Cagan
text: And he called it the disease of the stakeholders, of the managers, where they think that an idea is 90% of the work. And that's how he called it out. And he's like, 'They don't understand. The idea is minor.
keySentence: The idea is minor.
text_ko: 그는 그걸 이해관계자들이나 관리자들이 가진 병이라고 불렀어요. 그 사람들이 아이디어가 일의 90%라고 생각한다고 꼬집었죠. '그들은 모르는 거야. 아이디어는 사소해. 아이디어는 그냥 시작일 뿐이야.'라고 말했고, '아이디어에서 제품으로 가는 전체적인 장인정신'이라고 했던 것 같아요. 이게 우리가 제품 발견(product discovery)이라고 부르는 거예요.
text_zh: 他把这个叫做利益相关者和管理层的通病，就是他们觉得有了想法就等于完成了90%的工作。他就是这么说的。他说："他们根本不懂，想法其实很次要，想法只是个开始而已。"我记得他说过："从想法到产品这整个打磨过程才是关键。"这就是我们说的产品探索(product discovery)。
text_es: Y él le puso "la enfermedad de los stakeholders, de los managers", donde piensan que una idea es el 90% del trabajo. Así lo describió. Y decía: "No entienden. La idea es lo de menos. La idea es solo para empezar." Creo que dijo algo como "Todo el arte de llevar una idea hasta convertirla en producto." A eso le llamamos product discovery.
fullContext: Lenny asks about executives who believe they know exactly what to build without going through discovery processes. Marty references Steve Jobs's insights about management diseases, specifically the misconception that having an idea represents most of the work in product development. Jobs emphasized that ideas are just starting points, and the real work lies in the craftsmanship of transforming ideas into successful products through what is now called product discovery.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or groups that have an interest in or are affected by a company's operations and decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, stakeholders can include employees, customers, investors, suppliers, and the community, all of whom can influence or be influenced by the company's success.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a sense of responsibility and involvement, suggesting that their needs and perspectives should be considered in decision-making processes.

vocabulary.definition: Systematic methods used to identify, explore, and validate new ideas, opportunities, or solutions within a business context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and innovation-driven companies, discovery processes are crucial for developing products or services that meet market needs and for minimizing risks associated with new ventures.

insight.nuance: This term often emphasizes the iterative nature of exploration and learning, distinguishing it from more linear project management approaches.

vocabulary.definition: Metaphorical terms used to describe common pitfalls or ineffective practices in management that hinder organizational performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, management diseases can manifest as poor communication, lack of vision, or overemphasis on ideas without execution, leading to stagnation or failure.

insight.nuance: The phrase carries a negative connotation, suggesting that these issues are pervasive and detrimental to the health of an organization.

vocabulary.definition: Of lesser importance, significance, or impact compared to other elements or factors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, labeling an idea as minor suggests that it should not be the primary focus or that it lacks the weight necessary to drive significant outcomes.

insight.nuance: The term can sometimes downplay the potential value of an idea, so it should be used carefully to avoid dismissing contributions that may have merit.

speaker: Matt Abrahams
text: You actually have to prepare to be spontaneous. And that's counterintuitive, but when you think about it in athletics or jazz music, it's like of course you would prepare and practice.
keySentence: Prepare to be spontaneous is counterintuitive but essential for success.
text_ko: 사실 즉흥적(spontaneous)이 되려면 미리 준비해야 해요. 직관에 어긋나는(counterintuitive) 말이긴 하지만, 운동이나 재즈 음악을 생각해 보면 당연히 준비하고 연습하잖아요.
text_zh: 其实你得为即兴发挥做准备，这听起来挺矛盾的，但你想想体育或者爵士乐，当然要提前准备和练习啊。
text_es: En realidad tienes que prepararte para ser espontáneo. Y sí, suena contradictorio, pero si lo piensas en el deporte o en el jazz, pues claro que te vas a preparar y practicar.
fullContext: Lenny points out that most public speaking we do is on the spot rather than prepared talks. Matt responds by explaining one of the fundamental principles for getting better at spontaneous speaking. He argues that while it seems contradictory, you must actually prepare in order to be effective when speaking spontaneously, just like athletes and jazz musicians practice extensively to perform well in unpredictable situations.

vocabulary.definition: Contrary to what one would intuitively expect; something that goes against common sense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a counterintuitive strategy may involve taking risks that seem illogical but can lead to innovative solutions or competitive advantages.

insight.nuance: This term is often used to describe ideas or strategies that challenge conventional wisdom, making it important to provide justification for their effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: Essential or foundational; forming a necessary base or core of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding fundamental principles is crucial in business, as they guide decision-making and strategy development.

insight.nuance: While 'fundamental' often refers to basic concepts, it can also imply a deeper significance in the context of business strategies or values.

vocabulary.definition: To make ready or equip oneself for a specific purpose or event.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, preparation is vital for successful project management, ensuring that teams are equipped with the necessary resources and knowledge.

insight.nuance: While 'prepare' generally implies a proactive approach, it can also suggest a level of anticipation for unforeseen challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Occurring as a result of a sudden inner impulse or inclination; not planned or premeditated.
vocabulary.businessContext: Spontaneous decision-making can sometimes lead to creative breakthroughs in brainstorming sessions, but it may also risk inconsistency in business operations.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation of creativity and innovation, but in a business context, it should be balanced with strategic planning.

speaker: Matt Abrahams
text: Strive for connection over perfection by daring to be dull. Just answer the question. Just give the feedback. Just be engaged in the small talk.
keySentence: Strive for connection over perfection by daring to be dull and engaging.
text_ko: 완벽함보다 연결을 목표로 하세요. 지루해지는 걸 감수할 용기를 내보세요. 그냥 질문에 답하세요. 그냥 피드백을 주세요. 그냥 가벼운 잡담에 참여하세요. 그러면 자기평가의 소음을 낮추고, 그 여유를 진짜 성공에 도움이 되는 일에 쓸 수 있어요.
text_zh: 与其追求完美，不如专注建立联系，敢于做个"普通人"。问什么答什么，该给反馈就给反馈，闲聊的时候就好好参与进去。这样做能让你不那么纠结自己的表现，把精力真正用在能让你成功的事情上。
text_es: Busca conectar en lugar de ser perfecto, y atrévete a ser aburrido. Simplemente responde la pregunta. Simplemente da el feedback. Simplemente participa en la plática casual. Al hacer eso, reduces la autocrítica mental, liberando energía que puedes usar para realmente tener éxito.
fullContext: Lenny asks about techniques for calming anxiety when speaking. Matt explains his "dare to be dull" concept, which comes from improvisation. He argues that when we try to be perfect in communication, we waste mental bandwidth on self-evaluation rather than focusing on connecting with our audience and delivering our message effectively.

vocabulary.definition: To make a great effort to achieve or attain something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'strive for' often refers to the pursuit of goals such as excellence, innovation, or customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of determination and ambition, and is typically used in motivational contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Involved or participating actively in an activity or conversation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, being 'engaged' often refers to employees who are emotionally invested in their work and contribute positively to team dynamics.

insight.nuance: While 'engaged' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply a superficial level of involvement if not paired with genuine interest.

vocabulary.definition: Information or criticism about a person's performance or work, intended to guide future improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, feedback is crucial for employee development, performance reviews, and enhancing team collaboration.

insight.nuance: Feedback can be constructive or critical; it's important to deliver it thoughtfully to foster a positive response.

vocabulary.definition: A relationship or link between people or concepts, often characterized by mutual understanding or shared interests.
vocabulary.businessContext: In networking and business development, establishing a strong connection can lead to collaborations, partnerships, and increased opportunities.
