text_ko: 어떤 사람들은 전환율(conversion rate)에만 신경 쓰면서 "이걸 정말 깔끔하게 만들 거야"라고 해요. 그건 좋아요, 어느 정도 성장도 얻고요. 하지만 추천(recommendation)까지 가려면 사용자를 완전히 놀라게 해야 해요. 이전에는 그런 게 가능하다고도 생각하지 못했던 경험을 줘야 해요. 그리고 아무도 해본 적 없는 걸 해냈을 때 비로소 그게 따라와요.
text_zh: 有些人就盯着转化率(conversion rate)，想着"我要把这个做得特别特别炫"。这也挺好的，能带来一些增长。但是要想让用户主动推荐你，那就得让他们彻底震撼到。你得给他们一种他们以前想都想不到的体验。当你做出了前无古人的东西时，那就对了。
text_es: Hay gente que se enfoca solo en la tasa de conversión, como "voy a hacer esto súper pulido y elegante." Y está bien, logras crecer un poco más. Pero para llegar a que te recomienden, tienes que dejar a tus usuarios completamente impresionados (blow their socks off). Tienes que darles una experiencia que ni sabían que era posible. Y cuando estás en ese punto de hacer algo que nadie ha hecho antes, ahí es cuando lo logras.
fullContext: Lenny is discussing with Nilan how to drive word-of-mouth growth for products. Nilan is explaining that most teams stop when their product simply works, or they focus on incremental improvements like conversion rate optimization. However, to get customers to actively recommend your product to others, you need to exceed their expectations dramatically. He argues that you must create experiences that customers never knew were possible before - essentially doing something completely new rather than just improving existing solutions.

vocabulary.definition: The percentage of users who take a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a newsletter, out of the total number of visitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, conversion rate is a critical metric used to evaluate the effectiveness of marketing strategies and user experience design.

insight.nuance: While a high conversion rate indicates successful user engagement, it is important to also consider the quality of the conversions and customer satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: Small, gradual enhancements made to a product, service, or process over time, rather than large, radical changes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech environments, incremental improvements are often employed in agile methodologies to refine offerings based on user feedback and performance metrics.

insight.nuance: This approach emphasizes continuous development and adaptability, contrasting with disruptive innovation that seeks to overhaul existing systems.

vocabulary.definition: A suggestion or endorsement made by an individual or organization, often based on personal experience or expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, recommendations can significantly influence consumer behavior, often driving sales and fostering brand loyalty through trust and credibility.

insight.nuance: Recommendations carry weight when they stem from genuine experiences, making them more impactful than mere advertisements.

vocabulary.definition: A marketing phenomenon where customers share their positive experiences with a product or service, leading to organic growth through personal referrals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, word-of-mouth growth is often a key strategy for scaling, as it relies on authentic customer advocacy rather than paid advertising.

insight.nuance: This type of growth is highly valued for its cost-effectiveness and credibility, though it can be unpredictable and relies heavily on customer satisfaction.

speaker: Nilan Peiris
text: So building a brand led money transfer business, the brand's got to be pretty damn good, right? You're going to feel pretty special afterwards, in order to have less money afterwards.
keySentence: the brand's got to be pretty damn good, right?
text_ko: 그래서 브랜드 주도형 송금 비즈니스(brand-led money transfer business)를 만들려면 브랜드가 정말 좋아야 해요, 그렇죠? 결국 돈이 줄어들 텐데도 사람들이 '나 특별하네'라고 느껴야 하니까요. 그래서 우리가 항상 찾는 건 어떤 채널(channels)이 엄청 확장 가능(scalable)하고 전체 고객층(audience)에 닿을 수 있으면서 배포 비용(distribution cost)이 아주 낮은지예요.
text_zh: 所以要做品牌驱动的转账业务，这个品牌得相当牛才行，对吧？用户花了钱之后还得觉得特别值，钱虽然少了但心里美滋滋的。所以我们一直在找的就是，哪些渠道既能大规模推广，又能覆盖我们所有的目标用户，但是推广成本还特别低。
text_es: Entonces, para construir un negocio de transferencias de dinero basado en marca, la marca tiene que estar súper buena, ¿no? El cliente se tiene que sentir muy especial después, para justificar que se quede con menos dinero. Así que lo que siempre buscamos es qué canales por ahí son súper escalables, que puedan llegar a toda nuestra audiencia, pero que tengan un costo de distribución increíblemente bajo.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the biggest shift that helped Wise grow word-of-mouth significantly. Nilan explains why word-of-mouth was essential for Wise's business model. Since money is the ultimate commodity and customers end up with less money after using any money transfer service, building a brand-led business in this space requires an exceptionally good customer experience. He's outlining the challenge of finding marketing channels that can scale broadly while having very low distribution costs, which led them to focus on word-of-mouth growth.

vocabulary.definition: A brand is a unique name, symbol, or design that identifies and differentiates a product or service from others in the market. It encompasses the perceptions and experiences associated with a company or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strong brand can lead to customer loyalty, higher perceived value, and competitive advantage, making it a crucial element for startups and established companies alike.

insight.nuance: While 'brand' often refers to the visual identity, it also implies the emotional connection and reputation a company builds over time.

vocabulary.definition: Money transfer refers to the process of sending funds from one individual or entity to another, often facilitated by financial institutions or digital platforms. It can occur domestically or internationally.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the fintech sector, money transfer services are critical for enabling seamless transactions, especially in global markets where traditional banking may be less accessible.

insight.nuance: The term can imply various methods, including electronic transfers, wire transfers, or remittances, and is often associated with speed and security.

vocabulary.definition: Word-of-mouth refers to the informal communication of information about a product or service from person to person, often based on personal experiences and recommendations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing, word-of-mouth is a powerful tool for building brand awareness and trust, as consumers often rely on peer recommendations over traditional advertising.

insight.nuance: While it can be a positive force for a brand, negative word-of-mouth can also spread quickly and harm a company's reputation.

vocabulary.definition: A business model outlines how a company creates, delivers, and captures value, detailing the revenue streams, customer segments, and operational structure.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding and articulating a business model is essential for startups to attract investors and for established companies to adapt to changing market conditions.

insight.nuance: The term can imply various frameworks, such as subscription-based, freemium, or direct sales, and is critical for strategic planning.

speaker: Nilan Peiris
text: We only got the advocacy when we were eight to 10 times cheaper. That's when people started talking about it. So the bar is all the way up there. And to put that in context, that means figuring out how to move money instantly.
keySentence: Advocacy only emerged when we were all the way down to 0.35.
text_ko: 우리는 가격이 8~10배쯤 더 낮았을 때만 고객들의 지지(advocacy)를 얻었어요. 그때야 사람들이 입소문을 내기 시작했죠. 그래서 기준이 훨씬 높아졌어요. 좀 더 풀어 말하면, 돈을 즉시 옮기는 방법(move money instantly)을 찾아야 한다는 뜻이에요. 즉 단가를 6에서 0.35까지 완전히 낮추는 방법을 찾아야 해요.
text_zh: 只有当我们的价格便宜了8到10倍的时候，才真正赢得了用户的支持。那时候大家才开始议论我们。所以说这个门槛是相当高的。具体来说就是，我们得想办法实现瞬时转账，还得把价格从6块钱一路降到3毛5。
text_es: Solo conseguimos que la gente nos recomendara cuando éramos 8 o 10 veces más baratos. Ahí fue cuando empezaron a hablar de nosotros. O sea, el listón está súper alto. Y para que te hagas una idea de lo que significa esto, hablamos de conseguir que el dinero se mueva al instante. Hablamos de bajar el precio desde seis hasta 0.35.
fullContext: Nilan is explaining a key insight about driving word-of-mouth for Wise. When entering new markets, they discovered that being marginally better (like pricing at 5.9% versus competitors at 6%) would get customers to use their service, but wouldn't generate recommendations. Only when they achieved dramatically better pricing - 8 to 10 times cheaper than alternatives - did customers become evangelical and start talking about the product. This taught them that the bar for recommendation is extremely high, requiring breakthrough improvements rather than incremental ones.

vocabulary.definition: Advocacy refers to the act of supporting or promoting a cause or proposal, often through persuasive communication and action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, advocacy can involve lobbying for policy changes, promoting a product, or rallying support from stakeholders to influence decision-making.

insight.nuance: While advocacy is generally positive, it can sometimes carry a connotation of bias or partisanship, so it's important to ensure that the support is based on sound reasoning and evidence.

vocabulary.definition: Context refers to the circumstances or background information surrounding a particular event, situation, or concept that helps to clarify its meaning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, providing context is crucial for understanding market trends, customer behavior, or the rationale behind strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a broader perspective, so it's important to use it when the surrounding details significantly affect interpretation or understanding.

vocabulary.definition: Marginally means to a small extent or degree; it indicates a slight difference or change.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business analysis, marginally is often used to describe incremental improvements in performance metrics, costs, or market share that may not be significant but are still noteworthy.

insight.nuance: This term can imply that while changes are present, they may not be impactful enough to warrant major strategic shifts or decisions.

vocabulary.definition: Drive refers to the motivation or force that propels individuals or organizations to achieve goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, drive can be associated with leadership, innovation, and the pursuit of growth, often reflecting a company's culture and ambition.

insight.nuance: While drive is generally seen as a positive trait, it can also suggest a relentless pursuit that may overlook important ethical considerations or team dynamics.

speaker: Nilan Peiris
text: It's this thing around growth rate. So, especially product net growth, which is what we're talking about. So you can imagine, we're going to open a new market to Indonesia, and the fastest way to do it is to take...
keySentence: the fastest way to do it is to take...
text_ko: 바로 성장률(growth rate)에 관한 얘기예요. 특히 우리가 말하는 건 제품 순성장(product net growth)이구요. 예를 들어 우리가 인도네시아 시장을 새로 열려 한다고 하면, 가장 빠른 방법은… 이미 누군가가 인도네시아로 진출하는 방법을 알아냈잖아요. 그 인프라를 가져다가 우리 서비스에 붙이면, '이건 할 수 있겠다' 해서 사용자 몇 명은 얻을 수 있어요. 근데 그게 하키스틱(hockey stick)처럼 확 폭발적으로 성장하진 않아요.
text_zh: 就是关于增长率的问题。特别是产品净增长，这就是我们在讨论的。你可以想象，我们要进入印尼这个新市场，最快的方式就是找到...别人已经摸清了怎么进入印尼市场。我们拿过来那套基础设施，然后接到Wise平台上，你知道吧？我们确实可以这么做，也能获得一些用户。但是这样不会出现爆发式增长(hockey stick growth)。
text_es: Es esto del ritmo de crecimiento. O sea, especialmente el crecimiento neto del producto, que es de lo que estamos hablando. Entonces te puedes imaginar, vamos a abrir un nuevo mercado en Indonesia, y la forma más rápida de hacerlo es tomar... Alguien más ya se las ingenió para entrar a Indonesia. Tomamos esa infraestructura, y la conectamos a Wise, ¿sabes qué? Podemos hacer esto, vamos a conseguir algunos usuarios. Pero no crece como palo de hockey (hockey stick).
fullContext: Lenny asks about common mistakes people make when trying to drive word-of-mouth growth. Nilan explains a key misstep that many companies, including Wise, have made. When entering new markets, the tempting shortcut is to use existing infrastructure solutions that others have already built - for example, plugging into existing money transfer systems for Indonesia. While this approach can quickly acquire some users, it doesn't create the exponential growth curve needed for strong word-of-mouth because it hasn't fundamentally solved the underlying problems customers face.

vocabulary.definition: The percentage increase in a company's revenue, customer base, or market share over a specific period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the growth rate is a critical metric used to assess the performance and potential of a company, especially in evaluating investment opportunities and market strategies.

insight.nuance: While a high growth rate is generally viewed positively, it is important to consider the sustainability of that growth and the context in which it occurs.

vocabulary.definition: The overall increase in a company's size or value after accounting for losses or reductions, such as customer churn or product returns.
vocabulary.businessContext: Net growth is often used to provide a more accurate picture of a company's performance, as it reflects the actual gain after subtracting any losses.

insight.nuance: Net growth can sometimes mask underlying issues if not analyzed alongside gross growth figures, making it essential to consider both metrics.

vocabulary.definition: The process of introducing a product or service to a new geographical area or demographic segment where it has not previously been available.
vocabulary.businessContext: Opening a new market is a strategic move for businesses seeking to expand their customer base and increase revenue, often requiring market research and tailored marketing strategies.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies not just entry into a new market but also the establishment of a presence and the cultivation of customer relationships in that area.

vocabulary.definition: To encourage and facilitate organic promotion of a product or service through customer recommendations and discussions, rather than through paid advertising.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, driving word-of-mouth growth is often seen as a cost-effective marketing strategy that can lead to increased brand loyalty and customer acquisition.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a focus on customer satisfaction and engagement, as positive experiences are crucial for generating genuine word-of-mouth referrals.

speaker: Nilan Peiris
text: So it comes from a very logical place, how do I get users quickly? I can take a shortcut in doing this, but that, you kind of realize is wasted effort. So the step then becomes this much harder question of these types of questions.
keySentence: but that, you kind of realize is wasted effort.
text_ko: 이건 굉장히 논리적인 출발이에요. '어떻게 하면 사용자들을 빨리 모을 수 있을까?'에서 시작하죠. 지름길을 써서 해볼 수도 있는데, 그게 결국엔 쓸데없는 수고였다는 걸 깨닫게 돼요. 그래서 다음 단계는 훨씬 더 어려운 질문들로 옮겨가요. 예를 들어, 시장에 자금을 유입시키는 데(moving money into a market)의 이론상 최소 비용(theoretical minimum cost)은 얼마일까? 이론상 최대 속도(theoretical maximum speed)는 어느 정도일까?
text_zh: 所以这个想法其实很合理，就是我怎么能快速获客？我可以走捷径，但后来你会发现这其实是白费功夫。然后问题就变成了更难回答的那种，比如说，把资金投入市场的理论最低成本是多少？理论上的最高速度又是什么？
text_es: Entonces viene de un lugar muy lógico, ¿cómo consigo usuarios rápido? Puedo tomar un atajo para hacer esto, pero eso, te das cuenta de que es esfuerzo perdido. Entonces el paso se convierte en esta pregunta mucho más difícil, este tipo de preguntas. Como ¿cuál es el costo teórico mínimo para mover dinero a un mercado? ¿Cuál es la velocidad teórica máxima?
fullContext: Continuing his explanation about avoiding shortcuts in product development, Nilan describes how teams naturally want to find quick wins to acquire users rapidly. However, he learned that these shortcuts ultimately represent wasted effort because they don't create the transformative experiences needed for word-of-mouth growth. Instead, teams should ask fundamental questions about the theoretical limits of what's possible - like the absolute minimum cost or maximum speed achievable - and work backwards from those ideals rather than making incremental improvements.

vocabulary.definition: A quicker or more direct route to achieve a goal or complete a task, often bypassing standard procedures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, taking a shortcut may refer to using less rigorous methods to achieve results faster, which can sometimes compromise quality or thoroughness.

insight.nuance: While shortcuts can save time, they may lead to incomplete solutions or future complications, so they should be used judiciously.

vocabulary.definition: Exertion or resources spent on a task that yields little to no productive outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, wasted effort often refers to time and resources that could have been better allocated to more impactful projects or strategies.

insight.nuance: This phrase carries a negative connotation, suggesting inefficiency and lack of foresight in planning or execution.

vocabulary.definition: To gain possession of something, typically through effort, purchase, or learning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, acquiring can refer to obtaining assets, companies, or knowledge that enhance capabilities or market position.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a strategic intention behind the gain, such as growth or competitive advantage.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by clear, sound reasoning or consistent principles that lead to rational conclusions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, logical thinking is crucial for decision-making, problem-solving, and strategic planning, ensuring that actions are based on evidence and rationality.

insight.nuance: While 'logical' suggests a rational approach, it may sometimes imply a lack of creativity or emotional consideration in decision-making.

speaker: Nilan Peiris
text: You can't split test your way to love. So, this experiment led product management approach, where you throw a bunch of things on the wall, and then you kind of see what sticks, and generally we don't advocate this.
keySentence: You can't split test your way to love.
text_ko: A/B 테스트(A/B test)만으로 사용자의 '사랑'을 얻을 수는 없어요. 그래서 여러 가지를 닥치는 대로 시도해 보고 뭐가 통하는지 보는 실험 주도형 제품 관리 접근법(experiment-led product management)은 보통 추천하지 않아요. 물론 어느 정도 그런 일이 일어나긴 하지만, 전반적으로 권장하지 않아요. 주된 이유는 엔지니어링(engineering)이 비용이 많이 들고, 고객에게 정말 중요한 게 무엇인지는 다른 방법으로도 충분히 파악할 수 있기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 你不能靠A/B测试来获得用户的喜爱。所以说，这种实验导向的产品管理方式，就是往墙上扔一堆东西，然后看看哪个能粘住，我们一般不太推荐这么做。当然了，这种情况肯定会有一些，但总的来说我们不建议这样。主要是因为开发成本很高，而且你其实可以通过别的方式来搞清楚客户真正在意什么。
text_es: No puedes hacer A/B testing para conseguir que la gente se enamore de tu producto. Entonces, este enfoque experimental en gestión de producto, donde lanzas un montón de cosas a ver qué funciona, pues en general no lo recomendamos. Obvio que algo de esto siempre pasa, pero por lo general no lo recomendamos. Principalmente porque el desarrollo es caro, y en realidad puedes averiguar qué les importa a los clientes por otros medios.
fullContext: Lenny and Nilan are discussing Wise's approach to product development and experimentation. Nilan is explaining why Wise doesn't rely heavily on A/B testing and experiment-driven product management. He argues that constantly running experiments to see what works is ineffective for building products that customers will love and recommend. Instead of this "throw things at the wall" approach, he advocates for building conviction about what matters to customers through direct customer feedback and insights before building features, since engineering resources are expensive and limited.

vocabulary.definition: The process of overseeing the development, marketing, and lifecycle of a product from conception to market launch and beyond.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product management involves coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure that products meet customer needs and align with business goals.

insight.nuance: While product management focuses on strategic planning and execution, it is often seen as a collaborative role that requires balancing various stakeholder interests.

vocabulary.definition: A methodology that emphasizes the use of experiments to guide decision-making and validate hypotheses.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, an experiment-driven approach is often used to test product features or marketing strategies before full-scale implementation, minimizing risk and optimizing resources.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a reliance on empirical evidence rather than intuition, making it suitable for data-centric environments but potentially limiting in creative or subjective contexts.

vocabulary.definition: To publicly support or recommend a particular cause, policy, or idea.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, advocating for a product or strategy often involves rallying support from stakeholders and influencing decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: While 'advocate' implies strong support, it can also suggest a level of persuasion that may not always be welcomed, especially in contentious discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term 'approach' is often used to describe the strategy taken to achieve goals, whether in project management, marketing, or product development.

insight.nuance: The term can imply flexibility and adaptability, but may also suggest a lack of specificity if not defined clearly.

speaker: Nilan Peiris
text: And closing this delta between what you've done, and what's perceived to be done is what I call product marketing within the product. And that in its own right is a discipline, I've learned.
keySentence: Closing this delta between actions and perceptions is product marketing in its own right.
text_ko: 여러분이 실제로 해놓은 것과 사람들이 해놓은 것으로 인식하는 것 사이의 격차를 줄이는 것이 제가 말하는 제품 안에서의 프로덕트 마케팅(product marketing within the product)이에요. 그리고 그게 그 자체로 하나의 전문 분야라는 걸 배웠어요.
text_zh: 要缩小你实际做的事情和别人认为你做的事情之间的差距，我把这叫做产品内的产品营销(product marketing within the product)。我发现这本身就是一门学问。
text_es: Y cerrar esa brecha entre lo que realmente has hecho y lo que se percibe que has hecho es lo que yo llamo marketing del producto dentro del producto. Y eso por sí solo es toda una disciplina, he aprendido.
fullContext: Nilan is sharing insights about a breakthrough that 3x'd their referral sharing rates. He discovered that customers were getting great value from Wise but weren't fully aware of how much value they were receiving. For example, customers saved money but didn't believe the actual savings amount, or received instant transfers without realizing they were instant. The key was creating visual comparisons and animations within the product to help customers understand the true value they received, which then made them more likely to share with others.

vocabulary.definition: The process of reducing the gap between the current state and the desired state in a project or initiative.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'closing the delta' often refers to aligning actual performance with expected outcomes, particularly in product development and marketing strategies.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies a proactive approach to addressing discrepancies, and is best used in discussions about performance improvement or strategic alignment.

vocabulary.definition: Regarded or understood in a particular way, often based on subjective interpretation rather than objective reality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, 'perceived' is crucial as it influences customer attitudes and behaviors toward products or services.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a connotation of subjectivity, suggesting that perceptions may not always align with facts, making it important to clarify the distinction in discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A field of study or a branch of knowledge, often characterized by a systematic approach to learning and practice.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'discipline' refers to the structured methodologies and practices that guide teams in achieving goals, such as product marketing or project management.

insight.nuance: While it can refer to a specific area of expertise, it also implies a level of rigor and commitment to standards, making it suitable for discussions about professional development.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something, often assessed in terms of benefits relative to costs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'value' is a key concept that drives decision-making, influencing pricing strategies, customer satisfaction, and competitive positioning.

insight.nuance: This term can refer to both tangible and intangible benefits, and is often used in discussions about customer perception and product differentiation.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: I went to Alibaba and I bought myself one of these flip phones from China like we used to have in the 1990s with no apps, no internet connection.
keySentence: I bought myself one of these flip phones from China like we used to have in the 1990s with no apps, no internet connection.
text_ko: 알리바바에 가서 1990년대에 쓰던 것처럼 중국산 플립폰(flip phone) 하나를 샀어요. 앱(apps)도 없고 인터넷 연결(internet connection)도 안 되는 그런 거예요. 그리고 이베이(eBay)에서 워드 프로세서(word processor)를 하나 구해서 그냥 앉아서 글만 쓰고 중요한 일만 하려고 했어요. 그런데 기술을 다 끊고 앱도 다 지웠는데도 책상에 앉으면 "아, 맞다, 내가 좀 조사해보려고 했던 그 책이 있지"라든가 "책상만 좀 치울까", "쓰레기라도 버려야겠다" 같은 생각이 자꾸 들더라고요.
text_zh: 我去阿里巴巴上给自己买了个中国产的翻盖手机，就像我们90年代用的那种，没有任何应用，也连不上网。然后我又在eBay上买了台文字处理器，这样我就能专心坐下来写东西，做真正重要的事。但是你知道吗，就算我不用那些科技产品了，就算我把所有应用都删了，我坐在桌子前还是会想："哎，对了，有本书我一直想查点资料"，或者"让我先把桌子收拾一下"，再不就是"我应该去倒个垃圾"。
text_es: Me metí a Alibaba y me compré uno de esos teléfonos de tapa de China como los que teníamos en los noventa, sin aplicaciones ni conexión a internet. Y después me conseguí un procesador de textos en eBay para poder sentarme tranquilo a escribir y hacer lo importante. Pero incluso cuando dejé de usar toda la tecnología, cuando me deshice de todas las apps, me sentaba en mi escritorio y decía: "Ah, ¿sabes qué? Ahí está ese libro en el que quería investigar algo", o "Déjame ordenar el escritorio rapidito", o "¿Sabes qué? Debería sacar la basura".
fullContext: Lenny asks Nir about his personal experience with distraction and what techniques he tried. Nir explains how he attempted to solve his distraction problem by completely removing technology from his environment - buying a basic flip phone and an old word processor. However, he discovered that even without any digital distractions, he still found ways to procrastinate and avoid the important work he needed to do. This led him to realize that the root cause of distraction isn't external technology, but internal discomfort.

vocabulary.definition: A distraction is anything that diverts attention away from a primary task or focus. It can be an external stimulus or an internal thought that interrupts concentration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, distractions can significantly reduce productivity and hinder team collaboration, especially in environments that require deep focus and innovation.

insight.nuance: While distractions can sometimes lead to creative breakthroughs, they are generally viewed negatively in professional contexts where efficiency is paramount.

vocabulary.definition: Technology refers to the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry, encompassing tools, machines, and systems designed to solve problems or enhance efficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, technology is a critical driver of innovation, enabling companies to streamline operations, improve customer experiences, and gain competitive advantages.

insight.nuance: While technology is often associated with modern advancements, it can also refer to traditional tools and methods, making it important to specify the context when discussing its implications.

vocabulary.definition: A connection is a relationship or link between two or more entities, which can be physical, emotional, or digital in nature. It often implies a sense of engagement or interaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, connections are vital for networking, collaboration, and building partnerships that can lead to new opportunities and growth.

insight.nuance: The term can carry different weights depending on the context, such as a personal connection versus a professional one, and is often used to emphasize the importance of relationships in achieving success.

vocabulary.definition: Experience refers to the knowledge or skill acquired through practical involvement in a particular activity or event over time. It encompasses both personal and professional encounters.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, experience is highly valued as it often translates into expertise, influencing hiring decisions and the effectiveness of leadership within organizations.

insight.nuance: While experience is generally seen as beneficial, it can also imply a resistance to change if individuals become overly reliant on past practices rather than adapting to new trends.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: identify what is that internal trigger... that is the source of 90% of our distractions... it's just a feeling... it's just an emotion.
keySentence: identify what is that internal trigger... that is the source of 90% of our distractions...
text_ko: 그래서 제가 제 자신에게 적용한 방법이자 이런 상황에 처한 누구에게나 권하고 싶은 건요, 항상 그 내적 트리거(internal trigger)가 뭔지, 주의가 산만해질 때 벗어나고 싶게 만드는 그 근질거림이 뭔지 먼저 찾아보라는 거예요. 사실 우리의 산만함(distraction)의 90%는 바로 거기서 오거든요. 핑·딩·벨소리 같은 알림음 때문이 아니라 그 감정 때문이에요. 그런데 제게는 그게 오히려 엄청난 힘이 되는 깨달음이에요. '잠깐, 그냥 느낌이구나'라고 인지하면 모든 게 달라지거든요. 그러면 미리 쓸 도구들을 준비해 두고, 불편함이 느껴지자마자 꺼내 쓸 대응책들—비유하자면 화살통에 화살을 담아두는 것처럼—을 갖춰둘 수 있어요.
text_zh: 所以，我自己的做法，也是我建议任何遇到这种情况的人去做的，就是一定要搞清楚那个内在触发点(internal trigger)是什么，就是当你分心的时候，你到底想逃避的那种心里痒痒的感觉是什么，因为这才是我们90%分心的根源。不是那些手机的叮咚响声，而是我们内心的感受。但对我来说，这个发现特别有力量，因为一旦你意识到，"等等，这就是一种感觉而已。"就这么简单，就是一种情绪罢了。那你就可以准备好各种应对工具了。你可以在箭袋里准备好各种箭，一感觉到不舒服就马上拿出来用。
text_es: Entonces, lo que he adoptado para mí y lo que le recomendaría a cualquiera que se encuentre en esta situación es siempre identificar cuál es ese disparador interno (internal trigger), cuál es esa comezón de la que estás tratando de escapar cuando te distraes, porque esa es la fuente del 90% de nuestras distracciones. No son los pitidos, timbres y sonidos. Son los sentimientos. Pero para mí, eso es increíblemente empoderador porque una vez que te das cuenta de que "Oye, espera, es solo un sentimiento." Eso es todo, es solo una emoción. Entonces puedes tener herramientas listas para usar. Puedes tener flechas en tu aljaba (quiver) preparadas para sacar en cuanto sientes esa incomodidad.
fullContext: Nir continues explaining his discovery about the true source of distraction. He reveals that research shows 90% of distractions come from internal triggers (emotions like boredom, anxiety, or discomfort) rather than external triggers like notifications. He emphasizes that understanding this is empowering because emotions are temporary and manageable. The 'arrows in your quiver' metaphor refers to having multiple strategies prepared to handle uncomfortable feelings when they arise, rather than escaping them through distraction.

vocabulary.definition: An internal trigger refers to a psychological or emotional stimulus that prompts a specific response or behavior within an individual. It often relates to feelings or thoughts that initiate actions, particularly in the context of habits or decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, understanding internal triggers can help organizations design products or marketing strategies that resonate with users' emotional states, thereby enhancing user engagement and retention.

insight.nuance: While 'internal trigger' often implies a personal or psychological aspect, it is important to differentiate it from external triggers, which are environmental or situational stimuli.

vocabulary.definition: Distraction is the process of diverting attention away from a primary task or focus, often resulting in reduced productivity or effectiveness. It can stem from internal thoughts or external stimuli.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, distractions can significantly impact employee performance and efficiency, prompting businesses to implement strategies that minimize interruptions and enhance concentration.

insight.nuance: Distraction can have both negative and positive connotations; while it typically refers to an unwanted diversion, some distractions can foster creativity or provide necessary breaks.

vocabulary.definition: A source is the origin or starting point from which something derives or is obtained. It can refer to information, materials, or causes that lead to a particular outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying the source of problems or opportunities is crucial for effective decision-making and strategic planning, as it allows organizations to address root causes rather than symptoms.

insight.nuance: The term 'source' can imply reliability or credibility, particularly in contexts involving information or data; thus, it is essential to evaluate the trustworthiness of a source.

vocabulary.definition: Emotion is a complex psychological state that encompasses subjective experience, physiological response, and behavioral or expressive response. It plays a significant role in influencing human behavior and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding emotions can enhance customer relations, marketing strategies, and team dynamics, as emotional intelligence is key to effective leadership and communication.

insight.nuance: While 'emotion' generally refers to feelings, it can carry different weights depending on context; for instance, in negotiations, emotions can be both a powerful motivator and a potential source of conflict.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: What I tell myself is, "Okay, I'm just going to wait 10 minutes before I check email, before I scroll social media, before I Google something that is just trying to procrastinate doing the work." I can do that. I'm a grown man.
keySentence: I'm just going to wait 10 minutes before I check email, before I scroll social media, before I Google something that is just trying to procrastinate doing the work.
text_ko: 저는 스스로에게 이렇게 말해요. "좋아, 이메일 확인하기 전에, 소셜 미디어를 스크롤하기 전에, 일을 미루려고 뭔가를 구글링하기 전에 10분만 기다리자." 그 정도는 할 수 있어요. 전 어른이고 제가 하고 싶은 건 할 수 있죠. 10분이면 충분해요. 그래서 그 10분 동안 제가 할 일은 지금 하던 일로 돌아가거나 글쓰기로 다시 집중하거나, 아니면 충동을 관찰하기(urge surfing)를 하는 것뿐이에요. 그건 그 느낌을 그냥 겪으면서, "아, 이건 힘든 일이구나. 괜찮아. 그래서 답답하고 지루하고 불안한 거구나." 하고 인정하는 거예요.
text_zh: 我就跟自己说："好吧，我先等十分钟再去看邮件，再去刷社交媒体，再去谷歌搜那些其实就是在拖延正事的东西。"这个我能做到。我是个成年人了，想做什么都行，十分钟后再做这些也没问题。所以在这十分钟里，我就做两件事：要么回到手头的活儿，继续写东西；要么就让这种冲动过去，就是感受一下这种感觉，然后承认："你知道吗？这活儿确实不好干，没关系的。所以我才会觉得烦躁，觉得无聊，觉得焦虑。"
text_es: Lo que me digo es: "Bueno, voy a esperar 10 minutos antes de revisar el email, antes de meterme a redes sociales, antes de buscar algo en Google que solo es para procrastinar y no hacer el trabajo." Eso sí puedo hacerlo. Soy un adulto. Puedo hacer lo que quiera. Puedo esperar 10 minutos. Entonces, durante esos 10 minutos, lo único que tengo que hacer es volver a la tarea, regresar a escribir, o aguantar el impulso, que simplemente es sentir esa sensación y reconocer: "¿Sabes qué? Este trabajo está difícil. No pasa nada. Por eso me siento frustrado. Por eso me siento aburrido. Por eso me siento ansioso."
fullContext: Nir explains his '10-minute rule' technique for managing distraction urges. When he feels tempted to check social media or email instead of doing important work, he sets a timer for 10 minutes and tells himself he can do those distracting activities after the timer goes off - but not yet. During those 10 minutes, he either returns to his intended task or 'surfs the urge' by acknowledging and experiencing the uncomfortable emotion without trying to escape it. This technique treats the urge as temporary rather than permanent.

vocabulary.definition: To delay or postpone action or tasks, often by engaging in less urgent activities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, procrastination can lead to missed deadlines and decreased productivity, impacting overall team performance and project timelines.

insight.nuance: While procrastination often carries a negative connotation, it can sometimes be a symptom of deeper issues like burnout or lack of motivation.

vocabulary.definition: To organize, coordinate, and oversee the execution of tasks or operations to achieve specific objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective management is crucial in business for ensuring that resources are utilized efficiently and that teams work cohesively towards common goals.

insight.nuance: The term can imply varying levels of authority and responsibility, from managing a small team to overseeing an entire organization.

vocabulary.definition: An interruption or diversion that prevents focus on a primary task or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, distractions can significantly hinder productivity, leading to errors and inefficiencies in work processes.

insight.nuance: While distractions are often viewed negatively, they can sometimes foster creativity or provide necessary breaks, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: A method or way of doing something, often involving a specific skill or approach to achieve a desired outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, employing effective techniques can enhance problem-solving capabilities and improve efficiency in project execution.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a level of expertise or specialized knowledge, making it more appropriate in professional or academic discussions.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: You can't call something a distraction unless you know what it distracted you from. I'll say that again. You can't call something a distraction unless you know what it distracted you from.
keySentence: You can't call something a distraction without knowing what it distracted you from.
text_ko: 무엇 때문에 주의가 흐트러졌는지 모르면 그걸 산만하다고 부를 수 없어요. 다시 말할게요. 무엇 때문에 주의가 흐트러졌는지 모르면 그걸 산만하다고 부를 수 없어요. 적어도 제 경우엔, "이메일 잠깐만 확인해볼까, 트위터에서 뭐 있는지 잠깐만 볼까" 하고 유혹에 넘어갈 때가 있었는데, 그 이유 중 하나는 스스로에게 "이건 업무 관련이니까 언젠가는 해야 할 일이야"라고 합리화했기 때문이에요. 근데 캘린더에 딱 정해둔 시간이 없으니 계속 "언젠가는 해야 하니까 지금 하는 게 낫지"라고 생각하게 됐던 거예요.
text_zh: 你要是不知道自己本来该干什么，就没资格说别的事情让你分心了。我再说一遍啊，你要是不知道自己本来该干什么，就没资格说别的事情让你分心了。就拿我自己来说吧，以前我总是忍不住想"哎呀，我就快速看一眼邮件，就看一分钟"，或者"我就瞄一眼推特(Twitter)上有什么动态，就一分钟"，其实很大程度上是因为我会给自己找借口，想着"这也算工作相关的事儿嘛，反正早晚得做"，但我日程表上又没专门安排时间来处理这些事，所以就老想着"反正早晚得做，不如现在就做了吧"。
text_es: No puedes decir que algo te distrajo si no sabes de qué te distrajo. Lo voy a repetir. No puedes decir que algo te distrajo si no sabes de qué te distrajo. Entonces, por lo menos en mi caso, cuando caía en el "Ah, déjame revisar el email rapidito, déjame ver qué está pasando en Twitter un momentito," parte de eso era porque me justificaba pensando, "Bueno, esto es algo relacionado con el trabajo. Lo tengo que hacer en algún momento," y como no tenía un horario específico para hacerlo en mi calendario, seguía pensando, "Bueno, lo tengo que hacer en algún momento. Mejor lo hago ahorita."
fullContext: Nir discusses the importance of having a scheduled plan to identify what constitutes distraction versus traction. He explains that without a clear calendar showing what you intended to do at specific times, it becomes easy to justify any work-related activity as productive. The key insight is that even checking work email can be a distraction if it's not what you planned to do during that time block. This justification trap keeps people from focusing on their most important tasks.

vocabulary.definition: A distraction is anything that diverts attention away from a primary focus or task. It can be an external stimulus or an internal thought that interrupts concentration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business environments, distractions can hinder productivity and efficiency, impacting project timelines and team performance. Identifying distractions is crucial for maintaining focus in a fast-paced work setting.

insight.nuance: While distractions are often viewed negatively, they can sometimes lead to creative insights or necessary breaks, making context important in their evaluation.

vocabulary.definition: Traction refers to the progress or momentum gained by a business or project, often measured by user engagement, sales, or market penetration. It indicates the ability to attract and retain customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startup culture, gaining traction is a critical milestone that demonstrates product-market fit and validates the business model, often influencing investment decisions.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a sense of stability and growth, but it can also suggest that a business is still in the early stages of development and may need further validation.

vocabulary.definition: A scheduled plan is a detailed outline of tasks and timelines designed to achieve specific objectives within a set timeframe. It serves as a roadmap for project execution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management, a scheduled plan is essential for coordinating resources, tracking progress, and ensuring that deadlines are met, thereby facilitating effective team collaboration.

insight.nuance: While a scheduled plan provides structure, it should remain flexible to accommodate unforeseen changes or challenges that may arise during project execution.

vocabulary.definition: To identify means to recognize or establish the characteristics or qualities of something, often through analysis or observation. It involves pinpointing specific elements within a broader context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying key issues, opportunities, or target markets is crucial for strategic decision-making and effective problem-solving, enabling organizations to align their resources effectively.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a deeper understanding or analysis, suggesting that mere recognition is insufficient without a thorough examination of the implications.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: What you want to do instead is to book time in your schedule for this reflective work time, which is where you do the kind of work that requires you to work without distraction.
keySentence: Book reflective work time in your schedule to avoid distractions and plan effectively.
text_ko: 대신 해야 할 건 이런 성찰적 작업 시간(reflective work time)을 일정에 미리 잡아두는 거예요. 이 시간에는 방해받지 않고 해야 하는 일들—계획 세우기, 전략 짜기, 정말로 깊게 생각하기 같은—을 하는 거예요. 그래서 일정도 금방 차게 돼요. 그러다 보면 모든 걸 다 할 시간은 결코 충분하지 않다는 걸 알게 될 거예요. 그런데 그게 오히려 좋은 이유는, 그게 당신에게 강제로 우선순위를 정하게 만들기 때문이에요. 이게 바로 할 일 목록(to-do lists)이 별로인 주된 이유 중 하나예요 — 할 일 목록에는 제약이 없으니까요.
text_zh: 你应该做的是在日程里专门安排时间来做这种需要深度思考的工作，就是那种必须专心致志、不能被打扰的活儿。规划啊、制定战略啊、思考问题啊，说真的，这些事儿只有在不被打扰的情况下才能做好。这样你的日历也就排满了。然后你会发现，时间永远不够用，但这其实是好事，因为这会逼着你做选择，这也是为什么待办清单(to-do list)不好用的主要原因——待办清单没有任何约束。
text_es: En cambio, lo que deberías hacer es bloquear tiempo en tu agenda para este trabajo de reflexión, que es donde haces el tipo de trabajo que necesita que te concentres sin distracciones. Planificar, crear estrategias, pensar, ¡por Dios!, solo se puede hacer sin distracciones. Así que esto también te va a llenar el calendario. Y lo que vas a descubrir es que nunca hay tiempo suficiente para todo, lo cual está bien porque esto te obliga a hacer algo, y esta es una de las razones principales por las que las listas de pendientes no sirven: porque las listas de pendientes no tienen límites.
fullContext: Nir explains the importance of scheduling 'reflective work time' - periods dedicated to deep thinking, planning, and strategizing that require full attention. He distinguishes this from reactive work (responding to emails and notifications). He argues that to-do lists are inadequate because they lack time constraints - you can always add more items without considering how much time you actually have. A time-blocked calendar forces you to make realistic trade-offs and prioritize what truly matters.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by deep thought or consideration, often involving introspection about past experiences or decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, reflective practices are crucial for evaluating past strategies and improving future decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: While 'reflective' often carries a positive connotation of thoughtful analysis, it can imply indecisiveness if overused.

vocabulary.definition: Anything that diverts attention away from a primary task or focus, often leading to decreased productivity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, distractions can significantly hinder performance, making it essential for teams to create environments that minimize interruptions.

insight.nuance: The term 'distraction' typically has a negative connotation, suggesting a loss of focus that can be detrimental to achieving goals.

vocabulary.definition: The process of developing a plan or method to achieve specific goals, often involving analysis and foresight.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and corporate environments, strategizing is vital for aligning resources and efforts towards long-term objectives and competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: While 'strategizing' implies careful planning, it can also suggest a level of complexity that may overwhelm less experienced teams.

vocabulary.definition: The act of outlining a course of action or setting objectives to achieve desired outcomes in a systematic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective planning is fundamental in business for resource allocation, project management, and setting measurable goals.

insight.nuance: Although 'planning' is generally viewed positively, it can imply rigidity if it does not allow for flexibility in execution.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: You don't tell your boss no, you ask your boss to help you prioritize. That is your boss' most important job is to prioritize. So, you're not saying no. You're saying, "Here's my calendar. Here's this list of stuff you've asked me to do.
keySentence: Ask your boss to help you prioritize tasks instead of saying no.
text_ko: 상사한테 그냥 "안 돼요"라고 말하는 게 아니라, 상사에게 우선순위(prioritize)를 정해 달라고 요청하는 거예요. 사실 상사의 가장 중요한 역할 중 하나가 우선순위를 정하는 거예요. 그러니까 당신은 "아니요"라고 하는 게 아니라, "여기 제 캘린더예요. 여기 요청하신 업무 목록도 있어요. 우선순위를 도와주세요."라고 말하는 거예요. 그럼 어떻게 될까요? 상사가 캘린더를 보면서 "사실 그 회의에는 굳이 안 가도 돼요. 그런데 여기 적어둔 이 일이 훨씬 더 중요하네요. 그걸로 바꿔줄 수 있나요?"라고 말해 줄 거예요.
text_zh: 你不要直接跟老板说不行，而是要请老板帮你排个优先级。其实排优先级就是老板最重要的工作之一。所以你不是在拒绝，而是在说："老板你看，这是我的日程表，这是你让我做的那些事儿，你帮我理理头绪吧。" 然后会发生什么呢？你老板会看看你的安排，然后说："你知道吗，那个会议你其实不用参加。但是你这里写的这件事儿，这个重要多了。你能把时间调一下吗？"
text_es: A tu jefe no le dices que no, le pides que te ayude a priorizar. Esa es la función más importante de tu jefe: establecer prioridades. O sea, no estás diciendo que no. Estás diciendo: "Mira, aquí tienes mi agenda. Esta es la lista de todo lo que me has pedido que haga. Ayúdame a priorizar." ¿Y sabes qué va a pasar? Tu jefe va a ver tu agenda y te va a decir: "¿Sabes qué? Esa reunión, realmente no necesitas estar en esa reunión. Pero esto que pusiste aquí en tu lista, esto es muchísimo más importante. ¿Puedes cambiar una cosa por la otra?"
fullContext: Nir addresses how to manage competing demands from your manager without saying 'no' directly. He calls this technique 'schedule syncing' or 'managing your manager.' Instead of refusing requests, you show your boss your time-blocked calendar and a separate list of additional tasks they've requested. You then ask them to help prioritize what's most important. This approach leverages the fact that prioritization is a key management responsibility while giving you control over your time.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange or deal with tasks or responsibilities in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, prioritizing helps teams focus on high-impact activities that align with strategic goals, ensuring efficient use of resources.

insight.nuance: While prioritizing is generally viewed positively, it can imply that some tasks may be deprioritized, which could lead to tension if not communicated effectively.

vocabulary.definition: Conflicting requirements or expectations that require attention and resources simultaneously.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, employees often face competing demands from different projects, clients, or stakeholders, necessitating effective time and resource management.

insight.nuance: The phrase suggests a challenge in balancing multiple responsibilities, which can lead to stress or burnout if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: The process of aligning and coordinating schedules among multiple parties to ensure availability for meetings or collaborative work.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, schedule syncing is crucial for effective teamwork, as it helps avoid conflicts and ensures that all relevant stakeholders can participate in discussions.

insight.nuance: While schedule syncing is essential for collaboration, it can become cumbersome if not managed efficiently, leading to frustration among team members.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of effectively communicating and influencing your superior to ensure alignment on priorities and expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, managing your manager is vital for career progression, as it helps establish a productive working relationship and clarifies roles and responsibilities.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies a proactive approach to leadership dynamics, suggesting that employees should take initiative rather than passively waiting for direction.

speaker: Nir Eyal
text: The antidote for impulsiveness is forethought. The antidote for impulsiveness is forethought. Fundamentally, distraction is an impulse control issue. That's all it is, and it's a skill like any other. We learn skills.
keySentence: The antidote for impulsiveness is forethought; distraction is an impulse control issue.
text_ko: 충동성에 대한 해독제는 사전 숙고(forethought)예요. 본질적으로 산만함은 충동 조절(impulse control)의 문제예요. 그게 전부고, 다른 기술(skill)들처럼 배워야 하는 능력이에요. 우리는 기술을 배워요. 왜 산만함을 이겨내는 이런 능력을 그냥 타고나야 한다고 생각하죠? 다른 기술과 다르지 않아요. 그래서 충동성에 대한 해독제는 사전 숙고예요. 미리 계획하고, "내일 산만해지지 않도록 이런 조치를 취하겠다"고 정해두면 못 이길 산만함이 없어요.
text_zh: 冲动的解药就是提前想好。冲动的解药就是提前想好。说白了，分心就是个自控力的问题，就这么简单，这跟其他技能一样。技能都是学出来的嘛。我们凭什么觉得自己天生就该有对抗分心的本事？这就是个技能，跟别的技能没什么两样。所以说，冲动的解药就是提前想好。如果我们提前规划，如果我们知道今天要采取一些措施来防止明天分心，那就没有克服不了的分心。
text_es: El remedio para ser impulsivo es pensar las cosas antes. En el fondo, distraerse es un tema de autocontrol, nada más. Es una habilidad como cualquier otra. Las habilidades se aprenden. ¿Por qué esperamos nacer ya sabiendo cómo luchar contra las distracciones? Es una habilidad como cualquier otra. Entonces, el remedio para ser impulsivo es pensar las cosas antes. Si planificamos con tiempo, si sabemos que vamos a tomar medidas hoy para no distraernos mañana, no hay distracción que no podamos vencer.
fullContext: Nir provides his core philosophy for becoming indistractable. He emphasizes that distraction is fundamentally about impulse control, which is a learnable skill rather than an inherent character trait. His key insight is that the solution lies in planning ahead - taking deliberate steps today to prevent tomorrow's distractions. This forward-thinking approach empowers people to take control of their attention rather than feeling helpless against distraction.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic or essential way; at the core or foundation of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'fundamentally' is often used to emphasize the underlying principles or values that drive a company's strategy or operations.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a sense of depth and importance, suggesting that the point being made is not just superficial but central to understanding the issue.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to resist immediate temptations or urges in order to achieve long-term goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, impulse control is critical for decision-making, particularly in financial management and strategic planning, where hasty decisions can lead to negative outcomes.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a struggle against natural instincts, highlighting the importance of discipline and self-regulation in professional settings.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to perform tasks and solve problems effectively, often acquired through practice and experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business environment, skills are essential for employee performance, innovation, and competitive advantage, with companies often investing in training to develop these capabilities.

insight.nuance: While 'skill' can refer to both hard and soft abilities, it often emphasizes the proficiency gained through experience rather than innate talent.

vocabulary.definition: A thing that prevents someone from giving full attention to something else; a diversion of focus.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, distractions can significantly reduce productivity and efficiency, prompting organizations to implement strategies for minimizing interruptions and enhancing focus.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that distractions are obstacles to achieving goals or maintaining concentration.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: We have this mental metaphor that we talk a lot about, getting to the next hill.
keySentence: getting to the next hill.
text_ko: 우리가 자주 쓰는 정신적 은유가 하나 있어요 — '다음 언덕으로 가는 것'이요. 원문 표현은 '더 큰 바위에 베팅하세요 (Take bigger boulder bets)'예요. 팀들은 종종 그 언덕을 기어오르느라 길을 잃어서, 그 뒤에 엄청나게 크고 아름다운 산맥이 펼쳐져 있다는 걸 깨닫지 못하곤 해요. 우리는 시간이 지나면서 새로운 영역이 본격적으로 성숙하기 전에 그곳에서 초기 단계로 키운 팀들을 처음부터 만들어 옮겨 배치해 왔어요.
text_zh: 我们经常用一个比喻来形容这种思维模式，就是"登上下一座山头"。具体的说法是"押注更大的石头"(Take bigger boulder bets)。我觉得团队往往会埋头苦干爬山，却没意识到山后面还有一片巨大的、美不胜收的山脉。我们一直以来都会从零开始组建新团队，让他们在新领域孵化项目，等这些领域成熟起来。
text_es: Tenemos esta metáfora mental de la que hablamos mucho: llegar a la siguiente colina. La frase exacta es "apostar por rocas más grandes" (take bigger boulder bets). Creo que los equipos a menudo se pierden arrastrándose por esa colina, sin darse cuenta de que hay una cordillera enorme e increíblemente hermosa detrás, donde con el tiempo hemos creado equipos completamente nuevos que se incubaron en áreas nuevas antes de que esas áreas maduraran.
fullContext: At the beginning of the podcast, Noah explains Slack's approach to product innovation and avoiding incremental thinking. He describes how product teams can get trapped in constant small improvements without seeing bigger opportunities. The metaphor of "getting to the next hill" refers to moving beyond immediate tasks to see the broader landscape of possibilities that exists beyond current projects.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to small, gradual changes or improvements rather than large, radical shifts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, incremental changes are often preferred for risk management, allowing companies to adapt and improve processes or products without significant upheaval.

insight.nuance: While 'incremental' suggests a careful, measured approach, it may imply a lack of ambition compared to more disruptive strategies.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating new ideas, products, or methods that significantly improve or transform existing practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, innovation is crucial for competitive advantage, driving growth and attracting investment.

insight.nuance: Innovation often carries a positive connotation of creativity and forward-thinking, but it can also imply risk and uncertainty.

vocabulary.definition: A figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that isn’t literally true, often used to illustrate a concept or idea.
vocabulary.businessContext: Metaphors are commonly used in business communication to simplify complex ideas and make them more relatable to stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While effective for illustration, metaphors can sometimes obscure meaning if overused or poorly chosen.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the choice of approach can determine the success of projects, influencing everything from management styles to marketing strategies.

insight.nuance: The term 'approach' suggests a level of flexibility and adaptability, but may also imply a lack of decisiveness if not clearly defined.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: I think the biggest probably lesson learned, frankly, is that we were really close with the Instagram folks early on. They were big developers on our platform. They used the Foursquare API before they were bought by Facebook.
keySentence: we were really close with the Instagram folks early on.
text_ko: 솔직히 말하면, 가장 큰 교훈은 우리가 초기에 인스타그램 팀과 정말 가까웠다는 거예요. 그들은 우리 플랫폼에서 큰 개발자였고, 페이스북에 인수되기 전에 Foursquare API를 사용했어요. 지금 생각해보면, 우리가 '원자 단위(atomic unit)'가 사람과 그 사람이 있는 장소에 대한 이야기라는 생각을 좀 잘못한 것 같아요. 사실, 물리적인 장소에 연결해야 한다기보다, 사람들이 세상에서 경험하고 있는 순간이나 경험을 공유하는 게 더 중요했을 수도 있죠.
text_zh: 我觉得最大的教训，说实话，就是我们早期跟Instagram那帮人关系特别铁。他们算是我们平台上的大开发者，在被Facebook收购之前一直在用我们的Foursquare API。现在回头看，我觉得我们当时的想法有点问题——我们以为最基本的单位应该是一个人在谈论他所在的地方，必须得绑定到一个实体的地点，而不是一个人在分享他在世界上正在经历的某个瞬间或体验。
text_es: Creo que la lección más grande que aprendimos, la verdad, es que teníamos una relación muy estrecha con la gente de Instagram desde el principio. Eran grandes desarrolladores en nuestra plataforma. Usaban el API de Foursquare antes de que Facebook los comprara. Pienso que, visto en retrospectiva, nos equivocamos un poco al creer que la unidad básica sería una persona hablando de un lugar donde está y que tenías que vincularla a un lugar físico, en lugar de una persona compartiendo un momento o una experiencia que está viviendo en el mundo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Noah whether Foursquare could have built a massive consumer business or if pivoting to B2B data was inevitable. Noah reflects on what went wrong with Foursquare's social strategy. He explains that they focused on location-based sharing (person + place) while Instagram succeeded with experience-based sharing (person + moment), which sometimes included location but wasn't dependent on it.

vocabulary.definition: Pivoting refers to the act of making a fundamental change in a business strategy or direction, often in response to market feedback or challenges.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startup environments, pivoting is a common practice when initial business models do not yield expected results, prompting companies to explore new avenues for growth or customer engagement.

insight.nuance: While pivoting can indicate flexibility and responsiveness, it may also suggest a lack of initial clarity or focus in the business approach.

vocabulary.definition: A platform is a foundational technology or service that enables the development and deployment of applications, products, or services, often facilitating interactions between users and providers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, platforms like social media networks or software ecosystems serve as critical infrastructures that support third-party developers and enhance user engagement.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a broader ecosystem of services and users, and is often associated with scalability and network effects.

vocabulary.definition: Developers are individuals or teams responsible for creating, building, and maintaining software applications or systems, often possessing specialized technical skills.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology companies, developers play a crucial role in product development, innovation, and the implementation of new features that meet user needs.

insight.nuance: The term can encompass a range of roles, from front-end to back-end developers, and is often associated with collaboration and problem-solving in tech environments.

vocabulary.definition: Strategy refers to a comprehensive plan or approach designed to achieve specific goals or objectives, often involving the allocation of resources and assessment of competitive dynamics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a well-defined strategy guides decision-making processes, shapes marketing efforts, and influences operational practices to gain a competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: While strategy implies long-term planning, it can also be adapted to reflect short-term tactical shifts in response to market conditions.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: I would say to folks in general, if you're joining company and the CEO does the role that is your functional area of expertise, it's probably the area where you'll learn the most because they're hopefully world class at it.
keySentence: Joining a company with a CEO in your functional area of expertise offers less agency.
text_ko: 일반적으로 드리는 말인데요, 입사해서 최고경영자(CEO)가 여러분의 전문 업무 영역(functional area)을 직접 맡고 있다면 그 분야에서 가장 많이 배우게 될 가능성이 커요 — 보통 그분들이 그 일에 대해 세계적 수준이니까요. 다만 동시에 가장 답답함을 느낄 때도 많은데, 그건 스스로 영향력을 발휘하기 어려워 자율성(agency)이 줄어든다고 느끼기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得大家要知道，如果你加入一家公司，而CEO恰好是你这个专业领域的专家，那这块儿你肯定能学到最多东西，因为他们在这方面应该是顶尖的。但同时呢，这也是最容易让你憋屈的地方，因为你会觉得自己没什么发挥空间，很多事情做不了主。
text_es: Yo les diría en general, si te unes a una empresa donde el CEO maneja el área que es tu especialidad, probablemente sea donde más vas a aprender porque se supone que es un crack en eso. Pero también va a ser donde más te frustres a veces, porque vas a sentir que tienes menos autonomía para tomar decisiones.
fullContext: Lenny asks Noah about working with strong product-minded founders like Dennis Crowley and Stewart Butterfield. Noah shares advice for product managers joining companies where the CEO is deeply involved in product decisions. He explains the trade-off between learning opportunities and potential frustration when working under a product-focused founder who may limit your decision-making authority.

vocabulary.definition: A specific division or department within an organization that focuses on a particular set of tasks or responsibilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, functional areas such as marketing, finance, and human resources are essential for the overall operation and strategic direction of the company.

insight.nuance: While often used to describe distinct departments, 'functional area' can also imply a specialization within a broader role, highlighting the importance of expertise in that domain.

vocabulary.definition: A high level of knowledge or skill in a particular area or field, often acquired through experience and education.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, having expertise is crucial for making informed decisions, driving innovation, and maintaining competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of authority and trustworthiness, suggesting that the individual is not only knowledgeable but also respected in their field.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the highest standard of quality or performance, often recognized internationally as exemplary.
vocabulary.businessContext: Companies strive to achieve world-class status to enhance their reputation, attract top talent, and gain a competitive edge in the global market.

insight.nuance: The phrase implies not just excellence, but also a benchmark against which others are measured, making it a powerful descriptor in marketing and branding.

vocabulary.definition: A mindset focused on understanding and prioritizing the needs and experiences of users in relation to a product's development and lifecycle.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, being product-minded is essential for creating solutions that resonate with customers and drive business success.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a proactive approach to product development, emphasizing empathy for the user experience and a commitment to continuous improvement.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: I think what we would wind up doing with Stewart at Slack, for example, is we would get the entire development team, engineers design product, user research and Stewart together in a room and we almost do a bug bash together.
keySentence: We wind up doing a bug bash together to clean up the mess collaboratively.
text_ko: 예를 들어 Slack에서 Stewart랑 같이 일할 때는 결국 개발팀 전체 — 엔지니어, 디자이너, 프로덕트팀, 유저 리서치(user research)와 Stewart를 한자리에 모아서 거의 다 같이 버그 배시(bug bash)를 했어요. 요지는 '우리 모두 같이 하는 거예요. 최고의 제품을 만들려고 하는데, 훌륭한 소프트웨어를 만드는 과정은 원래 되게 지저분하니까 그 지저분한 걸 다 같이 치워나가자'는 느낌이었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得我们在Slack和Stewart合作的时候，基本上就是把整个开发团队——工程师、设计师、产品经理、用户研究，还有Stewart，所有人都拉到一个房间里，然后一起做bug bash。就是那种"咱们一起搞定这事儿"的感觉。我们就想做出最好的产品，但是做好软件这事儿本来就很乱，所以大家一起收拾这个烂摊子。
text_es: Creo que lo que terminábamos haciendo con Stewart en Slack, por ejemplo, era juntar a todo el equipo de desarrollo - ingenieros, diseño, producto, investigación de usuarios y Stewart - todos en una sala y básicamente hacíamos como un bug bash juntos. La idea era "Lo vamos a hacer todos juntos. Estamos tratando de hacer el mejor producto posible, crear buen software es súper desordenado y todos estamos tratando de limpiar ese desorden juntos."
fullContext: Noah explains how to successfully involve product-minded founders in the final stages of product development. He describes Slack's collaborative approach where the entire team, including founder Stewart Butterfield, would gather to review and refine products before launch. A "bug bash" is a collaborative session where team members test software together to find and fix issues.

vocabulary.definition: Involving two or more parties working together to achieve a common goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, a collaborative approach often enhances innovation and problem-solving by leveraging diverse perspectives and expertise.

insight.nuance: While 'collaborative' implies teamwork, it can also suggest a need for compromise and shared responsibility, which may not be suitable in every competitive context.

vocabulary.definition: To include or engage someone or something as a necessary part or participant in a process or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and team dynamics, to involve stakeholders ensures that their insights and needs are considered, leading to better outcomes.

insight.nuance: The term 'involve' can imply varying degrees of engagement, from passive participation to active contribution, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: A group of professionals, typically including software engineers, designers, and product managers, responsible for creating and improving products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech companies, the development team plays a crucial role in the product lifecycle, from initial concept through to deployment and maintenance.

insight.nuance: The term can vary in composition and focus depending on the organization, with some teams emphasizing agile methodologies or cross-functional collaboration.

vocabulary.definition: Having a focus on the product's value, user experience, and market fit, often prioritizing customer needs in decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech firms, being product-minded is essential for aligning development efforts with market demands and ensuring successful product launches.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a proactive approach to product management, which may contrast with a purely technical or sales-driven mindset.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: What we started doing with these complaints storms and idea was really simple, which is we'd get a team together often Stewart myself would also join and we'd actually start off with other products first in adjacent spaces and we'd say, "Okay.
keySentence: we'd actually start off with other products first in adjacent spaces
text_ko: 우리가 이런 불만 폭주(complaints storms)랑 아이디어로 뭘 시작한 건 사실 되게 단순했어요. 팀을 모았고, 종종 스튜어트도 저도 같이 참여해서 실제로는 인접한 영역의 다른 제품들부터 먼저 살펴봤어요. 그리고 "좋아요, 우리 팀이 웹사이트에 들어온 순간부터 고객 여정(customer journey)을 쭉 따라가자"라고 했죠. 예를 들어 직장용 제품(workplace product)이라면 첫 계정을 만들고, 처음 몇 명의 사용자를 온보딩(onboard)하고, 가치를 느끼는 지점(point of value)에 도달하는 것까지요.
text_zh: 我们应对这些投诉风暴的做法其实很简单，就是把团队拉到一起，我和Stewart也经常会参与进来，然后我们会先从相关领域的其他产品开始着手，大家一起梳理整个用户旅程——从用户刚进入网站那一刻开始，比如说是个企业级产品的话，就跟着用户走完开通第一个账户、让前几个用户上手使用、一直到他们真正体验到产品价值的整个过程。
text_es: Lo que empezamos a hacer con estas oleadas de quejas y la idea era súper sencillo - juntábamos un equipo, muchas veces Stewart y yo también nos metíamos, y arrancábamos primero con otros productos de espacios relacionados. Decíamos, "Bueno, como grupo vamos a repasar todo el recorrido del cliente (customer journey) desde que aterriza en la web hasta, digamos si es un producto para empresas, activar su primera cuenta, subir a los primeros usuarios, y llegar hasta ese punto donde ven el valor real."
fullContext: Lenny asks Noah about Slack's "Complaint-Storms" process. Noah explains this method for helping teams look at their product with fresh eyes and build empathy for new users. The process involves teams critically examining customer journeys in competing products first, then applying the same critical lens to their own product to identify pain points and areas for improvement.

vocabulary.definition: Next to or adjoining something else; having a common boundary.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'adjacent' often refers to markets or sectors that are closely related or similar to a company's current operations, allowing for potential expansion or synergy.

insight.nuance: While 'adjacent' implies proximity, it often carries a connotation of strategic relevance, suggesting that the adjacent area is worth exploring for growth opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another person.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, empathy is crucial for effective leadership, team collaboration, and customer relations, as it fosters a supportive environment and enhances communication.

insight.nuance: Empathy goes beyond sympathy; it involves actively engaging with others' perspectives and emotions, making it vital in conflict resolution and team dynamics.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a 'process' refers to structured activities that organizations implement to improve efficiency, ensure quality, and achieve strategic objectives.

insight.nuance: While 'process' implies a systematic approach, it can also suggest rigidity; thus, it's important to balance process adherence with flexibility for innovation.

vocabulary.definition: A group of individuals working collaboratively towards a common goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, a 'team' is essential for leveraging diverse skills and perspectives, driving projects forward, and fostering innovation through collaboration.

insight.nuance: The term 'team' often implies a sense of unity and shared responsibility, but it can also carry implications of hierarchy or role differentiation depending on the context.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: I think teams can often get lost crawling up that hill, not realizing that there's a huge, incredibly beautiful range behind it. Take bigger boulder bets. Get to the next hill to see what the horizon wants around you.
keySentence: Take bigger boulder bets to see what the horizon wants around you.
text_ko: 팀들이 종종 그 언덕을 기어 올라가느라 정작 그 뒤에 엄청 크고 정말 멋진 산맥이 있다는 걸 모를 때가 많아요. 더 큰 바위 같은 베팅(boulder bets)을 해보세요. 다음 언덕까지 올라가서 주변의 지평선이 무엇을 보여주는지 확인해 보세요. 우리가 전략을 생각하는 방식이 바로 그거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得团队经常会陷在眼前这点小坡上爬不出来，根本没意识到后面还有一片超级美的大好河山。要敢于下大注，爬到下一个山头去看看周围到底有什么机会。这就是我们在战略上的思路。
text_es: Creo que los equipos muchas veces se quedan atascados subiendo esa cuesta, sin darse cuenta de que hay una cordillera enorme e increíblemente hermosa detrás. Hay que apostar por cosas más grandes, por proyectos que realmente muevan la aguja. Llegar a la siguiente colina para ver qué oportunidades te esperan en el horizonte. Así es como lo vemos estratégicamente.
fullContext: Lenny asks how Slack enables innovation and zero-to-one bets despite being a large company. Noah explains Slack's strategic philosophy using a mountain climbing metaphor. He describes how teams can get trapped focusing on immediate incremental improvements ("crawling up that hill") without seeing the much larger opportunities that exist beyond their current scope.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'strategic' often refers to planning and decision-making processes that align with an organization's long-term goals and competitive positioning.

insight.nuance: While 'strategic' implies careful planning, it can sometimes suggest a level of complexity or forethought that may not be present in more tactical decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The process of translating an idea or invention into a good or service that creates value or for which customers will pay.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, innovation is crucial for staying competitive, as it involves developing new products, services, or processes that meet changing market demands.

insight.nuance: Innovation often carries a positive connotation of progress and improvement, but it can also imply risk and uncertainty in its implementation.

vocabulary.definition: The line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet; metaphorically, it refers to the limit of one's knowledge, experience, or interest.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'horizon' is often used to describe future opportunities or challenges that an organization may face, encouraging teams to look beyond immediate concerns.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a sense of optimism and potential, suggesting that there are greater opportunities ahead if one looks beyond current limitations.

vocabulary.definition: A term used to describe significant, high-stakes investments or decisions that have the potential for substantial returns or consequences.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and business strategy, 'boulder bets' refer to bold moves that can define a company's future direction and success, often involving considerable risk.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a willingness to take calculated risks for potentially transformative outcomes, and it is typically used in discussions about innovation and growth strategies.

speaker: Noah Weiss
text: I think when we have those teams, I think it's important to just give them space to run, to give them ... get a gel free card for maybe the normal process of, "Okay.
keySentence: it's important to just give them space to run, to give them ... get a gel free card for maybe the normal process
text_ko: 그런 팀들이 있을 때는 그냥 마음껏 해볼 수 있는 여지를 주는 게 중요하다고 생각해요. 예를 들어 분기별 계획 검토(quarterly reviews) 같은 평소의 프로세스에서 잠시 자유로울 수 있는 일종의 면죄부를 줘서, 중요한 건 학습 속도(pace of learning)라는 느낌이 들게 해야 해요. 얼마나 빨리 프로토타이핑(prototyping)하고 사용자에게서 얼마나 빨리 배우느냐, 그걸 공개적으로 파일럿(pilot)해보고 결국 사람들을 완전히 놀라게 하는 멋진 결과물을 출시(launch)하는 속도가 핵심이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得当我们有这样的团队时，重要的是要给他们足够的空间去发挥，给他们一张免死金牌，让他们可以跳过那些常规流程，比如"好吧，我们的季度规划评审"这些，让他们感觉学习的节奏才是最重要的。你们原型做得多快？从用户那里学到东西的速度有多快？然后公开试点，最后推出一个让人眼前一亮的产品。
text_es: Creo que cuando tenemos esos equipos, es importante simplemente darles espacio para que corran, darles... como una carta libre para salirse del proceso normal de "bueno, nuestras revisiones trimestrales de planificación" y hacer que sientan que lo que importa es el ritmo de aprendizaje. Qué tan rápido están haciendo prototipos, qué tan rápido están aprendiendo de los usuarios y luego poder hacerlo públicamente como piloto y después sacar algo al mercado que sea increíble, que deje a la gente con la boca abierta.
fullContext: Noah continues explaining how Slack structures innovation teams to work on new product areas like AI. He emphasizes giving these teams freedom from normal corporate processes and focusing on learning velocity rather than traditional planning cycles. The goal is rapid prototyping and user learning that eventually leads to breakthrough products that exceed customer expectations.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating new ideas, products, or methods that improve efficiency or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, innovation is critical for maintaining competitive advantage and driving growth through the development of novel solutions.

insight.nuance: While innovation often implies technological advancements, it can also refer to new business models or processes that enhance organizational performance.

vocabulary.definition: The structured activities and workflows that organizations implement to achieve their objectives and manage operations effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, well-defined processes are essential for ensuring consistency, efficiency, and compliance across various departments.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a formalized approach, which may sometimes stifle flexibility and adaptability in rapidly changing environments.

vocabulary.definition: The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance or restraint.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, freedom can refer to the autonomy employees have in decision-making and creativity, which can foster innovation and job satisfaction.

insight.nuance: While freedom is generally viewed positively, excessive freedom without guidance can lead to a lack of direction and accountability.

vocabulary.definition: The acquisition of knowledge or skills through experience, study, or teaching.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, continuous learning is vital for employee development and adapting to market changes, often facilitated through training programs and knowledge sharing.

insight.nuance: Learning can encompass both formal education and informal experiences, and its importance is increasingly recognized in fostering a culture of innovation.

speaker: Noam Lovinsky
text: it's like a whole different game where when you see a team that's sort of down and out... sometimes they just need a change of scene, a change of pace.
keySentence: A motivated team has inertia; a down and out team needs a change of scene.
text_ko: 정말 신나서 뭔가를 만들고 있는 팀을 보면 관성(inertia)도 그렇고 결과물의 퀄리티도 완전히 달라요. 반대로 오랫동안 벽에 부딪혀서 기운 빠진 팀은 분위기 자체가 처져 있어서, 그런 팀들은 때로는 단순히 환경이나 속도를 바꿔주는 것만으로도 훨씬 나아져요. 솔직히 말하면 보통은 결국 언제 기운이 다하느냐가 관건이에요.
text_zh: 当你看到一个团队特别有干劲，在做一个他们真正兴奋的项目时，那种势头啊，那个质量啊，完全就是另一个层面的东西。但如果你看到一个团队垂头丧气的，已经撞南墙撞了很久了，有时候他们就是需要换个环境，换个节奏，这样就能进入一个更好的状态。所以我的真心话就是，关键问题通常是，你什么时候会没劲儿了。
text_es: Cuando ves un equipo que está motivado, que está construyendo algo que realmente les emociona, o sea, la inercia, la calidad... es como un juego completamente diferente. Pero cuando ves un equipo que está como decaído y que lleva mucho tiempo dándose contra la pared, a veces lo que necesitan es simplemente cambiar de aires, cambiar el ritmo, y llegan a una situación mucho mejor. Entonces mi respuesta honesta es, sí, se trata de... cuándo se te acaba la gasolina, esa suele ser la pregunta clave.
fullContext: Lenny asks how long you should stick with a project that isn't going well before deciding to move on.
