text_ko: 제 생각에는 템포 프레임워크(tempo framework)가 조직 설계(org design)보다 더 중요해요. 그래서 만약 정말 똑똑해 보이는 팀이 있는데 항상 계획만 하고 실제로는 자주 결과물을 내지 못하거나, 리더십 레벨에서는 다들 이해하는 것 같은데 그 아래 팀들이 어딘가 다른 방향으로 움직인다면, 아마 충분한 정렬(alignment)이 안 돼 있는 거고 특히 템포 관점에서 무엇이 '잘하는 모습'인지에 대한 공감대가 부족한 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得吧，节奏框架(tempo framework)比组织架构设计更重要。你肯定遇到过这种情况：有些团队看起来特别聪明，但总是在那儿规划规划的，实际出活儿不多；或者领导层都挺明白的，但下面的人、再下面的人，好像都在各干各的，方向不太一致。这种情况多半是大家没有达成共识，特别是在节奏把控上，什么叫"做得好"，大家心里都没个准儿。
text_es: En mi opinión, tu marco de ritmo de trabajo es más importante que el diseño organizacional. Entonces, si alguna vez has tenido un equipo que parece súper inteligente, pero siempre están planeando o no entregan mucho, o has tenido problemas donde todos los líderes lo entienden, pero después el equipo que está debajo de ellos y así sucesivamente parece ir en otra dirección, probablemente no tienes suficiente alineación y no tienes suficiente alineación sobre cómo se ve un buen ritmo de trabajo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Patrick about shipping and building productive teams. Patrick shares his framework for creating high-output teams by establishing clear tempo expectations. He explains that many smart teams fail to ship effectively not because of organizational structure, but because they lack alignment on what good performance looks like in terms of shipping frequency and output expectations.

vocabulary.definition: A framework is a structured system or set of guidelines that provides a foundation for understanding or developing a particular concept or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, frameworks are often used to establish best practices, methodologies, or standards that guide project development and organizational processes.

insight.nuance: While 'framework' suggests a supportive structure, it can imply rigidity, so it is important to ensure flexibility within the framework when necessary.

vocabulary.definition: Productive refers to the ability to generate significant output or results efficiently and effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, productivity is often measured in terms of employee performance, project outcomes, and overall organizational efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term can sometimes carry a connotation of being overly focused on output, potentially neglecting quality or employee well-being.

vocabulary.definition: Tempo refers to the speed or pace at which an activity or process occurs, often influencing the rhythm of work and productivity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, tempo can relate to project timelines, the pace of team collaboration, and the overall speed of decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: Using 'tempo' can suggest a dynamic and adaptable approach, but it may also imply pressure if the pace is too fast.

vocabulary.definition: Expectations are beliefs or assumptions about what will happen in the future, often guiding behavior and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, managing expectations is crucial for stakeholder satisfaction, project success, and team morale.

insight.nuance: Expectations can be both explicit and implicit, and failing to meet them can lead to disappointment or conflict, so clear communication is essential.

speaker: Patrick Campbell
text: Everything in your business, it does not matter what type of business you have, everything is used to drive someone to a point of conversion or justify the product or the price that you're offering up.
keySentence: Everything drives a point of conversion or justifies the product offered.
text_ko: 어떤 비즈니스를 운영하든 상관없이, 비즈니스의 모든 요소는 결국 누군가를 구매 같은 전환 지점(conversion)으로 이끌거나, 당신이 제시하는 제품이나 가격을 납득시키는 데 쓰여요. 그 고객은 결국 한 사람이고, 당신의 역할은 그들이 당신을 어떻게 인식하는지, 자신의 문제를 어떻게 바라보는지, 그리고 당신의 제품을 둘러싼 세상을 어떻게 생각하는지를 이해하는 거예요.
text_zh: 不管你做什么生意，所有的一切都是为了让客户最终下单买你的东西，或者让他们觉得你的产品和价格物有所值。那个客户是活生生的人，你要让他们最终转化(conversion)，你就得搞清楚他们怎么看你，怎么看他们自己遇到的问题，还有他们对你产品周围这个世界是怎么理解的。
text_es: Todo en tu negocio, no importa qué tipo de empresa tengas, todo se usa para llevar a alguien a ese punto de conversión o para justificar el producto o el precio que estás ofreciendo. Ese cliente es un ser humano al que estás llevando a ese punto de conversión y tu trabajo es entender cómo te percibe a ti, cómo percibe su problema, cómo percibe el mundo que lo rodea, el mundo alrededor de tus productos.
fullContext: Lenny asks Patrick about customer research and his perspective on why companies often fail to do it properly. Patrick gives his "85-year-old curmudgeonly man perspective" on customer research, emphasizing that despite everyone talking about its importance, only one in five companies have proper buyer personas and only one in ten do regular customer research, even though it dramatically improves all business metrics.

vocabulary.definition: The process of changing or transforming something into a different state, often referring to turning potential customers into actual buyers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, conversion typically refers to the effectiveness of marketing strategies in persuading customers to complete a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a service.

insight.nuance: While 'conversion' can refer to any change, in a business context it specifically implies a successful outcome in customer engagement.

vocabulary.definition: To provide valid reasons or explanations for an action, decision, or belief, often to defend its legitimacy or necessity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, justifying a product or price involves presenting arguments or data that support the value proposition to customers or stakeholders.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of rationalization, suggesting that the justification may be necessary to alleviate doubts or objections.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of considering something, which can influence decision-making and understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, perspective is crucial as it shapes how leaders and teams interpret market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscapes.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a subjective viewpoint, suggesting that different stakeholders may have varying perspectives on the same issue.

vocabulary.definition: The process of gathering and analyzing information about consumers' needs, preferences, and behaviors to inform business strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: Customer research is essential for businesses to understand their target market, improve products, and tailor marketing efforts effectively.

insight.nuance: While it is a systematic approach, the term can also imply an ongoing effort to adapt to changing consumer dynamics.

speaker: Paul Adams
text: This is a meteor coming towards you. This is going to radically transform society. And I think if people don't explore AI properly, it will leave them behind. I'd start with the thing your product does. "What's the core premise behind it?
keySentence: AI is a meteor coming towards you, radically transforming society.
text_ko: 이건 당신 쪽으로 날아오는 운석이에요. 사회를 근본적으로 바꿔 놓을 거예요. 그리고 사람들이 인공지능(AI)을 제대로 들여다보지 않으면 뒤처질 거라고 생각해요. 저는 우선 제품(product)이 하는 일부터 살펴볼 것 같아요. "그 제품의 핵심 전제(core premise)는 뭔가요? 사람들이 왜 쓰죠? 어떤 문제를 해결해 주나요?" 이런 식으로요. 기본으로 돌아가서, 그리고 나서 "인공지능(AI)이 그걸 할 수 있을까요?"라고 물어보세요.
text_zh: 这就像一颗流星朝你砸过来一样。这会彻底改变整个社会。我觉得如果大家不好好研究AI的话，肯定会被甩在后面。我建议先从你们产品本身入手。"它的核心逻辑是什么？用户为什么要用它？它帮他们解决了什么痛点？"就是这些基本问题。所以，回到原点去思考。然后再问自己，"AI能做这件事吗？"
text_es: Esto es como un meteorito que viene hacia ti. Va a transformar la sociedad de manera radical. Y creo que si la gente no explora bien la IA, se va a quedar atrás. Yo empezaría con lo que hace tu producto. "¿Cuál es la idea central? ¿Por qué lo usa la gente? ¿Qué problema les resuelve?" Ese tipo de cosas. O sea, volver a lo básico. Y después preguntarte: "¿Puede la IA hacer eso?"
fullContext: Lenny asks Paul about his broader insights on AI and how it will integrate into product strategy. Paul explains his belief that AI represents a massive technology shift comparable to or bigger than mobile and the internet. He advocates for a methodical approach to evaluating AI's impact on your product: first understand your core value proposition and user problems, then assess whether AI can solve those same problems.

vocabulary.definition: To change something in a fundamental or significant way, often resulting in a complete overhaul of its structure or function.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'radically transform' is often used to describe innovations or disruptions that alter market dynamics or operational processes.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of urgency and importance, implying that the change is not merely incremental but rather revolutionary.

vocabulary.definition: To investigate or examine a subject in depth to gain a better understanding or to discover new insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, 'explore' often refers to the process of researching new markets, technologies, or ideas to identify opportunities for innovation.

insight.nuance: While 'explore' suggests a proactive approach to discovery, it can also imply uncertainty or the need for further investigation before making decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The fundamental idea or underlying assumption that serves as the foundation for a concept, product, or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, understanding the 'core premise' of a product or service is crucial for aligning team efforts and communicating value propositions to stakeholders.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the essential elements of a concept, suggesting that clarity around the core premise is vital for effective communication and execution.

vocabulary.definition: A significant change in technology that alters the landscape of industries, markets, or consumer behavior on a large scale.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, a 'massive technology shift' can create new business models, disrupt existing markets, and necessitate strategic pivots for companies to remain competitive.

insight.nuance: This phrase often carries a sense of urgency and importance, indicating that organizations must adapt quickly to leverage new technologies or risk obsolescence.

speaker: Paul Adams
text: You can get sidetracked by the technology, for sure. And I do. I just mentioned, hey, going out for dinner and taking a photo of my food. You can get sidetracked by the tech and some of it's really cool. I wouldn't start there.
keySentence: You can get sidetracked by the tech and some of it's really cool.
text_ko: 물론 기술(technology)에 신경이 쓰여 곁길로 새는 경우가 있어요. 저도 그래요 — 아까 말한 것처럼 저녁 먹으러 가서 음식 사진 찍는 것처럼요. 기술이 멋진 건 맞지만 거기서 시작하진 않아요. 저는 제품(product)이 실제로 뭘 하는지부터 시작해요. 그 밑에 있는 핵심 전제(core premise)는 뭔가요? 사람들이 왜 쓰나요? 어떤 문제를 해결해 주나요? 그런 것들이요.
text_zh: 技术确实容易让人分心，我也会这样。就像我刚说的，出去吃饭还要给菜拍照。你很容易被那些酷炫的技术带跑偏，有些确实挺有意思的。但我不会从这里入手。我会从你的产品本身做什么开始。它的核心价值主张(core premise)是什么？用户为什么要用它？它帮他们解决了什么问题？就是这些东西。
text_es: Claro que te puedes distraer con la tecnología, sin duda. Y a mí me pasa. Como te decía, salir a cenar y tomarle foto a la comida. Te puedes ir por las ramas con la tecnología y algunas cosas están padrísimas. Pero yo no empezaría por ahí. Yo empezaría con lo que hace tu producto en realidad. ¿Cuál es la premisa central? ¿Por qué la gente lo usa? ¿Qué problema les resuelve? Ese tipo de cosas.
fullContext: Lenny asks Paul to elaborate on how to think strategically about whether your product is in the path of AI disruption. Paul warns against getting distracted by flashy AI capabilities and instead recommends starting with fundamental product questions. He emphasizes understanding your product's core value proposition before determining how AI might impact it.

vocabulary.definition: To be diverted from the main focus or objective, often due to distractions or interruptions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being sidetracked can lead to inefficiencies, as teams may lose sight of their primary goals while engaging with less critical tasks or technologies.

insight.nuance: While sidetracked can imply a temporary diversion, it often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of discipline or focus.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that relates to the identification and pursuit of long-term goals and objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, acting strategically involves making decisions that align with the overall vision and direction of the organization.

insight.nuance: This term implies a thoughtful and planned approach, as opposed to a reactive or impulsive one.

vocabulary.definition: Unable to concentrate or focus due to external stimuli or internal thoughts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a professional environment, being distracted can hinder productivity and lead to mistakes, particularly in fast-paced tech or startup settings where focus is crucial.

insight.nuance: While distraction can be temporary, it often suggests a need for better time management or prioritization skills.

vocabulary.definition: The skills, resources, or potential that an individual or organization possesses to perform tasks or achieve goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding one's capabilities is essential for strategic planning, resource allocation, and competitive analysis.

insight.nuance: Capabilities often imply inherent strengths and can be contrasted with limitations or weaknesses.

speaker: Paul Adams
text: We literally ripped up our strategy almost entirely, and started again, from first principles and said, "Okay, why do people use Intercom?" Intercom is a customer support product.
keySentence: We ripped up our strategy and started again from first principles.
text_ko: 우리는 전략을 거의 완전히 갈아엎고 처음부터 다시 시작했어요. 기본 원칙(first principles)부터 다시 되짚어 보면서 “사람들이 왜 Intercom을 쓰는 거지?”라고 물었죠. Intercom은 고객 지원(customer support) 제품이에요. 그리고 얼마 지나지 않아 OpenAI의 창업자 겸 대표인 샘 올트먼이 “가장 먼저 영향을 받게 될 산업 중 하나가 고객 서비스(customer service)다”라고 했어요. 우리는 “그렇죠”라고 했어요.
text_zh: 我们基本上把原来的战略全部推倒重来，从最基本的问题开始思考："用户为什么要用Intercom？"Intercom本质上就是个客服产品。然后没过多久，OpenAI的创始人兼负责人Sam Altman就说："客服行业肯定是首批被AI颠覆的行业之一。"我们当时就想："没错，就是这样。"
text_es: Literalmente tiramos nuestra estrategia casi por completo a la basura y empezamos de cero, desde los principios básicos, y dijimos: "A ver, ¿por qué la gente usa Intercom?" Intercom es un producto de atención al cliente. Y luego, muy poco después, Sam Altman, que es el fundador y director de OpenAI, dijo: "Oye, una de las primeras industrias que va a ser revolucionada es el servicio al cliente." Y nosotros: "Exacto."
fullContext: Lenny asks for an example of how AI can fully replace existing product functionality. Paul describes how Intercom completely changed their strategy after ChatGPT launched on November 29th. When OpenAI's Sam Altman identified customer service as one of the first industries AI would disrupt, Intercom realized they needed to pivot their entire approach and build AI-first solutions.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, strategy refers to the comprehensive approach organizations take to reach their goals, often involving market analysis and resource allocation.

insight.nuance: While 'strategy' implies a well-thought-out plan, it can also suggest rigidity; thus, it is important to remain adaptable in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: Fundamental truths or propositions that serve as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, principles guide decision-making and organizational culture, often reflecting the core values of the company.

insight.nuance: Using 'principles' conveys a sense of integrity and foundational thinking, suggesting that decisions are made based on established beliefs rather than arbitrary choices.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being suited to serve a purpose well; the range of operations that can be run on a system or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and product development, functionality refers to the specific features and capabilities that a product offers to meet user needs.

insight.nuance: While 'functionality' emphasizes practical aspects, it can sometimes imply a lack of aesthetic or user-friendly design, so it's important to balance both in product development.

vocabulary.definition: Services provided to assist customers in resolving issues with a product or service, ensuring satisfaction and loyalty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, customer support is critical for maintaining customer relationships and enhancing user experience, often involving various channels like phone, email, and chat.

insight.nuance: The term 'customer support' implies a reactive approach to customer needs, while 'customer success' suggests a more proactive strategy focused on long-term satisfaction and engagement.

speaker: Paul Adams
text: The advice I have for people, and the advice I have for myself, I'm in that too, I wake up every day to too many emails, and Slack chats, and people knocking on my door, and my desk, and all things.
keySentence: I wake up every day to too many emails, and Slack chats, and people knocking on my door.
text_ko: 사람들에게 해주는 조언이자 제 자신에게도 하는 말인데요, 저도 그래요. 매일 너무 많은 이메일과 슬랙 메시지, 사람들이 문을 두드리거나 제 책상으로 불쑥 찾아오는 등으로 하루가 시작돼요. 저한테도 큰 도전이에요. 그래서 시간을 따로 내야 해요. 저한텐 다른 방법이 없더라고요. 그리고 그게 의미하는 건… 결국 우선순위의 문제예요.
text_zh: 我给别人的建议，也是给自己的建议，我也是这样的，每天一醒来就是一堆邮件，Slack消息，还有人敲门找我，桌子上也是乱七八糟的，什么都有。所以我也面临这个挑战。你就得挤时间出来，对我来说没别的办法。这不是说... 关键还是看你怎么排优先级。
text_es: El consejo que les doy a otros, y que me doy a mí mismo porque yo también estoy en la misma, es que me levanto cada día con demasiados emails, chats de Slack, gente tocando mi puerta, cosas en mi escritorio, de todo. O sea, para mí también es un reto. Simplemente tienes que darte el tiempo. Para mí no hay de otra. Y eso no significa... Se trata de prioridades.
fullContext: Lenny asks what advice Paul would give to people who want to go deeper into AI but don't have time due to their existing workload. Paul acknowledges he faces the same challenge with emails and meetings, but emphasizes that learning about AI must become a priority. He stresses that staying current with AI isn't optional - it requires dedicated time and prioritization.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of work assigned to or expected from a person in a specific period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, managing workload is crucial for ensuring productivity and preventing employee burnout, especially in high-pressure environments like startups.

insight.nuance: While 'workload' typically refers to quantity, it can also imply the complexity and difficulty of tasks involved.

vocabulary.definition: Messages sent electronically, typically via the internet, used for communication in personal and professional contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: Emails are a primary mode of communication in business, facilitating information exchange, project updates, and client interactions.

insight.nuance: While emails are efficient, they can also contribute to information overload if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance or recommendations offered with regard to prudent future action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, advice can come from mentors, colleagues, or industry experts and is often sought for decision-making and strategy development.

insight.nuance: The term 'advice' carries a connotation of wisdom and experience, implying that the source has relevant knowledge to share.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulties or obstacles that require a solution or response.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, challenges can arise from market competition, resource limitations, or internal processes, necessitating strategic problem-solving.

insight.nuance: The term 'challenges' often implies an opportunity for growth and innovation, rather than merely a setback.

speaker: Paul Adams
text: I think customer support is definitely... Like I said, number one, customer support. So you're like, "Okay, I guess we should adapt." Adapt or die is our mantra. Adapt or die.
keySentence: Adapt or die is our mantra for customer support.
text_ko: 저는 고객 지원이 확실히... 아까 말했듯이, 가장 중요한 건 고객 지원이에요. 그래서 사람들이 “그럼 우리도 적응해야겠다”라고 생각하죠. '적응하라 아니면 도태된다(Adapt or die)'가 저희 신조예요. 다른 업종들도 같은 길을 가고 있다고 생각하는데, 그게 그렇게 뚜렷하게 보이진 않을 뿐이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得客户服务绝对是...就像我刚说的，排第一位的就是客户服务。所以你就会想，"好吧，看来我们得适应变化了。"适应或淘汰(adapt or die)就是我们的座右铭。要么适应，要么被淘汰。我觉得其他行业其实也在走同样的路，只是没有那么明显而已。
text_es: Creo que el soporte al cliente es definitivamente... Como te dije, número uno, soporte al cliente. Entonces piensas, "Bueno, supongo que tenemos que adaptarnos." Adaptarse o morir es nuestro lema. Adaptarse o morir. Creo que hay otras industrias que están en el mismo camino, simplemente no es tan obvio.
fullContext: Lenny asks what helps people gain conviction about AI's importance, noting that customer support seems like a clear opportunity for AI integration. Paul confirms that customer support was identified as the top industry for AI disruption, making their decision clearer. He introduces Intercom's core philosophy of "adapt or die" while acknowledging that other industries face similar AI transformation challenges, though the path may be less obvious.

vocabulary.definition: To modify or adjust to new conditions or environments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, adapting often refers to the ability of a company to change its strategies or operations in response to market demands or technological advancements.

insight.nuance: While 'adapt' suggests a positive and proactive approach to change, it may imply a sense of urgency or necessity in competitive environments.

vocabulary.definition: A repeated phrase or slogan that encapsulates a guiding principle or belief.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, a mantra can serve as a motivational slogan that reflects the company's core values or strategic focus, often used to inspire employees and align efforts.

insight.nuance: The term 'mantra' carries a spiritual connotation, suggesting a deeper commitment to the principle it represents, which can enhance its motivational impact.

vocabulary.definition: A firmly held belief or opinion, often accompanied by a strong sense of certainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, conviction can drive decision-making and leadership, influencing how leaders communicate their vision and rally their teams around a common goal.

insight.nuance: While 'conviction' implies a strong belief, it can also suggest inflexibility; thus, it's important to balance conviction with openness to new ideas.

vocabulary.definition: The process of combining or coordinating different components into a unified whole.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, integration often refers to the seamless incorporation of various systems, processes, or teams to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.

insight.nuance: Integration suggests a collaborative effort and can imply complexity, as it often requires careful planning and execution to ensure all parts work together harmoniously.

speaker: Paul Adams
text: Number one thing I would say is keep it simple. Keep it simple. It's so tempting to...
keySentence: Number one thing I would say is keep it simple.
text_ko: 제일 먼저 드리고 싶은 말은 단순하게 하라는 거예요. 정말 단순하게 유지하세요. 복잡하게 확장하고 싶어지는 유혹이 크거든요. 예를 들어 우리 같은 경우 많은 SaaS 제품(SaaS products)은 애드온(add-ons)이 있어서 “우리가 X를 만들었고 그게 X의 가격이에요—10달러일 수도 있고 100,000일 수도 있어요(판매하는 제품에 따라 달라요).” 그런 다음에 “방금 Y를 만들었어요. Y는 멋지고 새로운 기능이라서 이걸로 여러 새로운 가능성이 열려요”라고 계속 추가하는 식이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得最重要的一点就是保持简单。一定要保持简单。真的特别容易陷入这样的陷阱...比如说我们这种情况，很多SaaS产品都有附加功能，你会说："嘿，我们开发了X功能，卖10块钱。"或者10万块，这得看你卖的是什么产品了。"我们开发了X功能，X功能就是这个价格。嘿，我们刚开发了Y功能。Y功能超棒的，是个全新的东西，能解锁各种新能力。"
text_es: Lo principal que te diría es que lo mantengas sencillo. Que lo mantengas sencillo. Es súper tentador... Con nosotros, por ejemplo, muchos productos SaaS tienen complementos (add-ons), donde dices, "Oye, creamos X y eso cuesta 10 dólares." O 100,000, depende del producto que vendas. "Creamos X y ese es el precio de X. Oye, acabamos de crear Y. Y está padrísimo y es algo nuevo que puedes hacer, y te abre un montón de nuevas posibilidades."
fullContext: Lenny asks for pricing wisdom based on Paul's experience with Intercom's complex pricing challenges. Paul emphasizes that pricing is deceptively difficult, comparing it to onboarding as one of the hardest design problems. He explains how companies often start simple but gradually add complexity through add-ons and tiers, making customer bills incomprehensible. His key lesson is to resist the temptation to add multiple pricing models.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is misleading or gives a false impression.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'deceptively' can describe marketing strategies that may appear straightforward but are actually more complex than they seem, potentially leading to misunderstandings.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that something is not as it appears, and should be used cautiously to avoid implying dishonesty.

vocabulary.definition: Consisting of many interconnected parts; not simple or straightforward.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'complex' often refers to systems, processes, or problems that require careful analysis and strategic thinking to navigate effectively.

insight.nuance: While 'complex' can indicate sophistication, it may also imply unnecessary complication, so it's important to assess whether complexity is beneficial or detrimental.

vocabulary.definition: To give special importance or prominence to something in speaking or writing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, 'emphasizes' is often used to highlight key points in presentations or reports, ensuring that critical information is not overlooked.

insight.nuance: Using 'emphasizes' suggests a deliberate focus on certain aspects, which can be positive for clarity but may also imply that other areas are less important.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulties or obstacles that require a solution or response.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, 'challenges' often refer to issues that organizations must address to achieve their goals, such as market competition or operational inefficiencies.

insight.nuance: While 'challenges' can imply a negative situation, it can also suggest opportunities for growth and innovation when approached positively.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: I think the default path is different for everyone and slightly different in every different culture. It's really the story in your head about what you should do. And most of us have some sort of script that we're living out.
keySentence: The default path varies for everyone, shaped by the story in your head.
text_ko: 사람마다 '기본 경로(default path)'는 다르고, 문화마다도 조금씩 달라요. 본질적으로 그건 '내가 뭘 해야 한다'고 생각하게 만드는 머릿속 이야기예요. 대부분은 저마다 어떤 식의 대본(script)을 가지고 그걸 따라 살고 있어요. 특히 10대 후반에서 20대 초반에는 그 영향력이 더 커서, 그 시기엔 대본을 실행하려고 애쓰죠.
text_zh: 我觉得每个人的默认路径都不一样，在不同文化里也会有差别。其实就是你脑子里那个关于"我应该怎么做"的故事。我们大多数人都在按照某种剧本生活。这在十八九岁到二十出头的时候特别明显，对吧？我们就是在努力按剧本演下去。
text_es: Creo que el camino que seguimos por defecto es diferente para cada persona y varía un poco según la cultura. En realidad es esa historia que tienes en la cabeza sobre lo que deberías hacer. Y la mayoría de nosotros tenemos como un guión que estamos siguiendo. Esto se nota especialmente cuando tienes entre 17-18 y 22-23 años, ¿no? Estás tratando de cumplir con ese guión.
fullContext: Lenny asks Paul to define what he calls the 'default path' - a central concept from Paul's book 'The Pathless Path.' Paul explains that the default path is the conventional life script people follow without conscious choice, typically including going to college, getting a good job, making a good salary, buying a house, getting married, and having a family. He emphasizes that this unconscious script is particularly influential during late teens and early twenties when people are trying to execute what they think they 'should' do rather than what they actually want to do.

vocabulary.definition: A default path refers to a pre-set or standard course of action that is typically followed unless an alternative is chosen. It represents the most common or expected trajectory in decision-making processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, the default path often outlines the standard procedures or workflows that employees are expected to follow, which can influence project management and operational efficiency.

insight.nuance: While 'default path' suggests a normative approach, it may imply a lack of creativity or individualization if adhered to too rigidly.

vocabulary.definition: Conventional describes practices, methods, or ideas that are widely accepted and used, often based on tradition or established norms. It implies adherence to established standards rather than innovation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, conventional strategies may refer to traditional marketing methods or organizational structures that are commonly employed in an industry.

insight.nuance: While 'conventional' can denote reliability, it may also suggest a lack of innovation or adaptability in rapidly changing environments.

vocabulary.definition: A script is a predefined set of instructions or guidelines that dictate how an individual should behave or respond in specific situations. It can also refer to a written document for a performance or presentation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, scripts are often used in sales or customer service to ensure consistent messaging and responses, enhancing communication effectiveness.

insight.nuance: While scripts can provide clarity and structure, they may also limit spontaneity and authenticity in interactions.

vocabulary.definition: Culture encompasses the shared beliefs, values, norms, and practices of a group or organization, influencing behavior and decision-making. It shapes the identity and functioning of communities and workplaces.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, organizational culture plays a crucial role in employee engagement, productivity, and overall company performance, affecting how teams collaborate and innovate.

insight.nuance: Culture can be a double-edged sword; while it fosters unity and identity, it can also lead to resistance to change if not managed carefully.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: A lot of times when people quit their jobs, they forget to fire the manager in their head. They don't realize they can take the afternoon off to spend it with their kids.
keySentence: People forget to fire the manager in their head and accept the implicit contract.
text_ko: 사람들이 회사를 그만둘 때면 머릿속에 있는 ‘상사’를 해고하는 걸 잊는 경우가 많아요. 오후에 아이들과 시간을 보내기 위해 오후를 쉬어도 된다는 걸 깨닫지 못하죠. 월요일부터 금요일까지 하루 8~10시간은 일해야 한다는 암묵적 계약(implicit contract)을 스스로 만들어놓은 건데, 그 방식이 누군가에게는 잘 맞을 수 있어요. 그런데 그걸 진짜로 스스로 선택한 건가요, 아니면 그냥 기본값(default)을 수용한 건가요?
text_zh: 很多人辞职创业后，脑子里还是摆脱不了以前那个老板的影子。他们想不到其实可以下午请假去陪孩子玩。在他们心里还是默认周一到周五必须得工作8到10个小时，好像签了什么隐形合同似的。这种模式对有些人来说可能没问题，但你得问问自己：这真的是你主动选择的，还是你就这么稀里糊涂地接受了这个默认设置？
text_es: Muchas veces cuando la gente deja su trabajo, se les olvida despedir al jefe que tienen en la cabeza. No se dan cuenta de que pueden tomarse la tarde libre para estar con sus hijos. Han creado este contrato implícito de que de lunes a viernes tienes que trabajar de ocho a diez horas al día. Y eso puede funcionar para algunas personas, pero ¿realmente estás eligiendo eso conscientemente, o simplemente estás aceptando lo que viene por defecto?
fullContext: Lenny asks about signs that people are still on the default path even when they think they're not. Paul responds by explaining that even when people leave traditional jobs, they often carry the same mental constraints and work patterns with them. He emphasizes the difference between consciously choosing your path versus unconsciously accepting default assumptions about how work should be structured, using the metaphor of 'firing the manager in your head' to describe breaking free from internalized workplace expectations.

vocabulary.definition: A predetermined route or method that is automatically selected unless an alternative is specified.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a default path often refers to the standard procedure or workflow that employees follow unless they choose to deviate from it, impacting efficiency and decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a lack of customization or choice, and it is often used in discussions about innovation versus traditional practices.

vocabulary.definition: To accept responsibility for a task or project, demonstrating accountability and initiative.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, taking ownership is crucial for leadership and teamwork, as it fosters a culture of accountability and encourages employees to take proactive measures in their roles.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of empowerment and commitment, and is often encouraged in high-performing teams; however, it can imply a heavier burden if misused.

vocabulary.definition: To become fully aware of something as a fact; to understand or grasp the significance of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, realizing a concept or opportunity often leads to strategic decisions and actions that can drive growth and innovation.

insight.nuance: While it generally has a positive connotation of awakening or enlightenment, it can also imply a belated understanding of a situation.

vocabulary.definition: An internalized voice or mindset that reflects one's self-imposed expectations and standards, often resembling a critical supervisor.
vocabulary.businessContext: This phrase is used to describe how individuals may hold themselves to high standards or feel pressured by their internal dialogue, which can affect their work-life balance and decision-making.

insight.nuance: It suggests an internal conflict between personal desires and professional expectations, and is often used in discussions about mental health and work-life balance.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: My hot take is that we're all on a pathless path. You were at Airbnb. Airbnb, every two years were there was a different company. Right? And so we're constantly needing to reinvent and reevaluate.
keySentence: We're all on a pathless path, constantly needing to reinvent and reevaluate.
text_ko: 제 핫테이크(hot take)는 우리 모두가 '길 없는 길'을 걷고 있다는 거예요. 에어비앤비에 계실 때도 2년마다 완전히 다른 회사에 있는 것 같았잖아요. 그래서 우리는 계속해서 스스로를 재창조하고 재평가해야 해요. 삶을 회사에서 쭉 승진해 올라가는 매끈한 궤적처럼만 생각하면 오히려 우리 삶의 가능성을 제한한다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 我的观点是，咱们其实都在走一条没有路的路。你之前在Airbnb工作，Airbnb每两年就像换了个公司似的，对吧？所以我们得不断地重新定位、重新思考。我觉得如果把人生想象成在公司里一路平稳往上爬的轨迹，这样反而限制了我们人生的各种可能性。
text_es: Mi opinión sincera es que todos estamos en un camino sin rumbo fijo. Estuviste en Airbnb. Airbnb, cada dos años era prácticamente una empresa diferente, ¿no? Y entonces constantemente necesitamos reinventarnos y reevaluar todo. Y creo que pensar en nuestras vidas como esta trayectoria lisa hacia arriba en el ascenso corporativo como que limita las posibilidades de nuestra propia vida.
fullContext: Paul is explaining to Lenny how even traditional corporate careers are actually more uncertain and constantly changing than people realize. He uses Airbnb as an example of how companies evolve so rapidly that employees must constantly adapt and reinvent themselves. Paul argues that the illusion of a 'smooth trajectory up this corporate ascent' actually limits people's thinking about what's possible in their careers, since the reality is that everyone is already navigating uncertainty and change.

vocabulary.definition: To change something fundamentally, often to improve it or adapt it to new circumstances.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, reinventing can refer to altering a company's strategy, product offerings, or operational processes to remain competitive in a rapidly changing market.

insight.nuance: While 'reinvent' implies a significant transformation, it is often used positively to suggest innovation and adaptability rather than mere change.

vocabulary.definition: To assess or review something again, often with the intention of making changes based on new information or insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, reevaluating strategies, goals, or performance metrics is crucial for ensuring alignment with market demands and organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: Reevaluating suggests a critical and thoughtful approach to decision-making, indicating that previous assessments may no longer be valid or effective.

vocabulary.definition: Continuously over a period of time; without interruption.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the fast-paced world of business and technology, companies must constantly innovate and adapt to stay relevant and competitive.

insight.nuance: The term conveys a sense of urgency and necessity, indicating that ongoing action is required rather than sporadic efforts.

vocabulary.definition: To develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complex form.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, businesses must evolve their products and services to meet changing consumer needs and technological advancements.

insight.nuance: Evolving implies a natural and gradual process of change, often viewed positively as an adaptation to external factors rather than forced change.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: I really shied away from trying to define it super clearly. I think I have this passage at the beginning of the book that it's like the pathless path is basically a shift away from the default.
keySentence: the pathless path is basically a shift away from the default.
text_ko: 저는 그걸 아주 분명하게 정의하려고 하진 않았어요. 책 초반에 이런 구절을 썼는데, 길 없는 길(pathless path)은 기본값에서 벗어나는 변화예요. 다시 말하면, '무엇을 하고 있는지 모르는 상태'를 해결해야 할 문제로 보던 태도에서 벗어나, 불편함과 불확실성을 기꺼이 받아들이는 쪽으로 옮겨가는 거예요.
text_zh: 我当时真的很避免把它定义得太清楚。我觉得在书的开头有这么一段话，就是说这个"无路之路"本质上就是要跳出常规思维。不再把"不知道自己在干什么"当成一个需要解决的问题，而是要学会拥抱那些不舒服、不确定的感觉。
text_es: La verdad es que evité a toda costa tratar de definirlo súper claramente. Creo que tengo un pasaje al inicio del libro donde digo que el sendero sin camino es básicamente un cambio de paradigma, alejándose de lo establecido. Es pasar de ver el no saber qué haces como un problema que hay que resolver, a abrazar la incomodidad y la incertidumbre.
fullContext: Lenny asks Paul to explain his core concept of the 'pathless path' in simple terms. Rather than giving a rigid definition, Paul describes it as a fundamental shift in mindset - moving away from viewing uncertainty as something to be eliminated toward embracing discomfort and not knowing what comes next. He explains this as a personal journey from operating from scarcity toward operating from abundance, requiring faith that things might work out even without a clear plan.

vocabulary.definition: To state the precise meaning or nature of something, often clarifying its boundaries and characteristics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, defining a product, service, or strategy is crucial for establishing clear objectives and expectations among stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While 'define' suggests clarity, it can also imply rigidity; sometimes, a flexible interpretation may be more beneficial.

vocabulary.definition: To change or move from one position, state, or condition to another, often implying a significant transformation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, a shift can refer to changes in market trends, consumer behavior, or organizational strategy that require adaptation.

insight.nuance: The term 'shift' often carries a sense of urgency and can imply a need for proactive response rather than passive acceptance.

vocabulary.definition: The preselected option or setting that is automatically chosen if no alternative is specified.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and finance, the term 'default' can refer to standard settings in software applications or the failure to meet financial obligations, respectively.

insight.nuance: While 'default' often suggests a baseline or norm, it can also imply a lack of choice or initiative, which may not be desirable in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: A particular way of thinking or a set of beliefs that shapes an individual's attitudes and behaviors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, cultivating a growth mindset among employees can enhance innovation, resilience, and adaptability in the face of challenges.

insight.nuance: The term 'mindset' often implies a deep-seated perspective that can be difficult to change, highlighting the importance of fostering a positive organizational culture.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: The big aha for me was, 'Oh, you can design around liking work.' The hidden assumption I had around work for the first 32, 33 years of my life was work sucks. You have to figure out how to tolerate it.
keySentence: The big aha was designing around liking work instead of suffering through it.
text_ko: 제게 큰 아하 순간은 '일을 좋아하는 쪽으로 설계할 수 있구나'였어요. 제 인생 첫 32~33년 동안 무의식적으로 갖고 있던 일에 대한 전제는 '일은 괴롭다'였어요. 그 틀 안에서는 어떻게든 참아내는 법을 찾아야 하고, 그 안에서 일부를 최대한 즐기려고 애쓰는 식이었죠. 결국엔 시간을 대가로 치르는 거래라고 생각했고, 참아내야만 한다고 믿었어요.
text_zh: 我最大的顿悟就是，"哦，原来工作是可以设计得让人喜欢的。" 我人生前三十二三年一直有个隐性的假设，就是工作就是很痛苦的。你得想办法忍受它。在这个框架里，你尽量让自己享受其中的一些部分。但说到底，这就是拿时间做交换。你必须硬撑过去。
text_es: Para mí el momento de revelación fue: "Ah, puedes diseñar tu trabajo para que te guste". La creencia oculta que tenía sobre el trabajo durante los primeros 32, 33 años de mi vida era que el trabajo apesta. Tienes que averiguar cómo aguantarlo. Y dentro de esa mentalidad, hacer lo posible por disfrutar algo de vez en cuando. Pero al final, es un intercambio de tu tiempo. Tienes que sufrirlo.
fullContext: Paul is sharing his personal transformation in how he thinks about work. He explains that after leaving his traditional job and spending time writing and creating, he discovered he could actually enjoy work rather than just endure it. This was a major revelation that challenged his lifelong assumption that work was inherently something to be tolerated rather than enjoyed. He contrasts his old mindset of work as suffering with his new approach of actively designing work around activities he genuinely likes doing.

vocabulary.definition: To create a system, product, or process that is tailored to accommodate specific preferences or needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'designing around' often refers to user-centered design, where products are developed with a focus on enhancing user experience and satisfaction.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies a proactive approach to problem-solving, suggesting that solutions should be crafted with particular considerations in mind.

vocabulary.definition: An unspoken belief or idea that influences decision-making and behavior without being explicitly acknowledged.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, recognizing hidden assumptions can lead to more effective strategies and innovations by uncovering biases that may hinder progress.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that unexamined beliefs can lead to flawed reasoning or outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: To endure or accept something unpleasant or undesirable without interference.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, employees may need to tolerate certain aspects of their job, such as challenging tasks or difficult colleagues, to maintain productivity and harmony.

insight.nuance: While 'tolerate' suggests a level of endurance, it may imply a lack of satisfaction or enthusiasm, making it less favorable in discussions about workplace culture.

vocabulary.definition: A significant change or alteration in form, structure, or appearance, often resulting in a marked improvement or evolution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, transformation can refer to organizational change initiatives, such as digital transformation, aimed at enhancing efficiency and competitiveness.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a thorough and fundamental change rather than superficial adjustments, suggesting a deep impact on the entity involved.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: Take three hours during a workday. Has to be during a workday. Block off your schedule, sneak out. People can pull this off. Go for a walk without a destination or do something from your childhood that you used to do all the time.
keySentence: Block off your schedule and pay attention to activities from your childhood.
text_ko: 근무일 중 하루에 3시간 정도 확보하세요. 반드시 근무일에 해야 해요. 일정에 그 시간 블록을 잡고 잠깐 자리를 비워도 돼요—사람들 대부분 해낼 수 있어요. 목적지 없이 산책을 하거나, 어릴 때 늘 하던 일을 해보세요. 예전에 농구를 자주 했나요? 그림을 그리곤 했나요? 악기 연주를 자주 했나요? 그리고 그냥 그 순간에 주의를 기울여 보세요.
text_zh: 找个工作日抽出三个小时，一定要是工作日啊。把日程清空，偷偷溜出去。这个大家都能做到的。去随便走走，不用想去哪儿，或者做点小时候经常做的事情。以前爱打篮球吗？爱画画吗？爱弹琴吗？做这些的时候，就静下心来好好感受。
text_es: Tómate tres horas en un día laboral. Tiene que ser en horario de trabajo, ¿eh? Bloquea tu agenda, escápate un rato. La gente lo puede hacer. Sal a caminar sin rumbo fijo o haz algo de cuando eras niño, algo que hacías todo el tiempo. ¿Jugabas básquet? ¿Pintabas? ¿Tocabas algún instrumento? Y simplemente presta atención.
fullContext: Paul is giving practical advice for people who can't take a full sabbatical but want to start exploring alternatives to their current path. He suggests a simple but powerful exercise: taking a few hours during a workday to reconnect with yourself and activities that used to bring you joy. The key is paying attention to what emerges from this experience - how you feel about sneaking away from work, what activities energize you, and what this reveals about your relationship with work and your definition of what it means to be productive.

vocabulary.definition: To reserve a specific time or space for a particular purpose, preventing others from using it.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, blocking off time on a calendar is crucial for ensuring uninterrupted work periods or meetings.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a need for prioritization and can suggest the importance of maintaining focus.

vocabulary.definition: To leave a place quietly and secretly, often to avoid being noticed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, sneaking out might refer to taking an unscheduled break or leaving work early without drawing attention.

insight.nuance: This phrase carries a slightly mischievous connotation, suggesting that the action may not be entirely sanctioned.

vocabulary.definition: To successfully achieve or accomplish something that is challenging or unlikely.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, pulling something off often refers to executing a project or meeting a deadline under tight constraints or with limited resources.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of surprise or admiration at the successful completion of a difficult task.

vocabulary.definition: The process of considering different options or solutions to a problem or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, exploring alternatives is essential for decision-making, allowing teams to evaluate various paths before committing to one.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive and open-minded approach to problem-solving, often indicating a willingness to innovate.

speaker: Paul Millerd
text: I think getting creative, especially now that remote work is so much more common about these opportunities, to let people become the people they want to be. People leave companies because they don't see a path to be the person they want to be.
keySentence: Getting creative allows people to become the people they want to be.
text_ko: 저는 이런 기회들에 대해, 특히 원격 근무(remote work)가 훨씬 더 보편화된 지금, 좀 더 창의적으로 접근해서 사람들이 원하는 모습으로 성장할 수 있게 해야 한다고 생각해요. 사람들은 자신이 되고 싶은 사람이 될 길이 보이지 않으면 회사를 떠나요.
text_zh: 我觉得现在远程办公这么普及，我们得更有创意地给员工提供机会，让他们成为自己想成为的人。员工离职往往就是因为看不到成长路径，觉得在公司里实现不了自己的目标。
text_es: Creo que hay que ser creativos, especialmente ahora que el trabajo remoto es mucho más común, para crear estas oportunidades que permitan a la gente convertirse en quien quieren ser. La gente se va de las empresas porque no ven un camino para llegar a ser la persona que quieren ser.
fullContext: Paul is addressing founders who might worry about offering sabbaticals to employees, fearing they'll lose good people. He reframes this concern by explaining that people actually leave companies when they can't see opportunities for personal growth and becoming who they want to be. Paul suggests that creative approaches to work arrangements, especially with remote work becoming more common, can actually help retain talent by giving people space to develop into the person they aspire to become.

vocabulary.definition: Circumstances or situations that provide a chance for advancement or improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, opportunities often refer to potential markets, partnerships, or innovations that can lead to growth and competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: While 'opportunities' generally have a positive connotation, they can also imply risk if not pursued carefully.

vocabulary.definition: A course of action or development that one follows to achieve a particular goal or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, a 'path' often refers to career progression or the strategic direction a company intends to take.

insight.nuance: The term can suggest a sense of direction and purpose, but may also imply rigidity if not adaptable to change.

vocabulary.definition: Extended breaks from work, often for personal development, research, or rest, typically granted after a period of employment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, sabbaticals are increasingly offered as a benefit to retain talent and encourage employee well-being and creativity.

insight.nuance: While sabbaticals are generally viewed positively, they may be perceived as a luxury in high-pressure environments.

vocabulary.definition: To change the way something is perceived or considered, often by presenting it in a new context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, reframing can be a powerful tool for problem-solving and innovation, allowing teams to view challenges from different angles.

insight.nuance: Reframing is often used in a positive light, but it can also imply manipulation if not done transparently.

speaker: Pete Kazanjy
text: The thing that I just like to encourage founders and product managers and what have you is just don't be afraid of sales.
keySentence: just don't be afraid of sales.
text_ko: 창업자(founders)나 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)분들께 드리고 싶은 말은, 영업(sales)을 너무 두려워하지 말라는 거예요. 영업이 마법 같다고 하거나 “타고난 판매자여야 해”라고 말하는 사람들이 많은데, 사실 전혀 그렇지 않아요. 그런 사람들은 자기 이익을 위해 그런 얘기를 하는 거고요. 그러니까 그런 행동들을 잘 익혀두면 여러모로 도움이 될 거예요.
text_zh: 我就是想鼓励那些创始人、产品经理什么的，千万别害怕销售这件事。外面有很多人会跟你说什么销售很神秘啦，或者"哎呀，你得天生就会卖东西"之类的话，其实根本不是这么回事。这些人就是在为自己说话罢了，所以你把这些销售技能练好了，对你各方面都有好处。
text_es: Lo que me gusta decirles a los fundadores y product managers y demás es simplemente que no le tengan miedo a las ventas. Hay mucha gente por ahí que te va a querer vender el cuento de que es algo mágico o que "ay, tienes que haber nacido para vender" y toda esa historia, pero la verdad es que no es así. Esa gente simplemente está defendiendo su negocio, ¿sabes? Así que ponerte bueno en esas habilidades te va a beneficiar de mil maneras.
fullContext: Lenny asks Pete for his final pieces of wisdom about sales for founders and product managers. Pete emphasizes that sales isn't a mystical skill that requires natural talent, contrary to what some people claim. He explains that the people who perpetuate the myth that sales is magical are simply promoting their own interests or expertise. Pete argues that learning sales behaviors will benefit professionals in many ways, even beyond direct selling situations.

vocabulary.definition: To inspire confidence or support in someone to take action or pursue a goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, encouraging team members can foster a positive work environment and motivate individuals to achieve their targets.

insight.nuance: While 'encourage' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a level of persuasion that may not always be welcomed.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who establish or create a company or organization, often taking on significant risks and responsibilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, founders are crucial as they drive the vision, culture, and initial operations of the business.

insight.nuance: The term 'founder' often carries a sense of innovation and leadership, but can also imply a lack of experience in some contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals responsible for the development, launch, and ongoing management of a product, ensuring it meets market needs and business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech companies, product managers play a pivotal role in bridging the gap between engineering, design, and marketing teams to deliver successful products.

insight.nuance: The role of a product manager can vary significantly between organizations, sometimes encompassing strategic, technical, and customer-focused responsibilities.

vocabulary.definition: A seemingly magical or extraordinary ability that is not easily understood or explained, often associated with intuition or creativity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In creative industries or startups, a 'mystical skill' may refer to an individual's unique talent that drives innovation or problem-solving.

insight.nuance: While 'mystical skill' can evoke admiration, it may also imply a lack of tangible evidence or replicability in a business context.

speaker: Pete Kazanjy
text: Never mistake your lead gen for your business.
keySentence: Never mistake your lead gen for your business.
text_ko: 리드 생성(lead gen)을 당신의 비즈니스 그 자체로 착각하지 마세요. 좋은 소식은 많은 사람들이 그 과정에서 시행착오를 많이 겪으면서 배웠다는 거예요. 아마 슬랙은 그걸 거의 놓칠 뻔했는데, 결국 세일즈포스 출신 등 여러 사람들을 영입해서 바로잡았어요.
text_zh: 千万别把获客渠道当成你的核心业务。我觉得好消息是很多人在这方面都吃过亏，大家也都学到了教训。Slack可能差点在这上面栽跟头，但后来他们找来了一批Salesforce的人和其他行业老手。
text_es: Nunca confundas tu generación de leads (lead gen) con tu negocio real. Lo bueno es que mucha gente se pegó buenos golpes ahí y aprendió la lección. Slack casi la cagó con eso, pero luego trajeron a un montón de gente de Salesforce y otras empresas que sabían del tema.
fullContext: Lenny asks Pete whether founders have to get good at sales, especially those building PLG (product-led growth) companies. Pete explains why many PLG companies eventually need to add sales teams to scale beyond their initial self-serve motion. He uses Dropbox as an example of a company that may have delayed building sales capabilities too long, and contrasts it with Slack which successfully added enterprise sales.

vocabulary.definition: The process of identifying and attracting potential customers for a business's products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, lead generation is crucial for building a sales pipeline and converting prospects into paying customers.

insight.nuance: While lead generation is essential, it should not be confused with actual sales or revenue, as it merely represents potential opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: A business strategy that relies on the product itself as the primary driver of customer acquisition, retention, and expansion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, product-led growth emphasizes creating a product that delivers value and encourages users to spread the word, often leading to organic growth.

insight.nuance: This approach contrasts with sales-led strategies, where sales teams primarily drive growth through direct outreach and engagement.

vocabulary.definition: The ability of a business to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance or losing revenue potential.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, scaling often refers to expanding operations, increasing production, or enhancing service delivery to accommodate a larger customer base.

insight.nuance: Scaling should be approached carefully to ensure that quality and customer satisfaction are maintained as the business grows.

vocabulary.definition: Groups of individuals within an organization responsible for selling products or services and managing customer relationships.
vocabulary.businessContext: Sales teams play a critical role in driving revenue, often working closely with marketing and customer service to ensure a cohesive approach to customer engagement.

insight.nuance: The effectiveness of sales teams can vary based on their structure, training, and alignment with overall business strategy.

speaker: Pete Kazanjy
text: The way to think about what sellers are is they're the microeconomic agents in the market that bring supply to demand rather than waiting for demand to find supply.
keySentence: Sellers are microeconomic agents bringing supply to demand, elucidating needs.
text_ko: 판매자를 이해하는 한 가지 방식은, 그들이 시장에서 수요가 공급을 찾아오길 기다리지 않고 공급을 수요 쪽으로 가져다주는 미시경제적 행위자들(microeconomic agents)이라고 보는 거예요. 판매자들은 공급을 항상 가지고 다니면서, 지금 당장 수요를 가지고 있거나 본인은 모를 수도 있는 사람들을 찾아다니고, 왜 그들이 그 수요를 가져야 하는지(또는 그 제품·서비스가 왜 필요한지)를 설명해줘요.
text_zh: 销售人员其实就是市场里的微观经济主体(microeconomic agents)，他们的作用是主动把供应推向需求，而不是坐等需求自己找上门。他们手里握着货源，到处跑着找那些应该有需求的人——有些人现在就有需求，有些人还没意识到自己有需求，然后销售就去给他们分析为什么他们应该有这个需求。
text_es: La forma de entender a los vendedores es que son los agentes microeconómicos del mercado que llevan la oferta hacia la demanda, en lugar de esperar a que la demanda encuentre la oferta. Tienen la oferta guardada bajo la manga y salen a buscar gente que debería tener esa demanda - tal vez ya la tienen, tal vez no se dan cuenta de que la tienen - y entonces les explican por qué deberían tenerla.
fullContext: Lenny asks Pete to explain what "modern sales" means versus traditional or old-school sales. Pete reframes the perception of salespeople from the stereotypical "sleazy used car salesman" image to viewing them as economic facilitators. He describes modern sales as a more thoughtful, measurable approach where salespeople actively connect solutions to problems in the market, rather than waiting for customers to discover solutions on their own.

vocabulary.definition: Microeconomic refers to the branch of economics that studies individual agents, such as households and firms, and their interactions in markets.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, microeconomic principles are used to analyze consumer behavior, pricing strategies, and the allocation of resources within a company.

insight.nuance: While microeconomic focuses on small-scale economic factors, it is often contrasted with macroeconomic, which looks at the economy as a whole.

vocabulary.definition: Agents are individuals or entities that act on behalf of others in economic transactions, influencing market dynamics through their decisions and actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, agents can refer to sales representatives, brokers, or any party that facilitates transactions between buyers and sellers.

insight.nuance: The term 'agents' can imply a level of authority or responsibility, distinguishing them from mere participants in a market.

vocabulary.definition: Supply and demand is an economic model that describes the relationship between the quantity of a good or service available and the desire of consumers to purchase it.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding supply and demand is crucial for pricing strategies, inventory management, and forecasting sales trends.

insight.nuance: The concept is foundational in economics, but its application can vary widely across different markets and industries.

vocabulary.definition: To reframe means to change the way a situation or concept is perceived, often by presenting it in a new context or perspective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, reframing can be used in marketing strategies to alter consumer perceptions or in problem-solving to find innovative solutions.

insight.nuance: Reframing is often employed in negotiations or conflict resolution to shift focus from problems to opportunities.

speaker: Pete Kazanjy
text: You really just can't do that, not for the first couple dozen customers, it's just not tenable. You lose that feedback loop, you lose the learnings of whether or not your message fits the market, all that sort of stuff.
keySentence: You lose that feedback loop, you lose the learnings of whether or not your message fits the market.
text_ko: 그건 정말로 할 수 없어요, 처음 몇십 명의 고객을 위해서는 더더욱 그렇고요. 피드백 루프(feedback loop)를 잃게 되면, 메시지가 시장에 맞는지에 대한 배움도 놓치게 돼요. 그렇게 되면 제3자 판매자와 전화게임을 하는 것과 같고요. 처음에는 그 모든 걸 한 사람의 머릿속에 두고 시작한 다음, 패키징해서 반복 가능한 판매 루프(selling while loop)가 생기면 그때 다른 사람에게 넘기는 게 좋죠.
text_zh: 这样做真的不行，至少前几十个客户不能这么搞，根本站不住脚。你会失去反馈循环(feedback loop)，学不到你的信息是否符合市场需求，这些东西都没了。通过第三方销售就像在玩传话游戏一样，还不如一开始就自己掌控全局，等摸清套路了再打包。等你有了可重复的销售循环(selling while loop)，再包装好交给别人去做。
text_es: Simplemente no puedes hacer eso, no con los primeros veinte o treinta clientes, no es viable. Pierdes ese ciclo de retroalimentación (feedback loop), pierdes el aprendizaje de si tu mensaje realmente conecta con el mercado, todas esas cosas. Es como jugar al teléfono roto con un vendedor externo, cuando lo que realmente necesitas es mantener todo eso en una sola cabeza al principio, luego empaquetarlo, y cuando ya tengas un proceso repetible de venta, un bucle de venta (selling while loop) que funcione, ahí sí lo empaquetas y se lo pasas a alguien más.
fullContext: Pete explains why founders must do sales themselves initially rather than outsourcing it to hired salespeople. He describes founder-led sales as the natural sequel to customer development and product building phases. Pete argues that founders are uniquely positioned to become experts at selling their solution because they understand the problem and technology better than any third party could initially learn to.

vocabulary.definition: Able to be maintained or defended against criticism or attack; reasonable or valid.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a tenable strategy or approach is one that can be realistically implemented and sustained over time, particularly in the face of challenges or competition.

insight.nuance: While 'tenable' suggests a level of viability, it often implies that the situation may be precarious and requires ongoing support to remain valid.

vocabulary.definition: A system where outputs of a process are circled back and used as inputs, creating a continuous cycle of improvement or adjustment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, feedback loops are crucial for refining products and services based on customer input, ensuring that offerings align with market needs.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a dynamic and iterative process, emphasizing the importance of responsiveness to feedback rather than static decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Insights or knowledge gained from experience, particularly through analysis or reflection on past actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'learnings' often refer to the valuable lessons derived from both successes and failures, which inform future strategies and decisions.

insight.nuance: The term is informal and may be perceived as jargon; in formal writing, 'insights' or 'lessons learned' might be preferred.

vocabulary.definition: Refers to a product, service, or message that aligns well with the needs, preferences, and expectations of the target audience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market analysis, determining whether something 'fits the market' is essential for ensuring that offerings resonate with consumers and achieve commercial success.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests not only compatibility but also a strategic alignment that can lead to competitive advantage; it is often used in discussions about product-market fit.

speaker: Pete Kazanjy
text: What ends up happening is it's just a skill. You just start doing it, you start doing it, you start doing it, and you just become used to it, you become calloused. You're like, "I'm incorrigible now.
keySentence: Sales is a skill; you become calloused and incorrigible over time.
text_ko: 결국엔 그냥 기술이에요. 계속 하다 보면 자연스럽게 되고 익숙해져서 무뎌져요. 이제는 '아, 나 고쳐지지 않겠구나'라고 느낄 정도예요. 엘리베이터에 넣어놔도 누구하고든 얘기할 수 있어요.
text_zh: 结果就是这变成了一种技能。你就是不断地练，不断地练，不断地练，然后就习惯了，就练出厚脸皮了。你会想："我现在是没救了，把我扔电梯里，我跟谁都能聊。"
text_es: Lo que termina pasando es que simplemente se vuelve una habilidad. Empiezas a hacerlo, sigues haciéndolo, sigues haciéndolo, y te acostumbras completamente, te vuelves como inmune. Llegas al punto donde dices: "Ya no hay quien me pare. Me metes en un ascensor y puedo hablar con cualquiera."
fullContext: Lenny asks Pete for his number one tip for getting better at sales. Pete first explains that sales requires a major mindset shift - from working with the same few people daily to meeting multiple new people every day and managing parallel conversations. He describes how this initially uncomfortable behavior becomes natural through repetition, comparing it to building calluses through repeated practice.

vocabulary.definition: A mindset shift refers to a fundamental change in the way an individual thinks about a particular situation, challenge, or opportunity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a mindset shift can be crucial for innovation and adapting to new market conditions, often leading to improved strategies and outcomes.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in discussions about personal development and organizational change, implying a positive transformation in perspective.

vocabulary.definition: Incorrigible describes a person or behavior that is resistant to correction or reform, often implying a stubbornness in habits or attitudes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, labeling an employee as incorrigible may suggest they are unlikely to change their ineffective practices despite feedback or training.

insight.nuance: While it can carry a negative connotation, it may also be used humorously or endearingly in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A skill is the ability to perform tasks and solve problems effectively, often acquired through practice and experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, skills are essential for executing tasks, driving productivity, and achieving organizational goals, making skill development a priority for many companies.

insight.nuance: The term can refer to both hard skills (technical abilities) and soft skills (interpersonal abilities), and context is important to clarify which type is being discussed.

vocabulary.definition: Calloused describes a state of being emotionally or mentally hardened, often as a result of repeated exposure to difficult situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, being calloused may indicate a level of resilience or desensitization to stress, which can be both beneficial and detrimental depending on the context.

insight.nuance: While it can imply strength and endurance, it may also suggest a lack of empathy or emotional engagement, so care should be taken in its use.

speaker: Pete Kazanjy
text: As a seller, the way that I like to frame it to people is that you're a consultant that has a particular predilection for a given solution, your solution. Use Atrium as an example.
keySentence: you're a consultant that has a particular predilection for a given solution, your solution.
text_ko: 판매자로서 제가 사람들에게 설명하는 방식은, 여러분이 특정 솔루션에 대한 선호가 있는 컨설턴트라는 거예요. 예를 들어 Atrium을 생각해보면, Atrium의 최소 ICP는 아마도 조직 내에서 SDR과 AE가 10명에서 300명 정도는 되어야 할 것 같아요. 그래서 누군가가 나타나서 "아, 나 정말 세일즈를 잘해야 해, 너희 소프트웨어를 사야겠어, Pete"라고 하면, 제가 "좋아, 세일즈맨이 몇 명이나 있어?"라고 물어볼 거예요. 그 사람이 "한 명 있어요"라고 대답하면, 저는 "아, Atrium은 팔지 않을 거야"라고 말할 거예요.
text_zh: 作为销售，我喜欢这样跟大家说：你其实就是个咨询顾问，只不过你对某个特定的解决方案情有独钟，也就是你自己的产品。拿Atrium举例吧，Atrium的最小理想客户画像(ICP)大概是一个组织里要有SDR加AE总共10到300人这样。所以如果有人过来跟我说："哥们，我得把销售搞好，我要买你的软件，Pete。"我就会问："行啊，那你们有多少销售？"他们说："就一个人。"我就会说："兄弟，那我不会卖Atrium给你的。"
text_es: Como vendedor, la forma en que me gusta planteárselo a la gente es que eres un consultor que tiene una preferencia particular por una solución específica, tu solución. Usa Atrium como ejemplo. El ICP mínimo de Atrium probablemente son SDRs más AEs en una organización que debería estar entre 10 hasta 300. Entonces, si llega alguien y me dice, "Oye, tengo que volverme muy bueno en ventas, necesito comprar tu software, Pete," y yo le digo, "Perfecto. ¿Cuántos vendedores tienes?" Y me responde, "Tengo uno." Le voy a decir, "Mira, no te voy a vender Atrium."
fullContext: Lenny asks Pete about shifting mindset from trying to convince someone to buy something to trying to help them. Pete contrasts old-school sales (like "selling ice to an Eskimo") with modern sales where you act as a consultant with expertise in a particular solution. He gives a practical example of how he would actually refuse to sell Atrium to someone who doesn't fit their ideal customer profile, even if they want to buy.

vocabulary.definition: To present or structure information in a particular way to influence perception or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, framing is often used in marketing and sales to shape how a product or service is perceived by potential customers.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of strategic presentation, suggesting that the way information is framed can significantly affect decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: A professional who provides expert advice in a particular area, often to organizations or businesses.
vocabulary.businessContext: Consultants are commonly hired to offer specialized knowledge and insights that help companies improve performance or solve specific problems.

insight.nuance: While often associated with external advisors, the term can also apply to internal experts who provide guidance within an organization.

vocabulary.definition: A preference or inclination towards a particular option or course of action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding a client's predilection can help tailor solutions that align with their specific needs and desires.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a strong bias or fondness, suggesting that the preference is not merely casual but rather significant.

vocabulary.definition: A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation, often in the form of a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, solutions are typically developed to address specific challenges faced by clients, enhancing operational efficiency or effectiveness.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a comprehensive approach to problem-solving, rather than just a quick fix, and is often associated with innovation.

speaker: Peter Deng
text: I think education is going to change in a big way. And I think a lot about this because I'm involved in my kid's school quite a bit, and that's something I've done after I left OpenAI.
keySentence: I think education is going to change in a big way.
text_ko: 교육이 크게 변할 거라고 생각해요. 제가 아이 학교에 많이 참여하고 있어서 이 부분에 대해 많이 고민하게 되는데, OpenAI를 떠난 이후로 계속 그렇게 하고 있어요. 그리고 저에게 흥미로운 점은, 제 아들이 공개되기 전에 OpenAI의 여러 제품을 사용해 본 경험이 있다는 거예요. 그때 그가 ChatGPT 같은 최신 모델을 가지고 놀 때, 아홉 살이었는데, 그의 사고 방식이 이미 바뀌고 있는 걸 느낄 수 있었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得教育肯定会有翻天覆地的变化。我经常想这个问题，因为离开OpenAI之后，我在我儿子学校那边参与得挺多的。最让我觉得神奇的是，看着我儿子体验那些OpenAI还没公开的产品——我觉得可以这么说吧，应该没什么问题。当时他才九岁，在玩ChatGPT和一些最新的模型时，我已经能看出来他的思维方式在发生变化。
text_es: Creo que la educación va a cambiar de manera radical. Y pienso mucho en esto porque estoy bastante involucrado en el colegio de mi hijo, algo que he estado haciendo después de dejar OpenAI. Y lo que me parece fascinante es que al ver a mi hijo, que pudo probar internamente (dog food) un montón de cosas de OpenAI antes de que fueran públicas, creo que puedo decir con seguridad que eso estuvo bien. Y cuando estaba jugando con ChatGPT y algunos de los modelos más recientes - tenía nueve años en ese momento - ya podía ver cómo se le estaba reconfigurando el cerebro.
fullContext: Lenny asks Peter what specific thing will change in a big way with AI that people don't think enough about. Peter explains that education will transform dramatically as young people's minds adapt to AI tools. He shares how his nine-year-old son used ChatGPT and other OpenAI models before they were public, and Peter observed how exposure to AI at an early age was literally changing how his son's brain processed information and approached problems.

vocabulary.definition: To make a significant change in form, appearance, or character; to convert or alter fundamentally.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'transform' often refers to the process of changing business models, operations, or strategies to improve efficiency or adapt to market demands.

insight.nuance: While 'transform' implies a thorough and often positive change, it can also suggest upheaval or disruption, so it should be used carefully in contexts where stability is valued.

vocabulary.definition: In a striking or noticeable manner; significantly or substantially.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, 'dramatically' is often used to describe substantial changes in performance metrics, market trends, or organizational shifts that capture attention.

insight.nuance: This term carries a sense of urgency or intensity, making it suitable for emphasizing major changes, but it may be overused in less significant contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Being engaged or participating actively in a particular activity or situation; having a role or connection.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being 'involved' often refers to stakeholders or team members who actively contribute to projects, decisions, or organizational processes.

insight.nuance: While 'involved' suggests active participation, it can also imply complexity or entanglement, so it should be used with awareness of the context.

vocabulary.definition: To adjust or modify something in response to changing conditions or environments; to become suitable for a new purpose.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, 'adapt' is crucial for organizations that must respond to market changes, technological advancements, or consumer preferences to remain competitive.

insight.nuance: The term 'adapt' suggests a proactive approach to change, which is generally positive, but it may also imply a struggle to keep up with rapid developments.

speaker: Peter Deng
text: Sometimes your product actually doesn't matter. At Uber, I learned this because, really, the price and the ETA at Uber was the product. Looking at it from a holistic perspective, we humans consume the entirety of the product.
keySentence: Humans consume the entirety of the product, not just fixing bugs.
text_ko: 사실 때로는 제품(product) 자체가 크게 중요하지 않을 때가 있어요. 우버에서 일하면서 그걸 배웠어요. 우버에서는 사실 가격과 도착 예정 시간(ETA)이 곧 그 제품이나 마찬가지였거든요. 전체적인 관점에서 보면 사람들은 제품 전체의 경험을 소비해요. 버그(bug)를 안 고치라는 얘기는 아니에요. 다만 사람들에게 더 중요한 것들에 비하면 그런 건 영향력이 크지 않을 때가 많아요.
text_zh: 有时候你的产品本身其实没那么重要。我在优步(Uber)的时候就发现了这一点，因为说白了，优步真正的产品就是价格和预估到达时间(ETA)。从整体角度来看，我们人类消费的是整个产品体验。这不是说你不用修bug，而是这些东西的影响力远不如那些用户真正在意的东西。
text_es: A veces tu producto en realidad no importa tanto. En Uber aprendí esto porque, la verdad, el precio y el tiempo estimado de llegada eran realmente el producto. Si lo ves desde una perspectiva más amplia, nosotros como usuarios consumimos la experiencia completa del producto. No es que no debas arreglar el bug, pero no va a tener tanto impacto como algo que realmente le importa más a la gente.
fullContext: Lenny asks Peter about the most counterintuitive lesson he's learned about building products. Peter shares a hard-learned insight from his time leading the Uber Rider product team - that the digital interface and app features he was optimizing weren't actually the core product. Instead, the real product was the operational elements like pricing and estimated time of arrival, which had much more impact on user satisfaction than any UI improvements.

vocabulary.definition: Contrary to what one would intuitively expect; an outcome or idea that seems illogical or unexpected at first glance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a counterintuitive strategy may lead to surprising results, such as prioritizing customer experience over immediate profit, which can ultimately enhance brand loyalty.

insight.nuance: This term is often used to highlight ideas that challenge conventional wisdom, making it suitable for discussions about innovative or disruptive practices.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or considering the whole rather than just the parts; an approach that emphasizes the interconnectedness of components within a system.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a holistic approach might involve integrating various departments to improve overall efficiency and customer satisfaction, rather than optimizing each department in isolation.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a sense of comprehensive understanding and is often used in discussions about strategy, management, and wellness in corporate environments.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of regarding something; a point of view that influences how one interprets information or situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding different perspectives is crucial for effective decision-making, as it allows leaders to consider diverse viewpoints and potential impacts on stakeholders.

insight.nuance: This term can imply a subjective interpretation, making it important to clarify whether one is discussing a personal or organizational perspective.

vocabulary.definition: The whole of something; the complete and undivided state of an object or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, considering the entirety of a product or service can lead to better strategic decisions, as it encompasses all aspects that affect customer experience and satisfaction.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes completeness and is often used in contexts where a full understanding is necessary, such as in assessments or evaluations.

speaker: Peter Deng
text: You have to plan your chess moves out in advance. You have to really think before you act and build systems that were going to let you go sustainably faster.
keySentence: Plan your chess moves out in advance to achieve hyperscale sustainably faster.
text_ko: 체스처럼 몇 수 앞을 미리 내다보고 계획해야 해요. 행동하기 전에 충분히 생각하고, 속도를 내되 지속 가능하게 더 빨리 움직일 수 있게 해주는 시스템을 만들어야 해요. 왜냐하면 제로 투 원(zero to one)은 제품-시장 적합도(product-market fit)를 찾는 단계이고, 1에서 100(1 to 100)은 가능한 한 빨리 하이퍼스케일(hyperscale)에 도달할 수 있도록 준비하는 단계이기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 你得提前规划好每一步棋。在行动之前必须深思熟虑，搭建能让你可持续快速发展的体系。因为从零到一(zero to one)阶段，你要找的是产品市场契合度(product market fit)，而到了一到一百(one to 100)阶段，你得确保能以最快速度实现超大规模增长(hyperscale)。
text_es: Tienes que planear tus jugadas de ajedrez con anticipación. Realmente tienes que pensar bien antes de actuar y crear sistemas que te permitan crecer de manera sostenible y más rápido. Porque en la fase de cero a uno estás tratando de encontrar ese ajuste producto-mercado (product market fit), y después cuando llegas a la fase de uno a cien, tienes que asegurarte de poder llegar al hiperescalamiento (hyperscale) lo más rápido posible.
fullContext: Lenny asks Peter about important lessons for building products from idea to billions of users, drawing on Peter's experience scaling products like Facebook Newsfeed, Messenger, Instagram, and ChatGPT.
