insight.nuance: This term often conveys a sense of depth and seriousness, suggesting that the differences are not superficial but rather intrinsic.

vocabulary.definition: Introducing or using new ideas, methods, or products; characterized by originality and creativity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, being innovative is crucial for companies to differentiate themselves and capture market share.

insight.nuance: While 'innovative' is generally viewed positively, it can imply a risk of failure if the new ideas are not well-received or executed.

vocabulary.definition: A set of strategies, guidelines, or best practices for achieving specific goals or handling particular situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, the absence of a playbook means that entrepreneurs must create their own strategies based on unique circumstances and challenges.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a structured approach, but in dynamic environments, flexibility and adaptation are equally important.

speaker: Scott Belsky
text: I always tell them to optimize for the problems they want to have.
keySentence: optimize for the problems they want to have.
text_ko: 저는 항상 이렇게 말해요. 당신이 '겪고 싶어 하는' 문제들에 맞춰 최적화하라고요. 예를 들어 고객들이 퍼널(funnel)을 잘 통과해서 성공감을 느끼고, 제품을 써서 가치를 얻은 다음에 "아, 그런데 이 플랫폼(platform)에도 필요해요", "이런 기능(capability)이 필요해요", "이걸 공유하고 싶어요"라고 말하게 되는 그런 문제들을 원한다는 거예요. 그런 문제들이 생기길 바라니까 지금 당장 그런 기능(features)을 만들지 마세요.
text_zh: 我总是跟他们说，要为你想要的问题做优化。你希望遇到的问题应该是客户顺利通过你的漏斗(funnel)，感到成功，使用你的产品并获得价值，然后对你说："哎，但是我需要在这个平台上用，或者我需要这个功能，或者我想能够分享这个。" 我的意思是你就想要这些问题。所以现在别急着做那些功能。
text_es: Siempre les digo que se enfoquen en los problemas que sí quieren tener. Quieren el problema de que los clientes pasen por su embudo (funnel), se sientan exitosos, usen su producto y obtengan valor, y después les digan: "Oye, pero lo necesito en esta plataforma, o necesito esta funcionalidad, o quiero poder compartir esto." O sea, esos son los problemas que quieren tener. Así que no desarrollen esas características ahorita.
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott about his advice to only build half the features you want to build and how to decide which features to include in an MVP. Scott explains his philosophy of prioritizing the core user journey over additional features. He believes teams should focus on eliminating fundamental barriers that prevent users from experiencing value, rather than building nice-to-have features that users will only request once they're already engaged.

vocabulary.definition: To make the best or most effective use of a resource or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, optimizing often refers to improving processes, systems, or products to enhance performance and efficiency.

insight.nuance: While 'optimize' suggests a focus on improvement, it can imply a trade-off where certain aspects may be sacrificed for greater overall effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: The act of arranging or dealing with tasks or issues in order of importance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, prioritizing is crucial for resource allocation, project management, and strategic planning to ensure that the most critical tasks are addressed first.

insight.nuance: Prioritizing can sometimes imply a difficult choice, as it may require setting aside less urgent tasks in favor of those deemed more critical.

vocabulary.definition: The central or most important part of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'core' often refers to the essential functions, values, or competencies that define a company's identity and strategic focus.

insight.nuance: Using 'core' can convey a sense of fundamental importance, suggesting that the element in question is indispensable to the overall structure or mission.

vocabulary.definition: Distinctive attributes or aspects of a product or service that provide value to users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and product development, features are critical for differentiating products in the market and enhancing user experience.

insight.nuance: While 'features' can refer to positive attributes, it is important to ensure they align with customer needs to avoid overcomplicating offerings.

speaker: Scott Belsky
text: In the first 30 seconds of using a new product, you are lazy, vain, and selfish. You want to get it done super quickly. You want to look good to your colleagues or to your friends.
keySentence: You are lazy, vain, and selfish when using a new product; avoid learning curves.
text_ko: 새 제품을 처음 써보는 첫 30초 동안은 사람들은 게으르고, 허영심 많고, 이기적이에요. 일은 정말 빨리 끝내고 싶어하고, 동료나 친구들에게 잘 보이고 싶어해요. 이 제품을 쓰면서 금방 성공한 느낌을 받고 싶어해요. 제품 투어를 보거나 뭔가를 읽고 싶지 않고, 어떤 학습 곡선(learning curve)도 겪고 싶어하지 않아요.
text_zh: 用户在使用新产品的前30秒，基本上都是懒、爱面子、还很自私的。他们就想快速搞定，想在同事或朋友面前显得很厉害，想马上就有成就感。他们可不想看什么产品介绍，也不想读说明，更不想经历任何学习过程。
text_es: En los primeros 30 segundos usando un producto nuevo, eres flojo, vanidoso y egoísta. Quieres que todo salga súper rápido. Quieres quedar bien con tus colegas o amigos. Quieres sentirte exitoso de inmediato al usar este producto. No quieres tener que ver un tutorial ni leer nada, en realidad no quieres lidiar con ninguna curva de aprendizaje (learning curve).
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott how he built his product sense and what advice he has for younger PMs. Scott explains his framework about the psychology of first-time users, describing what he calls the 'first mile' experience. He argues that understanding human psychology is crucial for product development, particularly recognizing that new users have very specific mental states and low tolerance for friction when they first encounter a product.

vocabulary.definition: Product sense refers to an individual's ability to understand and evaluate the needs of users and the market to create effective products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, product sense is crucial for product managers and designers to ensure that products resonate with users and meet market demands.

insight.nuance: Having strong product sense implies a deep intuition about user behavior and market trends, often developed through experience and observation.

vocabulary.definition: First-time users are individuals who are experiencing a product or service for the very first time.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the behavior and expectations of first-time users is vital for businesses, as it helps in designing onboarding experiences that can lead to higher retention rates.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the initial experience, which can significantly influence a user's perception and future engagement with the product.

vocabulary.definition: A framework is a structured approach or system that provides guidance for solving problems or developing projects.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, frameworks are often used to standardize processes, facilitate collaboration, and ensure consistency across teams and projects.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a level of flexibility within a structured approach, allowing for adaptation while still adhering to core principles.

vocabulary.definition: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior, exploring how individuals think, feel, and act.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding psychology is essential for marketing, user experience design, and organizational behavior, as it helps in predicting consumer behavior and improving employee engagement.

insight.nuance: The term often carries connotations of understanding deeper motivations and behaviors, which can be critical in tailoring strategies to meet user needs.

speaker: Scott Belsky
text: If you've lost conviction, you should not be doing what you're doing in the world of entrepreneurship. And I'll tell you, I get different answers. Some people are like, "Oh, Scott, I mean, I have more conviction.
keySentence: If you've lost conviction, you should not be doing what you're doing in the world of entrepreneurship.
text_ko: 확신을 잃었다면, 기업가 정신의 세계에서 지금 하고 있는 일을 계속하면 안 돼요. 제가 여러 사람에게 물어보면, 반응이 다 달라요. 어떤 사람들은 "아, 스콧, 나는 더 확신이 있어요. 내가 배운 것들, 고객들한테 받은 검증들, 아직 해결하지 못한 것들 뿐이에요. 이게 나를 미치게 해요."라고 하더라고요.
text_zh: 如果你对自己做的事情没信心了，那你就不应该搞创业这一套。我跟你说，我得到的回答各种各样。有些人会说："哦，Scott，我的信心其实更足了。我学到的这些东西，客户给我的这些验证，我们只是还没找到门道而已。这事儿快把我逼疯了。"
text_es: Si has perdido la convicción, no deberías estar haciendo lo que estás haciendo en el mundo del emprendimiento. Y te digo, recibo respuestas muy diferentes. Algunas personas me dicen: "Ay, Scott, o sea, tengo más convicción que nunca. Todo lo que he aprendido, toda la validación que he recibido de los clientes, simplemente no hemos dado en el clavo todavía. Me tiene loco."
fullContext: Lenny asks about Scott's advice on when founders should quit versus persevere through difficult times. Scott shares his framework for helping founders make this decision by asking them to evaluate their current conviction level compared to when they started. He explains that founders who maintain or increase conviction despite setbacks should continue, while those who have lost belief in their solution should consider pivoting or quitting entirely.

vocabulary.definition: A firmly held belief or opinion that is often accompanied by a strong sense of certainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, conviction refers to the strong belief in one's ideas, products, or strategies, which can inspire confidence among investors, employees, and customers.

insight.nuance: While conviction can be a positive driving force, excessive conviction without evidence can lead to stubbornness or poor decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: The process of starting and operating a new business, typically characterized by innovation and risk-taking.
vocabulary.businessContext: Entrepreneurship is crucial in the business landscape as it drives economic growth, creates jobs, and fosters innovation through the establishment of startups and new ventures.

insight.nuance: Entrepreneurship often implies a willingness to take risks and face challenges, and it is not limited to starting new businesses but also includes scaling and sustaining them.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides guidance and support for understanding or addressing a particular issue or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, frameworks are used to develop strategies, analyze problems, and guide decision-making, such as the SWOT analysis or business model canvas.

insight.nuance: While frameworks provide valuable structure, they should be adapted to fit specific contexts rather than applied rigidly.

vocabulary.definition: To assess or appraise the value, quality, or significance of something based on specific criteria.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, evaluating performance, projects, or strategies is essential for making informed decisions and optimizing resources.

insight.nuance: Evaluation should be objective and based on data, but it can also involve subjective judgment depending on the context and criteria used.

speaker: Scott Belsky
text: I love bringing design upstream. In fact, that's probably been the cheat code of my career as a product leader, has just been disproportionately empowering design throughout the process.
keySentence: Bringing design upstream has been the cheat code of my career as a product leader.
text_ko: 저는 디자인을 초기 단계부터 참여시키는 걸 정말 좋아해요(bringing design upstream). 사실 제품 리더로서 제 커리어에서 그게 거의 치트 코드(cheat code)였어요 — 프로세스 전반에 걸쳐 디자인에 훨씬 더 많은 권한을 실어준 것이죠.
text_zh: 我特别喜欢把设计往前提，提到整个流程的上游去。说实话，这可能就是我作为产品负责人的一个秘诀吧，就是在整个过程中给设计更大的话语权，让它发挥更重要的作用。
text_es: Me encanta meter el diseño desde el principio del proceso. De hecho, esa ha sido probablemente la clave secreta de mi carrera como líder de producto: darle un peso desproporcionadamente grande al diseño en todo el proceso.
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott about how he's helping PMs at Adobe leverage AI tools and new ways of working. Scott explains his approach to product development, emphasizing the importance of involving designers earlier in the product development process rather than just at the end for visual execution. He describes this as collapsing traditional organizational boundaries between product management and design functions.

vocabulary.definition: Providing someone with the authority or power to do something, often leading to increased confidence and autonomy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, empowering employees can enhance decision-making capabilities and foster innovation by encouraging initiative and ownership.

insight.nuance: While empowering is generally positive, it should be used carefully to ensure that it does not lead to a lack of accountability.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is out of proportion or not in balance, often referring to an unequal distribution of effects or resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business analysis, one might find that certain groups or sectors are disproportionately affected by market changes or policy decisions.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a critical connotation, suggesting unfairness or imbalance that warrants attention.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to processes or activities that occur earlier in a supply chain or development cycle, often influencing subsequent stages.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development, bringing design upstream means integrating design considerations at the initial stages to enhance overall product quality.

insight.nuance: While commonly used in supply chain contexts, it can also apply metaphorically to any early-stage influence in a process.

vocabulary.definition: To use something to maximum advantage, often referring to resources, skills, or relationships to achieve a desired outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, companies leverage their assets, such as technology or partnerships, to gain competitive advantages and drive growth.

insight.nuance: Leverage can imply a strategic use of resources, but overuse may suggest manipulation or exploitation, which can have negative connotations.

speaker: Scott Belsky
text: If resources are carbs, resourcefulness is like muscle. It stays with you. It makes you stronger, and it helps you have a better intuition and better performance over time.
keySentence: Resourcefulness brings you further than resources, making you stronger over time.
text_ko: 자원(resources)이 탄수화물이라면, 자원 활용력(resourcefulness)은 근육 같아요. 몸에 남아서 점점 더 강하게 해주고, 시간이 지날수록 직관력과 성과도 더 좋아지게 해줘요. 지난 7~10년 동안 사실상 모든 문제에 자원을 쏟아부었지만, 저는 항상 자원 활용력(resourcefulness)이 자원(resources)보다 더 멀리 데려다준다는 걸 느껴왔어요.
text_zh: 如果说资源就像碳水化合物的话，那么机智应变(resourcefulness)就像肌肉一样。它会一直跟着你，让你变得更强，时间长了你的直觉会更准，表现也会更好。我一直觉得机智应变比光有资源更能让你走得远，虽然这七八年来，我们基本上遇到什么问题都是拿资源砸。
text_es: Si los recursos son como los carbohidratos, el ingenio es como el músculo. Se queda contigo. Te hace más fuerte y te ayuda a desarrollar mejor intuición y mejor rendimiento con el tiempo. Siempre he visto que el ingenio te lleva más lejos que los recursos, a pesar de que en los últimos siete a diez años básicamente hemos estado tirando recursos a cada problema que surge.
fullContext: Scott shares his final words of wisdom for product builders, focusing on the current economic environment where companies have fewer resources. He contrasts the recent trend of solving problems by throwing money and headcount at them versus being forced to find more creative, efficient solutions. Scott argues this resource-constrained environment actually creates opportunities for teams to develop stronger problem-solving capabilities.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to find quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties or solve problems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, resourcefulness is crucial for entrepreneurs and teams to navigate challenges, optimize limited resources, and innovate under pressure.

insight.nuance: While often associated with creativity, resourcefulness implies a practical approach to problem-solving rather than just theoretical ideas.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, intuition can guide decision-making processes, especially in uncertain or rapidly changing environments where data may be incomplete.

insight.nuance: Intuition is often seen as a valuable complement to analytical thinking, but relying solely on it can lead to biased decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The act of carrying out or accomplishing a task or function, often measured against established standards or expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: Performance metrics are critical in evaluating employee effectiveness, project outcomes, and overall organizational success in business environments.

insight.nuance: While performance typically refers to measurable outcomes, it can also encompass qualitative aspects such as teamwork and leadership.

vocabulary.definition: The overall state of the economy in which businesses operate, including factors like inflation, employment rates, and consumer behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the economic environment is essential for strategic planning and risk management, as it influences market opportunities and operational costs.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a broader context that includes both macroeconomic indicators and microeconomic factors affecting specific industries.

speaker: Scott Belsky
text: Creative professionals can now explore 10X the surface area of possibility. These tools are making them so much more efficient. And some people are like, "Oh my gosh, creative pros are going to be replaced." No. No, no, no. They're not.
keySentence: Creative pros explore 10X the surface area of possibility, finding 10X better solutions.
text_ko: 크리에이티브 전문가들은 이제 탐색할 수 있는 가능성의 폭을 10배(10X)로 넓혀볼 수 있어요. 이런 도구들 덕분에 훨씬 더 효율적으로 일하게 됐고요. 그러면 어떤 사람들은 "오 마이 갓, 창의 전문가들이 대체되는 거 아니야?"라고 말해요. 아니에요. 전혀 아니에요. 그들은 사라지는 게 아니라, 단지 10배 더 나은 해결책을 찾아내게 될 거예요.
text_zh: 现在创意工作者能探索的可能性比以前多了十倍。这些工具让他们的效率大大提升。有些人就说"哎呀，创意专业人士要被取代了"。不对，完全不是这么回事。他们不会被取代，只是能找到比现在好十倍的解决方案。
text_es: Los profesionales creativos ahora pueden explorar diez veces más posibilidades. Estas herramientas los están haciendo muchísimo más eficientes. Y hay gente que dice: "Ay, Dios mío, van a reemplazar a los creativos". No. No, no, no. Para nada. Lo que van a hacer es encontrar soluciones diez veces mejores.
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott to talk about what Adobe is working on and Scott explains three waves of transformation driving Adobe's strategy. One key wave is how AI tools are empowering creative professionals rather than replacing them. Scott argues that generative AI allows designers and creatives to explore far more possibilities in the same amount of time, leading to better creative solutions rather than job displacement.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, being efficient often refers to optimizing processes, reducing costs, and improving output to enhance overall performance.

insight.nuance: While 'efficient' implies a positive connotation of effectiveness, it can sometimes suggest a lack of flexibility or creativity in problem-solving.

vocabulary.definition: A potential or likelihood of something happening or being true.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and innovation, 'possibility' often refers to the exploration of new ideas, markets, or technologies that could lead to growth and success.

insight.nuance: The term carries an optimistic connotation, suggesting hope and opportunity, but can also imply uncertainty or risk.

vocabulary.definition: A thorough or dramatic change in form or appearance, often leading to significant improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, transformation can refer to changes in organizational structure, processes, or technology that enhance efficiency and competitiveness.

insight.nuance: While 'transformation' suggests a positive evolution, it can also imply disruption and resistance from stakeholders who are accustomed to the status quo.

vocabulary.definition: Giving someone the authority or power to do something, often leading to increased confidence and self-efficacy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate settings, empowering employees can lead to greater innovation, engagement, and productivity, as individuals feel more invested in their work.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, emphasizing support and encouragement, but can be misused if it leads to unrealistic expectations without adequate resources.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: Our whole team is only like 15 engineers a year. We use a ton of Devin when we're building Devin.
keySentence: We use a ton of Devin when we're building Devin.
text_ko: 우리 팀 전체는 한 해에 대략 엔지니어 15명 정도밖에 안 돼요. Devin을 만들 때 우리는 Devin을 진짜 많이 활용해요. 팀원 대부분은 한 번에 최대 다섯 개의 Devin을 다루고 있고, 그래서 Devin은 매달 코드베이스(code bases)에 수백 건의 풀 리퀘스트(pull requests)를 프로덕션(production)으로 머지(merge)해요.
text_zh: 我们整个团队一年也就15个工程师左右。我们在开发Devin的时候大量使用Devin本身。团队里大部分人都是同时和最多5个Devin一起干活，所以每个月Devin都会往生产环境合并几百个pull request到Devin的代码库里。
text_es: Nuestro equipo completo son como 15 ingenieros al año nada más. Usamos Devin un montón cuando estamos desarrollando Devin. La mayoría del equipo definitivamente está trabajando con hasta cinco Devins a la vez, y entonces Devin fusiona como varios cientos de pull requests a producción en las bases de código de Devin cada mes.
fullContext: Lenny is asking Scott about how Cognition, the company that builds Devin, uses their own AI engineer internally. Scott explains how their small engineering team of 15 people leverages multiple Devin instances to accelerate their development process. This demonstrates the practical application of AI engineers in a real production environment, where each human engineer manages multiple AI assistants simultaneously.

vocabulary.definition: To use something to maximum advantage or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, leveraging often refers to utilizing resources, skills, or relationships to enhance performance or achieve strategic goals.

insight.nuance: While 'leverage' can imply a strategic advantage, it can also suggest a reliance on external resources, so it should be used carefully to avoid negative connotations.

vocabulary.definition: The process of constructing or developing something, often referring to products or systems in a business context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, 'building' typically refers to the development of software, applications, or infrastructure that supports business operations.

insight.nuance: While 'building' can imply physical construction, in business it often has a broader meaning related to creating value through innovation and development.

vocabulary.definition: The application of scientific and mathematical principles to design and create structures, machines, and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, engineering encompasses the technical aspects of product development, ensuring that solutions are feasible, efficient, and meet user needs.

insight.nuance: The term 'engineering' can imply a rigorous, methodical approach to problem-solving, which is essential in tech industries but may not resonate in more creative fields.

vocabulary.definition: A group of individuals working collaboratively towards a common goal or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a team is often formed to leverage diverse skills and perspectives, enhancing productivity and innovation in projects or initiatives.

insight.nuance: The term 'team' conveys a sense of collaboration and shared responsibility, making it more positive than terms like 'group' or 'staff,' which may lack the same connotation of unity.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: AI is going to be the biggest technology shift of our lives... One of the things which is already I'd say different in AI, is just how explosive the technology can be. There's no weight on hardware distribution.
keySentence: AI is the biggest technology shift, with explosive potential and no weight on hardware distribution.
text_ko: 인공지능(AI)은 우리 삶에서 겪게 될 가장 큰 기술적 전환일 거예요. 지난 50년 동안 있었던 큰 기술 혁명들—개인용 컴퓨터(personal computer), 인터넷(internet), 휴대전화(mobile phone)—은 모두 유통에서 큰 비중을 차지한 하드웨어 요소가 있었어요. 그런데 인공지능(AI)은 이미 다른 점이 하나 있어요: 기술 자체가 얼마나 폭발적으로 확산될 수 있는지예요. 하드웨어 유통(hardware distribution)에 얽매여 있지 않거든요.
text_zh: AI会是我们这辈子遇到的最大的技术变革。你看过去50年那些重大的科技革命，比如个人电脑、互联网、手机，它们都有一个共同点，就是硬件是很重要的一块，硬件的普及决定了技术能推广到什么程度。但AI这次不一样，我觉得最明显的区别就是这技术爆发力太强了，完全不受硬件分发的限制。
text_es: La IA va a ser el cambio tecnológico más grande de nuestras vidas. Fíjate que todas las grandes revoluciones tecnológicas que hemos tenido en los últimos 50 años - como la computadora personal, el internet, el celular - todas tenían ese componente de hardware que era clave para su distribución. Pero algo que ya veo diferente con la IA es lo explosivo que puede ser esta tecnología. No depende para nada de la distribución de hardware.
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott about the future impact of AI technology. Scott compares AI to previous major technological shifts like personal computers, the internet, and mobile phones, explaining why AI adoption could be more rapid. Unlike previous technologies that required physical hardware distribution limiting their spread, AI can scale instantly without hardware constraints, making its growth potentially more explosive than past innovations.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by rapid and intense growth or change, often in a way that is unexpected or dramatic.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'explosive' often describes the rapid adoption of new technologies or market trends that can significantly disrupt existing industries.

insight.nuance: While 'explosive' conveys a sense of urgency and potential, it may also imply volatility or unpredictability, so it should be used with caution.

vocabulary.definition: A significant change in the way technology is developed, utilized, or integrated into society or business practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, a 'technology shift' can lead to new business models, competitive advantages, or the obsolescence of existing products and services.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a transformative impact, so it is best used when discussing major advancements rather than minor updates.

vocabulary.definition: The process of accepting and integrating a new idea, product, or technology into use by individuals or organizations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'adoption' is crucial for the success of new technologies, as it determines how quickly and widely a product is embraced by the market.

insight.nuance: While 'adoption' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply resistance or challenges in the integration process, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: The process of delivering products or services from producers to consumers, encompassing logistics, supply chain management, and sales channels.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective distribution strategies are essential for businesses to ensure that their products reach the target market efficiently and effectively.

insight.nuance: The term can also refer to the allocation of resources or information, so it is important to clarify the context in which it is used.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: I think there's going to be way more programmers and way more engineers a few years from now. Pretty quickly.
keySentence: I think there's going to be way more programmers and way more engineers a few years from now.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 앞으로 몇 년 안에 프로그래머(programmer)랑 엔지니어(engineer)가 훨씬 더 많아질 거예요. 꽤 빠르게요. 프로그래머라는 개념의 형태(form factor)는 분명히 바뀔 텐데, 결국 이 분야는 컴퓨터(computer)에게 무엇을 하라고 지시할 수 있는 능력에 관한 거예요. 그런 관점에서 보면 인공지능(AI)이 더 강력해질수록 프로그래밍(programming)은 점점 더 중요해질 거라고 정말 생각해요.
text_zh: 我觉得再过几年，程序员和工程师的数量会大幅增加，而且会很快。当程序员的形式肯定会变，但说到底，这个行业本质上就是要能告诉电脑该做什么。从这个角度看，我真的认为随着AI越来越强大，编程只会变得越来越重要。
text_es: Creo que va a haber muchísimos más programadores e ingenieros en unos años. Bastante rápido, la verdad. Obviamente va a cambiar completamente lo que significa ser programador, pero al final del día, claro, la disciplina se trata simplemente de poder decirle a tu computadora qué tiene que hacer. Y desde esa perspectiva, realmente creo que la programación va a ser cada vez más importante mientras la IA se vuelve más poderosa.
fullContext: Lenny asks how the role of being an engineer and building software is changing. Scott argues against the common fear that AI will reduce the need for programmers. Instead, he believes AI will actually increase demand for engineers by making programming more accessible and powerful. He emphasizes that programming fundamentally remains about instructing computers what to do, which becomes more valuable as AI capabilities expand.

vocabulary.definition: A professional who applies scientific and mathematical principles to design, develop, and analyze technological solutions and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, engineers are crucial for product development, system optimization, and ensuring technical feasibility of projects.

insight.nuance: The term 'engineer' often implies a formal education and expertise in a specific field, such as software, civil, or mechanical engineering.

vocabulary.definition: A specialist who writes, tests, and maintains the code that enables software applications to function.
vocabulary.businessContext: Programmers are essential in tech startups for creating software solutions, debugging issues, and implementing new features to meet user needs.

insight.nuance: While often used interchangeably with 'developer,' 'programmer' may emphasize the coding aspect more than the overall software development process.

vocabulary.definition: The function or position that an individual holds within an organization, encompassing their responsibilities and duties.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding roles within a team is vital for effective collaboration, project management, and ensuring that all tasks are covered in a business setting.

insight.nuance: The term 'role' can imply a formal designation but may also refer to informal contributions or expectations within a group.

vocabulary.definition: To make something smaller or less in amount, degree, or size.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, to reduce costs or waste is often a key objective for improving profitability and operational efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term 'reduce' can carry a negative connotation if it implies cutting essential services or quality, so it should be used thoughtfully.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: And then the other thing that we felt very strongly about was that the product experience was going to shift from what I'll call text completion to agents basically.
keySentence: We felt very strongly about shifting from a text to text model to autonomous systems.
text_ko: 그리고 우리가 특히 확신했던 또 하나는 제품 경험이 제가 '텍스트 완성(text completion)'이라고 부르는 것에서 기본적으로 '에이전트(agents)'로 전환될 거라는 점이에요. 우리가 정말로 예상한 큰 변화는 일종의 텍스트-투-텍스트 모델(text-to-text model)에서 벗어나 스스로 결정을 내리고 현실 세계와 상호작용하며 피드백(feedback)을 받아들여 반복(iterate)하고 여러 단계를 거쳐 문제를 해결할 수 있는 실제 자율 시스템(autonomous system)으로 옮겨간다는 거예요.
text_zh: 然后还有一点我们特别坚信的就是，产品体验会从我说的文本补全转向智能体(agents)。我们真正感受到的大变化是，从这种文本到文本的模式转向真正的自主系统，这个系统能做决策，能跟现实世界交互，能接收反馈，能不断迭代，还能通过多个步骤来解决问题。
text_es: Y después, lo otro en lo que teníamos clarísimo es que la experiencia del producto iba a cambiar de lo que yo llamaría completar texto a básicamente agentes. El gran cambio que realmente veíamos venir era pasar de este modelo de texto a texto a un sistema autónomo de verdad que puede tomar decisiones, que puede interactuar con el mundo real, que puede recibir feedback, que puede iterar y dar varios pasos para resolver problemas.
fullContext: Scott is explaining Cognition's founding thesis and why they chose to focus on autonomous coding agents rather than simpler AI coding tools. He describes their early belief that AI would evolve beyond basic text completion (like GitHub Copilot) toward fully autonomous systems. This represents a fundamental shift from AI tools that assist with writing code to AI systems that can independently complete entire software engineering tasks.

vocabulary.definition: The overall perception and interaction a user has with a product, encompassing usability, functionality, and emotional response.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, enhancing product experience is crucial for customer satisfaction and retention, often driving product development and marketing strategies.

insight.nuance: While 'product experience' emphasizes user interaction, it is distinct from 'user experience' which may include broader aspects like customer service.

vocabulary.definition: Functioning independently without human intervention, often referring to systems or technologies that can operate on their own.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, autonomous systems are pivotal in fields like artificial intelligence and robotics, where they can enhance efficiency and reduce operational costs.

insight.nuance: While 'autonomous' suggests independence, it may also imply a level of reliability and sophistication that not all systems possess.

vocabulary.definition: To develop gradually, especially in response to changing conditions or environments, leading to a more advanced state.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, companies must evolve their products and strategies to adapt to market trends and consumer demands to remain competitive.

insight.nuance: The term 'evolve' carries a positive connotation of growth and improvement, suggesting a natural progression rather than forced change.

vocabulary.definition: Entities or systems that perform tasks or make decisions on behalf of others, often utilizing artificial intelligence to automate processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology, agents are increasingly used in customer service and data analysis, streamlining operations and enhancing user interactions.

insight.nuance: The term 'agents' can imply a level of intelligence or autonomy, which may not apply to all automated systems or tools.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: I think there are certain things that it is much better at than a human. There are certain things that it's much worse at than a human.
keySentence: There are certain things that it's much worse at than a human.
text_ko: 저는 어떤 일들은 사람보다 훨씬 잘하는 부분이 분명히 있다고 생각해요. 반대로 어떤 일들은 사람보다 훨씬 못하는 부분도 있어요. 그리고 지난 1년 동안 우리는 특히 코딩 에이전트(coding agents)뿐만 아니라 에이전트(agents) 전반에 대해, 에이전트를 우리의 워크플로(workflow)의 일부로서 어떻게 함께 일하고 상호작용하게 할지에 대해 많은 걸 배웠어요.
text_zh: 我觉得AI在某些方面确实比人强很多，但在另一些方面又比人差得远。这一年下来我们学到了不少东西，特别是不光是代码智能体(coding agents)，而是各种智能体(agents)，就是怎么把这些智能体融入到我们的工作流程里，大家该怎么跟它们配合。
text_es: Creo que hay ciertas cosas en las que es mucho mejor que los humanos. Hay otras en las que es mucho peor que nosotros. Y creo que durante el último año hemos aprendido muchísimo, especialmente no solo sobre los agentes de programación sino sobre los agentes en general, realmente desarrollando cómo todos nosotros deberíamos trabajar e interactuar con los agentes como parte de nuestro flujo de trabajo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott to compare Devin's current capabilities to human engineers using a seniority framework. Scott introduces the concept of 'jagged intelligence' - the idea that AI systems have very uneven capabilities, excelling dramatically in some areas while performing poorly in others. He explains that much of their learning has focused not just on improving Devin's coding abilities, but on figuring out optimal human-AI collaboration workflows.

vocabulary.definition: The skills, resources, or abilities that enable an individual or organization to perform tasks or achieve objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, capabilities often refer to the specific functions or features that a product or service can offer, which can influence competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: While 'capabilities' can imply a positive potential, it may also suggest limitations when discussing what is not possible.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding, analyzing, or developing a particular concept or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, frameworks are often used to guide project management, software development, or strategic planning, ensuring consistency and efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a rigid structure, but it may also suggest flexibility depending on the context in which it is applied.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills, often associated with cognitive functions such as reasoning, problem-solving, and learning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, intelligence can refer to data-driven insights, artificial intelligence, or competitive intelligence that inform decision-making.

insight.nuance: While 'intelligence' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply a comparison with others, particularly when discussing human versus machine capabilities.

vocabulary.definition: Not uniform, consistent, or equal in quality, quantity, or degree; characterized by irregularity or disparity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'uneven' can describe market conditions, performance metrics, or resource allocation that vary significantly across different areas or periods.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting instability or unpredictability, and is typically used to highlight disparities that need addressing.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: computers are obviously getting more and more intelligence and are able to do more and more... there may come a day where computers truly do everything that we do and humans are not responsible for any of it.
keySentence: AI has layers of abstraction, and computers may one day do everything, leaving humans not responsible.
text_ko: 제가 보기에 우리가 늘 그렇게 생각해온 방식은 추상화 계층(layers of abstraction)과 여러 도구들이 있다는 거예요. 한마디로 말하면, 인공지능(AI)을 대체로 이렇게 생각해요. 그러니까 컴퓨터가 점점 더 지능을 갖추고 할 수 있는 일이 늘어나고 있고, 어쩌면 언젠가는 컴퓨터가 우리가 하는 모든 일을 진짜로 다 해내서 인간은 아무런 책임도 지지 않는 날이 올 수도 있다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 我觉得我们一直以来的想法就是，技术有很多层级，也有各种工具，从宏观角度来说，我对AI的理解就是，电脑明显是越来越聪明了，能干的事也越来越多，说不定哪天电脑真的能把我们人类做的所有事都包了，到时候可能就不需要人来负责任何事情了。
text_es: Mira, yo creo que siempre lo hemos visto así: hay diferentes niveles de abstracción (layers of abstraction) y hay herramientas, y si lo digo a grandes rasgos, pienso en la IA en general como... bueno, es obvio que las computadoras cada vez son más inteligentes y pueden hacer más y más cosas, y es posible que llegue el día en que las computadoras realmente hagan todo lo que hacemos nosotros y los humanos ya no seamos responsables de nada.
fullContext: Lenny asks Scott how the act of being an engineer is changing for companies using Devin today. Scott provides his philosophical perspective on AI's role in programming, emphasizing that software engineering has always been about instructing computers through layers of abstraction. He acknowledges the possibility of full automation while focusing on the current reality where humans remain essential to the programming process.

vocabulary.definition: Having an obligation to ensure something is done or to take care of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being responsible often refers to accountability for decisions, actions, and their consequences, particularly in leadership roles.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of trustworthiness and reliability, often implying a moral or ethical duty.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills; in technology, it often refers to the capacity of machines to perform tasks that typically require human cognitive functions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, 'intelligence' frequently pertains to artificial intelligence (AI) systems that enhance decision-making processes and automate tasks.

insight.nuance: While it generally denotes cognitive ability, in a business context, it can imply advanced analytical capabilities or the potential for automation.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the study of fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence; often involves critical thinking and reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, a philosophical approach may influence corporate culture, ethical decision-making, and long-term strategic planning.

insight.nuance: This term can suggest a deep, reflective approach to problems, often implying a consideration of ethical implications and broader impacts.

vocabulary.definition: The application of scientific and mathematical principles to design and build structures, machines, and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, engineering is critical for developing software and hardware solutions, driving innovation, and ensuring product functionality.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a systematic and methodical approach to problem-solving, and can also connote creativity in design and functionality.

speaker: Scott Wu
text: One of the ways that we've kind of thought about Devin in building Devin is really allowing engineers to go from bricklayer to architect, so to speak.
keySentence: allowing engineers to go from bricklayer to architect, so to speak.
text_ko: 우리가 Devin을 만들면서 생각한 것 중 하나는 엔지니어들이 벽돌공에서 건축가로 역할을 전환할 수 있게 해주는 거예요. 많은 부분이 결국 상위 수준의 지시(high-level directing)를 할 수 있는 단계에 이르고, 원하는 대로 정확히 지정(specify)할 수 있게 되는 거죠. 핵심은 여전히 사람이 주도권을 가지고 전체 사양(full specification)을 직접 작성할 수 있다는 점이고, 다만 하루나 한 시간 같은 짧은 시간 안에 할 수 있는 일과 만들 수 있는 것들의 규모를 훨씬 더 키워준다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我们在开发Devin的时候，有个想法就是让工程师能够从搬砖工变成架构师，这么说吧。很大程度上就是让你能够做高层次的指导工作，基本上可以完全按照你想要的方式去指定需求。我觉得这还是要让人来掌控全局，让人能够做完整的需求规划，只不过是把你一天或者一小时内能完成的工作量和能搭建的东西成倍放大。
text_es: Una de las formas en que hemos pensado en Devin al desarrollarlo es realmente permitir que los ingenieros pasen de ser albañiles a ser arquitectos, por decirlo así. Mucho de esto se trata de llegar al punto donde puedes hacer la dirección de alto nivel y básicamente especificar las cosas exactamente como las quieres. Creo que se trata mucho de seguir teniendo al humano en control y que el humano pueda hacer toda la especificación, pero simplemente multiplicar la magnitud de lo que puedes hacer y lo que puedes construir en un día o en una hora o el tiempo que sea.
fullContext: Scott is describing how Devin changes the role of software engineers by handling routine implementation tasks. The 'bricklayer to architect' metaphor illustrates how engineers can shift from hands-on coding work to high-level design and specification. Scott emphasizes that humans remain in control of decision-making and architectural choices while AI handles the detailed implementation work, effectively multiplying human productivity.

vocabulary.definition: To change position, direction, or focus; a movement from one state to another.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a shift often refers to a change in strategy, market focus, or organizational structure that can impact operations and outcomes.

insight.nuance: While 'shift' implies a change, it can also suggest a gradual transition rather than an abrupt alteration.

vocabulary.definition: A figure of speech that implies a comparison between two unlike entities, suggesting that one embodies the qualities of the other.
vocabulary.businessContext: Metaphors are frequently used in business communication to simplify complex ideas, making them more relatable and understandable for stakeholders.

insight.nuance: Using a metaphor can enhance clarity and engagement, but it should be used judiciously to avoid confusion or misinterpretation.

vocabulary.definition: The process of putting a decision or plan into effect; execution of a strategy or system.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business or tech environment, implementation refers to the actual deployment of new processes, technologies, or policies that were previously planned.

insight.nuance: Implementation can involve challenges and requires careful planning and resource allocation to ensure success.

vocabulary.definition: The function or position that an individual or entity occupies within a particular context or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, roles define responsibilities and expectations for employees, teams, and departments, influencing collaboration and productivity.

insight.nuance: Understanding one's role is crucial for effective teamwork; however, roles can evolve over time as organizations change.

speaker: Sean Ellis
text: if I go into it and I have no idea how we'll acquire those customers, I'm not real confident I'll figure it out when I'm there.
keySentence: if I go into it and I have no idea how we'll acquire those customers, I'm not real confident I'll figure it out when I'm there.
text_ko: 제가 직접 고객 확보(acquisition) 쪽으로 회사에 들어가서 관여할 때는, 고객 확보에 대한 가설을 꽤 일찍부터 세워요. 왜냐하면 들어가서 그 고객들을 어떻게 확보할지 전혀 감이 없다면, 현장에서 가서 그걸 알아낼 수 있을 거라는 확신이 별로 안 들거든요.
text_zh: 当我直接参与一家公司的收购时，我会很早就开始思考我对这次收购的假设，因为如果我进去的时候对怎么获取那些客户一点头绪都没有，我可不敢保证到时候能想出办法来。
text_es: Cuando me meto de lleno y me involucro directamente con una empresa en el tema de adquisición, desde muy temprano ya estoy pensando en mis hipótesis sobre cómo vamos a captar clientes, porque si entro sin tener ni idea de cómo vamos a conseguir esos clientes, la verdad es que no me da mucha confianza que lo vaya a resolver una vez que ya esté ahí metido.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sean about his approach to helping companies figure out growth strategy. Sean explains that even though he focuses on activation and onboarding first, he still develops early hypotheses about customer acquisition channels before taking on a project. He wants to have 2-3 viable acquisition ideas going in, knowing he'll likely discover more, so that at least one channel will work profitably.

vocabulary.definition: To obtain or gain possession of something, often through effort or purchase.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'acquire' frequently refers to gaining new customers, assets, or companies, often as part of a growth strategy or merger.

insight.nuance: While 'acquire' can imply a straightforward transaction, it may also suggest a strategic effort to enhance market position or capabilities.

vocabulary.definition: A plan or approach designed to increase a company's market share, revenue, or overall size.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and established companies alike, a growth strategy outlines the methods and tactics to achieve expansion, whether through new markets, products, or customer acquisition.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a long-term vision and may include various tactics such as market penetration, diversification, or partnerships.

vocabulary.definition: The process of making something active or operational, often referring to engaging users or customers with a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and marketing, 'activation' typically refers to the steps taken to ensure that new users engage with a product effectively, thereby increasing retention and satisfaction.

insight.nuance: While 'activation' can denote initial engagement, it often carries a connotation of ongoing interaction and value realization.

vocabulary.definition: The process of integrating new employees or customers into an organization or system, providing them with the necessary tools and information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, effective onboarding is crucial for ensuring that new hires or customers understand their roles and how to use products, which can significantly impact retention and productivity.

insight.nuance: Onboarding is often viewed as a critical phase that can determine the long-term success of the relationship, and it should be tailored to the specific needs of the individual.

speaker: Sean Ellis
text: Customer acquisition is so hard that if you're not really efficient at converting and retaining and monetizing people, you're going to really struggle on the customer acquisition side.
keySentence: You're going to really struggle on customer acquisition without efficient monetizing people.
text_ko: 고객 획득(customer acquisition)이 워낙 힘들어서, 전환(converting)·유지(retaining)·수익화(monetizing)을 효율적으로 못하면 고객 확보 쪽에서 진짜 고생해요.
text_zh: 获客这么难，如果你在转化、留存和变现这块做得不够好的话，那获客这边你肯定会很吃力。
text_es: Conseguir clientes nuevos es tan difícil que si no eres realmente eficiente convirtiendo, reteniendo y monetizando a la gente, te va a costar muchísimo en el lado de adquisición de clientes.
fullContext: Sean explains his prioritization approach to growth - focusing first on activation, then engagement and referrals, then revenue optimization, and only lastly on customer acquisition. He argues that in today's competitive environment, companies must be extremely efficient at converting, retaining, and monetizing customers before they can succeed at scalable customer acquisition.

vocabulary.definition: The process of attracting and converting new customers to purchase a company's products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, customer acquisition is critical for growth, often involving strategies like marketing campaigns, sales tactics, and customer relationship management.

insight.nuance: While it emphasizes the initial engagement, it is often discussed in conjunction with retention strategies to ensure long-term success.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, being efficient means optimizing processes to reduce costs and increase output, which is essential for competitiveness.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting not just speed but also effectiveness in resource use.

vocabulary.definition: The process of converting an asset, service, or product into a source of revenue.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, monetizing often refers to strategies for generating income from users, such as through subscriptions, advertising, or sales.

insight.nuance: It implies a strategic approach to generating profit, and is often discussed in the context of balancing user experience with revenue generation.

vocabulary.definition: The action or process of deciding the relative importance or urgency of tasks or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, prioritization is crucial for effective project management and resource allocation, ensuring that the most impactful tasks are addressed first.

insight.nuance: It suggests a strategic decision-making process, often involving trade-offs and considerations of long-term versus short-term goals.

speaker: Sean Ellis
text: If you start paying attention to what your somewhat disappointed users are telling you and then you start tweaking onboarding and product based on their feedback, maybe you're going to dilute it for your must have users.
keySentence: Paying attention to disappointed users may dilute it for must-have users.
text_ko: 다소 실망한 사용자들이 하는 말에 귀 기울여 그 피드백을 바탕으로 온보딩(onboarding)과 제품을 조금씩 손봐서 맞추기 시작하면, 오히려 핵심 사용자들(must-have users)에게는 제품의 강점이 희석될 수 있어요.
text_zh: 如果你开始关注那些有点失望的用户的反馈，然后根据他们的意见去调整用户引导(onboarding)和产品，可能会让你的核心用户体验变差。
text_es: Si empiezas a hacerle caso a lo que te dicen los usuarios que están medio decepcionados y luego te pones a ajustar el onboarding y el producto basándote en sus comentarios, a lo mejor vas a terminar diluyendo la experiencia para tus usuarios que realmente no pueden vivir sin tu producto.
fullContext: Lenny asks what to do when only 10% of users would be very disappointed without the product. Sean advises ignoring users who say they'd be 'somewhat disappointed' because they view the product as nice-to-have. He warns that optimizing for these users might make the product good for everyone but great for no one, potentially weakening its value for the core must-have users.

vocabulary.definition: Making small adjustments or modifications to improve something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, tweaking often refers to refining processes, products, or strategies based on user feedback or performance metrics.

insight.nuance: The term suggests minor changes rather than major overhauls, implying a careful and thoughtful approach to improvement.

vocabulary.definition: Information or criticism about a product, service, or performance, used as a basis for improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup environment, feedback is crucial for product development and customer satisfaction, guiding decisions on enhancements and features.

insight.nuance: Feedback can be positive or negative, and it is often seen as a valuable tool for growth when solicited and acted upon appropriately.

vocabulary.definition: To weaken or lessen the strength or effectiveness of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, diluting a product or service can refer to making changes that may reduce its appeal or core value to a specific audience.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that the essence or quality of something is being compromised.

vocabulary.definition: An essential item or feature that is deemed necessary for success or satisfaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development, identifying must-have features is critical for meeting user needs and ensuring competitive advantage in the market.

insight.nuance: The phrase implies a strong necessity, often associated with consumer expectations and market trends, and should be used to emphasize importance.

speaker: Sean Ellis
text: Half the people feel like we're years from having this product ready to grow, and half the people are like, 'What are we waiting for?
keySentence: Half the people feel like we're years from having this product ready to grow.
text_ko: 제 생각에 초창기 스타트업(early stage startup)에서 가장 큰 문제 중 하나는 팀의 절반은 '이 제품이 성장할 준비가 되려면 몇 년은 더 걸리겠구나'라고 느끼고, 나머지 절반은 '우린 도대체 뭘 기다리고 있는 거야?'라고 생각하는 거예요. 그런데 제품-시장 적합성(product market fit)이 우리 비즈니스에서 어떤 모습이어야 하는지 모두가 같은 페이지에 있으면, 바로 그때부터 움직이기 시작하는 거죠.
text_zh: 我觉得早期创业公司最大的挑战之一就是，一半的人觉得我们的产品离能够规模化还有好几年，另一半的人就说"我们还在等什么？"这时候如果你能让大家对什么叫产品市场契合度(product market fit)达成共识，明确到了那个点我们就要开始行动。
text_es: Creo que uno de los mayores retos en una startup que está empezando es que la mitad del equipo siente que nos faltan años para tener el producto listo para crecer, y la otra mitad está como "¿qué estamos esperando?" Entonces, si logras que toda la gente esté en la misma página sobre cómo se ve el product market fit para nuestro negocio, ahí es cuando vamos a...
fullContext: Lenny asks about how firm the 40% threshold is in the Sean Ellis test. Sean explains that having a specific target like 40% helps align teams on when to start scaling growth efforts. Without this alignment, startup teams often split between those who think the product needs years more work and those eager to start growing immediately.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange in a straight line or to bring into agreement or cooperation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, aligning refers to ensuring that all team members or departments are working towards the same goals and objectives, often used in strategic planning and project management.

insight.nuance: While 'align' suggests a harmonious agreement, it can also imply the need for negotiation or compromise to achieve consensus.

vocabulary.definition: The process of increasing the size, capacity, or scope of a business or its operations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, scaling refers to the ability to grow the business efficiently without compromising performance or quality, often involving the expansion of resources and infrastructure.

insight.nuance: Scaling can imply both growth and the challenges that come with it, such as maintaining quality and managing increased complexity.

vocabulary.definition: A point or level at which something begins or changes; a minimum requirement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a threshold often refers to the minimum criteria that must be met for a decision to be made, such as sales targets or performance metrics.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a sense of urgency, indicating a critical point that, once crossed, may lead to significant changes or actions.

vocabulary.definition: A specific goal or objective that one aims to achieve.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, targets are often set for sales, marketing, or performance metrics to guide efforts and measure success.

insight.nuance: While 'target' implies a clear goal, it can also suggest pressure to meet expectations, making it important to set realistic and attainable objectives.

speaker: Sean Ellis
text: Even when I first moved to Silicon Valley, I remember the conversations back at LogMeIn in the mid 2000s of kind of like, 'When do we step on the gas?
keySentence: When do we step on the gas?
text_ko: 실리콘밸리(Silicon Valley)로 처음 왔을 때도, 2000년대 중반 LogMeIn에서 나눴던 대화가 기억나요. 대충 이런 얘기였어요: "언제 엑셀을 밟아야 할까요? 초기 불씨에 연료를 더 붓기 전에 어떤 요소들이 갖춰져야 할까요?"
text_zh: 我记得2000年代中期刚到硅谷的时候，我们在LogMeIn内部经常讨论这样的问题："什么时候该全力冲刺？需要哪些条件都到位了，我们才能开始给这个刚起步的项目大力投入资源？"
text_es: Incluso cuando me mudé por primera vez a Silicon Valley, recuerdo las conversaciones que teníamos en LogMeIn a mediados de los 2000, algo así como: '¿Cuándo le metemos el acelerador a fondo? ¿Qué combinación de factores tiene que estar en su lugar antes de echarle más leña al fuego inicial?'
fullContext: Sean continues explaining why having a clear product-market fit threshold is important for startup teams. He shares how even before the term 'product-market fit' existed, his team at LogMeIn in the mid-2000s struggled with the same fundamental question of when exactly to start aggressively scaling their growth efforts.

vocabulary.definition: To accelerate or increase the pace of an activity or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in startups, this phrase often refers to intensifying efforts in marketing, product development, or scaling operations to achieve growth.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of urgency and proactive action, and is typically used in contexts where speed is critical to success.

vocabulary.definition: The degree to which a product satisfies a strong market demand.
vocabulary.businessContext: Achieving product-market fit is crucial for startups, as it indicates that the product is well-received by the target audience, leading to sustainable growth and profitability.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the alignment between a product's features and the needs of its customers, and is often used in discussions about scaling and investment readiness.

vocabulary.definition: A level or point at which something begins or changes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, thresholds can refer to financial metrics, performance indicators, or market conditions that, once crossed, trigger specific actions or strategies.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a critical juncture that can lead to significant consequences, making it important in strategic planning and risk management.

vocabulary.definition: Groups of individuals working collaboratively to develop and grow a new business venture.
vocabulary.businessContext: Startup teams are typically characterized by their dynamic, agile structures and are essential for fostering innovation and driving the company's vision forward.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a collaborative and often informal environment, which can vary greatly in composition and roles compared to traditional corporate teams.

speaker: Sean Ellis
text: I think basically for each business it's just thinking about what's unique for that business that is going to open up channel opportunities and everyone's going to be a little bit, I think jaded from whatever the last thing that worked really well.
keySentence: Thinking about what's unique will open up channel opportunities despite being jaded from whatever worked well.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 기본적으로 각 비즈니스는 자기만의 고유한 게 뭔지 생각해서 그걸로 채널 기회(channel opportunities)를 만들어내는 게 중요해요. 그리고 사람들은 이전에 효과가 좋았던 것 때문에 다들 좀 식상해져 있을 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得基本上每个生意都要想想，自己有什么独特的地方能开拓新的渠道机会，而且大家对之前那些很成功的做法多少都会有点审美疲劳。
text_es: Mira, creo que básicamente para cada negocio se trata de pensar qué es lo único de ese negocio que va a abrir oportunidades de canal, y todo el mundo va a estar un poco escamado por lo último que funcionó realmente bien.
fullContext: Lenny asks how to help businesses figure out which growth channel to focus on - whether paid acquisition, SEO, sales, or virality. Sean explains that each business has unique characteristics that make certain channels more viable, and warns that people often get biased by their previous successful experiences and try to apply the same approach to different businesses.

vocabulary.definition: Potential avenues or methods through which a business can reach its target market or distribute its products and services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying channel opportunities is crucial for optimizing marketing strategies and enhancing customer engagement.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a proactive approach to exploring new markets or distribution methods, rather than relying solely on established channels.

vocabulary.definition: Distinctive traits or features that differentiate a product, service, or business from its competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a competitive landscape, emphasizing unique characteristics can help a business establish its brand identity and attract customers.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a focus on individuality and innovation, often used in marketing and product development discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A specific pathway or strategy that a business utilizes to achieve expansion and increase its market share.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying effective growth channels is essential for startups and established companies alike, as it informs resource allocation and strategic planning.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting proactive measures for scaling a business rather than merely maintaining current operations.

vocabulary.definition: The process of gaining customers through paid marketing efforts, such as advertisements, rather than organic methods.
vocabulary.businessContext: Paid acquisition strategies are commonly employed in digital marketing to quickly increase customer base and drive sales.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a focus on immediate results, contrasting with organic growth strategies that may take longer to yield results.

speaker: Seth Godin
text: Well, the first question is what's a brand? Because it's not a logo. A brand is a promise. It's what do I expect from you. It's would I miss you if you were gone. And Hyatt Hotels has a logo, Nike has a brand.
keySentence: A brand is a promise.
text_ko: 첫 번째 질문은 '브랜드가 뭐예요?'예요. 왜냐하면 브랜드는 로고(logo)가 아니거든요. 브랜드(brand)는 약속이에요. 그 브랜드에게서 무엇을 기대하느냐는 거예요. 그 브랜드가 사라지면 그리울까 하는 거죠. 하얏트 호텔(Hyatt Hotels)은 로고(logo)가 있고, 나이키(Nike)는 브랜드(brand)가 있어요. 우리가 이걸 아는 방법은, 만약 나이키가 호텔을 연다면 어떤 느낌일지 알 수 있기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 首先，什么叫品牌？品牌可不是一个标志那么简单。品牌其实是一种承诺，就是我对你的期待是什么，你要是没了我会不会想念你。凯悦酒店有的只是个标志，但耐克有的是品牌。怎么证明呢？如果耐克开酒店，我们马上就能想象出那会是什么样子。
text_es: Bueno, la primera pregunta es ¿qué es una marca? Porque no es un logo. Una marca es una promesa. Es qué espero de ti. Es si te echaría de menos si desaparecieras. Y Hyatt Hotels tiene un logo, Nike tiene una marca. Y sabemos esto porque si Nike abriera un hotel, sabríamos exactamente cómo sería.
fullContext: Lenny asks Seth how new AI companies can build brands to distinguish themselves in an increasingly crowded market. Seth first clarifies what a brand actually is - not a logo, but a promise and set of expectations. He explains that true brands transcend product categories because people understand what the brand stands for, using Nike as an example of a strong brand versus Hyatt as just a logo.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or point out the differences between two or more items or concepts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, distinguishing a product or service from competitors is crucial for branding and market positioning.

insight.nuance: Often used in contexts where clarity and differentiation are essential, it implies a deeper understanding rather than superficial recognition.

vocabulary.definition: A declaration or assurance that one will do something or that a particular thing will happen.
vocabulary.businessContext: In branding, a promise represents the commitment a company makes to its customers regarding the quality and experience of its products or services.

insight.nuance: While it conveys reliability, it can also imply a risk if the promise is not fulfilled, impacting customer trust.

vocabulary.definition: To regard something as likely to happen or to anticipate a particular outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, managing customer expectations is vital for satisfaction and loyalty, influencing how products and services are perceived.

insight.nuance: This term carries a sense of anticipation that can be positive or negative depending on the context and prior experiences.

vocabulary.definition: Filled with a large number of people or things, often resulting in a lack of space or comfort.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market analysis, a crowded market indicates high competition, which can affect pricing strategies and market entry decisions.

insight.nuance: While it can imply vibrancy and activity, it may also suggest challenges related to saturation and differentiation.

speaker: Seth Godin
text: AI very soon is going to stop being a feature the same way electricity is not a feature. What AI companies and all companies need to do is say, what's in this for the user?
keySentence: AI very soon is going to stop being a feature the same way electricity is not a feature.
text_ko: 머지않아 인공지능(AI)은 전기(electricity)처럼 더 이상 '기능(feature)'으로 여겨지지 않을 거예요. AI 회사든 모든 회사든 스스로에게 물어봐야 할 건 '이게 사용자에게 어떤 가치가 있지?'예요. 내가 어떤 약속을 하고 싶은가요? 어렵지만 의미 있는, 눈에 띄는 약속을 정하고 그 약속을 어떻게 지킬지 고민해야 해요.
text_zh: AI很快就不会再是一个功能特色了，就像电力一样——你不会说电力是个特色功能对吧？AI公司也好，其他公司也好，都得想清楚一个问题：用户能从中得到什么好处？我要给用户一个什么样的承诺？这个承诺得有挑战性，得让人眼前一亮，然后最关键的是——我怎么兑现这个承诺？
text_es: Muy pronto la IA va a dejar de ser una funcionalidad, igual que la electricidad ya no es una funcionalidad. Lo que las empresas de IA y todas las empresas tienen que preguntarse es: ¿qué gana el usuario con esto? ¿Qué promesa quiero hacer - una promesa difícil, una promesa que realmente marque la diferencia - y entonces cómo la voy a cumplir?
fullContext: Following up on his brand definition, Seth addresses how AI companies specifically should approach branding. He predicts that AI will become ubiquitous infrastructure rather than a differentiating feature, similar to how electricity powers many products but isn't considered special. He emphasizes that companies should focus on making and keeping meaningful promises to users rather than promoting their use of AI technology.

vocabulary.definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere; pervasive.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'ubiquitous' often describes products or services that are widely available and integrated into everyday life, such as smartphones or internet access.

insight.nuance: While it implies widespread presence, it can also suggest a lack of uniqueness or differentiation in a crowded market.

vocabulary.definition: The fundamental facilities and systems serving a country, city, or area, including services and installations necessary for economic activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, 'infrastructure' refers to the underlying systems and services that support operations, such as cloud computing, networking, and data management.

insight.nuance: It often implies a foundational role that is critical for growth and scalability, and can encompass both physical and digital components.

vocabulary.definition: The process of distinguishing or setting apart a product or service from others in the market.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'differentiating' is crucial for competitive advantage, as it helps companies highlight unique features, benefits, or value propositions to attract customers.

insight.nuance: It often carries a positive connotation, suggesting innovation and strategic positioning, but can also imply a challenge in a saturated market.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'approach' can refer to the strategic methods employed to solve problems, develop products, or engage with customers, such as agile or customer-centric approaches.

insight.nuance: It suggests a thoughtful and systematic method, but can also imply flexibility and adaptability depending on the context.

speaker: Seth Godin
text: I define good taste as knowing what other people want just before they do.
keySentence: Good taste means knowing what others want just before they do.
text_ko: 저는 좋은 취향을 '다른 사람들이 원하기 직전에 그들이 뭘 원하는지 알아내는 능력'이라고 정의해요. 그러니까 만약 당신 혼자만 땅콩버터를 바른 리코리스를 좋아한다면, 그걸 먹을 권리는 있어요. 다만 그건 좋은 취향이라고 보긴 어려워요 — 다른 사람들은 그걸 이상하게 생각하니까요.
text_zh: 我觉得品味好就是能比别人早一步知道他们想要什么。比如说，如果全世界就你一个人想吃花生酱裹甘草糖，那你当然可以吃，但这不叫有品味，因为别人都觉得这太奇怪了。
text_es: Yo defino el buen gusto como saber lo que otros quieren justo antes de que ellos se den cuenta. O sea, si eres la única persona que quiere regaliz cubierto de mantequilla de maní, perfecto, tienes todo el derecho de comértelo, pero no tienes buen gusto porque todos los demás piensan que eso está rarísimo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Seth how to recognize and develop good taste and high standards, based on advice from Wes Kao who worked with Seth. Seth provides his definition of good taste - the ability to anticipate what others will want before they realize it themselves. He uses a humorous food example to illustrate that personal preference alone doesn't constitute good taste; it must resonate with others.

vocabulary.definition: To expect or predict something before it occurs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, anticipating market trends or consumer needs can provide a competitive advantage and inform strategic planning.

insight.nuance: While 'anticipate' often has a positive connotation of foresight, it can imply uncertainty if the prediction is not based on solid data.

vocabulary.definition: To grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, developing products or services involves research, design, and iterative improvement to meet market demands.

insight.nuance: The term 'develop' suggests a process of evolution and improvement, rather than a one-time action.

vocabulary.definition: A level of quality or attainment used as a measure, norm, or model in comparative evaluations.
vocabulary.businessContext: Establishing standards in a business ensures consistency in product quality and service delivery, which can enhance customer satisfaction and brand reputation.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both minimum requirements and aspirational benchmarks, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: To identify someone or something from previous encounters or knowledge; to acknowledge the existence or validity of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, recognizing employee contributions or market opportunities can foster a positive culture and drive innovation.

insight.nuance: While 'recognize' often conveys acknowledgment, it can also imply a deeper understanding or appreciation of value.

speaker: Seth Godin
text: Standards, it's worth understanding what quality is and the people who listen to this podcast know better than most. Quality is not luxury. Quality is not perfection. Quality means meeting spec, and if you meet spec, you're done.
keySentence: Quality means meeting spec; if not, make a better spec.
text_ko: 기준(standards) 얘기인데요, 품질이 무엇인지 제대로 이해하는 게 중요해요. 이 팟캐스트를 들으시는 분들은 대부분 그걸 더 잘 아세요. 품질은 사치가 아니고, 품질은 완벽함도 아니에요. 품질이란 스펙(spec)을 충족시키는 거예요. 스펙을 충족하면 그걸로 끝이에요. 스펙이 충분히 좋지 않다고 생각되면 더 나은 스펙을 만드세요.
text_zh: 说到标准，咱们得先搞清楚什么是质量，听这个播客的人比大部分人都更懂这个道理。质量不等于奢华，也不等于完美。质量就是达到规格要求，只要你达标了，就算完成任务了。如果你觉得现有的规格标准不够好，那就制定一个更好的标准。
text_es: Mira, hablando de estándares, vale la pena entender qué es realmente la calidad, y la gente que escucha este podcast lo sabe mejor que nadie. La calidad no es lujo. La calidad no es perfección. Calidad significa cumplir con las especificaciones, y si cumples con las especificaciones, ya está, listo. Si crees que las especificaciones no son lo suficientemente buenas, pues haz mejores especificaciones.
fullContext: Continuing the discussion about building high standards, Seth clarifies what quality actually means in product development. He argues that quality isn't about luxury or perfectionism, but about clearly defining specifications and meeting them consistently. His advice is that if you're unsatisfied with the current standard, improve the specification rather than endlessly tweaking a product that already meets requirements.

vocabulary.definition: Standards are established norms or requirements that serve as a basis for comparison or judgment in various contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, standards ensure consistency, safety, and quality across products and services, facilitating interoperability and compliance.

insight.nuance: While standards imply a baseline level of quality, they can vary significantly across industries and may evolve over time.

vocabulary.definition: Quality refers to the degree of excellence or the inherent characteristics of a product or service that meet specified requirements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, quality is crucial for customer satisfaction and can influence brand reputation, operational efficiency, and competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: Quality is often subjective and can differ based on customer expectations and industry standards, making it essential to define clearly in business contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Spec, short for specification, is a detailed description of the design, materials, and performance criteria for a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, specs guide the development process, ensuring that products meet the intended requirements and functionalities.

insight.nuance: While specs are critical for development, they can sometimes be perceived as rigid, potentially stifling innovation if not managed flexibly.

vocabulary.definition: Perfection is the state of being flawless or without any defects, often considered an ideal that is difficult to achieve.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, striving for perfection can lead to high-quality outcomes, but it may also result in inefficiencies or delays if it hinders timely delivery.

insight.nuance: While perfection is often desired, it can be counterproductive in fast-paced environments where meeting deadlines and specifications is prioritized over flawless execution.

speaker: Seth Godin
text: Tension is at the heart of every art form and every innovation.
keySentence: Tension is at the heart of every art form and every innovation.
text_ko: 긴장감은 모든 예술과 모든 혁신의 핵심이에요. 신제품을 출시할 때(launch) 우리가 하는 건 “이게 X를 할 수 있다”라고 말하는 거고, 그러면 사람들은 그게 사실이라면 자신의 삶이 어떻게 달라질지 상상해요. 그 가능성에 마음이 끌리면 긴장감이 생겨요. 진실을 말했나요? 그게 그들에게 통할까요?
text_zh: 张力是所有艺术形式和创新的核心。我们推出新产品的时候，其实就是在说，我们有个东西能做到X，然后用户就开始想象，要是真能这样，我的生活会变成什么样。如果他们爱上了这种可能性，张力就产生了。你说的是真话吗？这个产品对他们来说真的有用吗？
text_es: La tensión está en el corazón de cualquier forma de arte y de toda innovación. Lo que hacemos cuando lanzamos un producto nuevo es decir: "Tenemos esto que puede hacer X", y entonces la persona se imagina cómo podría ser su vida si eso fuera cierto. Si se enamoran de esa posibilidad, ahí surge la tensión. ¿Les dijiste la verdad? ¿Realmente les va a funcionar?
fullContext: Lenny asks Seth about a key concept from his new book - why great strategies need tension at their center. Seth distinguishes between harmful stress and productive tension, explaining that tension drives creativity and innovation. He describes how product launches create tension by making promises that cause customers to imagine better futures, creating suspense about whether the product will actually deliver on those promises.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating new ideas, products, or methods that improve efficiency or effectiveness. It often involves the application of creative thinking to solve problems or meet market needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, innovation is crucial for staying competitive, driving growth, and adapting to changing market demands, often leading to the development of new technologies or business models.

insight.nuance: While innovation typically has a positive connotation, it can also imply disruption or significant change, which may not always be welcomed by all stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: Yielding favorable results or outputs, particularly in relation to time and resources. It refers to the ability to generate significant outcomes efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, being productive is essential for maximizing profits and achieving organizational goals, often measured through performance metrics and output ratios.

insight.nuance: The term can imply not just quantity but also quality of work, and should be used carefully to avoid suggesting that mere output is sufficient without considering effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: A state of mental or emotional strain, often arising from conflicting demands or interests. It can also refer to the pressure that drives creativity and innovation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, tension can be a catalyst for innovation, as it often leads teams to confront challenges and develop creative solutions, though it can also lead to conflict if not managed properly.

insight.nuance: While tension can have a negative connotation, it can also be viewed positively as a necessary element for growth and creativity, particularly in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, often involving the allocation of resources and consideration of various factors and contingencies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, strategies are essential for guiding decision-making and resource allocation to achieve competitive advantage and meet organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: The term implies a level of foresight and planning, and should be used when discussing comprehensive approaches rather than ad-hoc or reactive measures.

speaker: Seth Godin
text: When you choose your smallest viable audience... you have chosen everything that's going to go into the product and what your future is going to be like.
keySentence: Choosing your smallest viable audience shapes your product and future.
text_ko: 당신이 최소 유효 고객층 (smallest viable audience)을 정할 때, 그들이 어떤 언어를 쓰는지, 재정 상태가 어떤지, 어떤 문제를 해결하려 하는지, 기술 숙련도 (technical facility)는 어떤지, 성미가 급한지, 친절한지, 당신과 계속 함께해줄 사람들인지까지 모두 선택하는 거예요. 그 선택들이 결국 제품에 들어갈 모든 것과 당신의 미래를 결정해요.
text_zh: 你选择最小可行受众(smallest viable audience)的时候，比如他们说什么语言、有多少钱、想解决什么问题、技术水平怎么样、是不是急性子、人品好不好、会不会跟你走到底，这些其实就已经决定了你的产品会做成什么样，你的未来会是什么样子。
