Era carísimo, como te digo, era como un tercio de la inversión que íbamos a hacer en contenido, casi la mitad de la inversión que íbamos a destinar al contenido.
fullContext: Tom is explaining what went wrong with Quibi's business model when they launched during COVID. He's describing how they had planned to create daily content in professional studios as a key differentiator from YouTube content, but the pandemic forced them to produce content from hosts' garages, undermining their value proposition and making their content indistinguishable from typical YouTube productions.

vocabulary.definition: A collection of previously released works or products that are still available for sale or distribution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in media and entertainment, a back catalog can represent a valuable asset for generating ongoing revenue through licensing, sales, or streaming.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a wealth of historical content that can be revisited or repackaged, but it may also suggest a lack of new offerings.

vocabulary.definition: Created or planned with a specific purpose or intention in mind, often involving careful consideration of aesthetics and functionality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term 'designed' is frequently used to describe products, services, or marketing strategies that have been thoughtfully developed to meet consumer needs or enhance user experience.

insight.nuance: While it generally conveys a positive connotation of intentionality and quality, it can also imply rigidity or lack of adaptability if overemphasized.

vocabulary.definition: The information, material, or substance that is presented or communicated, often in digital formats such as text, video, or audio.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, 'content' is crucial for engaging audiences, driving traffic, and building brand identity, particularly in digital marketing and media.

insight.nuance: While it typically refers to valuable or informative material, it can also imply a vast quantity of information that may lack depth or quality.

vocabulary.definition: A framework or strategy that outlines how a company creates, delivers, and captures value, including its revenue streams and cost structure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and established companies alike, a well-defined business model is essential for sustainability and growth, guiding decision-making and operational strategies.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both innovation and stability, but it may also suggest rigidity if a company fails to adapt its model to changing market conditions.

speaker: Tom Conrad
text: When I met our early audience in an incredibly genuine way. For example, when we launched the support@pandora.com was an alias for all@pandora.com. So if you sent a customer service request to Pandora, every single person in the company received it.
keySentence: We engaged our audience in an incredibly genuine way through direct requests.
text_ko: 초기 고객층과 정말 진심으로 소통했어요. 예를 들어 런칭할 때 support@pandora.com을 all@pandora.com의 별칭(alias)으로 설정해뒀어요. 그래서 누군가 Pandora에 고객 문의를 보내면 회사에 있는 모든 사람이 그 메일을 받았어요. 그리고 첫 해에는 고객 지원팀을 따로 두지 않기로 해서, 그 요청을 가장 먼저 본 사람이 답을 하기로 되어 있었어요.
text_zh: 我们刚开始的时候是真心实意地和早期用户打交道的。比如说，我们刚上线的时候，support@pandora.com其实就是all@pandora.com的别名。所以你要是给潘多拉发个客服邮件，公司里每个人都能收到。而且我们当时决定第一年不设专门的客服团队，就是谁先看到邮件谁就回复。
text_es: Cuando conecté con nuestra audiencia inicial de una manera súper auténtica. Por ejemplo, cuando lanzamos, el support@pandora.com era básicamente lo mismo que all@pandora.com. O sea, si mandabas una consulta de atención al cliente a Pandora, absolutamente toda la gente de la empresa la recibía. Y como decidimos no tener un equipo de atención al cliente el primer año, la cosa era que el que viera primero la consulta, esa persona tenía que responderla.
fullContext: Tom is sharing lessons from Pandora's early success when Lenny asks about what he learned from that experience. He's explaining how they built genuine relationships with users in the early days by having every employee handle customer support directly, without scripts or restrictions, which helped create authentic word-of-mouth growth that powered Pandora from zero to 80 million users without any paid acquisition.

vocabulary.definition: Authentic and sincere; not false or pretended.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being genuine often refers to building trust with customers and stakeholders through honest communication and actions.

insight.nuance: While 'genuine' conveys a positive connotation of sincerity, it should be used carefully to avoid implying that others are insincere.

vocabulary.definition: A group of individuals who receive or engage with content, products, or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and communications, understanding the target audience is crucial for tailoring messages and strategies effectively.

insight.nuance: The term 'audience' can imply a passive group, so it is important to consider their level of engagement when discussing interactions.

vocabulary.definition: Support and assistance provided to customers before, during, and after purchasing products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective customer service is vital for maintaining customer satisfaction and loyalty, often serving as a key differentiator in competitive markets.

insight.nuance: While 'customer service' generally has a positive connotation, poor service can lead to negative perceptions of a brand.

vocabulary.definition: Connections or associations between individuals or groups, often characterized by mutual interests or goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: Building strong relationships with customers, partners, and employees is essential for fostering collaboration and achieving long-term success.

insight.nuance: The term 'relationships' can imply varying degrees of intimacy and trust, so it is important to specify the nature of the relationship when discussing it.

speaker: Tom Conrad
text: I think we just completely misjudged one really important thing, which is that we were really inspired by disrupting terrestrial radio. Terrestrial radio is the predominant form of music consumption in the country.
keySentence: We completely misjudged the predominant form of music consumption: terrestrial radio.
text_ko: 우리는 한 가지를 완전히 잘못 판단한 것 같아요. 지상파 라디오(terrestrial radio)를 흔들어놓는 데서 많이 영감을 받았는데, 그 라디오는 이 나라에서 음악 소비의 주된 방식이었어요. 정확한 수치는 기억이 안 나지만, 재생 시간(분 기준)으로 보면 2000년대와 2010년대 초반에는 한 달에 라디오에서 소비되는 음악 시간이 소유 음악(owned music)보다 대략 10배 정도 많았던 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得我们完全看错了一个特别重要的点，就是我们当时特别想颠覆传统电台。传统电台是这个国家音乐消费的主要方式。人们花在听电台上的时间，我记不清具体数字了，但按分钟数算，在2000年代和2010年代初，每个月听电台音乐的时间比听自己买的音乐要多大概10倍。
text_es: Creo que nos equivocamos completamente con algo súper importante: estábamos obsesionados con revolucionar la radio tradicional. La radio tradicional es como la gente consume música principalmente en el país. La gente pasa, no me acuerdo de las cifras exactas, pero por minutos consumidos, es como 10 veces más minutos de música al mes en radio en los 2000 y principios de los 2010 que en música propia.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tom if there was a path for Pandora to become like Spotify and avoid being disrupted. Tom explains that Pandora's strategic mistake was focusing on disrupting terrestrial radio rather than the owned music market. They believed the radio advertising market was larger and less competitive, but this positioning put them at odds with record labels who preferred the Spotify subscription model.

vocabulary.definition: To form an incorrect opinion or conclusion about something or someone, often leading to poor decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, misjudging market trends or consumer behavior can result in failed products or strategies.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a lack of insight or understanding, and should be used when discussing errors in judgment rather than mere mistakes.

vocabulary.definition: Causing a disturbance or interruption, particularly in a way that alters the traditional way of doing things.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, disrupting existing markets often refers to introducing innovations that significantly change consumer behavior or industry standards.

insight.nuance: While 'disrupting' can have negative connotations, in a business context it is often viewed positively as a sign of innovation and progress.

vocabulary.definition: Being the most common or influential in a particular context or environment.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the predominant trends in a market is crucial for businesses to position themselves effectively against competitors.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a sense of dominance or superiority, and is best used when discussing market leaders or major influences.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
vocabulary.businessContext: Strategic planning is essential for businesses to allocate resources effectively and to achieve their objectives in a competitive landscape.

insight.nuance: The term 'strategic' implies a thoughtful and deliberate approach, and should be used when discussing plans that are designed to have a significant impact over time.

speaker: Tom Conrad
text: While companies are definitely the software that they make and the products that they deliver and that there is an art and science to that, as I described, there is also, if you step back, there is an equation that describes the business.
keySentence: there is also, if you step back, there is an equation that describes the business.
text_ko: 회사는 분명히 그들이 만드는 소프트웨어(software)와 제공하는 제품(products)이에요. 제가 설명한 대로 그 일에는 예술이자 과학(art and science)이 있죠. 하지만 한 걸음 물러나 보면 사업을 설명하는 수식(equation)이 있어요. 그 수식은 투자를 어떻게 수익(returns)으로 바꾸는지를 말해요. 만약 제가 금융학(finance)을 배우고 경영학 전공(business major)이었다면, 아마 애초부터 회사를 그렇게 생각했을 거예요.
text_zh: 公司当然就是他们开发的软件和交付的产品，这里面确实有技术和艺术的成分，就像我刚说的那样。但是你往后退一步看，其实有个公式可以描述这个生意本质，就是怎么把投资变成回报。我觉得如果我当初学的是金融，读商科出身的话，可能一开始就会这么看公司了。
text_es: Mira, las empresas obviamente son el software que desarrollan y los productos que entregan, y sí hay todo un arte y ciencia detrás de eso, como te decía, pero si das un paso atrás, también hay una ecuación que describe el negocio. Te explica cómo conviertes la inversión en retornos. Y supongo que si hubiera estudiado finanzas o hubiera sido especialista en negocios, tal vez esa habría sido mi forma de entender las empresas desde el principio.
fullContext: Tom is sharing what he's learned as a first-time CEO at Zero, his current health and longevity company. Lenny asks what he's learned as CEO that he wishes he knew as a product leader. Tom explains how his perspective evolved from seeing companies primarily as product and engineering challenges to understanding the fundamental business equations that drive success or failure.

vocabulary.definition: A mathematical statement that asserts the equality of two expressions, often used metaphorically to represent a relationship between different business variables.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an equation can symbolize the balance between various factors such as revenue, costs, and profits, helping leaders to make informed decisions.

insight.nuance: While often used in a literal mathematical sense, in business discussions, it conveys a broader conceptual relationship that may not be strictly quantifiable.

vocabulary.definition: To provide or bring something to a specified recipient or location, often referring to products, services, or results.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, delivering can refer to meeting customer expectations through timely provision of goods or services, which is critical for customer satisfaction and retention.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation when it implies reliability and efficiency; however, it can have negative implications if associated with missed deadlines or unmet expectations.

vocabulary.definition: A phrase that denotes the combination of creative intuition and analytical reasoning in a particular field or discipline.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the phrase 'art and science' often refers to the balance between creative marketing strategies and data-driven decision-making, emphasizing the need for both innovation and analysis.

insight.nuance: This expression suggests that successful outcomes require both subjective creativity and objective analysis, making it suitable for discussions about strategy and execution.

vocabulary.definition: To take a pause or to distance oneself from a situation in order to gain a broader perspective or reassess the circumstances.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, stepping back can be crucial for leaders to evaluate strategies, assess performance, and make informed decisions without being overly influenced by immediate pressures.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a need for reflection and strategic thinking, and is typically used in contexts where quick reactions may lead to poor decisions.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: When we look at the skills required to do your job, by 2030, it will change by 70%. So whether or not you're looking to change your job, your job is changing.
keySentence: by 2030, it will change by 70%.
text_ko: 여러분의 일을 해내는 데 필요한 스킬은 2030년까지 약 70%가 바뀔 거예요. 그래서 이직을 고려하든 안 하든, 지금 하고 있는 일이 변하고 있다는 뜻이에요. 경쟁력을 유지하려면 기본 원리(first principles)로 돌아가 백지에서 다시 시작하듯 도면을 다시 그려보고, ‘무엇을 만드는 것(building)’이 무엇인지 다시 상상해봐야 해요.
text_zh: 你看啊，到2030年的时候，你现在这份工作需要的技能会有70%都变掉。所以不管你想不想换工作，反正工作本身已经在变了。想要保持竞争力，你得回到最基本的原理上，重新来过，重新思考什么叫做"建设"。
text_es: Cuando miramos las habilidades que vas a necesitar para tu trabajo, para el 2030 van a cambiar en un 70%. O sea que quieras cambiar de trabajo o no, tu trabajo se está transformando. Para mantenerte competitivo, en realidad tienes que volver a lo básico, empezar desde cero y replantearte completamente lo que significa construir.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tomer why he decided to completely rethink how product development works at LinkedIn and why other leaders need to pay attention to this transformation. Tomer explains that LinkedIn has unique visibility into the changing nature of work, and their data shows that 70% of the skills required for any given job will change by 2030. This rapid pace of change means companies must fundamentally reimagine their approach to building products to stay competitive.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or characterized by significant change or transformation, often resulting in a fundamental shift in approach or perspective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'transformational' often describes initiatives or strategies that fundamentally alter an organization's operations, culture, or market position.

insight.nuance: This term carries a positive connotation, suggesting improvement and innovation, and is often used in contexts where change is viewed as necessary for growth.

vocabulary.definition: To consider or think about something again, especially in order to change or improve it.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'rethink' is often used when organizations evaluate their strategies, processes, or products to adapt to new market conditions or consumer needs.

insight.nuance: This term implies a critical reassessment and is often used in contexts where previous assumptions are challenged or need updating.

vocabulary.definition: The abilities or expertise that enable an individual to perform tasks effectively and efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of employment and career development, 'skills' refer to the competencies that are increasingly required in the workforce, particularly as technology and job roles evolve.

insight.nuance: The term can encompass both hard skills (technical abilities) and soft skills (interpersonal abilities), and its usage can vary based on the specific context of job requirements.

vocabulary.definition: The act or process of making something different, which can involve alterations in structure, function, or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'change' is often discussed in relation to organizational development, market dynamics, and the need for adaptation to remain competitive.

insight.nuance: While 'change' can have a neutral connotation, it often carries a sense of urgency or necessity in business discussions, particularly in fast-paced environments.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: So it wasn't like, "Oh, we have this cool technology, what can we do with it?" It was like, "Let go of what you've built.
keySentence: Let go of what you've built and focus on objectives with new technology.
text_ko: 그게 단순히 “우리에겐 멋진 기술이 있으니까 이걸로 뭐 해볼까?” 하는 식은 아니었어요. “지금까지 만든 것에 집착하지 말고, 원래 해결하려던 목표로 돌아가세요. 그리고 이 기술로 그 목표를 어떻게 더 잘 달성할 수 있을지부터 생각해보세요.”
text_zh: 所以不是说"哎，我们有这个酷炫的技术，能用它干点什么呢？"而是说"放下你已经做出来的东西，回到你最初想解决的问题上，现在有了这个技术，你怎么能把这个目标做得更好？"
text_es: No era como "Ay, tenemos esta tecnología súper cool, ¿qué podemos hacer con ella?" Era más bien "Suelta lo que ya construiste. Regresa a los objetivos que estabas tratando de resolver y ahora con esta tecnología, ¿cómo puedes lograr ese objetivo de manera más efectiva?"
fullContext: Lenny asks Tomer how he helps people shift to an AI-first mindset on the ground. Tomer explains that when LinkedIn started adopting AI more broadly, they didn't begin with the technology and then look for applications. Instead, he had teams abandon their existing roadmaps and return to their core objectives, then reimagine how AI could help them achieve those goals more effectively.

vocabulary.definition: A shift refers to a change or movement from one position, state, or condition to another.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a shift often describes changes in strategy, market trends, or organizational structure that can impact operations and decision-making.

insight.nuance: While 'shift' can imply a positive or negative change, it is often used in contexts where adaptation is necessary for growth or survival.

vocabulary.definition: A mindset is a set of beliefs or attitudes that shape how an individual thinks, feels, and behaves.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, a growth mindset is often encouraged to foster innovation, resilience, and adaptability among employees and leaders.

insight.nuance: Mindset can carry a connotation of rigidity or flexibility, depending on whether it is open to change or resistant to new ideas.

vocabulary.definition: Adopting refers to the act of taking up, accepting, or starting to use something new, such as a practice, idea, or technology.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, adopting new technologies or practices can be crucial for maintaining competitiveness and improving efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a proactive choice to embrace change rather than a passive acceptance of circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: Technology encompasses the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry, encompassing tools, systems, and methods.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startups, technology is a critical driver of innovation, efficiency, and competitive advantage, influencing everything from product development to customer engagement.

insight.nuance: While 'technology' can refer to both high-tech innovations and basic tools, it is often associated with modern advancements that transform industries.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: We call it the full stack builder model. The goal itself is to empower great builders to take their idea and to take it to market, regardless of their role and the stack and which team they're on.
keySentence: The full stack builder model empowers builders to take ideas to market.
text_ko: 우리는 그걸 풀스택 빌더 모델(full stack builder model)이라고 불러요. 목표는 훌륭한 빌더들이 자신의 아이디어를 어떤 역할을 맡고 있든, 어떤 스택(stack)을 쓰고 있든, 어떤 팀에 속해 있든 상관없이 아이디어를 실현해 시장에 내놓을 수 있도록 역량을 실어 주는 거예요. 사람과 기계가 유연하게 상호작용하는 방식이에요.
text_zh: 我们叫它全栈构建者模式(full stack builder model)。目标就是让那些厉害的构建者能够把自己的想法推向市场，不管他们在哪个岗位、用什么技术栈(stack)、在哪个团队。这其实就是人和机器之间很流畅的互动。
text_es: Lo llamamos el modelo de constructor integral (full stack builder). El objetivo en sí es empoderar a los grandes constructores para que tomen su idea y la lleven al mercado, sin importar cuál sea su rol, en qué parte del stack estén o en qué equipo trabajen. Es realmente una interacción fluida entre el humano y la máquina.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tomer to explain the name and concept of the new program LinkedIn has developed. The full stack builder model is LinkedIn's radical approach to product development that enables individual contributors to take products from idea to launch regardless of their traditional function. Unlike traditional teams where product managers, designers, and engineers work in sequence, this model creates a seamless collaboration between humans and AI tools.

vocabulary.definition: To give someone the authority or power to do something; to enable or support individuals to take control of their own actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, empowering employees often leads to increased innovation and productivity, as individuals feel more confident in making decisions and taking initiative.

insight.nuance: While 'empower' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a shift in responsibility that may not always be welcomed by all team members.

vocabulary.definition: To introduce a product or service to the marketplace, making it available for consumers to purchase.
vocabulary.businessContext: This phrase is commonly used in product launches and marketing strategies, indicating the transition from development to sales and customer engagement.

insight.nuance: The phrase suggests not only the act of launching but also the strategic planning involved in ensuring the product meets market needs.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the complete set of technologies and layers involved in software development, from front-end user interfaces to back-end databases and servers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, a 'full stack' approach allows teams to develop and manage all aspects of a product, enhancing flexibility and efficiency in development processes.

insight.nuance: While 'full stack' implies versatility, it can also suggest a lack of specialization, which may not always be ideal for complex projects.

vocabulary.definition: The process of designing, creating, and bringing a new product to market, encompassing all stages from ideation to launch.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, effective product development is crucial for meeting customer needs and achieving competitive advantage in the marketplace.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a structured approach, but it may also encompass agile methodologies that allow for rapid iteration and adaptation.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: To really set the new purpose for it, which was this is not a springboard for other products. This is not a traffic jumpstart, it's not an upsell feed. It's really about people that matter, talking about things that I care about professionally.
keySentence: This is not a springboard for other products; it's about people that matter.
text_ko: 정말로 그 서비스의 새 목적을 분명히 하자면, 다른 제품으로 이어지는 발판(springboard)이 아니에요. 트래픽을 급증시키기 위한 수단(traffic jumpstart)도 아니고, 업셀용 피드(upsell feed)도 아니에요. 핵심은 정말 중요한 사람들하고 제가 직업적으로 관심 있는 주제에 대해 이야기하는 거예요.
text_zh: 重新给它定位的话，就是说这不是为了推其他产品做跳板，也不是为了快速拉流量，更不是什么向上销售(upsell)的渠道。真正的目的就是让那些重要的人，来聊聊我在职业上真正关心的事情。
text_es: Para realmente definir el nuevo propósito, que era: esto no va a ser una plataforma de lanzamiento para otros productos. No es para generar tráfico rápido (traffic jumpstart), ni un canal para ventas adicionales (upsell feed). Realmente se trata de que gente que importa hable sobre temas que me interesan a nivel profesional.
fullContext: Lenny asks about specific tactics that made LinkedIn's feed more engaging and social. Tomer explains how they transformed LinkedIn's feed from what was essentially an activity tracker into something more valuable. Previously, the feed served as a way to drive traffic to other LinkedIn products, but they redefined its purpose to focus purely on professional knowledge sharing between relevant people.

vocabulary.definition: The reason for which something is done or created; an intended or desired result.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, defining a clear purpose is essential for guiding strategy, aligning team efforts, and communicating value to stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While 'purpose' can refer to a general aim, in a business context, it often implies a deeper mission that resonates with both employees and customers.

vocabulary.definition: Attracting or holding interest or attention; captivating.
vocabulary.businessContext: Engaging content or presentations are crucial in marketing and communication strategies to foster customer loyalty and enhance brand perception.

insight.nuance: The term 'engaging' often carries a positive connotation, suggesting that something is not only interesting but also interactive and participatory.

vocabulary.definition: To make a thorough or dramatic change in form, appearance, or character.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, 'transform' often refers to the process of innovating or pivoting business models to adapt to market demands.

insight.nuance: While 'transform' implies significant change, it can also suggest improvement or evolution rather than just alteration.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is appropriate for a professional setting; with competence and skill.
vocabulary.businessContext: Conducting oneself professionally is vital in business environments, as it fosters respect, trust, and effective communication among colleagues and clients.

insight.nuance: The term 'professionally' often implies adherence to industry standards and ethical practices, distinguishing it from casual or informal behavior.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: Change management here is going to be a critical part, but it's not enough to give them the tools. You have to build the incentives programs, the motivation, the examples to how you do it.
keySentence: it's not enough to give them the tools.
text_ko: 여기서 변화 관리(change management)는 핵심인데, 도구만 주는 것으로는 부족해요. 인센티브 프로그램(incentive programs)과 동기 부여, 어떻게 하는지 보여주는 사례들을 만들어야 해요. 많은 회사들이 에이전트(agents)를 배포해 놓고 알아서 채택되길 기대하는데, 그렇게 되지 않아요.
text_zh: 变革管理(change management)在这里会是关键一环，但光给他们工具还不够。你得建立激励机制、调动积极性，还要给出具体的操作示例。我看到很多公司就是把代理工具(agents)一推出去，就指望企业会自动采用。这样搞肯定不行的。
text_es: La gestión del cambio va a ser clave aquí, pero no basta con darles las herramientas. Tienes que crear programas de incentivos, la motivación, ejemplos de cómo hacerlo. Veo muchas empresas que lanzan sus agentes y simplemente esperan que las compañías los adopten. Así no funciona la cosa.
fullContext: Lenny observes that top performers are finding the most success with AI tools and asks about adoption challenges. Tomer explains that simply providing AI tools to employees isn't sufficient for organizational transformation. He emphasizes that successful adoption requires comprehensive change management including performance incentives, motivational programs, and concrete examples of success. He notes that many companies fail by just deploying AI agents without supporting the cultural shift needed for adoption.

vocabulary.definition: Change management refers to the structured approach to transitioning individuals, teams, and organizations from a current state to a desired future state.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology settings, effective change management is crucial for implementing new processes, technologies, or organizational structures while minimizing resistance and maximizing engagement.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a systematic process that includes planning, communication, and support, and should be used when discussing formal strategies to manage transitions.

vocabulary.definition: Incentives programs are structured initiatives designed to motivate individuals or teams to achieve specific goals or behaviors through rewards or recognition.
vocabulary.businessContext: Incentives programs are commonly used in corporate environments to enhance employee performance, increase productivity, and foster loyalty by aligning individual goals with organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: While incentives programs can be effective, they should be carefully designed to ensure they promote desired behaviors without unintended consequences, such as unhealthy competition.

vocabulary.definition: Motivation is the internal or external drive that prompts individuals to take action towards achieving goals or fulfilling needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, understanding employee motivation is essential for leaders to create an environment that fosters engagement, productivity, and job satisfaction.

insight.nuance: The term encompasses both intrinsic and extrinsic factors, and should be used when discussing the reasons behind an individual's or team's actions.

vocabulary.definition: Adoption challenges refer to the obstacles and difficulties encountered when implementing new practices, technologies, or systems within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, addressing adoption challenges is critical for ensuring that new solutions are embraced by users and integrated into existing workflows.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a focus on the barriers to acceptance rather than the benefits of the new initiative, and is often used in discussions about user experience and change management.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: I start backwards. It's like what is the potential here? If you start from the premise that LinkedIn ultimately is a platform for economic opportunity that sits on top of a very strong social graph. Almost every aspect of economic transaction is possible.
keySentence: Start backwards to realize LinkedIn's potential as a platform for economic opportunity.
text_ko: 저는 뒤에서부터 시작해요. 여기서 잠재력이 뭔지부터 보는 식이에요. 만약 LinkedIn이 궁극적으로 아주 강한 소셜 그래프(social graph) 위에 자리한, 경제적 기회(economic opportunity)를 제공하는 플랫폼이라고 전제하면, 거의 모든 형태의 경제적 거래(economic transaction)가 가능해요.
text_zh: 我是倒着思考的。就是说这里的潜力到底有多大？如果你从这个角度出发——领英本质上就是一个经济机会的平台，而且建立在非常强大的社交图谱(social graph)基础上。这样的话，几乎所有的经济交易都是可能的。
text_es: Yo empiezo al revés. Es como ¿cuál es el potencial real aquí? Si partes de la base de que LinkedIn al final es una plataforma de oportunidades económicas que se monta sobre una red social súper sólida. Prácticamente cualquier tipo de transacción económica es posible.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the strategy behind LinkedIn's transformation into a platform people check frequently. Tomer describes his approach to product strategy, which involves starting with the end vision rather than current constraints. He explains LinkedIn's fundamental value proposition as connecting economic opportunities through professional relationships, which opens up massive possibilities for different types of value exchanges.

vocabulary.definition: The inherent ability or capacity for growth, development, or future success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'potential' often refers to the ability of a market, product, or individual to achieve significant success or profitability.

insight.nuance: While 'potential' is generally positive, it can imply that actual success has not yet been realized.

vocabulary.definition: A foundational idea or assumption upon which a theory, argument, or business model is based.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, a strong premise is essential for developing effective plans and justifying decisions.

insight.nuance: The term suggests that the validity of conclusions depends on the strength of the premise; a weak premise can lead to flawed outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: A situation or condition that allows for the potential to generate income or create wealth.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying economic opportunities is crucial for entrepreneurs and investors seeking to capitalize on market trends or gaps.

insight.nuance: This phrase often carries a positive connotation, suggesting growth and advancement, but can also imply competition and risk.

vocabulary.definition: A foundational technology or service that enables the development and delivery of applications, products, or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, a platform often refers to software or infrastructure that supports various applications and user interactions, such as social media or e-commerce sites.

insight.nuance: The term can imply scalability and versatility, but may also suggest dependency on the platform for success.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: Top talent has this tendency of continuously trying to get better at their craft. The key trait that I'm emphasizing for builders is where I want them to spend their time is where I think great builders should shine in.
keySentence: Top talent continuously tries to get better at their craft and shine in.
text_ko: 최고 인재들은 자신의 실력을 계속해서 더 나아지게 하려는 경향이 있어요. 제가 빌더들(builders)에게 특히 강조하는 핵심은 그들이 시간을 어디에 쓰느냐인데, 바로 그 지점에서 훌륭한 빌더들이 빛나야 한다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 顶尖人才都有一个特点，就是会不断地想要在自己的专业领域做得更好。我特别看重做产品的人(builders)的一个品质，就是我希望他们把时间花在真正能让优秀产品人发光发热的地方。
text_es: El talento de primera tiene esa tendencia de siempre estar tratando de mejorar en lo suyo. La característica clave que les recalco a los que construyen es en qué quiero que inviertan su tiempo, ahí es donde creo que los grandes constructores realmente deben brillar.
fullContext: Lenny questions whether AI makes average people better or makes great people even better. Tomer confirms that LinkedIn's top performers are the most successful with their new AI-powered tools, explaining that high performers naturally seek to improve their craft and stay at the cutting edge. He then transitions to describing the specific traits he wants builders to focus on - vision, empathy, communication, creativity, and judgment - rather than automatable tasks.

vocabulary.definition: A tendency refers to an inclination or a habitual pattern of behavior or thought. It indicates a likelihood or predisposition towards a certain action or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding the tendencies of employees or market trends can help organizations anticipate changes and make informed strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: While 'tendency' suggests a natural inclination, it does not imply certainty, making it important to consider context when discussing behaviors or trends.

vocabulary.definition: Emphasizing means to give special importance or prominence to something in order to highlight its significance or value. It often involves stressing particular points to ensure they are understood.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, emphasizing key messages during presentations or communications can enhance clarity and ensure that critical information is retained by the audience.

insight.nuance: The act of emphasizing can convey urgency or priority, so it should be used judiciously to avoid diluting the impact of the message.

vocabulary.definition: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic or quality, especially one that forms a part of an individual's personality. Traits can be inherent or developed over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying key traits in employees can help organizations in recruitment and team dynamics, as certain traits may be more conducive to specific roles or company cultures.

insight.nuance: While 'trait' often refers to positive attributes, it can also encompass negative characteristics, so context is essential when discussing traits in a professional environment.

vocabulary.definition: Performers are individuals who execute tasks or roles, often in a context that requires skill, talent, or effectiveness. This term can apply to various fields, including arts, sports, and business.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, high performers are often recognized for their contributions and are essential to driving success and achieving organizational goals.

insight.nuance: The term 'performers' can carry a connotation of excellence, so it is typically used to describe individuals who exceed standard expectations or deliver outstanding results.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: It's rooted in clarity and principles that ultimately lead to leadership. And the first time I got the inspiration from it was from a startup founder I met many, many years ago. Their company was on the brink of failure.
keySentence: It's rooted in clarity and principles that lead to effective leadership.
text_ko: 그건 결국 리더십(leadership)으로 이어지는 명확함과 원칙에 뿌리를 두고 있어요. 그걸로부터 영감을 처음 받은 건 아주 오래전에 만난 한 스타트업 창업자였어요. 그 회사는 거의 망하기 직전이었고, 마지막 기회로 앞으로 나아갈 한 길을 정했어요. 그런데 방향을 정한 뒤에도 사람들이 여전히 여러 쪽으로 눈치 보며 주저하는, 즉 헤지(hedging)를 하는 모습이 보였고 그 때문에 조직적으로 혼란이 생겼어요.
text_zh: 这个理念源于清晰的思路和原则，最终会带来领导力。我第一次受到启发是很多很多年前遇到的一个创业者。当时他们公司快要倒闭了，就剩最后一次机会，他们确定了前进方向。但是确定方向之后，他还是看到团队里的人在观望，往不同方向摇摆，这就造成了系统性的混乱——明明已经定了方向，大家还在那里犹豫不决。
text_es: Se basa en la claridad y en principios que al final te llevan al liderazgo. Y la primera vez que me inspiré en esto fue con un fundador de startup que conocí hace muchísimos años. Su empresa estaba al borde del fracaso. Era su último intento y decidieron el rumbo a seguir, pero después de decidir el rumbo, él seguía viendo que la gente se cubría las espaldas en diferentes direcciones y esto creó una confusión en el sistema donde ya habíamos decidido, pero la gente seguía protegiéndose por si acaso.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tomer to explain his famous phrase "We might be wrong but we're not confused." Tomer shares the origin story of this philosophy, describing how a startup founder realized that even after making a decision, team members were still pursuing different approaches. This hedging behavior created organizational confusion that prevented them from having any chance of success, even though alignment wouldn't guarantee success.

vocabulary.definition: Clarity refers to the quality of being clear and easy to understand, particularly in communication or thought processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, clarity is crucial for effective communication, ensuring that team members understand goals, strategies, and expectations.

insight.nuance: While clarity is generally positive, excessive simplification can sometimes overlook important complexities.

vocabulary.definition: Principles are fundamental truths or propositions that serve as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, principles guide decision-making processes and corporate culture, influencing how a company operates and interacts with stakeholders.

insight.nuance: Principles are often seen as immutable, but they can evolve as organizations grow and adapt to new challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Leadership is the act of guiding and influencing individuals or groups towards achieving common goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective leadership is vital in business environments, as it fosters motivation, drives performance, and shapes organizational culture.

insight.nuance: Leadership can be formal or informal; sometimes, individuals can lead without holding a designated leadership position.

vocabulary.definition: A startup is a newly established business, typically in the early stages of development, often focused on innovative products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, startups are frequently characterized by their pursuit of rapid growth and scalability, often seeking venture capital to fund their operations.

insight.nuance: While all startups are new businesses, not all new businesses are startups; the term usually implies a focus on innovation and high growth potential.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: We ended up building our own trust agent at LinkedIn.
keySentence: We ended up building our own trust agent at LinkedIn.
text_ko: 결국 LinkedIn에서 저희만의 트러스트 에이전트(trust agent)를 만들게 되었어요. 그래서 스펙(spec)을 만들거나 아이디어를 구체화할 때 그 에이전트로 쭉 검토해 보면, 어떤 취약점이 있는지와 그로 인해 어떤 피해 벡터(harm vectors)가 생기거나 유발될 수 있는지를 알려줘요.
text_zh: 我们最后在LinkedIn自己搭建了一个信任代理(trust agent)。所以当你在做规划、构思想法的时候，你把这些过一遍信任代理，它基本上就能告诉你有哪些漏洞，可能会带来什么样的风险点，或者说因为这个决定可能会产生什么隐患。
text_es: Terminamos creando nuestro propio agente de confianza en LinkedIn. Entonces, cuando armas una especificación, cuando desarrollas una idea, la pasas por el agente de confianza y básicamente te dice cuáles son tus vulnerabilidades, qué vectores de daño (harm vectors) potencialmente estás introduciendo o que se van a introducir como resultado de eso.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the specific AI agents LinkedIn has built to automate parts of product development. Tomer explains that LinkedIn couldn't use off-the-shelf AI tools and had to build custom agents tailored to their specific needs. The trust agent is one example - it analyzes product specifications and identifies potential security vulnerabilities and harm vectors that could affect users. This agent was built by LinkedIn's head of trust and incorporates all their unique trust considerations.

vocabulary.definition: To use technology to perform tasks without human intervention, thereby increasing efficiency and consistency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, automation is often employed to streamline processes, reduce labor costs, and enhance productivity across various operations.

insight.nuance: While 'automate' suggests efficiency, it may also imply a reduction in workforce, so it should be used carefully in discussions about job impacts.

vocabulary.definition: Tailored or made to meet specific requirements or preferences of an individual or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, custom products or services are often developed to satisfy unique client needs, enhancing customer satisfaction and loyalty.

insight.nuance: The term 'custom' conveys a sense of personalization, which can be a strong selling point, but it may also imply higher costs and longer delivery times.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating a new product or improving an existing one, from initial concept through design, testing, and market launch.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, effective product development is crucial for innovation and competitiveness, often involving cross-functional teams to ensure market fit.

insight.nuance: While 'product development' emphasizes innovation, it also requires balancing creativity with practical considerations like cost and feasibility.

vocabulary.definition: An individual or system that establishes and maintains trust between parties, often by ensuring transparency and reliability in interactions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, trust agents play a vital role in building relationships with customers and stakeholders, particularly in industries where trust is paramount, such as finance and technology.

insight.nuance: The term 'trust agent' implies a proactive role in fostering trust, which is essential in environments where skepticism may exist; however, it should not be confused with mere compliance or regulation.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: I get attached to clarity and focus.
keySentence: I get attached to clarity and focus.
text_ko: 제가 보기엔, 특히 알파 성향(alpha types)이 많은 환경을 만들면 사람들은 옳고 그름에 집착하게 돼요. 그게 시스템에 오래 남아 많은 혼란을 만들고 사람들이 자기 아이디어에 붙들려 있게 해요. 저는 대신 명확성(clarity)과 집중(focus)에 집착해요.
text_zh: 我发现很多人，特别是在那种聚集了很多强势型人才(alpha types)的环境里，他们就是放不下对错这个执念，这样一来整个团队就会拖泥带水的，大家都糊里糊涂的，还死抱着自己那套想法不放。但我不一样，我在乎的是把事情想明白，把注意力集中起来。
text_es: Lo que veo es que la gente se aferra mucho, especialmente cuando tienes un ambiente lleno de personalidades alfa, se aferran a tener razón o estar equivocados y eso realmente crea mucho estancamiento en el sistema, mucha confusión, y siguen pegados a sus ideas. En mi caso, yo me enfoco en la claridad y en mantener el rumbo.
fullContext: Tomer explains the first part of his "not confused" philosophy, which focuses on clarity of thought. He describes how in organizations with many driven, competitive people (alpha types), there's often too much emphasis on being right versus being clear about direction. This attachment to being correct causes people to linger on debates and remain stuck on their original ideas rather than moving forward with a clear, unified approach.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being clear and easy to understand, often relating to communication or thought processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, clarity is crucial for effective communication, ensuring that team members understand objectives, strategies, and tasks without ambiguity.

insight.nuance: While clarity is generally positive, excessive simplification can sometimes lead to oversights or a lack of depth in discussions.

vocabulary.definition: The concentration of attention or effort on a particular task or goal, often leading to improved productivity and outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, maintaining focus is essential for teams to achieve their objectives efficiently, especially in fast-paced or competitive markets.

insight.nuance: Focus can imply a narrowing of attention, which is beneficial but may also lead to neglecting other important areas if not balanced properly.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a strong desire to be more successful than others, often resulting in rivalry and the pursuit of excellence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, being competitive is vital for survival and growth, as companies strive to outperform their rivals in market share, innovation, and customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: While competitiveness can drive innovation and improvement, it can also foster unhealthy rivalries or unethical practices if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: A set of beliefs or principles that guide behavior and decision-making, often reflecting an organization's core values and mission.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a company's philosophy shapes its culture, influences strategic decisions, and can differentiate it from competitors in the marketplace.

insight.nuance: While philosophy can provide a strong foundation for decision-making, it may also need to adapt over time to remain relevant in a changing business environment.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: Whether you're in an organization, you're waiting for your leader to roll this out or you're a leader trying to roll this out, I would not wait. If you're looking for a formal reorg or declaration to start building differently, you're waiting too long.
keySentence: Don't wait for a formal reorg; start building differently now.
text_ko: 조직 안에서 리더가 이걸 도입(roll out)해 주길 기다리든, 리더로서 직접 도입하려 하든, 저는 기다리지 말라고 권해요. 형식적인 재편(reorg)이나 선언을 기다려서 다르게 만들어 가기 시작하려 한다면, 이미 너무 늦었어요.
text_zh: 不管你是在公司里等着领导推这个事儿，还是你就是那个要推的领导，我觉得都别等了。如果你还在等什么正式的重组或者官方声明才开始换个思路做事，那就等太久了。
text_es: Ya sea que estés en una organización esperando a que tu jefe implemente esto, o seas tú el líder tratando de implementarlo, yo no esperaría. Si estás esperando una reestructuración formal o una declaración oficial para empezar a construir de manera diferente, te estás tardando demasiado.
fullContext: In his final advice, Lenny asks what leaders should know about implementing similar AI-powered product development changes. Tomer emphasizes urgency and personal agency rather than waiting for organizational permission. He argues that individuals should start experimenting with AI tools and adopting a full-stack builder mindset immediately, regardless of whether their company has formally announced such programs. He believes waiting for official reorganizations or declarations will put people behind in the rapidly changing landscape.

vocabulary.definition: To introduce or launch a new product, service, or initiative gradually or systematically.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'rolling out' often refers to the phased implementation of a new strategy or technology across different departments or locations.

insight.nuance: The term implies a careful and planned approach rather than an abrupt or uncoordinated launch.

vocabulary.definition: The quality or state of requiring immediate attention or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, urgency can drive decision-making processes and prioritization of tasks, especially in fast-paced environments like startups.

insight.nuance: While urgency can motivate action, it may also lead to hasty decisions if not managed appropriately.

vocabulary.definition: The act of putting a plan or decision into effect.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, implementing refers to the execution of strategies, policies, or technologies to achieve organizational goals.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the practical application of ideas rather than just their conceptualization.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity of individuals to act independently and make their own choices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In organizational settings, fostering personal agency can empower employees, encouraging innovation and proactive problem-solving.

insight.nuance: While personal agency is often viewed positively, it may clash with hierarchical structures in some organizations.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: I love solutions that are based on first principles. That they have, there's a principle thinking about it, there's opinions about it.
keySentence: I love solutions that are based on first principles.
text_ko: 저는 기본 원칙(first principles)을 바탕으로 한 해결책을 정말 좋아해요. 그 해결책에는 원칙이 있고, 그에 대한 의견도 있어요. 저와 함께 일하는 사람들에게 물어보면, 저는 항상 여러분의 의견, 특히 논란이 될 수 있는 의견을 많이 강조한다고 말할 거예요. 가장 좋은 원칙은 확실한 힘이 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 我特别喜欢那种基于第一性原理(first principles)的解决方案。就是说，你得有原则性的思考，得有自己的观点。跟我共事过的人都知道，我经常会追问：你真正的观点是什么？你有什么可能比较有争议的看法？最好的原则都是有锋芒的。
text_es: Me encantan las soluciones que parten de principios fundamentales (first principles). Que tengan, que haya un pensamiento de principios detrás, que haya opiniones al respecto. Si hablas con la gente que trabaja conmigo, te van a decir que siempre presiono mucho para saber cuál es realmente tu opinión, cuál es tu opinión potencialmente polémica, porque los mejores principios tienen fuerza, tienen sustancia.
fullContext: Tomer continues explaining his approach to clarity of thought in product development. After spending time clearly defining problems, he focuses on developing solutions based on first principles - fundamental truths that guide decision-making. He emphasizes the importance of having strong, potentially controversial opinions rather than generic statements, because meaningful principles require making trade-offs that not everyone will agree with.

vocabulary.definition: A fundamental truth or proposition that serves as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, principles guide decision-making processes and strategic planning, ensuring that actions align with core values and objectives.

insight.nuance: While 'principle' often denotes a strong foundational belief, it can also imply rigidity; thus, it is important to balance principles with flexibility in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being clear and easy to understand, free from ambiguity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, clarity is essential for effective communication, ensuring that all stakeholders comprehend objectives, strategies, and expectations.

insight.nuance: Clarity is often sought in presentations and reports, but excessive simplification can lead to oversights; thus, it is important to maintain a balance between clarity and depth.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, an approach refers to the specific methodology employed to tackle challenges, innovate, or achieve goals, such as agile or lean methodologies.

insight.nuance: The term 'approach' can imply a particular style or perspective, and it is often used to describe both formal strategies and informal tactics; context is key to its interpretation.

vocabulary.definition: Answers or methods for effectively addressing a problem or challenge.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, solutions are often developed to meet customer needs, resolve operational issues, or enhance product offerings, emphasizing innovation and efficiency.

insight.nuance: While 'solutions' suggests a definitive answer, it can also imply ongoing processes or adaptations; thus, it is important to recognize that solutions may evolve over time.

speaker: Tomer Cohen
text: When I reflect back on what works across my early career, it really comes down in a nutshell to this career concept of explore and exploit.
keySentence: it really comes down in a nutshell to this career concept of explore and exploit.
text_ko: 제 초기 커리어를 되돌아보면, 결국 한마디로 요약하면 커리어 개념인 ‘탐색과 활용(explore and exploit)’이에요. 사람은 보통 두 가지 모드 중 하나에 있어요. 하나는 탐색자 모드로, 모르는 게 많아서 이게 맞는지, 좋아하는지 시험해 보는 단계고요. 다른 하나는 활용 모드로, 이미 정말 풍부하고 깊은 무언가를 찾아서 그걸 집중적으로 파고드는 단계예요.
text_zh: 回想我职业生涯早期那些成功的经验，说白了就是两个词：探索和深挖。你要么处在探索模式，面对一堆未知的东西，去试试看自己到底喜不喜欢；要么就是在深挖模式，已经找到了真正有价值、很有潜力的方向，然后全力去做。
text_es: Cuando miro hacia atrás y pienso en qué funcionó durante mis primeros años profesionales, todo se resume básicamente en este concepto de carrera: explorar y explotar. O estás en modo explorador, donde tienes un montón de incógnitas y estás probando a ver si te gusta o no, o estás explotando, donde ya encontraste algo que realmente vale la pena y tiene mucha sustancia.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tomer for specific career advancement advice based on his rapid rise at LinkedIn. Tomer shares what he learned about his own career journey, describing a framework he calls "explore and exploit." In the exploration phase, you test different opportunities to discover what you enjoy and excel at. In the exploitation phase, you go deep into areas where you've found something valuable and meaningful to build expertise.

vocabulary.definition: To think deeply or carefully about something, often to gain insight or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, reflecting on past experiences can help leaders identify successful strategies and areas for improvement.

insight.nuance: While 'reflect' suggests a thoughtful consideration, it may imply a more passive approach compared to active analysis or critique.

vocabulary.definition: To investigate or examine a subject or area in depth, often to discover new information or opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a startup context, teams often explore new markets or technologies to identify potential growth areas and innovations.

insight.nuance: The term 'explore' conveys a sense of curiosity and openness to new ideas, which is essential in dynamic business environments.

vocabulary.definition: To make full use of and benefit from a resource or opportunity, often with a connotation of taking advantage of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, exploiting market opportunities or technological advancements can lead to competitive advantages and increased profitability.

insight.nuance: While 'exploit' can have a negative connotation of unfair advantage, in a business context, it often refers to strategic utilization of resources.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a basis for understanding or organizing complex concepts or processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, frameworks are used to analyze situations, guide decision-making, and develop strategic plans.

insight.nuance: The term 'framework' suggests a foundational structure that supports further development, making it essential in strategic planning and analysis.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: The day I understood that speaking was a subconscious flow-oriented process and not a conscious process, completely changed the way I approached it.
keySentence: Speaking is a subconscious flow-oriented process, not a conscious process.
text_ko: 말하기가 의식적인 과정(conscious process)이 아니라 무의식적이고 흐름 중심의 과정(subconscious flow-oriented process)이라는 걸 알게 된 날, 말에 대한 제 접근 방식이 완전히 달라졌어요. 그래서 전술이나 프레임워크(tactics and frameworks)를 더 생각해서 말하기에 관해 겉으로 뭔가를 더 얹으려 하기보다는, 제가 가장 잘 말할 때는 사실 말하는 것 자체를 전혀 생각하고 있지 않다는 걸 깨달았어요.
text_zh: 当我意识到说话其实是一个下意识的流动过程，而不是有意识控制的过程时，我的整个思路就彻底变了。以前我总想着各种技巧和框架(frameworks)，脑子里装一堆要考虑的东西，但后来我发现，其实我说话最好的时候，恰恰是我根本没在想着怎么说话的时候。
text_es: El día que entendí que hablar era un proceso subconsciente que fluye naturalmente y no algo consciente, me cambió completamente la forma de enfocarlo. Entonces, en lugar de estar pensando en tácticas y esquemas mentales (frameworks) y agregar más cosas en las que tengo que pensar, cuando me di cuenta de cuándo hablo mejor, en realidad no estoy pensando en el acto de hablar.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tristan about core principles that inform his approach to teaching public speaking. Tristan explains that the biggest breakthrough in his understanding was realizing that effective speaking happens when you're in a flow state rather than consciously thinking about speaking techniques. He emphasizes that the best speakers aren't focused on the mechanics of speaking but are completely absorbed in conveying their message to the audience.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the part of the mind that is not fully aware but influences thoughts and behaviors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, understanding subconscious motivations can enhance marketing strategies and improve team dynamics.

insight.nuance: While often associated with hidden desires or instincts, the term can imply a lack of conscious control, which may not always be favorable in a professional context.

vocabulary.definition: A method or way of dealing with a situation or problem.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, a strategic approach can determine the success of projects, negotiations, and overall business operations.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a systematic or planned method, and should be used when discussing strategies rather than casual or informal methods.

vocabulary.definition: A significant and sudden advance or discovery that leads to a major improvement or change.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and innovation sectors, breakthroughs can lead to competitive advantages and market leadership.

insight.nuance: Often used in contexts of research and development, it suggests a level of innovation that is both impactful and transformative.

vocabulary.definition: Producing a desired or intended result; successful in achieving a goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, effective strategies and practices are crucial for maximizing productivity and achieving organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: While synonymous with success, 'effective' can also imply efficiency, so it should be used when results are achieved with optimal resource use.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: I actually think that the biggest misconception with tackling your speaking is that people grossly underestimate just how transformative it could be to your life. And the reason it's so transformative is because speaking is not a specialized skill, it's a meta skill.
keySentence: People grossly underestimate how transformative speaking is; it's a meta skill.
text_ko: 사실 말하기 실력을 다루면서 가장 큰 오해는 사람들이 그게 자기 삶을 얼마나 크게 바꿀 수 있는지를 과소평가한다는 거예요. 그게 그렇게 큰 변화를 만드는 이유는 말하기가 특정 분야의 전문 기술이 아니라 메타 스킬 (meta skill)이기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得大家对提升演讲能力最大的误解就是，严重低估了它对你人生的改变有多大。为什么说它这么有改变力呢？因为演讲不是什么专业技能，它是一种元技能(meta skill)。
text_es: En realidad creo que el mayor error que comete la gente al trabajar en su forma de hablar es que subestiman completamente lo transformador que puede llegar a ser para su vida. Y la razón por la que es tan transformador es porque hablar no es una habilidad especializada, es una meta-habilidad (meta skill).
fullContext: Lenny asks about the biggest misconceptions people have about becoming a better public speaker. Tristan explains that people don't realize how life-changing improving speaking skills can be. He introduces the concept that speaking is a 'meta skill' - meaning that getting better at speaking improves many other areas of your life, similar to how fitness benefits extend beyond just physical health.

vocabulary.definition: A misunderstanding or incorrect belief about a particular subject or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, misconceptions can lead to poor decision-making or ineffective strategies, as stakeholders may operate under false assumptions.

insight.nuance: While often unintentional, misconceptions can be deeply ingrained and may require significant effort to correct.

vocabulary.definition: Causing a marked change in someone or something, often leading to significant improvement or development.
vocabulary.businessContext: Transformative initiatives in business can lead to innovation, increased efficiency, and enhanced employee engagement, fundamentally altering the company's trajectory.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a positive change, but it can also refer to disruptive changes that may not be immediately beneficial.

vocabulary.definition: A specific ability or expertise that is developed through training or experience in a particular field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, specialized skills such as programming languages or data analysis are highly sought after for specific roles and projects.

insight.nuance: While valuable, specialized skills can sometimes limit flexibility, as they may not be applicable in broader contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A foundational skill that enhances the ability to learn and apply other skills effectively across various contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a rapidly changing business environment, meta skills such as communication, critical thinking, and adaptability are essential for long-term success and career advancement.

insight.nuance: Meta skills are often considered more valuable than specialized skills because they enable individuals to navigate diverse challenges and opportunities.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: People tend to self-sabotage a lot. I'm speaking, and obviously as I'm speaking, all of my senses are really, really heightened.
keySentence: People tend to self-sabotage a lot.
text_ko: 사람들은 스스로를 망치는 경우가 많아요(self-sabotage). 제가 말할 때는 당연히 모든 감각이 아주 예민해져요. 그래서 사소한 것까지 다 의식하게 돼요. 어떤 단어가 조금 이상하게 나오거나 제 입에서 나올 줄 예상했던 말과 다르면 그게 훨씬 더 신경 쓰여요, 기대했던 게 있는데 다른 일이 일어나니까요.
text_zh: 人很容易自我破坏。我在讲话的时候，很明显我所有的感官都特别敏锐。所以我能察觉到一切，如果有个词说得有点别扭，或者说出来的不是我本来想说的那个词，我马上就会意识到，因为我本来期待的是一个结果，结果出来的却是另一个。
text_es: La gente tiende a sabotearse mucho a sí misma. Cuando estoy hablando, obviamente mientras hablo, todos mis sentidos están súper alerta. Entonces me doy cuenta de todo - si una palabra sale medio rara o no es la palabra que esperaba que saliera de mi boca, me voy a dar cuenta enseguida porque estaba esperando una cosa y salió otra diferente.
fullContext: Tristan is explaining his third tactical tip about 'staying in character' while speaking. He describes how speakers become hyper-aware of small mistakes or imperfections during their presentation. This heightened awareness often leads to self-sabotage where speakers break character by commenting on their mistakes, even though the audience typically doesn't notice these minor issues.

vocabulary.definition: The act of undermining one's own success or well-being through negative thoughts or behaviors. It often manifests as procrastination, fear of failure, or self-doubt.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, self-sabotage can hinder personal and team performance, leading to missed opportunities and decreased productivity. Recognizing and addressing self-sabotaging behaviors is crucial for effective leadership and team dynamics.

insight.nuance: While self-sabotage is often discussed in personal development contexts, it can also be a critical factor in professional environments, especially when discussing mental health and resilience.

vocabulary.definition: Increased in intensity or degree; made more acute or pronounced. It often refers to heightened awareness or sensitivity to stimuli.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, heightened awareness can refer to increased vigilance in market trends, customer feedback, or competitive analysis, which can lead to better strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting improved focus or alertness, but can also imply stress or anxiety if the heightened state is excessive.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to actions or strategies that are designed to achieve a specific end or goal, often in a practical or immediate context. It contrasts with strategic, which refers to long-term planning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, tactical decisions are often made to address short-term challenges or opportunities, such as marketing campaigns or operational adjustments, that support broader strategic objectives.

insight.nuance: While tactical actions are essential for immediate results, over-reliance on them without a strategic framework can lead to reactive rather than proactive business practices.

vocabulary.definition: Having an acute awareness of one's surroundings or circumstances, often to an excessive degree. This state can lead to heightened sensitivity to details and potential issues.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business environment, being hyper-aware can be beneficial for leaders and teams in identifying risks, understanding customer needs, and adapting to market changes quickly.

insight.nuance: While hyper-awareness can enhance performance and responsiveness, it can also lead to stress or burnout if individuals become overwhelmed by the constant influx of information.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: If you start leaking and letting the insecurities come out, people are going to start thinking, this person doesn't really know what they're talking about. It's like a leader who isn't clear in their direction.
keySentence: people are going to start thinking, this person doesn't really know what they're talking about.
text_ko: 제가 조금이라도 흔들리거나 불안한 기색이 보이면, 사람들은 '저 사람은 진짜 뭘 아는 사람이 아니구나'라고 생각하기 시작해요. 마치 방향이 분명하지 않은 리더 같아요. 그러면 갑자기 '잠깐만, 여기 있는 모든 걸 다 다시 의심해야 하나?'라고 생각하게 돼요. 이 사람을 믿을 수 있을지 확신이 없으니까요.
text_zh: 你要是开始露怯，让人看出你心里没底，别人就会想，这人其实也不太懂啊。就像一个领导自己都说不清楚方向在哪儿，我就会想，等等，这人我得打个问号，他说的每件事我都得重新考虑考虑了。
text_es: Si empiezas a mostrar tus inseguridades y se te nota la falta de confianza, la gente va a pensar "este tipo realmente no sabe de qué está hablando". Es como un líder que no tiene clara la dirección que quiere tomar. De repente empiezas a pensar "oye, espera, creo que tengo que dudar de todo lo que dice porque no le tengo confianza a esta persona".
fullContext: Tristan continues explaining the concept of 'staying in character' by using an airplane analogy where a pilot unnecessarily worries passengers about potential problems. He explains how when speakers 'leak' their insecurities by commenting on their mistakes or expressing doubts, it forces the audience to view everything through a lens of uncertainty, similar to how unclear leadership makes people question decisions.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of uncertainty or lack of confidence in oneself or one's abilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, insecurity can manifest in decision-making processes, affecting leadership effectiveness and team dynamics.

insight.nuance: While insecurity can indicate vulnerability, it may also imply a lack of preparedness or competence, which can undermine credibility.

vocabulary.definition: The course along which someone or something moves or points; guidance or supervision in a particular endeavor.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, clear direction is essential for aligning team efforts and achieving strategic goals.

insight.nuance: Direction can imply a sense of purpose and leadership, but it may also suggest rigidity if not balanced with flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: Easily understood; free from ambiguity or confusion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, clarity is crucial for ensuring that messages are effectively conveyed and understood by all stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While clarity is generally positive, being overly simplistic may lead to a lack of depth in communication.

vocabulary.definition: The action of leading a group or organization; the ability to guide and influence others toward achieving goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective leadership is vital in business for motivating teams, driving change, and fostering a positive organizational culture.

insight.nuance: Leadership can encompass various styles, and the effectiveness of a leader often depends on their ability to adapt to different situations.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: What we're trying to do is we're trying to internalize all of these habits to the point where I don't need to consciously think about them. So it's like a gymnast who's doing their tumbling routine and jumps into the air.
keySentence: Internalize habits like a gymnast performing a tumbling routine without conscious thought.
text_ko: 우리가 하려는 건 이런 습관들을 완전히 내재화(internalize)해서 제가 굳이 의식적으로 생각하지 않아도 될 정도로 만드는 거예요. 마치 체조 선수가 텀블링(tumbling) 루틴을 하다가 공중으로 뛰어올라 회전할 때처럼, 그 순간엔 '어떻게 도는 거지?'라고 의식적으로 생각하지 않잖아요.
text_zh: 我们要做的就是把这些习惯都内化，内化到什么程度呢？就是我不用刻意去想它们。就像体操运动员做翻滚动作，跳到空中的时候，在翻跟头的过程中，他们不会有意识地去想怎么翻，已经成了本能反应。
text_es: Lo que estamos tratando de hacer es interiorizar todos estos hábitos hasta el punto donde ya no tenga que pensar conscientemente en ellos. Es como un gimnasta que está haciendo su rutina de saltos y se lanza al aire. Mientras está dando vueltas, no está tratando conscientemente de pensar en cómo hacer el salto.
fullContext: Lenny mentions his struggle with not 'leaking' his insecurities after speaking exercises, and Tristan reassures him that this self-critical voice diminishes with practice. Tristan explains that the goal is to internalize good speaking habits so they become automatic, comparing it to a gymnast who has practiced so much that complex moves become subconscious rather than requiring conscious thought.

vocabulary.definition: To incorporate knowledge or skills into one's own understanding or behavior, making them automatic or instinctive.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, internalizing processes or habits can lead to increased efficiency and productivity, as employees perform tasks without needing to consciously think about them.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a deep understanding or acceptance of concepts, rather than just surface-level knowledge.

vocabulary.definition: In a deliberate and aware manner, with full attention and intention.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, acting consciously often refers to making strategic decisions with awareness of their potential impact on the organization and its stakeholders.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of awareness and intention, contrasting with actions taken automatically or thoughtlessly.

vocabulary.definition: A regular, repeated sequence of actions or activities that are often performed in a specific order.
vocabulary.businessContext: Establishing routines in the workplace can enhance productivity and ensure consistency in operations, particularly in processes that require precision and reliability.

insight.nuance: While routines can be beneficial for efficiency, they may also lead to stagnation if not periodically reviewed or adjusted.

vocabulary.definition: To reduce in size, importance, or intensity; to lessen.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, diminishing returns refer to a decrease in the incremental output or benefit gained from an investment or effort as more resources are added.

insight.nuance: This term can carry a negative connotation when referring to value or quality, suggesting a decline that may need to be addressed.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this. And it drove us crazy with Michael, and that's what gave birth to the Accordion Method. What's the old way?
keySentence: The old way is broken; it drove us crazy and gave birth to the Accordion Method.
text_ko: 솔직히 기존 방식은 정말 엉망이라고 생각해요. 근본적으로 문제가 있고, 이걸 혁신하는 걸 아직 본 적이 없어요. 그게 마이클과 저를 미치게 했고, 그래서 아코디언 방식(Accordion Method)이 탄생했어요. 옛 방식이 뭐냐고요? 강연이 다가오면 제 아이디어를 한 장 혹은 여러 장의 종이에 전부 적어놓는 방식이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得以前那套方法真的很烂，完全不行，而且我也没看到市面上有什么创新的做法。这个问题把我和迈克尔都快逼疯了，所以才催生了手风琴方法(Accordion Method)。那以前是怎么做的呢？就是我有个演讲要准备，然后就把脑子里所有的想法都往纸上倒，一张纸不够就用好几张纸。
text_es: La forma tradicional me parece una porquería. Está rota, y no he visto a nadie que esté innovando en esto. Nos tenía locos a Michael y a mí, y de ahí nació el Método Acordeón. ¿Cuál es la forma tradicional? Pues que tienes una presentación pendiente y te pones a volcar todas tus ideas en un papel o en varios papeles.
fullContext: Tristan introduces the Accordion Method as an alternative to traditional speech preparation. He expresses strong criticism of the conventional approach where people write down all their ideas, rearrange them on paper, create detailed scripts, and then struggle to memorize everything. He and his co-founder Michael developed this new method because they found the traditional approach frustrating and ineffective.

vocabulary.definition: The process of introducing new ideas, products, or methods to improve or create value.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, innovating is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and meeting evolving customer needs.

insight.nuance: While 'innovating' implies a positive change, it can also suggest a departure from established practices, which may not always be well-received.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to long-established customs, practices, or methods that are generally accepted and followed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, traditional approaches may refer to established practices that have been used over time, often contrasted with innovative methods.

insight.nuance: The term 'traditional' can carry a sense of reliability but may also imply resistance to change or lack of modernization.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an approach often refers to the strategy employed to achieve goals, whether in management, marketing, or product development.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a systematic or thoughtful method, but it can also suggest a lack of flexibility if used in a rigid context.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic way of doing something, often involving a series of steps or procedures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a method is often formalized into a framework or process that guides teams in achieving specific outcomes.

insight.nuance: While 'method' suggests a structured approach, it can also imply a lack of creativity if overly rigid or prescriptive.

speaker: Tristan de Montebello
text: Switch your mindset from what I want to say to what I want people to remember and limit whatever that is you want them to remember as much as possible and that's going to give you extreme clarity.
keySentence: Switch your mindset to what you want people to remember for extreme clarity.
text_ko: 내가 말하고 싶은 것에서 '사람들이 기억하길 바라는 것'으로 사고방식(mindset)을 바꿔보세요. 사람들이 기억하길 바라는 핵심을 가능한 한 단순하고 최소화하면 훨씬 더 명확해져요.
text_zh: 转变一下思路，别想着"我要说什么"，而是想"我希望别人记住什么"，然后把你想让他们记住的东西尽可能精简，这样你的思路就会特别清晰了。
text_es: Cambia tu mentalidad: en lugar de pensar en qué quieres decir, piensa en qué quieres que la gente recuerde, y limita al máximo eso que quieres que recuerden. Eso te va a dar una claridad tremenda.
fullContext: Tristan explains the core principle behind the Bow and Arrow technique for speech preparation. He argues that most speakers focus too much on what they want to say rather than what their audience will actually remember. The Bow and Arrow method involves identifying the single most important message (the 'arrow') and supporting it with compelling content (the 'bow') to ensure maximum impact and retention.

vocabulary.definition: A mindset is a set of beliefs or attitudes that shape how an individual thinks and behaves in various situations. It influences decision-making and problem-solving approaches.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, a growth mindset can foster innovation and adaptability, while a fixed mindset may hinder progress and collaboration.

insight.nuance: While 'mindset' often refers to a general attitude, it can also imply a deeper psychological framework that affects one's approach to challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Clarity refers to the quality of being clear and easy to understand, particularly in communication or thought processes. It is essential for effective decision-making and strategic planning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, clarity is crucial for ensuring that team members understand objectives, roles, and expectations, which can enhance productivity and reduce misunderstandings.

insight.nuance: Clarity can imply not just simplicity but also precision and focus, especially in conveying complex ideas succinctly.

vocabulary.definition: To limit means to set a boundary or restrict the extent, amount, or scope of something. It can refer to both quantitative and qualitative constraints.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, limiting factors such as budget constraints or resource availability can significantly impact project planning and execution.

insight.nuance: While 'limit' often has a negative connotation of restriction, it can also imply a necessary focus that enhances efficiency and effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: An audience is a group of individuals who are the intended recipients of a message, presentation, or product. Understanding the audience is key to effective communication and marketing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and sales, identifying and understanding the target audience is essential for tailoring messages and strategies that resonate with potential customers.

insight.nuance: The term 'audience' can vary in scope, from a specific demographic group to a broader public, and it is important to consider the context when defining it.

speaker: Upasna Gautam
text: We hear a lot about having the skills to thrive in ambiguity in order to be a successful product manager, but to be a successful product manager in news you have to be able to thrive in chaos.
keySentence: to be a successful product manager in news you have to be able to thrive in chaos.
text_ko: 성공적인 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)가 되려면 불확실성 속에서 잘 버티는 능력이 필요하다고들 많이 얘기해요. 그런데 뉴스업계에서는 그 정도가 아니라 혼돈 속에서도 잘 버텨내야 해요. 제 인생 전체를 통틀어 제가 길러온 가장 중요한 능력은 평정심(equanimity)이라고 생각해요. 그건 오랜 시간 마인드풀니스(mindfulness)와 명상(meditation)을 꾸준히 해온 덕분이에요. 평정심(equanimity)은 제가 특히 좋아하는 단어 중 하나예요. 뜻은 정신적 차분함, 침착함, 감정의 평정 같은 건데, 특히 정신없고 스트레스가 많은 상황에서 그런 상태를 말해요.
text_zh: 我们经常听说要想成为成功的产品经理，得有在模糊环境中游刃有余的能力，但如果你要在新闻行业做产品经理，那你必须能在一片混乱中还能干得风生水起。我觉得平常心是我这辈子培养出来最重要的能力，这都得益于我这么多年练习正念和冥想。平常心(equanimity)是我最喜欢的词之一，它指的是内心的平静、沉着，脾气稳定，特别是在那些疯狂的、压力山大的情况下。
text_es: Se habla mucho de tener las habilidades para desenvolverse bien en la ambigüedad para ser un product manager exitoso, pero para ser un product manager exitoso en medios de comunicación tienes que ser capaz de prosperar en el caos total.
