keySentence: we believe there are massive productivity improvements.
text_ko: 제가 생각하기에 제일 안 좋은 상황 중 하나는, 누군가가 여기 와서 이런 도구 쓰는 걸 싫어하는 거예요. 우리는 이런 도구들이 생산성을 엄청 끌어올린다고 보고 있어요. 그래서 사람들을 실제로 사무실(온사이트 on-site)로 불러 화이트보드 앞에서 문제를 어떻게 풀어가는지 같은 과정을 직접 보려고 해요. 즉석에서 어떻게 생각하는지 보길 원하고, 단지 우리가 말한 걸 음성 번역기(voice translator)에 넣어서 ChatGPT에 붙여 넣고 답만 뽑아내는 식이 아니길 바래요.
text_zh: 我觉得最糟糕的情况就是，如果有人来了之后不愿意用这些工具，我们是真心相信这些工具能大幅提升工作效率的。我们会把人请到公司现场，这样就能实实在在地看到他们怎么在白板上思考问题，还有其他各种表现。所以我们确实想看看他们的临场反应能力，希望他们不只是把我们说的话丢进语音翻译器，然后再扔给ChatGPT来找答案。
text_es: Creo que una de las peores cosas es cuando alguien llega aquí y no le gusta usar estas herramientas, porque nosotros creemos que hay mejoras enormes de productividad. Por eso traemos a la gente a la empresa en persona para poder ver realmente cómo razonan los problemas en la pizarra y todo eso. Queremos ver cómo piensan sobre la marcha y ojalá que no estén simplemente tomando lo que decimos, metiéndolo en un traductor de voz y pegándolo en ChatGPT para sacar la respuesta.
fullContext: Lenny asks how Codeium conducts interviews in an era where AI tools like Windsurf can solve coding problems. Varun explains their approach to modern technical interviews - they actually encourage candidates to use AI tools during interviews because they believe in the productivity improvements these tools provide. However, they also conduct on-site interviews with whiteboarding to assess real-time problem-solving abilities and ensure candidates aren't just mechanically translating problems into AI prompts without genuine understanding.

vocabulary.definition: Enhancements in efficiency and output, often achieved through better processes, tools, or practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, productivity improvements are critical for increasing profitability and competitiveness, often measured through metrics such as output per hour or cost savings.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a positive connotation, suggesting not just increased output but also smarter work practices; it is often used in discussions about operational efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: Instruments or software applications designed to assist in completing tasks or improving processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, tools can refer to anything from software applications that facilitate project management to physical devices that enhance productivity.

insight.nuance: While 'tools' can refer to both physical and digital items, in a business context, it often implies software solutions that streamline operations; it is less commonly used to refer to manual tools.

vocabulary.definition: To carry out or direct an activity or process, often involving management or oversight.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, 'conducts' is frequently used to describe the execution of meetings, research, or performance evaluations, emphasizing leadership and accountability.

insight.nuance: This term carries a formal tone and is often used in contexts where authority or oversight is implied; it is less common in casual conversation.

vocabulary.definition: A method or way of dealing with a situation or problem, often characterized by a specific strategy or perspective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, an 'approach' refers to the strategic direction taken to achieve objectives, such as a marketing approach or problem-solving approach.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a thoughtful and planned method rather than a random or haphazard effort; it is often used in strategic planning contexts.

speaker: Varun Mohan
text: I think maybe in society and just school, we don't prioritize how do you make sure you get people with real agency that want to build something, right?
keySentence: we don't prioritize how do you make sure you get people with real agency that want to build something
text_ko: 저는 사회나 학교에서 진짜로 뭔가를 만들고 싶어 하는 사람들의 주체성(agency)을 어떻게 확보할지 우선순위로 두지 않는 것 같아요. 그들의 목표가 단지 대학을 졸업해서 빅테크(big tech) 회사에 들어가 거기서 시키는 대로만 하는 것—예를 들어 어떤 웹사이트의 픽셀(pixel)을 어디에 놓으라고 지시받는 일—이 아니잖아요. 이런 스킬셋(skill set)이 요즘, 아마 지난 10년 정도 동안 특히 저평가돼 온 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得可能在社会上，包括学校里，我们都没有重视一个问题：怎么培养那些真正有主动性、想要创造点什么的人才，对吧？他们的目标不应该只是从大学毕业，然后去大厂找个工作，每天被人安排得死死的，就负责在某个网页上调调像素位置什么的。我觉得这种能力可能被低估了，特别是最近这十年左右。
text_es: Creo que tal vez en la sociedad y en las escuelas no le damos prioridad a cómo asegurarnos de formar gente con verdadera iniciativa que quiera construir algo, ¿no? Su objetivo no es solo graduarse de la universidad y luego conseguir trabajo en una empresa tecnológica grande donde les digan exactamente qué hacer o dónde poner cada pixel en una página web. Pienso que esa habilidad está subvalorada justo ahora, probablemente en los últimos diez años más o menos.
fullContext: Varun continues explaining why agency is an undervalued skill in the AI era. He critiques how society and educational systems don't prioritize developing people with genuine agency who want to create meaningful things. Instead, many people follow a predictable path of graduating college and joining large tech companies where they're given very specific, narrow tasks like positioning pixels on websites. He argues this lack of agency has been undervalued for about a decade and will become increasingly important.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange or deal with tasks, projects, or responsibilities in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, prioritizing is crucial for effective project management and resource allocation, ensuring that the most critical tasks are addressed first.

insight.nuance: While prioritizing often implies a systematic approach, it can also suggest a need to make difficult choices about what to focus on, which may not always be well-received.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity of individuals to act independently and make their own choices, often in the context of social or organizational structures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, fostering agency among employees can lead to increased innovation and engagement, as individuals feel empowered to contribute ideas and solutions.

insight.nuance: Agency carries a positive connotation of empowerment and autonomy, but can also imply a lack of control if not supported by adequate resources or guidance.

vocabulary.definition: Regarded as less important or valuable than it actually is, often leading to insufficient recognition or compensation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, certain roles or contributions may be undervalued, which can result in employee dissatisfaction and high turnover rates if not addressed.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a disparity between perceived and actual worth, and is often used in discussions about equity and recognition in the workplace.

vocabulary.definition: The process of growth, progress, or evolution in skills, ideas, or products, often involving incremental improvements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, developing new products or services is a critical phase that requires innovation, research, and market testing to meet consumer needs.

insight.nuance: While developing suggests positive progress, it can also imply that something is still in a formative stage and may not yet be fully realized or effective.

speaker: Varun Parmar
text: Every single day, every single time somebody is pushing your code to production and you're releasing a feature or an enhancement, you are making the product better or you're making the product worse, but the products never remain same.
keySentence: Every release makes the product better or worse, never remains the same.
text_ko: 매일매일, 누군가 당신의 코드를 프로덕션에 배포(deploy)해서 기능(feature)이나 개선사항(enhancement)을 릴리스(release)할 때마다, 제품은 좋아지거나 나빠질 뿐 같은 상태로 남아 있지 않아요. 경쟁사가 내는 릴리스(release) 하나하나와 당신이 내는 릴리스 하나하나가 쌓여서, 상대에게 한 수 앞서는 건지(체스의 수, chess move) 아니면 뒤처지는 건지, 긍정적인 점수를 얻는 건지 아니면 잃는 건지를 결정해요.
text_zh: 每天都有人把代码推到生产环境(production)，每次发布新功能或者优化的时候，你要么是在让产品变得更好，要么就是在让它变差，反正产品肯定不会原地踏步。所以你的竞争对手每发一个版本，你每发一个版本，其实就像下棋一样，要么你走了好棋占了上风，要么就是走坏了让自己处于劣势。
text_es: Cada día, cada vez que alguien sube código a producción y lanzas una funcionalidad nueva o una mejora, estás haciendo que tu producto sea mejor o lo estás empeorando, pero nunca se queda igual. Entonces, con cada lanzamiento que hace tu competencia y cada lanzamiento que haces tú, estás ganando puntos a favor, haciendo jugadas estratégicas contra ellos, o te estás quedando atrás.
fullContext: Lenny asks Varun about his core product philosophies and how competition impacts product strategy. Varun explains his belief that products are never static - they're always improving or declining relative to competitors. He uses a chess metaphor to describe how every product release by you or your competitors creates relative gains or losses in the market. This framework helps product teams understand the competitive impact of their work and drives clarity around prioritization decisions.

vocabulary.definition: An enhancement refers to an improvement or upgrade that adds value or functionality to a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, enhancements are often implemented to improve user experience, increase efficiency, or address customer feedback, thereby contributing to the overall competitiveness of a product.

insight.nuance: While 'enhancement' implies a positive change, it is important to ensure that the improvements align with user needs and do not introduce new issues.

vocabulary.definition: Static refers to a state of being unchanging or lacking movement, often implying a lack of progress or development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a static product or strategy may indicate stagnation, where no new features or improvements are being introduced, potentially leading to a loss of market relevance.

insight.nuance: The term 'static' often carries a negative connotation in dynamic industries, suggesting that a company is not adapting to market changes.

vocabulary.definition: Product strategy is a plan that outlines how a company will develop, market, and sell its products to meet customer needs and achieve business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, a well-defined product strategy is crucial for guiding product development decisions, prioritizing features, and aligning resources with market demands.

insight.nuance: A product strategy should be flexible and adaptable, allowing for adjustments based on market feedback and competitive landscape.

vocabulary.definition: Core philosophies are the fundamental beliefs and values that guide an organization's culture, decision-making, and overall approach to business.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, core philosophies shape the company's mission, influence employee behavior, and can significantly impact customer perception and loyalty.

insight.nuance: While core philosophies are often aspirational, they should be reflected in everyday practices to maintain authenticity and trust within the organization.

speaker: Varun Parmar
text: The success of a company is a direct relation of what the competition allows you to do.
keySentence: Success is a direct relation to what the competition allows you to do.
text_ko: 회사의 성공은 경쟁이 허용하는 것과 직접적으로 연관돼요. 제가 본 모든 사례에서 어떤 회사의 성장이 가속화되거나 둔화된 건 전부 경쟁이 허용해 준 것과 직결됐어요.
text_zh: 一家公司能不能成功，说白了就看竞争对手给你留多少空间。我每次分析那些增长很快或者突然放缓的公司，发现都是一个道理——竞争对手让你做什么，你就只能做什么。
text_es: El éxito de una empresa tiene que ver directamente con lo que te permite hacer la competencia. Cada vez que he visto que una empresa aceleró su crecimiento o se le frenó, siempre fue por lo que la competencia le dejó hacer o no hacer.
fullContext: Lenny discusses how Miro continues to succeed despite intense competition in the collaborative whiteboarding space. Varun shares one of his core philosophies about business growth - that a company's success is fundamentally constrained or enabled by competitive dynamics. He argues that while companies must execute well internally, the competitive landscape is often the biggest variable determining whether growth accelerates or decelerates.

vocabulary.definition: The achievement of a desired aim or purpose, often measured by the attainment of goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, success is frequently evaluated through metrics such as profitability, market share, and customer satisfaction, indicating the effectiveness of strategies employed.

insight.nuance: While 'success' generally carries a positive connotation, it can also imply a narrow focus on financial gains, potentially overlooking other important factors like employee well-being or social responsibility.

vocabulary.definition: The rivalry among businesses or individuals to attract customers and achieve market dominance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, competition drives innovation and efficiency, compelling companies to improve their products and services to maintain or grow their market position.

insight.nuance: While competition can foster improvement and innovation, excessive competition may lead to unethical practices or market saturation, which can harm the industry as a whole.

vocabulary.definition: The process of increasing in size, value, or importance, often measured in terms of revenue, market share, or customer base.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, growth is a key indicator of a company's health and potential, often pursued through strategies like market expansion, product development, or mergers and acquisitions.

insight.nuance: While 'growth' is typically viewed positively, it can also imply unsustainable practices if pursued without regard for long-term viability or ethical considerations.

vocabulary.definition: A set of beliefs or principles that guide an individual's or organization's behavior and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a company's philosophy often shapes its culture, values, and strategic direction, influencing everything from employee engagement to customer relations.

insight.nuance: The term 'philosophy' can suggest a deep, reflective approach to business practices, but it may also be perceived as abstract or disconnected from practical execution if not aligned with actionable strategies.

speaker: Varun Parmar
text: What you want to do is that you want to be the first one to hit the brick wall.
keySentence: Be the first to hit the brick wall; speed is the single biggest determinant.
text_ko: 하고 싶은 건 먼저 한계에 부딪히는 사람이 되는 거예요. 스스로를 혁신 중심(innovation-centric) 회사라고 생각하고, 다른 곳엔 전혀 없는 근본적인 경험을 만들고 있다고 믿으며, 그 방식으로 업계의 다른 사람들에게 영감을 주고 있다면, 결국 가장 중요한 건 속도(speed)이에요.
text_zh: 你要做的就是第一个撞墙的人。如果你把自己定位成一家以创新为核心的公司，相信自己在打造的体验是其他地方根本没有的，而且你在为其他人铺路，让他们从你打造的这些体验中获得灵感，那速度就是最关键的决定因素。
text_es: Lo que quieres hacer es ser el primero en toparse con la pared. Si te consideras una empresa centrada en la innovación y crees que estás creando experiencias que básicamente no existen en ningún otro lugar, y que de alguna manera estás abriendo el camino para que el resto se inspire en cómo estás construyendo estas experiencias, entonces la velocidad es el factor más determinante.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Varun's product philosophies and how to balance moving fast versus moving carefully. Varun explains his belief that innovative companies should prioritize speed to discover learning faster than competitors. The 'hitting the brick wall first' metaphor means being the first to encounter and learn from failures, allowing you to course-correct while competitors are still pursuing the wrong path. This philosophy emphasizes speed as crucial for innovation leadership.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange or deal with tasks or issues in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, prioritizing is essential for effective project management and resource allocation, ensuring that critical tasks are addressed first to achieve strategic goals.

insight.nuance: While prioritizing can imply a focus on immediate needs, it should also consider long-term objectives to avoid short-sighted decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by the introduction of new ideas, methods, or products that significantly improve existing standards.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, being innovative is crucial for gaining competitive advantage and attracting investment, as it demonstrates the potential for growth and disruption.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting creativity and forward-thinking, but can also imply risk if innovations fail to meet market needs.

vocabulary.definition: A state in which different elements are equal or in the correct proportions, often referring to the management of competing priorities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, achieving balance is vital for maintaining operational efficiency, ensuring that resources are allocated appropriately among various departments or projects.

insight.nuance: While balance suggests stability, it can also imply the need for trade-offs, as perfect equilibrium is often unattainable in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: To find out or uncover something that was previously unknown or hidden.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, discovery often relates to market research, product development, or identifying new opportunities for growth.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a sense of exploration and innovation, but should be used carefully to avoid suggesting that the findings were not previously acknowledged or understood.

speaker: Varun Parmar
text: My fundamental belief here, Lenny, is that every product manager actually wants to move fast.
keySentence: every product manager actually wants to move fast.
text_ko: 레니, 제 기본적인 믿음은 모든 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)들이 사실 더 빨리 움직이고 싶어한다는 거예요. 어떤 경우에 우리가 빨리 움직이지 못하는 이유는 부딪히는 장애물들(roadblocks) 때문이라고 생각해요. 그런 장애물들은 기술적인 문제(technical challenges)로 나타날 수도 있고, 조직적인 문제(organizational challenges)의 형태로 드러날 수도 있으며, 우선순위 문제(priority challenges)일 수도 있어요.
text_zh: 伦尼，我的基本看法是这样的，其实每个产品经理都想快速推进项目。我觉得有时候我们推不快的原因，主要是遇到了各种阻碍，这些阻碍可能表现为技术难题，也可能是组织架构上的问题，或者是优先级不清楚的问题。
text_es: Mi convicción fundamental aquí, Lenny, es que todo product manager en realidad quiere avanzar rápido. Creo que la razón por la que a veces no logramos avanzar rápido es por los obstáculos que nos encontramos, y esos obstáculos pueden presentarse como desafíos técnicos, pueden manifestarse como problemas organizacionales, o pueden ser temas de prioridades.
fullContext: Lenny asks how to help teams move faster beyond just telling them to 'move faster.' Varun explains his philosophy that product managers are naturally driven by challenge and want to move quickly - it's their inherent personality type. He argues that slowness isn't due to lack of motivation but rather systemic roadblocks that need to be identified and removed. His approach focuses on enabling PMs to raise issues quickly so leadership can unblock them.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a foundation or basis; essential and primary.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'fundamental' often refers to core principles or beliefs that guide decision-making and strategy.

insight.nuance: While it implies something basic, it can also suggest a deep-seated importance that should not be overlooked.

vocabulary.definition: To act quickly or make rapid progress in decision-making or execution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup environments, 'move fast' is often associated with agile methodologies and the need to adapt quickly to market changes.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys urgency and a proactive approach, but it can also imply a risk of overlooking details or quality.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for the development and success of a product, overseeing its lifecycle from conception to launch.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, product managers play a crucial role in bridging the gap between engineering, marketing, and customer needs, ensuring that products meet market demands.

insight.nuance: The role requires a blend of technical knowledge, business acumen, and interpersonal skills, making it both challenging and rewarding.

vocabulary.definition: A task or situation that tests someone's abilities or skills; a difficulty that requires a solution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, challenges often arise in project management, market competition, or resource allocation, prompting teams to innovate and adapt.

insight.nuance: While it can denote a negative situation, 'challenge' is often used positively to encourage growth and problem-solving.

speaker: Varun Parmar
text: We have a motto in the product org, it's very simple, single sentence, deliver customer value faster with high quality.
keySentence: Deliver customer value faster with high quality is our guiding motto.
text_ko: 우리 제품 조직(product org)에는 모토가 하나 있어요. 아주 단순한 한 문장인데요: '고품질로 고객 가치를 더 빠르게 전달하자' — 우리가 하는 모든 일, 정말 말 그대로 모든 것, Lenny, 성과와 보상 시스템(performance and reward system)부터 측정(measurements)까지 전부 이 한 문장에 기반해 있어요.
text_zh: 我们产品团队有个座右铭，特别简单，就一句话：更快地为客户创造高质量的价值。我们做的所有事情，我说的是所有事情啊，Lenny，从绩效到奖励制度到各种考核指标，全都是围绕这一句话来的。
text_es: Tenemos un lema en el equipo de producto, es muy sencillo, una sola frase: entregar valor al cliente más rápido y con alta calidad. Todo lo que hacemos, y cuando digo todo, es TODO, Lenny, desde el sistema de rendimiento y recompensas hasta las métricas, absolutamente todo se basa en esta única declaración.
fullContext: Lenny asks about how Miro operationalizes their philosophy of moving fast and removing blockers. Varun explains Miro's core product organization motto that guides all their decisions and systems. The motto has three components: delivering customer value (measured by actual usage and metrics), moving faster (tracked through cycle times), and maintaining high quality (evaluated through design reviews). This simple statement drives their performance reviews, measurements, and organizational culture.

vocabulary.definition: To put into operation or use; to implement a plan or strategy in a practical manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, operationalizing often refers to translating strategic goals into actionable processes or systems that can be executed effectively.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in contexts where theoretical concepts need to be made practical, and it implies a focus on execution rather than just planning.

vocabulary.definition: To provide or bring something to a designated recipient or location, often in the context of services or products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, delivering refers to fulfilling commitments to customers, such as providing products or services on time and to specification.

insight.nuance: While it can refer to physical goods, in a broader sense, it encompasses delivering value, results, or experiences to stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: The perceived benefit or worth that a product or service provides to a customer, often measured against its cost.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding customer value is crucial for developing products and services that meet customer needs and drive satisfaction and loyalty.

insight.nuance: Customer value is subjective and can vary significantly among different customer segments, making it essential for businesses to tailor their offerings accordingly.

vocabulary.definition: A term used to describe products or services that meet or exceed established standards of excellence and reliability.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the competitive landscape of business, high quality is often a key differentiator that can influence customer choice and brand loyalty.

insight.nuance: While high quality is generally viewed positively, it can also imply higher costs, so businesses must balance quality with affordability to meet market demands.

speaker: Varun Parmar
text: You have two personas that you have to think about. The fundamental thing that you have to do is drive accountability. When you put on the persona hat of a stream leader, your number one goal that you have, is drive improvement.
keySentence: your number one goal that you have, is drive improvement.
text_ko: 생각해야 할 페르소나(persona)가 두 가지 있어요. 근본적으로 해야 할 일은 책임(accountability)을 확실히 하는 거예요. 스트림 리더(stream leader) 역할일 때는 최우선 목표가 개선을 추진하는 거고, 제품 리더십 팀(product leadership team)에 있을 때는 실제로 가장 중요한 건 이 부분에 대한 책임(accountability)을 분명히 하는 거예요.
text_zh: 你得考虑两个不同的角色。最根本的是，你必须推动问责制(accountability)。当你戴上流程负责人(stream leader)这顶帽子的时候，你的首要目标就是推动改进。但当你坐在产品领导团队里的时候，你的首要目标其实是围绕这个来推动问责制(accountability)。
text_es: Tienes que pensar en dos roles diferentes. Lo fundamental que tienes que hacer es impulsar la rendición de cuentas (accountability). Cuando te pones el sombrero de líder de flujo (stream leader), tu objetivo número uno es impulsar la mejora. Cuando te sientas en el equipo de liderazgo de producto, tu objetivo número uno es realmente impulsar la rendición de cuentas alrededor de esto.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Varun's philosophy for developing product leaders at Miro. Varun explains his framework where product leaders must balance two distinct roles or 'personas.' As stream leaders, they focus on continuously improving their team's performance and outcomes. As members of the product leadership team, they must hold each other accountable for company-wide decisions and performance. This dual responsibility ensures both individual team success and collective leadership effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a basis or foundation; essential to the nature of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'fundamental' often refers to core principles or values that guide decision-making and strategy.

insight.nuance: While it indicates something essential, it can also imply that other aspects may be secondary or less important.

vocabulary.definition: The obligation of an individual or organization to report, explain, and be answerable for resulting consequences.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, accountability is crucial for ensuring that team members take responsibility for their actions and outcomes.

insight.nuance: It carries a connotation of trust and reliability, often implying that one is held to a standard of performance.

vocabulary.definition: To actively promote or facilitate enhancements in processes, performance, or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'drive improvement' is often associated with initiatives aimed at increasing efficiency, quality, or customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive and continuous effort rather than a one-time change.

vocabulary.definition: The aspect of someone's character that is presented to or perceived by others; a social facade.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, 'persona' refers to the representation of a target customer or user, helping businesses tailor their strategies.

insight.nuance: It implies a crafted identity that may differ from one's true self, often used in contexts requiring role-playing or strategic positioning.

speaker: Vijay Iyengar
text: One of the things after you've been in engineering for a while is that develop this tendency to immediately respond with no to new ideas.
keySentence: develop this tendency to immediately respond with no to new ideas.
text_ko: 한동안 엔지니어링(engineering)을 하다 보면 새로운 아이디어에 바로 '안 돼'라고 반응하는 버릇이 생겨요. 엔지니어 관점에서는 그 이유가 아마도 대부분의 시간을 반쯤 생각만 해보고 끝나 버리거나 실제로는 잘 진행되지 않았던 아이디어들을 만들고 유지하는 데 쓰기 때문이에요. 그런 아이디어들의 유지 비용(maintenance cost)을 온전히 떠안는 느낌이 들고요. 그래서 흉터 조직(scar tissue)처럼 쌓인 경험이 면역 반응(immune response)을 만들면서, 새로운 아이디어에 대해 '아니야, 절대 안 해' 하는 식의 완전한 거부(hard no)를 하게 돼요.
text_zh: 搞技术搞久了，你就会发现自己有个毛病，一听到新想法就条件反射地说"不行"。我觉得从工程师的角度来看，这是因为你花了太多时间去搭建和维护那些想得不够成熟或者根本没啥前途的项目，维护成本(maintenance cost)全都压在你身上。时间长了你就有了心理阴影，形成了一种免疫反应(immune response)，一听到新想法就说不，而且是坚决不干的那种不。
text_es: Una de las cosas que pasa después de que llevas un tiempo en ingeniería es que desarrollas esta tendencia de responder inmediatamente que no a las ideas nuevas. Y creo que desde la perspectiva de la ingeniería, esto es porque pasas mucho tiempo construyendo y manteniendo ideas que tal vez están medio pensadas o que realmente no van a ningún lado, y sientes todo el peso del costo de mantenimiento de eso. Entonces te vas blindando y desarrollas como una respuesta inmune de decir que no a las ideas nuevas, y es un no rotundo, o sea no, definitivamente no lo vamos a hacer.
fullContext: Lenny asks Vijay what he had to unlearn as an engineer when transitioning to product leadership. Vijay explains how engineers develop a defensive mindset against new ideas because they experience the ongoing maintenance burden of poorly thought-out features. This creates what he calls 'scar tissue' - a protective response that makes engineers reflexively reject new proposals with a 'hard no' to avoid future problems.

vocabulary.definition: A tendency is an inclination or a habitual pattern of behavior or thought that is often observed over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, recognizing tendencies can help leaders anticipate employee reactions, market trends, or consumer behavior, which is crucial for strategic planning.

insight.nuance: While 'tendency' often implies a natural inclination, it can also suggest a lack of critical thinking or openness to change when used in a negative context.

vocabulary.definition: To respond means to react or reply to a stimulus, question, or situation in a timely manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, effective response mechanisms are essential for customer service, crisis management, and team collaboration, ensuring that issues are addressed promptly.

insight.nuance: The term can imply varying degrees of engagement, from a simple acknowledgment to a detailed and thoughtful reply, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: A defensive mindset refers to a psychological state characterized by a protective attitude, often leading to resistance against criticism or new ideas.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, a defensive mindset can hinder innovation and collaboration, as employees may be reluctant to embrace change or accept feedback.

insight.nuance: While a defensive mindset can sometimes be protective, it often stifles growth and adaptability, making it important to recognize and address in team dynamics.

vocabulary.definition: To unlearn means to discard previously acquired knowledge or habits, often in favor of new information or practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In fast-paced industries, unlearning outdated practices is crucial for innovation and staying competitive, as it allows organizations to adapt to new technologies and market demands.

insight.nuance: Unlearning can be challenging, as it requires individuals to confront their established beliefs and practices, making it a significant aspect of personal and professional development.

speaker: Vijay Iyengar
text: The issue for us at the time was that we took people away from the investment in our core product to go do those other things. We moved people, right?
keySentence: We took people away from the investment in our core product to go do those other things.
text_ko: 그때 우리의 문제는 핵심 제품(core product)에 대한 투자를 줄이고 사람들을 다른 일로 옮겼다는 점이었어요. 사람들을 옮겼죠? 그래서 생기는 함정은 누군가가 그 핵심에 우리보다 더 많이 투자(out-invest)하면 핵심 영역에서 스스로 교란(disruption)에 취약해진다는 거예요. 그래서 어떤 핵심 제품에서 리더(leader)라면, 결론은 그 핵심에 대해 계속 누구보다 더 많이 투자(out-invest)하고, 그 핵심에서 나오는 수익은 다음 벤처(next venture)에 재투자해야 한다는 것입니다.
text_zh: 我们当时的问题就是，把原本投入在核心产品上的人力都调去做别的事情了，对吧？这样做的风险就是，你的核心业务很容易被别人颠覆，因为竞争对手可能在这块投入比你更多。所以说，如果你在某个核心产品上是老大，我们的经验就是，你必须在这个核心业务上的投入要超过所有竞争对手，然后用核心业务赚来的钱去投资下一个项目。
text_es: El problema que tuvimos en ese momento fue que sacamos gente de la inversión en nuestro producto principal para ponerlos a hacer esas otras cosas. Movimos personal, ¿no? Y ahí está la trampa: te quedas vulnerable a que te interrumpan (disrupt) en tu área central porque alguien más puede invertir más que tú en esa área. Entonces, si eres el líder en algún producto central, lo que aprendimos es que tienes que seguir invirtiendo más que todos los demás en esa área principal, y luego usar las ganancias que salen de ahí para invertir en el siguiente proyecto.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Mixpanel's journey of expanding to multiple products and then refocusing back to their core analytics product. Vijay explains the strategic mistake they made - they moved engineering resources away from their core product to build adjacent products, which made them vulnerable to competitors who could outinvest them in analytics. His key insight is that market leaders should maintain their investment advantage in their core product while funding new ventures with profits, not people.

vocabulary.definition: The primary offering of a company that is central to its business model and value proposition. It represents the main source of revenue and customer interest.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, the core product is often the focus of development and marketing efforts, as it is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and customer loyalty.

insight.nuance: While 'core product' emphasizes the essential nature of the offering, it is important to differentiate it from ancillary products or services that may support the core but are not central to the business.

vocabulary.definition: The allocation of resources, typically financial, with the expectation of generating a return or profit over time. It can also refer to time or effort spent on a project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and business contexts, investment is crucial for funding operations, scaling growth, and developing new products or services.

insight.nuance: The term 'investment' can imply a long-term commitment, and it is often associated with risk; thus, it is important to assess potential returns carefully.

vocabulary.definition: An error in judgment or decision-making that adversely affects a company's long-term goals or competitive position. It often involves misallocation of resources or misinterpretation of market conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy discussions, identifying and analyzing strategic mistakes is essential for learning and avoiding similar pitfalls in the future.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of significant impact, suggesting that the mistake was not merely operational but fundamentally flawed in strategic thinking.

vocabulary.definition: The process of realigning a company's efforts and resources towards its primary objectives or core competencies. It often involves shifting priorities or altering strategies to enhance effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and businesses, refocusing is a common response to changing market conditions or internal challenges, aimed at improving performance and achieving strategic goals.

insight.nuance: Refocusing suggests a deliberate and often necessary adjustment rather than a reactionary measure, indicating a proactive approach to business management.

speaker: Vijay Iyengar
text: But one of the traps with RICE that we observed is that the C and E, the confidence and effort tends to cause you to prematurely deprioritize potentially high reach, high impact bets, really innovative things.
keySentence: RICE can prematurely deprioritize high reach, high impact bets due to murky confidence.
text_ko: 근데 RICE(Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort)를 쓰면서 우리가 관찰한 함정 하나는 C(Confidence, 확신)랑 E(Effort, 노력) 때문에 잠재적으로 리치(reach)도 크고 임팩트(impact)도 큰, 정말 혁신적인 베팅들을 너무 일찍 우선순위에서 밀어내게 만든다는 거예요. 작년 초에 한 팀에서 실제로 그걸 겪었어요. 그 팀은 모든 아이디어를 RICE로만 점수화했는데, 리치가 크고 임팩트가 큰 아이디어들이 많이 아래로 내려갔어요. 그런 아이디어들은 보통 확신이나 노력이 불투명한 경우가 많은데(그게 당연하죠), 그래서 우선순위가 낮아진 거예요.
text_zh: 但是我们发现RICE有个坑，就是那个C和E，信心度(confidence)和工作量(effort)这两项，容易让你过早地把那些潜在的高覆盖、高影响力的想法给排到后面去，就是那些真正有创新性的东西。去年年初我们有个团队就遇到过这种情况，把所有想法都用RICE打了分，结果那些高覆盖、高影响力的项目全跑到最底下去了，因为信心度和工作量这两项对它们来说就是很模糊的，其实对于高覆盖、高影响力的想法来说，本来就应该是这样的。
text_es: Pero una de las trampas que vimos con RICE es que la C y la E, o sea la confianza y el esfuerzo, tienden a hacerte que despriorities muy rápido apuestas que podrían tener mucho alcance y alto impacto, cosas realmente innovadoras. Y nos pasó esto con uno de nuestros equipos a principios del año pasado donde le aplicamos RICE a todo, a todas las ideas, y muchas de las cosas de alto alcance y alto impacto terminaron hasta abajo porque la confianza y el esfuerzo estaban súper confusos para esas ideas, como normalmente debería ser para ideas de alto alcance y alto impacto.
fullContext: Lenny asks about prioritization frameworks and Vijay's approach to helping product teams prioritize effectively. Vijay discusses the RICE framework (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) and explains a common pitfall - the Confidence and Effort components often cause teams to unfairly penalize innovative, high-impact ideas because these factors are inherently unclear for breakthrough concepts. He describes how his team experienced this when they applied RICE and all the most innovative ideas scored poorly.

vocabulary.definition: To assign a lower priority to something, often resulting in reduced focus or resources allocated to it.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, deprioritizing can occur when teams shift their focus away from certain projects or initiatives in favor of others deemed more critical to immediate goals.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that something valuable may be overlooked or undervalued.

vocabulary.definition: Having the capacity to develop into something in the future; possible but not yet actualized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'potentially' is frequently used to describe opportunities, risks, or outcomes that could arise based on current trends or decisions.

insight.nuance: While it indicates possibility, it does not guarantee success, so it should be used cautiously to avoid overpromising.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by the introduction of new ideas, methods, or products; creative and forward-thinking.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, being innovative is crucial for staying competitive and meeting evolving consumer demands.

insight.nuance: This term is often associated with positive change and progress, but it can imply risk if the innovation is untested or radical.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a particular issue or set of issues.
vocabulary.businessContext: Frameworks are commonly used in business strategy, project management, and product development to guide decision-making and ensure consistency.

insight.nuance: While frameworks provide valuable structure, they can also be seen as limiting if they are too rigid or not adaptable to specific situations.

speaker: Vijay Iyengar
text: you make the time box or an appetite the input, and you say, 'We want to solve X problem and we're willing to invest six weeks solving that problem.
keySentence: We want to solve X problem and we're willing to invest six weeks solving that problem.
text_ko: 제가 정말 흥미롭게 본 접근법 중 하나는 Basecamp(베이스캠프)의 책 'Shape Up(Shape Up)'에 나오는, '추정(estimate)보다 투자 의향(appetite)을 우선하는(appetite over estimates)'이라는 아이디어예요. 즉 계획의 산출물로 추정을 만드는 대신 타임박스(timebox)나 어피타이트(appetite) 같은 시간·투자 한도를 입력값으로 잡고, "우리는 X 문제를 해결하려고 하고 그걸 해결하는 데 6주를 투자하겠다"라고 정하는 방식이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得Basecamp那本《Shape Up》里有个思路特别有意思，就是用appetite来替代estimates，不是先做规划再估时间，而是反过来，先定个时间框或者说appetite作为输入条件，然后说"我们要解决X问题，愿意投入六周时间来搞定这个问题。"
text_es: Una estrategia que me pareció súper interesante es de este libro que se llama Shape Up de Basecamp, con esta idea del apetito (appetite) por encima de las estimaciones, donde en lugar de que la estimación sea el resultado de la planificación, haces que el tiempo disponible o el apetito (appetite) sea lo que determines desde el principio, y dices: 'Queremos resolver el problema X y estamos dispuestos a invertir seis semanas en resolver ese problema.'
fullContext: Lenny and Vijay are discussing estimation challenges in product development. Vijay explains the core problem with traditional estimation - teams are asked to estimate before they fully understand what they're building. He introduces the 'appetite over estimates' concept from Basecamp's Shape Up methodology, where instead of estimating how long something will take, you decide upfront how much time you're willing to invest in solving a particular problem.

vocabulary.definition: The allocation of resources, usually money, with the expectation of generating a profit or achieving a beneficial outcome in the future.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, investment often refers to funding received from investors to support growth, product development, or market expansion.

insight.nuance: While 'investment' typically implies a financial commitment, it can also refer to time or effort dedicated to a project, emphasizing the importance of resource allocation.

vocabulary.definition: An approximate calculation or judgment regarding the value, number, quantity, or extent of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, estimates are crucial for budgeting, project planning, and forecasting, helping teams make informed decisions based on available data.

insight.nuance: Estimates can carry a degree of uncertainty; thus, they should be communicated clearly to avoid misunderstandings about their accuracy.

vocabulary.definition: The fundamental issue or challenge that underlies a situation, requiring resolution to achieve desired outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying the core problem is essential in business strategy and problem-solving, as it directs efforts toward effective solutions rather than superficial fixes.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a deeper analysis beyond surface-level symptoms, indicating the need for critical thinking in addressing complex issues.

vocabulary.definition: To comprehend something in its entirety, grasping all aspects and implications involved.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, fully understanding a concept, market, or problem is crucial for making strategic decisions and developing effective solutions.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes a thorough and deep comprehension, often implying that surface-level knowledge is insufficient for effective action.

speaker: Vijay Iyengar
text: And one of the rituals that it's enabled is we'll find that engineers will go into that channel and react with a message with an email emoji, which means I'm going to email this customer and find out more, right?
keySentence: engineers will go into that channel and react with a message with an email emoji, which means I'm going to email this customer
text_ko: 그리고 그로 인해 생긴 습관 중 하나는 엔지니어들이 그 채널(channel)에 들어가 이메일 이모지(email emoji)로 반응하는 모습을 보는 거예요. 그건 '내가 이 고객에게 이메일을 보내서 더 알아볼게요'라는 뜻이에요. 실제로 그들은 고객에게 이메일을 보내서 "안녕하세요, 이 기능을 만든 엔지니어입니다. 말씀하신 이 부분을 봤는데, 좀 더 자세히 얘기해주실 수 있나요? 더 이해하고 싶어요."라고 보내요. 파이브 와이즈(5 Whys)를 묻고, 그 과정에서 스스로 제품을 개선해요.
text_zh: 这样就形成了一个习惯，我们发现工程师会在那个频道里看到用户反馈，然后用邮件的表情符号回应，意思就是"我要给这个客户发邮件了解一下情况"。然后他们就直接给客户写邮件说："嗨，我就是开发这个功能的工程师，我看到你提到了这个具体问题，能跟我详细说说吗？我特别想了解一下。" 他们会问五个为什么(five whys)，然后主动去优化产品。
text_es: Y uno de los hábitos que esto ha creado es que vemos que los ingenieros entran a ese canal y reaccionan a un mensaje con el emoji del email, que significa "voy a escribirle a este cliente para averiguar más", ¿sí? Y simplemente le mandan un correo al cliente diciéndole: "Hola, soy el ingeniero que desarrolló esta función. Vi que dijiste esto específico. ¿Me puedes contar más? Me encantaría entender mejor." Hacen los cinco porqués (five whys) y luego mejoran el producto por su cuenta.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Mixpanel's unique approach to keeping product teams close to customers. Vijay explains how they created an automated Slack feed of customer feedback that all engineers and designers can access directly. He describes a ritual that emerged where engineers use emoji reactions to signal they'll reach out to customers directly, then email them to dig deeper into problems using techniques like the 'five whys' to understand root causes and improve the product independently.

vocabulary.definition: To respond to a stimulus or situation, often with an action or message.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, 'react' often refers to how team members respond to communications or events, such as customer inquiries or internal discussions.

insight.nuance: While 'react' implies a spontaneous response, it can also suggest a need for quick decision-making in fast-paced settings.

vocabulary.definition: Performed by machines or software with minimal human intervention, often to increase efficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, 'automated' processes are crucial for scaling operations, reducing errors, and saving time on repetitive tasks.

insight.nuance: While 'automated' suggests efficiency, it can also imply a lack of personal touch, which may not always be suitable for customer interactions.

vocabulary.definition: Information or reactions provided regarding a product, service, or performance, often used for improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'feedback' is essential for understanding customer satisfaction, guiding product development, and enhancing team performance.

insight.nuance: Feedback can be constructive or critical; the context in which it is delivered can significantly affect its reception.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals who apply scientific and mathematical principles to design, develop, and maintain structures, systems, or products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology companies, engineers are pivotal in product development, ensuring that solutions are both functional and innovative.

insight.nuance: The term 'engineers' often connotes technical expertise, and it can imply a collaborative role within interdisciplinary teams.

speaker: Vijay Iyengar
text: I think the biggest mistake is setting up analytics using client side SDKs, client side tracking. So, web and mobile SDKs, putting a mixpanel.track or segment.track in your web app or your mobile apps.
keySentence: I think the biggest mistake is setting up analytics using client side SDKs, client side tracking.
text_ko: 제가 보기엔 가장 큰 실수는 애널리틱스를 클라이언트 쪽 SDK(client-side SDKs)나 클라이언트 측 트래킹(client-side tracking)으로 구축하는 거예요. 예를 들어 웹·모바일용 SDK(web and mobile SDKs)를 넣고 웹 앱이나 모바일 앱에 mixpanel.track이나 segment.track 같은 트래킹 코드를 심는 식이죠. 이게 핫테이크(hot take)인 이유는 많은 사람들이 제품 애널리틱스(product analytics)랑 SDK 트래킹을 동일시하기 때문이에요. 'Mixpanel이면 SDK다, 웹·모바일 앱에 SDK를 넣어야 해'라고 생각하는 건데, 그건 실수예요. 반복해서 보면 그렇게 하면 데이터 품질이 떨어지고 그 데이터를 유지·관리하기도 훨씬 어려워지거든요.
text_zh: 我觉得最大的错误就是用客户端SDK来做数据分析，也就是客户端追踪。比如在网页和移动端SDK里面加个mixpanel.track或者segment.track到你的web应用或者手机app里。我说这个观点比较激进，是因为很多人觉得产品分析(product analytics)和SDK追踪就是一回事儿。他们想的是，"好吧，Mixpanel就意味着SDK，我必须在我的网页和手机应用里装个SDK。" 但这其实是个误区，因为我们一次又一次地看到，这样做会导致数据质量很差，而且后期维护这些数据特别麻烦。
text_es: Creo que el error más grande es configurar la analítica usando SDKs del lado del cliente, o sea, tracking del lado del cliente. Me refiero a SDKs web y móviles, poniendo un mixpanel.track o segment.track en tu aplicación web o en tus apps móviles. Y la razón por la que esto es controversial es que para mucha gente la analítica de producto y el tracking por SDK son la misma cosa. Piensan: "Bueno, Mixpanel significa SDK, tengo que meter un SDK en mi app web y móvil." Pero eso es un error porque... Lo hemos visto una y otra vez, termina dando una calidad de datos pésima y hace súper difícil mantener esos datos.
fullContext: Lenny asks Vijay what most people get wrong when setting up product analytics, given his expertise as head of product at Mixpanel. Vijay shares what he calls a 'hot take' - that using client-side SDKs for tracking is a major mistake. He explains that many people assume product analytics requires putting tracking code directly in web and mobile apps, but this approach consistently leads to poor data quality and maintenance challenges, contradicting common industry practice.

vocabulary.definition: Analytics refers to the systematic computational analysis of data or statistics, often used to gain insights and inform decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, analytics is crucial for understanding customer behavior, measuring performance, and optimizing strategies based on data-driven insights.

insight.nuance: While often associated with quantitative data, analytics can also encompass qualitative insights, making it important to choose the right type for the context.

vocabulary.definition: Client-side refers to operations that are performed on the user's device rather than on a remote server, typically involving the user interface and user experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In web and mobile development, client-side processes are essential for creating interactive applications that respond quickly to user inputs without needing constant server communication.

insight.nuance: While client-side operations enhance user experience, they may also expose applications to security vulnerabilities if not properly managed.

vocabulary.definition: Tracking involves monitoring and recording user interactions or behaviors over time, often through various digital tools and technologies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and product development, tracking is vital for understanding user engagement, measuring campaign effectiveness, and improving product features based on user feedback.

insight.nuance: Tracking can raise privacy concerns, so it is important to balance data collection with ethical considerations and user consent.

vocabulary.definition: Expertise refers to a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular area, often acquired through experience and education.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, expertise is highly valued as it contributes to informed decision-making, strategic planning, and competitive advantage in specialized fields.

insight.nuance: While expertise implies a deep understanding, it is also important to remain open to new ideas and developments within the field to maintain relevance.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: When I was younger and I was starting off, I used to think it's all about the product. If you've got a really cool product to work on, your growth's guaranteed.
keySentence: I used to think it's all about the product.
text_ko: 젊었을 때, 커리어 초반엔 모든 게 프로덕트(product) 문제라고 생각했어요. 진짜 멋진 프로덕트를 다루고 있으면 성장(growth)은 보장된다고 믿었죠. 반대로 아무도 관심 없는 제품이나 사업 분야라면 성장 속도가 더딜 거라고도 생각했고요. 그런데 여러 훌륭한 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)들을 직접 보면서, 멋진 제품 분야에서 일하는 것만이 전부는 아니라는 걸 알게 됐어요.
text_zh: 我刚入行的时候比较年轻，总觉得产品就是一切。你要是做的产品特别酷，增长肯定没问题。要是做个没人关心的产品或者没人在意的业务线，那增长肯定会慢一些。但后来接触了越来越多厉害的产品经理，看他们怎么做事，我才发现光是做酷炫的产品并不是全部。
text_es: Cuando era más joven y estaba empezando, pensaba que todo se trataba del producto. Si tienes un producto realmente genial en el que trabajar, tu crecimiento está garantizado. Y si tienes un producto que a nadie le importa o un área que a nadie le interesa, entonces tu crecimiento va a ser más lento. Pero conforme empecé a ver a más y más product managers en acción, me di cuenta de que trabajar en un área de producto genial no es lo único que importa.
fullContext: Lenny asks Vikrama about the common traits of product managers who have had rapid career growth. Vikrama explains how his understanding of career success evolved from his early career misconception. He initially believed that working on exciting, high-impact products would automatically guarantee career advancement, while working on less visible products would slow growth. However, through observing many product managers over his decade and a half of experience, he discovered this assumption was flawed.

vocabulary.definition: The process of increasing in size, value, or importance over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, growth often refers to the expansion of a company's revenue, market share, or customer base, indicating its overall success and sustainability.

insight.nuance: While growth is generally viewed positively, it can also imply challenges such as scalability and resource management.

vocabulary.definition: Assured or promised, often in a formal or legal context, that something will happen or be delivered.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a guaranteed outcome may refer to a promise made to customers regarding product performance or service delivery, often used to build trust and credibility.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a strong commitment, but overuse may lead to skepticism if not backed by evidence.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to comprehend or grasp the meaning of something, often involving insight or awareness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding is crucial for effective communication, negotiation, and collaboration among team members and stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While understanding can denote knowledge, it also implies empathy and the ability to appreciate different perspectives.

vocabulary.definition: A view or opinion that is incorrect based on faulty thinking or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, misconceptions can lead to poor decision-making, ineffective strategies, or misalignment among team members regarding goals and processes.

insight.nuance: While misconceptions can stem from a lack of information, they can also arise from entrenched beliefs that resist change.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: I created a career growth framework for product managers, which comprises of three things, and I call it three W's. So what you produce, what you bring to the table, and what's your operating model?
keySentence: what you produce, what you bring to the table, and what's your operating model?
text_ko: 저는 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)를 위한 경력 성장 프레임워크(career growth framework)를 만들었어요. 세 가지 요소로 구성돼 있어서 저는 이를 '세 가지 W(three W's)'라고 부릅니다. 즉, 무엇을 만들어 내는지(what you produce), 어떤 가치를 제공하는지(what you bring to the table), 그리고 어떤 식으로 일하는지, 다시 말해 운영 모델(operating model)은 어떤지요. 진짜 강한 프로덕트 매니저들은 보통 이 세 가지 중 두 가지에 강해요. 반면에 실제로 성장하거나 승진하는 사람들은 세 가지 모두에서 잘해요.
text_zh: 我为产品经理做了一个职业发展框架，主要包括三个方面，我叫它"三个W"。就是你能产出什么，你能带来什么价值，还有你的工作方式是怎样的。真正厉害的产品经理通常在这三个方面能做好其中两个。而那些往上升的，正在上升期的产品经理，这三个维度他们都表现得很不错。
text_es: Creé un marco de desarrollo profesional para product managers que tiene tres componentes, y lo llamo "las tres W" (three W's). O sea: qué produces, qué aportas al equipo, y cuál es tu modelo operativo. Los product managers realmente sólidos por lo general dominan dos de estas tres áreas. Los que ascienden y están en pleno crecimiento son los que rinden bien en las tres dimensiones.
fullContext: After observing that product success doesn't guarantee career growth, Vikrama created his framework to explain what actually drives PM career advancement. The three W's framework identifies the core areas where product managers need to excel: outputs/deliverables, their unique contributions and skills, and how they collaborate with others. He notes that good PMs typically excel in two areas, but those experiencing rapid career growth perform well across all three dimensions.

vocabulary.definition: A structured plan or system that outlines the components and relationships within a particular domain or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a framework provides a foundational structure that guides decision-making, project management, or product development.

insight.nuance: While 'framework' often implies a comprehensive structure, it can also suggest flexibility, allowing for adaptation within defined boundaries.

vocabulary.definition: To consist of or be made up of various parts or elements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business contexts, 'comprises' is often used to describe the components of a product, service, or organizational structure.

insight.nuance: It is important to use 'comprises' correctly, as it suggests that the listed elements are included as part of a whole, rather than being separate or additional.

vocabulary.definition: A conceptual framework that defines how an organization delivers value, including its processes, structures, and governance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and established companies, an operating model serves as a blueprint for aligning resources and activities to achieve strategic objectives.

insight.nuance: The term 'operating model' often implies a level of strategic planning and operational efficiency, making it suitable for discussions about organizational effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: The process of progressing in one's professional life, often through promotions, skill development, or increased responsibilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, career advancement is a key focus for both employees and management, influencing talent retention and organizational growth.

insight.nuance: While 'career advancement' generally has positive connotations, it can also imply competition and pressure within a workplace setting.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: The mistake that I see a lot of product managers make is they start operating in either output or outcomes. And when you are transitioning to outcomes, it's very important that you continue to still hone your craft on outputs.
keySentence: Hone your craft on outputs while transitioning to outcomes.
text_ko: 제가 자주 보는 실수는 많은 프로덕트 매니저들이 일을 아웃풋(output)이나 아웃컴(outcome) 중 한쪽에만 치우쳐서 시작한다는 거예요. 아웃컴(outcome)으로 전환할 때에도 아웃풋(output)에 대한 역량을 계속 갈고닦는 게 정말 중요해요. 예를 들어, 그냥 고투마켓 전략(go-to-market strategy)을 포기해 버리나요, 아니면 마케팅 담당자들이 가져가서 실제로 그 고투마켓 전략을 만드는 데 쓸 수 있는 프로덕트 노드(product nodes)를 만들기 시작하나요?
text_zh: 我发现很多产品经理都会犯一个错误，就是要么只关注产出(output)，要么只关注结果(outcomes)。当你开始向结果导向转型的时候，继续打磨你在产出方面的能力还是很重要的。比如说，你是直接放弃市场推广策略不管了，还是说你会做一些产品要点(product nodes)，然后市场部的人可以拿去用来制定推广策略？
text_es: El error que veo mucho en los product managers es que empiezan a trabajar solo en outputs o solo en outcomes. Y cuando estás haciendo la transición hacia outcomes, es súper importante que sigas puliendo tu técnica en outputs. Por ejemplo, ¿vas a abandonar completamente la estrategia de go-to-market o empiezas a crear product nodes que después el equipo de marketing pueda usar para armar esa estrategia de go-to-market?
fullContext: Vikrama is explaining the first W of his framework - 'what you produce' - which progresses from outputs to outcomes to strategic direction. He warns against a common pitfall where PMs abandon execution skills as they advance in their careers. Even senior PMs should maintain their ability to create detailed, actionable deliverables rather than only focusing on high-level strategy and goals.

vocabulary.definition: The process of changing from one state or condition to another.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, transitioning often refers to shifting strategies, processes, or roles to adapt to new market conditions or organizational goals.

insight.nuance: Transitioning implies a gradual change rather than an abrupt shift, often requiring careful planning and management.

vocabulary.definition: To refine and improve one's skills or expertise in a particular area through practice and dedication.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a professional setting, honing your craft is essential for personal development and can lead to greater innovation and effectiveness in one's role.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the importance of continuous learning and improvement, suggesting that mastery is an ongoing process.

vocabulary.definition: The tangible products, results, or deliverables produced by a process or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, outputs are often measured to assess productivity and efficiency, serving as key performance indicators for teams and projects.

insight.nuance: While outputs are important, they may not always reflect the overall effectiveness or impact of a project, as they focus on quantity rather than quality.

vocabulary.definition: The end results or impacts of a process, initiative, or project, often evaluated in terms of effectiveness and value.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, outcomes are critical for understanding the success of strategies and initiatives, guiding future decision-making and resource allocation.

insight.nuance: Outcomes emphasize the broader implications and benefits of actions taken, highlighting the importance of aligning efforts with strategic goals.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: You must have that impact through the artifacts that you work on. For a lot of product managers, when I ask, 'Hey, I was working on this very impactful area.
keySentence: Impact through the artifacts you work on is essential.
text_ko: 여러분이 만든 산출물(artifacts)을 통해 그 영향력을 보여줘야 해요. 많은 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)들에게 제가 "저는 굉장히 영향력 있는 일을 했는데 그게 경력으로 이어지지 않아요. 뭐가 부족한가요?"라고 물어보면, 제가 "마지막 제품 요구사항 문서(PRD)를 보여줄 수 있어요? 마지막으로 보낸 제품 노트(product note)는요? 직접 작성했거나 함께 작업한 제품 전략 문서(product strategy doc)는요? 디자인팀에 보낸 문제와 그 우선순위를 정리한 브리프(brief)는요?"라고 물어보곤 해요. 보통 뭔가 하나쯤은 빠져 있더라고요.
text_zh: 你必须通过你做的这些具体产出来体现影响力。很多产品经理跟我说，"我在做一个很有影响力的项目，但对我职业发展没什么帮助，到底缺了什么？" 然后我就问他们，"你能给我看看你最近的PRD吗？你发的产品总结能看一下吗？你写的或者参与的产品策略文档在哪里？你给设计团队的需求说明，包括问题优先级排序，能给我看看吗？" 通常情况下，你总会发现这里面缺了点什么。
text_es: Tienes que lograr ese impacto a través de los entregables en los que trabajas. Con muchos product managers, cuando les pregunto: "Oye, estaba trabajando en un área muy impactante, pero no logro tener el impacto que quiero en mi carrera, ¿qué me está faltando?" Y cuando voy y les digo: "¿Me puedes enseñar tu último PRD? ¿Me puedes mostrar la última nota de producto que mandaste? ¿Me puedes enseñar el documento de estrategia de producto que tienes o en el que colaboraste? ¿Me puedes mostrar el brief que le mandaste al equipo de diseño sobre los problemas y la priorización de esos problemas?" Por lo general, vas a encontrar que algo les está faltando.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the second W - 'what you bring to the table.' Vikrama explains this means demonstrating your unique impact through tangible work products and documents. When PMs struggle with career growth despite working on successful products, he investigates their actual deliverables like PRDs, strategy docs, and design briefs. Often these artifacts are missing or poor quality, which prevents them from showing their individual contribution to the product's success.

vocabulary.definition: Having a significant effect or influence on a situation or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'impactful' often describes initiatives, strategies, or products that drive substantial change or improvement within an organization or market.

insight.nuance: While 'impactful' is generally positive, it can imply a degree of subjectivity regarding what constitutes significant impact.

vocabulary.definition: Tangible items or documents that are created as part of a process, often used for analysis or reference.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product management and development, 'artifacts' refer to deliverables such as prototypes, wireframes, or documentation that help communicate ideas and facilitate decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a sense of permanence and value, as artifacts are often used to represent the work and thought processes behind a project.

vocabulary.definition: Perceptible by touch; capable of being touched or physically measured; concrete.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'tangible' often refers to assets or results that can be quantified and assessed, such as revenue, products, or physical resources.

insight.nuance: While 'tangible' emphasizes physicality, it can also be used metaphorically to describe measurable outcomes in less concrete areas, such as customer satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: Showing or proving something through evidence or examples.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'demonstrating' is crucial for validating concepts, showcasing products, or illustrating the effectiveness of strategies to stakeholders or clients.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of clarity and proof, suggesting that mere claims are insufficient without tangible evidence to support them.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: There are three tenets that I define in working well as a product manager with others. Number one is raise difficult issues without being difficult to work with. Bring out important topics without drawing importance to yourself.
keySentence: Raise difficult issues without drawing importance to yourself.
text_ko: 다른 사람들과 잘 협업하는 제품 관리자(product manager)가 되기 위해 제가 정한 세 가지 원칙이 있어요. 첫째, 함께 일하기 어렵게 굴지 않으면서도 어려운 이슈는 제기해요. 둘째, 자신을 내세우지 않으면서도 중요한 사안은 꺼내요. 마지막으로, 결정을 내리게 하는 책임은 본인이 지되 모든 결정을 혼자 내리지는 않아요.
text_zh: 我觉得做好产品经理，跟别人配合好，有三个要点。第一个就是该提的难题必须提，但别让人觉得你这个人很难搞。第二个是要把重要的事情摆到台面上来讨论，但不要老想着突出自己。最后一个，你的职责是推动大家把决策做出来，而不是什么决定都你一个人说了算。
text_es: Hay tres principios que defino para trabajar bien como product manager con otros equipos. Primero, saca a la luz los temas complicados sin ser difícil de tratar. Pon sobre la mesa los asuntos importantes sin hacerte el protagonista. Y por último, tu trabajo es lograr que se tomen las decisiones, no tomarlas todas tú solo.
fullContext: Vikrama is describing the third W - 'your operating model' - which focuses on how PMs collaborate with stakeholders. Due to the 'mini CEO' mythology around product management, many PMs struggle with interpersonal dynamics. He provides three core principles for effective collaboration that help PMs avoid common pitfalls like being seen as difficult or self-important while still driving progress and decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Tenets are fundamental principles or beliefs that guide actions and decisions within a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, tenets often refer to the core values or guiding principles that shape a company's culture, strategy, and operational practices.

insight.nuance: While tenets are foundational, they may evolve over time as organizations adapt to new challenges and opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: To collaborate means to work jointly with others, especially in an intellectual endeavor or project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, collaboration is essential for fostering innovation, enhancing problem-solving, and achieving common goals among teams and departments.

insight.nuance: Collaboration implies a cooperative spirit and shared responsibility, distinguishing it from mere cooperation, which may lack the same depth of engagement.

vocabulary.definition: Stakeholders are individuals or groups that have an interest or investment in a particular project, organization, or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, stakeholders can include employees, customers, investors, suppliers, and the community, all of whom can influence or be affected by a company's actions and decisions.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the importance of considering diverse perspectives and interests in decision-making processes, particularly in corporate governance.

vocabulary.definition: Mythology refers to a collection of myths or stories that explain the beliefs, values, and practices of a particular culture or group.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, mythology can refer to the narratives and shared stories that shape an organization's identity, culture, and employee engagement.

insight.nuance: While often associated with ancient tales, in business, mythology can also encompass modern narratives that inspire and motivate employees, making it a powerful tool for branding and culture-building.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: The first thing is whether you are focusing on things you control or whether you're focusing on things that are beyond your control. Second, what's your relationship with change? And third is how you see yourself.
keySentence: Focus on your relationship with change, not just control.
text_ko: 첫째는 여러분이 통제할 수 있는 것에 집중하고 있는지, 통제할 수 없는 것에 신경 쓰고 있는지예요. 둘째는 변화와 어떤 관계를 맺고 있는지예요. 셋째는 자신을 어떻게 바라보는지예요. 이 셋째가 정말, 정말 강력해요. 그 부분도 이야기해볼게요.
text_zh: 第一点就是，你到底是把精力放在自己能掌控的事情上，还是老想着那些你根本管不了的事儿。第二点，你怎么看待变化这件事？第三点是你怎么看自己。这第三点特别关键，咱们待会儿也会聊到。
text_es: Lo primero es si te estás enfocando en las cosas que puedes controlar o si te estás enfocando en cosas que están fuera de tu control. Lo segundo, ¿cuál es tu relación con el cambio? Y lo tercero es cómo te ves a ti mismo. Este tercer punto es súper poderoso y también vamos a hablar de eso.
fullContext: Lenny asks what most impedes people's career growth and what causes PMs to shoot themselves in the foot. Vikrama identifies three critical mindset shifts that can either accelerate or hinder career advancement. He emphasizes that while growth frameworks and rubrics are helpful, these underlying mental patterns often determine whether someone actually progresses in their career, with self-perception being particularly influential.

vocabulary.definition: The act of concentrating attention or effort on a particular task or subject.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, focusing is essential for prioritizing goals, managing resources effectively, and ensuring that team efforts align with strategic objectives.

insight.nuance: While focusing implies a deliberate choice to direct attention, it can also suggest the need to avoid distractions that may hinder productivity.

vocabulary.definition: The way in which two or more parties are connected, often involving mutual interactions and dependencies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, relationships can refer to connections between colleagues, clients, or partners, which are crucial for collaboration, networking, and building trust.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both formal and informal connections, and its strength can vary from transactional to deeply personal.

vocabulary.definition: A set of beliefs or attitudes that shape how an individual perceives and reacts to situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, a growth mindset can foster innovation and resilience, while a fixed mindset may limit adaptability and responsiveness to change.

insight.nuance: Mindset often reflects deeper psychological patterns and can influence decision-making and leadership styles.

vocabulary.definition: To hinder or obstruct progress or movement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, factors that impede growth or efficiency can include bureaucratic processes, lack of resources, or poor communication.

insight.nuance: While impede suggests a significant barrier, it can also refer to minor obstacles that cumulatively affect overall performance.

speaker: Vikrama Dhiman
text: These things are not just signaling, they are also anti-signaling... I'm high agency. So it's sometimes okay if I'm little brash, if I cut corners somewhere, if I sometimes come across as a little rude to some people.
keySentence: High agency PMs may cut corners and come across as rude.
text_ko: 많은 프로덕트 매니저(product managers, PM)들이—저도 한때 그랬지만—이런 식으로 행동하는 걸 자주 봐요. 사람들은 "나는 되게 하이 에이전시(high agency)인 PM이에요" 혹은 "나는 협업형(collaborative) PM이에요"라고 말하죠. 초반에는 "아, 이런 종류의 일은 이런 타입의 PM들에게 맡겨야겠다"라고 생각했어요. 그런데 나중에 보니 이게 단순한 시그널링(signaling)만이 아니라 안티-시그널링(anti-signaling)이기도 하다는 걸 알게 됐어요. 즉 "내가 하이 에이전시니까"라며 가끔 거칠게 굴거나, 어딘가를 대충 넘어가거나, 어떤 사람들한테는 좀 무례하게 보여도 괜찮다고 스스로 정당화하는 면이 있다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我发现很多产品经理，包括我自己以前也是这样，老是爱给自己贴标签，会说"哎呀我是那种很有主动性(high agency)的PM"，或者"我是很善于合作(collaborative)的PM"。一开始我还真信了，觉得好啊，那就把这种活儿给这些产品经理做。但后来我才明白，这些话不光是在给自己加分，其实也在暴露问题。就像那些说自己很有主动性的，潜台词可能是"我很有主动性嘛，所以有时候态度冲一点也没事儿，偷个懒走个捷径也行，对人粗鲁一点也能理解"，你懂我意思吧？
text_es: He visto a muchos product managers, yo incluido en algún momento, haciendo estas cosas. La gente viene y te dice: "Ay, es que soy un PM muy proactivo" o "Soy un PM muy colaborativo". Antes yo pensaba que bueno, necesito darle este tipo de trabajo a estos product managers. Pero después empecé a entender que estas cosas no son solo señales, también son anti-señales. Es como decir: "Soy muy proactivo, entonces a veces está bien si soy un poco brusco, si tomo atajos por aquí y por allá, si a veces me ven medio grosero con algunas personas", ¿no?
fullContext: Vikrama is explaining the third career impediment - 'how you see yourself.' He describes how PMs often adopt limiting self-narratives that become career obstacles. When PMs label themselves with specific traits like being 'high agency' or 'collaborative,' these labels can inadvertently excuse problematic behaviors. These self-stories become anti-signaling - while meant to highlight strengths, they actually justify weaknesses and prevent growth.

vocabulary.definition: The act of conveying information or intentions through actions or behaviors, often to influence perceptions or decisions of others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, signaling can refer to actions taken by a company or individual to indicate their credibility, intentions, or market position to stakeholders, such as investors or competitors.

insight.nuance: Signaling often carries a strategic connotation, suggesting that the action is deliberate and aimed at shaping others' perceptions.

vocabulary.definition: Actions or behaviors that intentionally downplay or negate the typical signals expected in a given context, often to convey authenticity or humility.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, anti-signaling can be used to differentiate oneself from competitors by rejecting ostentatious displays of success or status, thus appealing to a more grounded audience.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a strategic choice to avoid conventional signaling in favor of a more genuine or relatable approach.

vocabulary.definition: A term describing an individual who possesses a strong sense of control over their actions and decisions, often taking initiative and responsibility.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and entrepreneurial settings, high agency individuals are valued for their ability to drive projects forward, make decisive choices, and adapt to challenges proactively.

insight.nuance: While high agency is generally seen as positive, it can sometimes lead to perceptions of recklessness if not balanced with consideration for others.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by boldness or audacity, often with a disregard for consequences or the feelings of others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, being brash can be seen as a double-edged sword; it may lead to innovative ideas and rapid decision-making, but can also result in conflicts or negative perceptions from colleagues.

insight.nuance: While brashness can be associated with confidence, it may also carry a negative connotation of being overly aggressive or inconsiderate.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: I think the blast radius of a poorly written memo is way bigger than most people think.
keySentence: The blast radius of a poorly written memo is bigger than most think.
text_ko: 부실하게 쓴 메모의 파급 반경(blast radius)은 대부분 사람들이 생각하는 것보다 훨씬 커요. 슬랙 채널(Slack channel)에서 15명 정도 있는 곳에 그냥 메시지를 툭 던졌는데 내용이 애매하거나 들어가야 할 정보를 빼먹었다면 확인이나 질문이 계속 오가게 돼요. 반면 한 번만 더 검토했더라면 그 15명은 바로 다음 단계로 넘어갔을 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得一份写得烂的备忘录(memo)造成的影响比大多数人想象的要大得多。如果你在一个有15个人的Slack频道里随便发个消息，写得乱七八糟的，该说的信息也没说清楚，那就会引起一大堆来回扯皮。但如果你当初多检查一遍，那15个人早就开始干活了。
text_es: Creo que el impacto de un memo mal redactado es mucho mayor de lo que la gente piensa. Si mandas un mensaje rápido en un canal de Slack con otras 15 personas, y está confuso, no incluiste información que debías haber puesto, va a haber un montón de idas y vueltas. Mientras que si le hubieras echado otro vistazo, esas 15 personas ya estarían trabajando a toda máquina.
fullContext: Lenny emphasizes the importance of reviewing your own writing before sending it, noting that many people skip this step due to time constraints. Wes explains why taking time to review written communication is crucial for workplace efficiency. She argues that poorly written messages create much more downstream work and confusion than people realize, affecting multiple team members who must then engage in clarifying conversations.

vocabulary.definition: The area or extent of impact resulting from a particular action or event.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'blast radius' often refers to the potential consequences of a decision or communication, particularly in terms of how it affects stakeholders and operations.

insight.nuance: This term implies a significant and often unintended ripple effect, highlighting the importance of careful planning and communication.

vocabulary.definition: Describes a document or piece of writing that lacks clarity, coherence, or professionalism.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, a poorly written memo or report can lead to misunderstandings, miscommunication, and a lack of credibility.

insight.nuance: This phrase carries a negative connotation and is often used to critique the quality of written communication, suggesting a need for improvement.

vocabulary.definition: The state or quality of being significant or valuable in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding the importance of various factors such as market trends, customer feedback, or employee engagement is crucial for strategic decision-making.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the necessity of prioritizing certain aspects over others, often depending on the specific goals of an organization.

vocabulary.definition: The process of examining or assessing something critically, often to provide feedback or make improvements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, reviewing documents, projects, or performance metrics is essential for ensuring quality and alignment with organizational goals.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a thorough and thoughtful evaluation, often implying a constructive approach to feedback rather than mere criticism.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: I think that most people assume that their boss has to manage them and they feel a little bit resentful that, why should I manage my boss? They're getting paid more. They are my manager. They have more responsibility.
keySentence: most people assume that their boss has to manage them and they feel a little bit resentful
text_ko: 대부분 사람들은 자신의 상사가 자신을 관리해야 한다고 생각해요. 그래서 '왜 내가 상사를 관리해야 하지?'라며 약간 불만을 느껴요. 상사는 월급도 더 받고, 내 상사고, 책임도 더 많으니까요. 그렇게 계속 생각해도 커리어가 괜찮게 갈 수도 있어요. 그런데 상사를 관리(manage up)하는 태도를 받아들이면 상사가 훨씬 더 고마워하고, 기회도 더 많이 생기고, 신뢰도 더 쌓여요. 상사를 능동적으로 관리하기로 마음먹으면 좋은 일들이 정말 많이 일어나요.
text_zh: 我觉得大部分人都认为应该是老板来管理他们，然后就有点不服气，凭什么要我去管理我老板啊？他们工资比我高，他们是我的上司，责任也比我大。你可以一直这么想，职业发展可能也还行，但是如果你能接受这个观点——主动管理你的老板，他们会更欣赏你，你会得到更多机会，和他们的信任关系也会更好。当你决定向上管理(manage up)的时候，会有很多好处。
text_es: Creo que la mayoría de la gente asume que su jefe tiene que gestionarlos a ellos y se sienten un poco resentidos pensando "¿por qué debería yo gestionar a mi jefe? A él le pagan más. Es mi manager. Tiene más responsabilidad." Y puedes seguir pensando así y tu carrera tal vez esté bien, pero si abrazas la idea de que si gestionas a tu jefe, te va a valorar mucho más, vas a conseguir más oportunidades, vas a tener más confianza con él, hay un montón de cosas buenas que pasan cuando decides hacer "managing up".
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes why managing up is important and why people aren't doing it well. Wes explains that many people feel resistant to managing their boss because they think it's their manager's job to manage them, not the other way around.
