She argues that this mindset limits career growth and that those who embrace managing up will see significant benefits in their professional relationships and opportunities.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a proactive approach to leadership dynamics, suggesting that employees should take initiative in guiding their managers rather than waiting for direction.

vocabulary.definition: The state or fact of having a duty to deal with something or having control over someone.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, responsibility often refers to the obligations assigned to individuals or teams, impacting accountability and performance metrics.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling or expressing bitterness or indignation at having been treated unfairly.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: MOO stands for Most Obvious Objection. A lot of times we're surprised by the questions that we get especially in meetings, we feel blindsided.
keySentence: A lot of times we're surprised by the questions that we get especially in meetings, we feel blindsided.
text_ko: MOO는 '가장 명백한 반대(Most Obvious Objection)'의 약자예요. 회의에서 특히 예상치 못한 질문을 받아 깜짝 놀라 당황할 때가 많죠. 그런데 사실 단 2분만이라도 내가 받을 만한 명백한 반대 의견들을 생각해 보면 금방 몇 가지가 떠오르는 경우가 많아요. 모든 이의를 다 예측할 수 있냐고요? 아니에요. 하지만 분명히 예상 가능한 건 충분히 대비할 수 있어요.
text_zh: MOO就是Most Obvious Objection的缩写，也就是最明显的反对意见。我们在开会的时候经常会被一些问题搞得措手不及，觉得很意外。但其实你要是花两分钟想想，我可能会遇到哪些明显的反对意见，往往马上就能想出来。你能预料到所有的反对意见吗？当然不可能。但是那些明显的，你绝对可以提前想到。
text_es: MOO significa Most Obvious Objection, o sea, la objeción más obvia. Muchas veces nos sorprenden las preguntas que recibimos, sobre todo en las juntas, y nos sentimos como que nos agarraron desprevenidos. Pero la verdad es que si te pones a pensar aunque sea dos minutos en cuáles son las objeciones obvias que seguramente me van a salir, casi siempre se te ocurren varias de una vez. ¿Vas a poder anticipar todas y cada una de las objeciones? No. ¿Pero puedes anticipar las obvias? Por supuesto que sí.
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes about her MOO framework after mentioning it briefly earlier. MOO stands for Most Obvious Objection, which is a preparation technique for presentations and meetings. Wes explains that people often feel caught off guard by questions or pushback in meetings, when they could have anticipated the most common objections with just a few minutes of preparation beforehand.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: The idea behind what I call the state change method is that you should punctuate your monologues with state changes. So state changes are anything that shakes your audience awake and adds some variety.
keySentence: Punctuate your monologues to shake your audience awake.
text_ko: 제가 '상태 변화 방법(state change method)'이라고 부르는 거의 핵심은, 혼자서 계속 말할 때 중간중간에 상태 변화를 넣으라는 거예요. 상태 변화(state change)란 청중의 집중을 깨우고 분위기에 변화를 주는 모든 행동을 말해요. 예를 들어 채팅창에 답을 입력해 달라고 요청하는 거나, 브래디 번치(Brady Bunch)처럼 모두가 보이는 갤러리 보기(gallery view)에서 화면 공유(screen share)로 전환해 뭔가를 보여준 뒤 다시 돌아오는 식일 수 있어요.
text_zh: 我说的这个状态切换法(state change method)，核心思想就是你在讲话的时候要不断地变换节奏。状态切换就是任何能让听众打起精神、增加点变化的东西。比如说让大家在聊天框里输入点什么，或者从画廊视图(gallery view)——就是那种能看到所有人的九宫格界面——切换到屏幕共享，展示点内容，然后再切回来。
text_es: La idea detrás de lo que yo llamo el método de cambio de estado es que tienes que interrumpir tus monólogos con cambios de estado. Los cambios de estado son cualquier cosa que despierte a tu audiencia y añada variedad. Puede ser pedirles que escriban algo en el chat. Puede ser cambiar de la vista de galería donde ves a todos en esa cuadrícula estilo Brady Bunch y pasar a compartir pantalla para mostrar algo, y luego regresar.
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes about her concept of creating state change in presentations and meetings. Wes explains that most Zoom meetings involve one person talking while everyone else listens silently, which is draining for participants. The state change method involves breaking up monologues with interactive elements to keep the audience engaged and prevent them from zoning out during virtual presentations.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: I have a framework called strategy, not self-expression. And so the idea here is that most of the time, by the time we are giving feedback to someone, we have been frustrated for a while.
keySentence: by the time we are giving feedback to someone, we have been frustrated for a while.
text_ko: 저는 '전략(strategy), 자기표현(self-expression)이 아니다'라는 프레임워크(framework)를 가지고 있어요. 요지는 대부분의 경우 누군가에게 피드백(feedback)을 줄 때쯤이면 이미 한동안 답답함과 불만이 쌓여 있다는 거예요. 그래서 동료와 일대일(one-on-one) 미팅을 잡아 피드백(feedback)을 전하면, 결국 '그들이 한 행동의 영향(impact)을 알려주겠다'는 명목으로 제가 쌓인 불만을 다 털어놓는 벤팅 세션(venting session)이 돼 버리곤 했어요.
text_zh: 我有个框架叫做策略性反馈，而不是情绪发泄。这个思路是什么呢？就是说大部分时候，等我们要给别人反馈的时候，其实心里早就憋了一肚子火了。然后我会约个一对一(one-on-one)，想着要跟同事说说这个反馈，结果到最后肯定变成了吐槽大会，打着"分享你的行为对我造成什么影响"的旗号，把我所有的不爽都倒出来了。
text_es: Tengo un marco de trabajo que llamo estrategia, no autoexpresión. Y la idea es que la mayoría de las veces, cuando ya vamos a darle feedback a alguien, llevamos un rato frustrados. Entonces yo programaba una reunión uno a uno con un compañero para darle el feedback y inevitablemente se convertía en una sesión de desahogo donde yo, con la excusa de compartir el impacto de lo que habían hecho, terminaba soltando todas mis frustraciones.
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes for advice on giving feedback effectively. Wes introduces her 'strategy, not self-expression' framework for constructive feedback. She explains that people often wait until they're very frustrated before giving feedback, which leads to unproductive venting sessions rather than strategic conversations focused on behavior change. The framework emphasizes focusing on motivating the desired outcome rather than expressing all your built-up frustrations.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a particular issue or concept.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: So the idea behind what I call eyes lighting up is that when you're talking to someone and you're explaining something, you're teaching them, you're sharing your startup idea or whatever the normal response is people will want to be polite.
keySentence: Eyes light up when someone is genuinely interested.
text_ko: 제가 '눈이 반짝이는 순간(eyes lighting up)'이라고 부르는 건, 누군가랑 얘기하면서 뭔가를 설명하거나 가르치거나 스타트업 아이디어를 공유할 때의 상황을 말해요. 대부분 사람들은 예의상 고개를 끄덕이며 "아, 그래요, 흥미롭네요"라고 하죠. 그런데 대화 중에 한순간 상대방의 눈이 확 반짝이는 때가 있어요. 그때는 진짜로 그 순간에 당신이 하는 말에 관심을 갖고 있는 거예요.
text_zh: 我说的"眼睛发光"是这个意思：你跟别人聊天的时候，解释什么东西，教他们，或者分享你的创业想法啥的，一般人都会比较客气，会点点头说"哦，好的，挺有意思的"。但通常聊着聊着会有那么一个瞬间，他们的眼睛突然就亮了，因为那一刻他们是真的对你说的东西感兴趣了。
text_es: Entonces la idea detrás de lo que yo llamo "que se les iluminen los ojos" es que cuando estás hablando con alguien y le estás explicando algo, le estás enseñando, le estás compartiendo tu idea de startup o lo que sea, la respuesta normal es que la gente quiere ser educada. Entonces van a asentir con la cabeza y van a decir "Ah, sí, qué interesante." Pero normalmente hay un momento en la conversación donde se les iluminan los ojos porque realmente están genuinamente interesados en lo que les estás diciendo en ese momento.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Wes's concept called 'eyes lighting up' in relation to state changes in meetings. Wes explains that when presenting or explaining ideas to people, most listeners will be polite and give generic positive responses. However, there are specific moments when someone becomes genuinely engaged - when their eyes literally light up with interest. This physical reaction provides valuable data about what content truly resonates with your audience.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: I have a framework called CEDAF. C-E-D-A-F. It's kind of like Cedar, but with an F at the end. The C is comprehension.
keySentence: The C is comprehension.
text_ko: CEDAF라는 프레임워크(framework)가 있어요. C-E-D-A-F. Cedar랑 비슷한데 끝에 F가 붙은 거예요. C는 이해(comprehension)이에요. 즉, 내가 위임(delegate)하려는 사람에게 내가 원하는 일이 무엇인지 이해하는 데 필요한 걸 다 줬는지 확인하는 거예요. E는 흥미(excitement)이에요. 이걸 가능한 한 흥미롭게 설명하고 있는지요. D는 리스크 제거(de-risk)이에요. 위임할 때 생길 수 있는 명백한 리스크들을 줄여주고 있는지요.
text_zh: 我有个框架叫CEDAF，C-E-D-A-F，有点像Cedar这个词，但最后加个F。C是理解度(comprehension)，就是说我有没有把这个被委派的人需要知道的所有信息都给到位了，让他们完全明白我要他们干什么。E是兴奋度(excitement)，我在解释的时候有没有把这事儿说得尽可能让人有干劲？D是去风险(de-risk)，就是我有没有把委派过程中那些明显的风险都提前化解掉？
text_es: Tengo un marco de trabajo que se llama CEDAF. C-E-D-A-F. Es como si dijeras "Cedar" en inglés, pero con una F al final. La C es de comprensión. O sea, ¿le he dado a la persona a la que le estoy delegando todo lo que necesita para entender qué es lo que quiero que haga? La E es de emoción. ¿Estoy explicando esto de una manera que lo haga tan emocionante como podría ser? La D es para eliminar riesgos (de-risk). ¿Estoy eliminando cualquier riesgo obvio de delegar esto?
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes about her advice for delegating effectively while maintaining high standards. Wes introduces her CEDAF framework for delegation, which provides a systematic approach to assigning work to others. She explains the first three components: ensuring the person understands what they need to do (comprehension), making the work engaging by explaining its importance (excitement), and identifying potential problems upfront (de-risk).

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides guidance for organizing and implementing processes or ideas.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a framework often refers to a set of guidelines or best practices that help teams develop projects or strategies efficiently.

insight.nuance: While 'framework' suggests a supportive structure, it can also imply rigidity; thus, it should be used when referring to established systems that allow for some flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand and grasp the meaning of information or concepts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, comprehension is crucial for effective communication, ensuring that team members and stakeholders fully understand project goals and strategies.

insight.nuance: Comprehension implies a deeper understanding than mere knowledge; it is best used in contexts where clarity and insight are essential.

insight.nuance: While 'systematic' connotes thoroughness and organization, it can also suggest inflexibility; use it when emphasizing structured methods that still allow for adaptability.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: And ironically, the most senior people are best at managing up.
keySentence: the most senior people are best at managing up.
text_ko: 아이러니하게도, 직급이 높은 분들이 상사와의 관계 관리(managing up)를 제일 잘해요. 사실 그게 바로 그들이 승진한 이유예요. 상사가 무엇을 걱정하는지, 뭐 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 이루는지 파악해서 그 부담을 덜어주거든요. 또 무슨 일이 진행되고 있는지 상사에게 꾸준히 공유해서 상사들이 매일매일 계속 확인하거나 질문을 던질 필요가 없게 만들어요.
text_zh: 很有意思的是，越是高层的人越会向上管理。他们之所以能升到现在的位置，就是因为特别会向上管理——能摸透老板在担心什么，什么事儿让老板睡不着觉，然后主动帮老板分担。他们特别会让老板及时了解情况，这样老板就不用天天追着问这问那了。
text_es: Y paradójicamente, la gente más senior es la que mejor sabe manejar hacia arriba (managing up). Por eso llegaron a donde están en primer lugar: porque eran excelentes manejando la relación con sus jefes, entendiendo qué los tenía preocupados, qué no los dejaba dormir por las noches, para poder quitarles esa carga de encima. Son expertos en mantener a sus jefes al tanto de lo que está pasando, así sus jefes no tienen que estar preguntando constantemente ni bombardeándolos con preguntas todos los días.
fullContext: Lenny asks why managing up is important and how to do it effectively. Wes addresses the misconception that senior people don't need to manage up anymore once they reach director or VP level. She explains that actually the opposite is true - the most successful senior leaders became successful precisely because they mastered the skill of managing up, understanding their bosses' concerns and proactively communicating to reduce their managers' workload.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of effectively communicating and working with one's superiors to ensure alignment and support for goals and initiatives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, managing up is crucial for fostering positive relationships with senior management and ensuring that one's contributions are recognized and valued.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a proactive approach to influence and support, rather than merely following directives.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals in an organization who hold high-level positions, typically with significant experience and authority.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, senior people are often responsible for strategic decision-making and guiding the overall direction of the company.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a level of respect and authority, but may also suggest a disconnect from day-to-day operations.

vocabulary.definition: A view or opinion that is incorrect based on faulty thinking or understanding.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of misunderstanding that can be corrected through education or clarification.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that produces a desired or intended result; efficiently and successfully.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: no matter how senior I got, managing up... actually became more important.
keySentence: managing up... actually became more important.
text_ko: 커리어 초반에 제가 분명히 느꼈던 상사 관리(managing up)에 대한 가장 흔한 오해 중 하나는, 주니어일 때만 상사 관리를 해야 하고 결국 시니어가 되면 더는 그걸 안 해도 될 거라는 생각이었어요. 그런데 막상 시니어가 돼도 상사 관리는 계속해야 하는 일이었고, 오히려 더 중요해졌다는 뼈저린 깨달음을 얻었어요.
text_zh: 我刚入职场的时候特别相信一个关于向上管理(managing up)的错误想法，就是觉得只有junior的时候才需要向上管理，等我做到高级别了，就不用再搞这套了。结果现实给了我当头一棒——不管我升到多高的位置，向上管理不但还得做，而且变得更加重要了。
text_es: Uno de los mitos más comunes sobre el "managing up" que definitivamente yo sentí al principio de mi carrera era que tendría que hacerlo siendo más junior, pero que eventualmente lo superaría, que llegaría a ser lo suficientemente senior como para ya no tener que hacerlo. Y fue una revelación dura darme cuenta de que sin importar qué tan senior me volviera, no solo tenía que seguir haciendo "managing up", sino que en realidad se volvía más importante.
fullContext: Lenny asks why managing up is important and why people might underappreciate this skill. Wes dispels a common misconception about managing up - that it's only necessary for junior employees. She explains that she initially believed she would eventually become senior enough to not need this skill, but discovered the opposite was true. Managing up becomes increasingly important as you advance in your career because senior roles involve more ambiguity and strategic decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of effectively communicating and aligning with one's superiors to ensure mutual understanding and support for goals and initiatives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, managing up is crucial for fostering positive relationships with higher management, ensuring that one's contributions are recognized and that strategic objectives are met.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a proactive approach to influence and support decision-making, rather than merely following orders.

vocabulary.definition: To fail to recognize the full worth or value of someone or something, often leading to a lack of acknowledgment or gratitude.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, underappreciating employees' efforts can lead to decreased morale and productivity, as well as increased turnover rates.

insight.nuance: This term carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of awareness or acknowledgment that can harm relationships and organizational culture.

vocabulary.definition: A view or opinion that is incorrect based on faulty thinking or understanding, often leading to misunderstandings.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, misconceptions can hinder innovation and collaboration, as they may prevent teams from effectively addressing challenges or leveraging opportunities.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a need for clarification or education to correct false beliefs, making it important to address misconceptions openly.

vocabulary.definition: Of great significance or value; having a major influence on outcomes or decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, identifying important tasks, projects, or relationships is essential for prioritizing resources and achieving strategic goals.

insight.nuance: While often used to denote priority, this term can also imply urgency or necessity, depending on the context in which it is applied.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: And so it went from being a conversation about yes or no, are you a helpful person or are you not, are you a team player or are you not into, hey, how do we make sure that the important right things get done?
keySentence: how do we make sure that the important right things get done?
text_ko: 그래서 그 대화는 '너는 도움이 되는 사람이냐, 아니냐', '팀 플레이어냐, 아니냐' 같은 예/아니오 식 논쟁에서 '어떻게 하면 정말로 중요하고 올바른 일들이 제대로 끝나게 할까?'로 바뀌었어요. 그 방식은 거절당하는 사람에게도 좋았고 알렉스에게도 좋았어요. 그런 얘기를 나눌 때마다 저는 알렉스가 우리가 하려는 가장 중요한 프로젝트들이 계속 우선순위에 남도록 정말 신중하게 신경 쓴다고 늘 느꼈거든요.
text_zh: 所以这个对话就从原来的"你到底帮不帮忙"、"你是不是团队合作的人"这种非黑即白的问题，变成了"我们怎么确保重要的事情能做好"。这样对被拒绝的人来说挺好的，对Alex来说也挺好，因为每次我们聊这些的时候，我都觉得他真的很用心在确保最重要的项目能保持优先级。
text_es: Y así pasó de ser una conversación sobre sí o no, ¿eres una persona que ayuda o no?, ¿eres alguien que trabaja en equipo o no?, a algo más como: oye, ¿cómo nos aseguramos de que se hagan las cosas importantes y correctas? Y esto es genial tanto para la persona a la que le estás diciendo que no como para Alex, porque cada vez que teníamos esas conversaciones, siempre me parecía que él realmente se tomaba el tiempo de asegurarse de que los proyectos más importantes en los que queríamos trabajar siguieran siendo prioridad.
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes for advice on how to say no effectively, mentioning his own struggles with declining requests politely. Wes shares a technique she learned from her colleague Alex, who would reframe 'no' conversations by discussing trade-offs instead of outright rejection. Rather than making it about whether someone is helpful or cooperative, Alex would explain what work would need to be deprioritized if he took on the new request, making it a strategic prioritization discussion.

vocabulary.definition: A team player is an individual who collaborates effectively with others to achieve common goals, demonstrating a cooperative attitude and a willingness to support teammates.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being a team player is essential for fostering a collaborative work environment, particularly in projects that require cross-functional teamwork and communication.

insight.nuance: While the term generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a lack of individual initiative if overemphasized in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Important refers to something that holds significant value or priority, often requiring attention or action due to its impact or relevance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, identifying important tasks or decisions is crucial for effective time management and strategic planning, ensuring that resources are allocated efficiently.

insight.nuance: The term can be subjective, as what is considered important may vary based on individual perspectives or organizational goals.

vocabulary.definition: To reframe means to change the way a situation or concept is perceived, often by presenting it in a new context or perspective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, reframing can be a powerful tool for problem-solving, allowing teams to approach challenges with fresh ideas and innovative solutions.

insight.nuance: Reframing is often used in discussions to shift focus from negative aspects to potential opportunities, but it should be done thoughtfully to avoid dismissing genuine concerns.

vocabulary.definition: Get done refers to the act of completing a task or achieving a goal, often emphasizing efficiency and effectiveness in execution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the fast-paced business environment, the ability to get things done is highly valued, as it reflects an individual's or team's productivity and commitment to meeting deadlines.

insight.nuance: While it conveys a sense of urgency, it can sometimes imply a focus on speed over quality, so it should be used in contexts where both aspects are balanced.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: I find that people tend to naturally be on the spectrum a little bit too confident as a baseline or not confident enough. So people who are too confident might state hypotheses as if they are fact. So I'm a big proponent of speaking accurately.
keySentence: people who are too confident might state hypotheses as if they are fact.
text_ko: 사람들은 보통 기본적으로 약간 과하게 자신감이 있거나, 반대로 자신감이 부족한 쪽으로 치우치는 경향이 있어요. 너무 자신감 있는 사람들은 가설을 마치 사실인 양 말해버리기도 해요. 그래서 저는 말을 정확하게 하는 걸 강력히 권해요. 자신의 확신 수준(level of conviction)과 그것을 뒷받침하는 실제 증거의 양(amount of evidence)을 솔직하고 정확하게 표현하면 많은 문제를 피할 수 있어요.
text_zh: 我发现大家天生都有点偏向两个极端——要么就是太自信了，要么就是信心不足。那些过于自信的人经常把假设当成事实来说。所以我特别推崇准确表达这件事。如果你能准确地说出自己有多大把握，以及你手头到底有多少证据支撑，就能避免很多麻烦。
text_es: Me he dado cuenta de que la gente por lo general tiende a estar en uno de dos extremos: o se sienten demasiado seguros de sí mismos por defecto, o no tienen suficiente confianza. Los que son demasiado confiados suelen presentar hipótesis como si fueran hechos comprobados. Por eso soy un gran defensor de hablar con precisión. Puedes evitarte muchos problemas si hablas con claridad sobre qué tan convencido estás realmente de algo y sobre la cantidad real de evidencia que tienes para respaldarlo.
fullContext: Lenny asks about finding the right level of confidence when presenting ideas or recommendations to leaders. Wes explains that people typically fall into two camps: being overconfident or underconfident in their communication. She emphasizes the importance of 'speaking accurately' - being precise about your level of certainty and the evidence supporting your statements rather than presenting hunches as established facts or being overly self-deprecating about solid recommendations.

vocabulary.definition: Hypotheses are proposed explanations or predictions that can be tested through research and experimentation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, hypotheses are often used to formulate strategies, test market assumptions, or evaluate product features before full implementation.

insight.nuance: While hypotheses are foundational in scientific inquiry, in business, they should be framed carefully to avoid overconfidence in untested ideas.

vocabulary.definition: A proponent is an individual who advocates for a particular idea, policy, or proposal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, a proponent may be a team member who champions a new product initiative or a stakeholder who supports a specific business strategy.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting active support, but can imply bias if the proponent does not consider opposing views.

vocabulary.definition: Accurately means in a manner that is correct, precise, and free from errors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, conveying information accurately is crucial for decision-making, reporting, and maintaining credibility with stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While accuracy is essential, it is important to balance it with clarity, as overly technical language can obscure meaning.

vocabulary.definition: A spectrum refers to a range of different but related ideas, qualities, or activities, often represented on a continuum.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, the term spectrum is frequently used to describe varying levels of confidence, market segments, or product features, helping to categorize complex concepts.

insight.nuance: Using 'spectrum' can imply a nuanced understanding of a topic, acknowledging that extremes exist but that most cases fall somewhere in between.

speaker: Wes Kao
text: A lot of times when we write a sentence, there's actually already a point of view or there's a point of view baked in, but you don't want it to be an accidental point of view.
keySentence: you don't want it to be an accidental point of view.
text_ko: 글을 쓸 때 문장 안에 이미 관점(point of view)이 녹아 들어가는 경우가 많은데, 그 관점이 의도치 않게 묻어나오는 건 원치 않아요. 방금 팀원이랑 이 얘기를 했는데, 팀원이 자기 글에 대해 피드백을 부탁했어요. 그런데 그가 쓴 단락(paragraph)의 표현 방식이 읽는 사람을 특정 방향으로 이끄는(leading) 식이었어요.
text_zh: 很多时候我们写一句话的时候，其实已经带了某种观点或者说观点已经融入进去了，但你不希望这个观点是无意中带出来的。我刚才跟我团队成员聊这个事，她让我给她写的东西提点意见，结果她那段话的写法明显在引导读者的想法。
text_es: Muchas veces cuando redactamos algo, ya llevamos un punto de vista incorporado, o sea, ya está ahí metido, pero no queremos que sea un punto de vista accidental. Justo estaba hablando de esto con una compañera de mi equipo - me pidió que le diera feedback sobre algo que había escrito y la forma en que había redactado su párrafo estaba dirigiendo al lector hacia una conclusión.
fullContext: Lenny asks Wes for general writing advice beyond the concepts they've already discussed. Wes emphasizes the importance of studying the technical craft of writing rather than just mimicking social media content. She explains how writers often unconsciously embed a point of view in their sentences, and shares an example of giving feedback to a team member whose writing was inadvertently leading the reader toward a specific conclusion.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of considering a matter; a perspective from which something is evaluated.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding different points of view can enhance decision-making and foster collaboration among diverse teams.

insight.nuance: While it often refers to personal perspectives, in a business context, it can also imply the importance of aligning viewpoints for strategic objectives.

vocabulary.definition: Happening by chance or unexpectedly; not planned or intended.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, accidental outcomes can lead to unintended consequences, highlighting the importance of strategic planning and risk management.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a negative connotation when referring to mistakes or errors that could have been avoided with careful consideration.

vocabulary.definition: To give special importance or prominence to something in speaking or writing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, emphasizing key points can enhance clarity and persuade stakeholders to take action or adopt a particular viewpoint.

insight.nuance: While it is often used to highlight positive aspects, it can also be employed to underscore critical issues that require immediate attention.

vocabulary.definition: The specialized skills and techniques required to produce a particular product or service, often involving a high level of expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and creative industries, possessing a strong technical craft is essential for innovation and maintaining competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a blend of artistry and precision, suggesting that mastery of technical craft is crucial for achieving excellence in one's field.

speaker: Will Larson
text: I think that we often treat engineers a little bit like children instead of giving them the responsibilities and ability to actually thrive as adults.
keySentence: giving them the responsibilities and ability to actually thrive as adults.
text_ko: 저는 우리가 엔지니어들(engineers)을 어른으로서 실제로 잘 자랄 수 있게 책임과 권한을 주기보다, 마치 아이처럼 대하는 경우가 종종 있다고 생각해요. '엔지니어들이 그런 일을 하려 하지 않을 거야'라고 말하는 사람들이 있는데, 중요한 일에서 그들을 보호막으로 감싸는 건 오히려 좋지 않아요. 그래서 제가 중요하게 보는 것 중 하나는 지금이 엔지니어들을 동료로 대우해서 진짜로 시니어 리더십 역할(senior leadership roles)에 기용하고, '우리가 그들을 애지중지하거나 실제 문제에서 숨겨줘야 해'라는 기본 가정을 버릴 수 있는 순간으로 돌아오는 것 같다는 점이에요. 그래야 엔지니어들도 성장할 기회를 얻어요.
text_zh: 我觉得我们经常把工程师当小孩一样对待，而不是给他们真正的责任和机会让他们像成年人一样发挥才能。就像，"哦，工程师肯定不愿意干这活儿。" 其实这样把工程师保护起来，不让他们接触重要的事情，对他们反而不好。所以我觉得现在有个很好的趋势，就是我们终于可以把工程师当作真正的同事来看待，让他们担任真正的高级领导职位，而不是默认觉得"哦，我们得哄着他们，不能让他们碰真正的难题。" 这样他们才有机会真正成长起来。
text_es: Creo que muchas veces tratamos a los ingenieros un poco como si fueran niños, en lugar de darles las responsabilidades y la oportunidad de realmente destacar como adultos. Y entonces es como, "Ay, a los ingenieros no les va a gustar hacer ese trabajo." Pero en realidad eso no les conviene a los ingenieros, que los protejan de lo que es importante. Y entonces, de hecho, creo que algo muy destacable es que estamos llegando a un momento donde podemos tratar a los ingenieros como nuestros pares y ponerlos en roles de liderazgo muy senior, sin tener esa suposición básica de "Ay, tenemos que mimarlos o esconderles los problemas reales." Y así es como van a tener la oportunidad de crecer también.
fullContext: Lenny asks about how engineers' leverage within companies has changed from the zero interest rate era to today's market. Will explains that while engineers previously had significant leverage, the current shift is actually creating opportunities for engineers to take on more meaningful responsibilities. He argues that the previous era of coddling engineers to retain them was actually harmful to their professional development, as it prevented them from engaging with important business problems and advancing to senior leadership positions.

vocabulary.definition: To utilize something to maximum advantage or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, leveraging often refers to using resources, such as capital or technology, to enhance productivity or gain a competitive edge.

insight.nuance: Leverage implies a strategic approach to using resources, and it is often used in contexts where there is a potential for significant impact or benefit.

vocabulary.definition: Duties or obligations that one is required or expected to fulfill.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, responsibilities often delineate the tasks and roles assigned to employees, which are crucial for organizational structure and accountability.

insight.nuance: Responsibilities carry a connotation of trust and expectation, suggesting that the individual is capable and reliable in fulfilling their role.

vocabulary.definition: To grow, develop, or be successful vigorously.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, thriving often refers to companies or individuals who not only survive but excel and outperform their competitors in the market.

insight.nuance: Thrive suggests a positive and dynamic growth, often associated with resilience and adaptability in challenging environments.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity or skill to perform a task or activity effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a professional context, ability often refers to the competencies and skills that employees possess, which are critical for job performance and career advancement.

insight.nuance: Ability implies a level of proficiency and potential, and it is often used in discussions about talent management and employee development.

speaker: Will Larson
text: Systems thinking is basically you try to think about stocks and flows. So stocks are things that accumulate and flows are kind of the movement from a stock to another thing. So what's a simple example of a stock?
keySentence: Systems thinking is basically you try to think about stocks and flows.
text_ko: 시스템 사고(systems thinking)는 기본적으로 스톡(stock, 쌓이는 것)과 플로우(flow, 흐름)을 생각해 보는 거예요. 스톡은 축적되는 것들이고, 플로우는 한 스톡에서 다른 곳으로 이동하는 움직임이에요. 간단한 예를 들면 스톡은 호수에 있는 물고기 수나 그 호수에서 낚시하는 사람 수가 될 수 있어요. 이 둘 사이의 플로우는 예를 들어 호수의 물고기 수가 낚시하는 사람 수에 따라 어떤 비율로 줄어드는 것일 수 있어요.
text_zh: 系统性思维(systems thinking)其实就是你要考虑存量和流量的关系。存量(stocks)就是那些会积累的东西，流量(flows)就是从一个存量流向另一个地方的变化过程。举个简单的例子，什么是存量呢？湖里鱼的数量可以算是存量，在湖边钓鱼的人数也可以算存量。那这两者之间的流量关系就是，湖里的鱼会按照一定的速度减少，这个速度取决于有多少人在那儿钓鱼。
text_es: El pensamiento sistémico básicamente es que trates de pensar en términos de inventarios y flujos (stocks and flows). Los inventarios son cosas que se acumulan y los flujos son como el movimiento de un inventario hacia otra cosa. ¿Cuál sería un ejemplo sencillo de un inventario? Podría ser el número de peces en un lago. Podría ser el número de personas pescando en ese lago. Y entonces el flujo entre esos dos sería que el número de peces en el lago va a disminuir a cierta velocidad dependiendo del número de personas que estén pescando en ese lago.
fullContext: Lenny asks Will to explain what systems thinking actually means in practical terms. Will provides a foundational definition using the concept of stocks and flows - where stocks are things that accumulate over time, and flows represent the movement or changes between different stocks. He uses the analogy of fish in a lake and fishermen to illustrate how these elements interact and influence each other in a system.

vocabulary.definition: To gather or collect items, resources, or information over time, often resulting in a significant total.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, accumulation can refer to the buildup of assets, customer data, or inventory, which can influence strategic decision-making.

insight.nuance: While 'accumulate' suggests a gradual process, it can imply both positive growth and negative overstocking, depending on context.

vocabulary.definition: The act of changing physical location or position, or a trend towards a particular direction in a broader context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'movement' can refer to the flow of goods, services, or information, as well as shifts in market trends or consumer behavior.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both physical and metaphorical transitions, and is often used in discussions of dynamic changes within organizations or markets.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as the basis or groundwork for something; essential for the development or support of a system or structure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, foundational elements such as core values, principles, or technologies are critical for establishing a sustainable and effective organization.

insight.nuance: While 'foundational' often carries a positive connotation of stability and reliability, it can also imply rigidity if not adapted to change.

vocabulary.definition: An abstract idea or general notion that represents a category or class of objects, events, or phenomena.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and innovation, a 'concept' often refers to a proposed idea for a product, service, or strategy that serves as a starting point for development.

insight.nuance: While 'concept' suggests creativity and potential, it may also imply a lack of practical application until further developed or validated.

speaker: Will Larson
text: The first rule of strategy is that if you write it down, then you can improve it.
keySentence: if you write it down, then you can improve it.
text_ko: 전략의 첫 번째 원칙은 문서로 적어두면 개선할 수 있다는 거예요. 문서화되어 있지 않으면 이 프로덕트 매니저(PM)가 그냥 실력이 부족한 건지, 전략을 잘못 이해해서 엉뚱하게 적용하고 있는 건지, 아니면 프로덕트 책임자(head of product)의 전략을 정확히 따르고 있는데 그 전략 자체가 지금 그들이 다루는 문제에는 적절하지 않은 건지 구분하기가 어렵습니다. 그럼 이걸 어떻게 파악하겠어요?
text_zh: 战略的第一条规则就是，你得把它写下来，这样才能改进。如果没有写下来，你就很难判断这个PM(产品经理)到底是能力不行，还是理解错了策略在瞎搞，或者说他其实理解对了，但产品负责人制定的策略本身就不适合他们要解决的问题。这些你怎么去排查？
text_es: La primera regla de estrategia es que si lo pones por escrito, entonces lo puedes mejorar. Si no está escrito, es difícil saber si este PM simplemente no es un buen PM o si está tratando de aplicar una estrategia que entendió mal, o si en realidad está aplicando correctamente la estrategia del head of product (jefe de producto) que simplemente no es la adecuada para los problemas en los que está trabajando. ¿Cómo vas a debuggear todo eso?
fullContext: Lenny asks about engineering strategy and Will's observation that engineers often lack clear strategy compared to other functions. Will challenges the notion that companies lack strategy, arguing that strategy always exists but is often not written down. He emphasizes that without documentation, it's impossible to diagnose whether problems stem from poor execution, misunderstanding, or inappropriate strategy application.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, strategy refers to the comprehensive plan that guides an organization in achieving its goals and objectives, often involving resource allocation and competitive positioning.

insight.nuance: While 'strategy' implies a thoughtful and deliberate approach, it can sometimes carry connotations of rigidity, suggesting that flexibility may be necessary in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: To make or become better, enhancing quality, value, or performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, improving processes, products, or services is crucial for maintaining competitiveness and meeting customer expectations.

insight.nuance: The term 'improve' suggests a positive change, but it can also imply that previous efforts were inadequate, so it should be used carefully to avoid negative implications.

vocabulary.definition: Easily understood; free from ambiguity or confusion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, clarity is essential for effective collaboration and decision-making, ensuring that all stakeholders have a shared understanding.

insight.nuance: While 'clear' is generally positive, over-simplifying complex ideas in an attempt to be clear can sometimes lead to a loss of important details.

vocabulary.definition: The specific purpose or role that something is designed to perform.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, understanding the function of various departments, roles, or technologies is critical for optimizing operations and achieving strategic objectives.

insight.nuance: The term 'function' can imply a mechanical or rigid role, so it may be less suitable in contexts where creativity or adaptability is emphasized.

speaker: Will Larson
text: The goal of good strategy is not to appease everyone. The goal of good strategy is to dictate how we invest the limited capacities we have or the limited capabilities we have into the problems we care about.
keySentence: Good strategy dictates how we invest limited capacities.
text_ko: 좋은 전략(strategy)의 목표는 모두를 만족시키려는 게 아니에요. 좋은 전략의 목표는 우리가 가진 제한된 자원이나 역량을 우리가 중요하게 생각하는 문제에 어떻게 투자할지 정하는 거예요. 그리고 저는 둘 다 그 목적을 달성하는 데 정말 효과적이었다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 好战略的目标不是让所有人都满意。好战略的目标是要明确我们怎么把有限的资源和能力投入到我们真正关心的问题上。我觉得这两个方面都很有效果。
text_es: El objetivo de una buena estrategia no es quedar bien con todo el mundo. El objetivo de una buena estrategia es decidir cómo vamos a invertir los recursos limitados que tenemos o las capacidades limitadas que tenemos en los problemas que realmente nos importan. Y creo que ambas fueron muy efectivas para lograr eso.
fullContext: Will discusses examples of engineering strategies from Uber (running their own data centers) and Stripe (using a Ruby monolith). He explains that while many engineers disliked these constraints, they were strategically valuable because they focused engineering effort on customer-facing innovation rather than internal tooling diversity. Will emphasizes that effective strategy requires making tough choices about resource allocation.

vocabulary.definition: To allocate resources, typically money, with the expectation of generating a profit or achieving a return in the future.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, investing can refer to funding projects, acquiring assets, or supporting startups to foster growth and innovation.

insight.nuance: While 'invest' often implies a financial commitment, it can also refer to time or effort dedicated to a particular initiative.

vocabulary.definition: The maximum amount or capability that an organization or system can handle or produce at a given time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, capacities often refer to production capabilities, workforce limits, or resource availability that determine operational efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term 'capacities' suggests a fixed limit, often used in discussions about scaling operations or resource management.

vocabulary.definition: The skills, resources, or competencies that an organization possesses, enabling it to perform specific tasks or functions effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, capabilities are critical for competitive advantage, as they define what an organization can achieve in the marketplace.

insight.nuance: Unlike 'capacities,' which focus on quantity, 'capabilities' emphasize quality and proficiency in executing tasks.

vocabulary.definition: Limitations or restrictions that hinder the ability to perform actions or achieve goals within a given context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, constraints can include budgetary limits, regulatory requirements, or resource shortages that impact decision-making and strategy formulation.

insight.nuance: The term 'constraints' often carries a negative connotation, implying obstacles that must be navigated or overcome in strategic planning.

speaker: Will Larson
text: I feel really strongly that you can write a lot more if you write what you want to write.
keySentence: you can write a lot more if you write what you want to write.
text_ko: 저는 쓰고 싶은 걸 쓰면 훨씬 더 많이 쓸 수 있다고 정말 확신해요. 그래서 돈을 벌려고 글을 쓰지 않고, 정해진 스케줄에 맞춰 많이 쓰지도 않아요. 잡지 같은 데에 몇 편 써본 적은 있지만, 사실 그런 건 되게 소모적이에요. 주제를 정하고 합의해야 하고, 그 주제가 점점 제가 쓰고 싶은 것과 달라지면 대부분 고칠 수가 없어요. 게다가 마감에 쫓기기도 하고요.
text_zh: 我特别坚信一点，写自己真正想写的东西，产出会高很多。所以我从来不为了赚钱而写作，也不会按什么固定计划来写。我确实给杂志写过几篇稿子什么的，但发现那样真的很消耗人——你得有个选题，还得和编辑商量确定选题。如果这个选题偏离了你真正想表达的内容，大多数时候你也没办法调整，而且还得赶截稿时间。
text_es: Estoy súper convencido de que puedes escribir mucho más cuando escribes sobre lo que realmente te gusta. Por eso yo no escribo por dinero y casi nunca escribo con fechas límites. He hecho algunos artículos para revistas y eso, pero la verdad es que me agota un montón cuando tienes que seguir un tema específico, cuando tienes que ponerte de acuerdo sobre el tema. Si el tema se desvía de lo que realmente querías escribir, muchas veces no lo puedes arreglar, y además estás con esa presión del deadline.
fullContext: Lenny asks how Will manages to write so prolifically while working intense full-time jobs. Will explains his philosophy that sustainable writing comes from writing about topics that genuinely energize you, rather than writing for external motivations like money or deadlines. He contrasts this with commissioned writing for magazines, which he finds draining because of the constraints and external pressures involved.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of being maintained over the long term without depleting resources or causing harm to the environment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, sustainability refers to practices that promote environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and economic viability, often influencing corporate strategies and consumer preferences.

insight.nuance: While often associated with environmental issues, 'sustainable' can also imply long-term viability in business practices, making it a versatile term in various contexts.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that produces a large quantity of work or output, often with great frequency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech, being prolific can refer to a team's ability to generate innovative ideas, products, or content rapidly, which is crucial for staying competitive.

insight.nuance: While 'prolifically' suggests high output, it can sometimes imply a lack of quality; thus, it is important to balance quantity with quality in business communications.

vocabulary.definition: To invigorate or stimulate, often leading to increased enthusiasm or productivity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, leaders often seek to energize their teams to enhance motivation and drive performance, especially during challenging projects or periods of change.

insight.nuance: The term 'energize' carries a positive connotation, suggesting not just motivation but also a dynamic and proactive approach to work.

vocabulary.definition: A set of beliefs or principles that guide an individual's or organization's behavior and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a company's philosophy often shapes its culture, values, and strategic direction, influencing everything from employee engagement to customer relations.

insight.nuance: While 'philosophy' can refer to abstract ideas, in a business context it is often practical and actionable, reflecting the core values that drive operations.

speaker: Will Larson
text: My biggest advice to both the EMs and the PMs, is before you try to solve the conflict, it's like pushing to ship this feature, pushing to change the approach. Just make sure you actually understand what they care about.
keySentence: Just make sure you actually understand what they care about.
text_ko: 엔지니어링 매니저(EM)와 프로덕트 매니저(PM)에게 가장 드리고 싶은 조언은요, 갈등을 해결하려 들기 전에—예를 들어 이 기능을 출시(ship)하려고 밀거나 접근 방식을 바꾸자고 밀어붙이기 전에—그들이 진짜로 무엇을 중요하게 생각하는지 먼저 제대로 이해하라는 거예요. 현장에서는 늘 많은 어려운 트레이드오프(trade-offs)가 있다고들 하지만, 제 경험상 모두가 진짜 원하는 걸 깊이 이해하면 보통은 모두에게 딱 맞는 절충안이 나오더라고요.
text_zh: 我给工程经理(EM)和产品经理(PM)最大的建议就是，在你想解决冲突之前——比如急着推某个功能上线，或者急着改变做事方法——你得先真正搞清楚对方在乎什么。大家总觉得做产品就得各种权衡取舍(trade-off)，这个领域有太多艰难的选择要做，但我的经验是，如果你真的深入理解每个人想要什么，通常都能找到一个折中的方案，让所有人都得到他们真正想要的东西。
text_es: Mi mejor consejo tanto para los EMs (engineering managers) como para los PMs (product managers), es que antes de tratar de resolver el conflicto, antes de presionar para lanzar esta función o cambiar el enfoque, asegúrense de que realmente entienden lo que les importa a todos. Existe esta idea de que tienes que hacer concesiones (trade-offs) y que hay un montón de decisiones difíciles que tomar en este campo, pero mi experiencia es que si realmente entiendes a fondo lo que cada uno quiere, por lo general hay una solución intermedia que le da a todos exactamente lo que necesitan.
fullContext: Lenny asks for advice on how product managers can build better relationships with engineering managers. Will identifies two core problems: misaligned incentives and lack of understanding of each other's needs. He emphasizes that before trying to resolve conflicts between EMs and PMs, both parties should invest time in truly understanding what the other person cares about, as this often reveals compromise solutions that satisfy everyone's core needs.

vocabulary.definition: Misaligned incentives refer to situations where the goals or motivations of different parties do not align, leading to potential conflicts or inefficiencies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, misaligned incentives can hinder collaboration between teams, such as product managers and engineering managers, resulting in suboptimal outcomes.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a need for realignment to achieve better cooperation and results.

vocabulary.definition: To understand means to grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something, often involving comprehension of complex ideas or perspectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, understanding the needs and concerns of stakeholders is crucial for effective communication and decision-making.

insight.nuance: While it is a common term, it implies a deeper level of insight beyond mere awareness, often requiring empathy and active listening.

vocabulary.definition: An approach refers to a method or way of dealing with a situation or problem, encompassing the strategies and techniques employed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, the approach can determine how teams tackle projects, innovate, or respond to challenges in the marketplace.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a systematic or strategic mindset, and it is often used to differentiate between various methodologies or philosophies.

vocabulary.definition: Conflict refers to a serious disagreement or argument, typically arising from differing opinions, interests, or needs among individuals or groups.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business environments, conflict can emerge between teams or stakeholders, necessitating resolution strategies to maintain productivity and morale.

insight.nuance: While conflict is often viewed negatively, it can also lead to constructive discussions and innovative solutions if managed effectively.

speaker: Will Larson
text: Metrics are about educating the people consuming the metrics about the reality of the rich data underneath.
keySentence: educating the people consuming the metrics about the reality of the rich data underneath.
text_ko: 지표(metrics)는 지표를 보는 사람들에게 그 밑에 깔린 풍부한 데이터(rich data)의 현실을 알려주는 수단이에요. 완벽하게 모든 걸 보여 주는 이상적인 데이터 세트가 목적이 아니에요. 보통 미흡한 것부터 출발하는 경우가 많은데, DORA 지표(DORA metrics)는 진단(diagnosis)에는 정말 도움이 돼요. 하지만 어쩔 수 없이 이사회(board)나 최고경영자(CEO), 다른 임원(executives)들에게 보고를 시작해야 할 때는 DORA 지표로 시작하는 것도 충분히 괜찮아요. 그러고 나면 '아, 이 지표들에 이런저런 문제가 있구나' 하고 알게 되는 거죠.
text_zh: 指标这个东西，说白了就是帮那些看数据的人理解底层丰富数据的真实情况。它们不是什么完美的数据集，能把所有从平庸开始的东西都展示出来。Dora指标在诊断方面确实很有用，但要是你非得用的话，它们也能作为一个不错的起点，拿去向董事会、CEO或者其他高管汇报。然后你就会发现："哎呀，原来这些指标有这么多问题。"
text_es: Las métricas se tratan de educar a la gente que las consume sobre la realidad de todos los datos ricos que hay por debajo. No se trata de tener ese conjunto de datos perfecto que muestre todo empezando con algo mediocre, y las métricas DORA son súper útiles para hacer diagnósticos, pero si no te queda de otra, también pueden servir como un punto de partida decente para empezar a reportar a tu junta directiva o a tu CEO o a otros ejecutivos, y después te das cuenta de que "Ay, tienen un montón de problemas estas métricas."
fullContext: Lenny asks about measuring engineering productivity and what metrics or tools Will finds useful. Will discusses the challenge engineers face when asked to provide metrics - they can explain why every measure is imperfect, leading to measuring nothing. He advocates for starting with imperfect but measurable metrics like the DORA metrics, then using questions about those metrics as opportunities to educate stakeholders about the complexities of engineering work.

vocabulary.definition: Metrics are quantifiable measures used to track and assess the status of a specific business process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, metrics are crucial for evaluating performance, guiding decision-making, and demonstrating progress towards goals.

insight.nuance: While metrics can provide valuable insights, they should be interpreted carefully to avoid misrepresentation of data.

vocabulary.definition: Educating refers to the process of imparting knowledge or skills to individuals or groups.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, educating employees or clients is essential for fostering understanding of products, processes, and data interpretation.

insight.nuance: The term implies a proactive approach to knowledge transfer, often involving training or workshops, rather than passive information sharing.

vocabulary.definition: Reality denotes the state of things as they actually exist, rather than as they may appear or be imagined.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, understanding the reality of a situation is critical for making informed decisions and setting realistic expectations.

insight.nuance: The term often contrasts with perceptions or assumptions, highlighting the importance of data-driven insights over subjective interpretations.

vocabulary.definition: Data refers to raw facts and figures that can be processed and analyzed to extract meaningful information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, data is foundational for analytics, decision-making, and strategic planning, driving innovation and efficiency.

insight.nuance: While data can be objective, its interpretation can vary widely, necessitating careful analysis to avoid misleading conclusions.

speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
text: if you ask an engineer about how much time it'll cost to go and build something... it's almost always half the time as something that you are asking for, as a PM. And that motivation is so different.
keySentence: that motivation is so different.
text_ko: 저는 많은 제품 관리자(PM)들이 이걸 깨닫게 된 것 같아요. 즉, 어떤 걸 만들자고 엔지니어(engineer)에게 얼마나 걸리냐고 물어보면, 그 아이디어가 엔지니어 본인이 제안했거나 본인이 밀고 있는 것이라면, PM이 요청했을 때 예상한 시간의 거의 절반밖에 안 걸리는 경우가 대부분이에요. 그리고 그 동기가 완전히 달라요.
text_zh: 我觉得很多PM(产品经理)现在都明白这个道理了，就是说，如果你问工程师做某个功能要花多长时间，要是这个想法是他们自己提出来的或者他们特别支持的，那估出来的时间基本上是你作为PM提需求时的一半。这个积极性真的差太多了。
text_es: Y creo que muchos PMs ya se han dado cuenta de esto: si le preguntas a un ingeniero cuánto tiempo va a tomar desarrollar algo, y es algo que se le ocurrió a él o que está promoviendo, casi siempre te va a decir la mitad del tiempo que si fueras tú, como PM, quien se lo está pidiendo. Y es que la motivación es completamente distinta.
fullContext: Lenny asks about how to balance letting engineers fix bugs they encounter versus maintaining team priorities and roadmaps. Yuhki explains the importance of bottom-up energy where developers notice problems and fix them organically. He shares insights about how engineer motivation dramatically affects project estimates and execution speed.

vocabulary.definition: The reason or reasons one has for acting or behaving in a particular way; the drive that compels individuals to pursue goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, motivation often refers to the factors that inspire employees to perform at their best, influencing productivity and engagement levels.

insight.nuance: While motivation can be intrinsic or extrinsic, in a corporate setting, it often implies a need for external incentives or recognition.

vocabulary.definition: The tasks or goals that are considered most important and are addressed first in a given context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and strategic planning, establishing clear priorities is essential for resource allocation and ensuring that critical objectives are met efficiently.

insight.nuance: Priorities can shift based on changing circumstances, making it important for leaders to regularly reassess and communicate them.

vocabulary.definition: A management approach that emphasizes the involvement and input of lower-level employees in decision-making processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and innovative companies, a bottom-up approach can foster creativity and empower employees, leading to more effective solutions and a collaborative culture.

insight.nuance: This term often contrasts with top-down management styles, which may stifle input from lower levels of the organization.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity for vigorous activity; the force that drives individuals to engage in tasks and pursue goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, energy can refer to the enthusiasm and dynamism that employees bring to their work, which can significantly impact team morale and productivity.

insight.nuance: While energy is generally positive, it can also imply a need for management to ensure that high energy levels are directed towards productive outcomes rather than chaos.

speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
text: I think one of the most powerful things, especially for startups, is that bottoms up energy, and maybe a developer noticing something is wrong and just going off and fixing it.
keySentence: one of the most powerful things, especially for startups, is that bottoms up energy
text_ko: 저는 특히 스타트업에선 그 보텀업(bottoms-up) 에너지가 정말 강력하다고 생각해요. 예를 들어 개발자가 뭔가 잘못됐다고 보고 그냥 가서 고쳐버리는 경우요. 저는 그런 움직임을 대체로 막지 않으려고 해요. 사람들이 계속 그렇게 하고, 회사에 있는 모두가 제품을 더 좋게 만들려고 한다면, 그게 위에서 내려오는 방식(top-down)으로 '자, 경험의 질(quality of experience) 지표(metric)를 정하고 모든 걸 바꿔보자'는 것보다 훨씬 더 효과적일 때가 많거든요. 위에서 정하는 방식으로는 이런 사소한 것들을 놓치기 쉬워요.
text_zh: 我觉得有一个特别厉害的地方，尤其是对创业公司来说，就是那种自下而上(bottoms up)的能量——比如说一个开发人员发现了什么问题，然后就自己跑去把它修好了。大部分时候，我都尽量不去阻止这种事情，因为如果大家都经常这么做，公司里每个人都想着怎么把产品做得更好，这种方式有时候比那种自上而下(top down)的做法要有效得多——你知道，就是那种"咱们先定义一个用户体验质量指标，然后改这改那"的做法，因为用那种方式你可能会漏掉很多东西。
text_es: Creo que una de las cosas más poderosas, sobre todo para las startups, es esa energía que viene de abajo hacia arriba (bottoms up), y que tal vez un desarrollador se dé cuenta de que algo anda mal y simplemente se ponga a arreglarlo. Y la mayoría del tiempo, trato de no meterme en su camino porque si la gente está haciendo eso constantemente, y todos en la empresa están tratando de mejorar el producto, a veces esa es una forma mucho más efectiva de mejorar la calidad de la experiencia que el enfoque de arriba hacia abajo (top down) de "ay, vamos a definir esta métrica de experiencia de calidad y tratemos de cambiar todas las cosas", porque te puedes perder esos detalles.
fullContext: Lenny discusses the tension between engineers wanting to fix bugs they encounter and product managers needing to maintain priorities. Yuhki advocates for allowing organic, bottom-up improvements rather than always enforcing top-down roadmap discipline, especially for startups where this grassroots energy can be more effective than formal quality metrics.

vocabulary.definition: A management approach that emphasizes the involvement and input of lower-level employees in decision-making processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, a bottom-up approach can foster innovation and agility by allowing team members to contribute ideas and solutions directly, rather than relying solely on top management directives.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting empowerment and collaboration, but may be less effective in highly structured organizations.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity for vigorous activity; an exertion of physical or mental effort.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'energy' often refers to the enthusiasm and drive that employees bring to their work, which can significantly impact productivity and innovation.

insight.nuance: While it generally has a positive connotation, excessive energy can sometimes lead to burnout if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: The act of repairing or resolving an issue or problem.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, 'fixing' often refers to troubleshooting software bugs or operational inefficiencies, which is crucial for maintaining product quality and customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a reactive approach to problems, suggesting that issues are addressed only after they arise rather than being proactively prevented.

vocabulary.definition: Tasks or goals that are considered more important than others and are addressed first.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a startup environment, setting clear priorities is essential for resource allocation and ensuring that the team focuses on high-impact activities that drive growth.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a hierarchy of importance, and misalignment in priorities can lead to confusion and inefficiency within teams.

speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
text: I think the most crazy version of it, maybe, is Dylan's always reading customer feedback. In fact, has reads the most customer feedback of all of us and has been doing that for a decade.
keySentence: Dylan reads the most customer feedback and shares concerning insights.
text_ko: 아마도 그 중에서 가장 극단적인 건 Dylan이 항상 고객 피드백(customer feedback)을 읽고 있다는 점이에요. 사실 우리 중에서 제일 많은 고객 피드백을 읽고 있고, 10년째 그걸 해오고 있어요. 예전에는 그가 본 트윗(tweets)을 여러 슬랙 채널(Slack channels)에 올리면서 “이거 좀 우려돼요”라거나 “이런 피드백이 들어오고 있어요”라고 알려주곤 했어요.
text_zh: 我觉得最疯狂的可能就是Dylan总是在看用户反馈。实际上，他看的用户反馈比我们所有人都多，而且已经坚持了十年了。以前经常有这种情况，他会把看到的推文扔到不同的Slack频道里，然后说"嘿，这个看起来有点问题"，或者"我们收到了这样的反馈"。
text_es: Creo que lo más loco de todo, tal vez, es que Dylan siempre está leyendo los comentarios de los clientes. De hecho, es el que más feedback de clientes lee de todos nosotros y lleva haciéndolo una década. Y muchas veces, antes había esto de que él llegaba y soltaba tweets que veía en diferentes canales de Slack como diciendo, oye, esto parece preocupante, o estamos recibiendo este tipo de comentarios.
fullContext: Lenny asks what sets Figma apart in terms of customer proximity. Yuhki describes Figma's obsessive focus on customer feedback, explaining how CEO Dylan Field personally reads customer feedback daily and shares concerning tweets with the team. This level of founder involvement in customer feedback has been consistent for a decade.

vocabulary.definition: Information and opinions provided by customers regarding their experiences with a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, customer feedback is crucial for understanding consumer satisfaction, guiding product development, and enhancing customer service strategies.

insight.nuance: While customer feedback is generally positive, it can also include negative critiques that are essential for improvement; thus, it should be approached with an open mind.

vocabulary.definition: An intense and unwavering concentration on a specific task, goal, or detail, often to the exclusion of other considerations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, obsessive focus can drive innovation and excellence, but it may also lead to neglecting broader business strategies or team dynamics.

insight.nuance: While obsessive focus can yield high-quality results, it may also be perceived negatively if it leads to burnout or tunnel vision.

vocabulary.definition: The state of being near or close to something in terms of physical distance or relationship.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, proximity can refer to the geographical closeness of a company to its customers or competitors, impacting logistics, market reach, and customer engagement.

insight.nuance: Proximity can also imply relational closeness, which may affect collaboration and communication within teams.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that relates to an individual’s personal feelings, opinions, or experiences rather than a professional or detached perspective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, using 'personally' can indicate a more human touch, suggesting that the speaker is emotionally invested in the matter at hand.

insight.nuance: While 'personally' can enhance relatability, it may also blur professional boundaries if overused in formal contexts.

speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
text: there's certain insights, data insights, research insights that were memified to the point where someone like Travis or Dara would just cite this insight in the middle of a meeting.
keySentence: certain insights, data insights, research insights that were memified to the point where someone like Travis or Dara would just cite this insight
text_ko: 저는 '밈화(memification)'에 대해 자주 얘기해요. 제 경험상 특히 우버에서 그걸 가장 많이 느꼈는데, 데이터 인사이트나 리서치 인사이트 같은 것들이 밈화돼서 회의 중에 트래비스(Travis)나 다라(Dara) 같은 사람이 그냥 그 인사이트를 꺼내 말하곤 했어요. 사람들이 그렇게 자연스럽게 그걸 끌어다 쓸 수 있다면 리서처(researcher)나 데이터 사이언티스트(data scientist), 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)로서 일을 잘한 거구나 하고 알게 돼요.
text_zh: 我经常提到一个概念叫"模因化"(memification)，这个想法主要是我在Uber的时候发现的。就是说，有些洞察，比如数据洞察啊、研究洞察啊，被"模因化"到什么程度呢？就是像Travis或者Dara这样的人，在开会的时候随口就能引用这些洞察。如果你作为研究员、数据科学家或者产品经理，能让别人这样自然地引用和运用你的成果，那你就真的把活儿干到位了。
text_es: A menudo hablo de la memificación (memification), que es esta idea que descubrí sobre todo en Uber, donde hay ciertos insights, insights de datos, insights de investigación que se memificaron tanto que alguien como Travis o Dara simplemente citaba este insight en medio de una reunión, y sabes que realmente hiciste bien tu trabajo como investigador o científico de datos o product manager si la gente puede hacer eso y recurrir a esa información de esa manera.

He introduces the concept of 'memification' - making insights so memorable and sticky that executives naturally reference them in meetings.

speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
text: There's something controversial about this idea that everyone can see what you're doing or that multiple designers can be in the file at the same time.
keySentence: There's something controversial about this idea that everyone can see what you're doing or that multiple designers can be in the file at the same time.
text_ko: 다른 사람들이 당신이 뭘 하는지 전부 볼 수 있다거나, 여러 디자이너가 동시에 같은 파일(file) 안에서 작업할 수 있다는 생각은 논란이 있어요. 우리는 피그마(Figma)에 대한 초기 반응 중 하나가 “이게 디자인의 미래라면 난 그만둘래, 진로를 바꿀 거야”였다고 말하곤 해요. 그런 서사에서 오는 긴장감이 분명 있지만, 그 자체가 당신이 이 혁명의 일부이고 뭔가를 바꾸려 하고 있다는 신호예요.
text_zh: 这个想法确实挺有争议的，就是说每个人都能看到你在做什么，或者多个设计师可以同时在一个文件里工作。我们经常说，当初Figma刚出来的时候，有人的第一反应就是，如果这就是设计的未来，那我不干了，对吧？我要转行了。这种冲突和叙事张力其实是个信号，说明你正在参与一场革命，你在试图改变什么东西。
text_es: Hay algo polémico en esta idea de que todos puedan ver lo que estás haciendo o que varios diseñadores puedan estar en el archivo al mismo tiempo. Nos gusta decir que una de las primeras reacciones que vimos hacia Figma fue: "si este es el futuro del diseño, yo renuncio, ¿no? Me cambio de carrera." Y ahí está esa tensión, esa tensión narrativa, pero eso es señal de que eres parte de esta revolución y estás tratando de cambiar algo.
fullContext: Yuhki discusses advice for product-led growth founders about building emotional connection with users. He explains how Figma's controversial approach to collaborative design - allowing multiple designers in the same file simultaneously - created strong reactions that actually signaled they were driving meaningful change in how people work.

speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
text: So Chris, our CTO, and I intervened. We created this new channel, private channel called Concerning Tweets, and it just, we're this small group of us that Dylan can drop us in. And these are tweets that aren't going viral, by any means.
keySentence: we created this new channel, private channel called Concerning Tweets
text_ko: 그래서 최고기술책임자(CTO)인 크리스와 제가 나섰어요. 'Concerning Tweets'라는 비공개 채널(private channel)을 새로 만들었고, 소수의 우리끼리 있는 곳이라 딜런이 필요할 때 우리를 여기로 불러올 수 있어요. 여기에 올라오는 트윗들은 결코 바이럴(go viral)되는 것들이 아니에요. 좋아요(likes)가 하나 있거나 때로는 아예 없을 때도 있는데, 딜런은 거기서 어딘가 진실의 기미를 느끼고 우리는 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지 꼼꼼히 살펴봐서 우리가 더 집중해야 할 훨씬 큰 문제가 있는지 확인해요.
text_zh: 所以我和我们的CTO Chris就出手了。我们建了一个新的私人频道，叫"值得关注的推文(Concerning Tweets)"，就是我们几个人的小群，Dylan可以把东西扔进来。这些推文根本不是什么病毒式传播的，就是那种只有一个赞，有时候零赞的内容，但Dylan觉得里面有些真实的东西，我们会确保去看看那里到底发生了什么，看看是不是有什么更大的事情需要我们关注。
text_es: Entonces Chris, nuestro CTO, y yo decidimos meternos en el asunto. Creamos este nuevo canal, un canal privado que llamamos Tweets Preocupantes, y somos un grupo pequeñito donde Dylan nos puede incluir. Y estos son tweets que para nada se están volviendo virales. Son simplemente cosas que ves con un like, a veces cero likes, pero él siente que tienen algo de verdad y nos aseguramos de revisar qué está pasando ahí para ver si no hay algo mucho más grande en lo que deberíamos estar enfocándonos.
fullContext: Yuhki continues describing Dylan Field's obsessive customer feedback monitoring. When Dylan's habit of sharing concerning tweets in team channels became disruptive, Yuhki and the CTO created a private 'Concerning Tweets' channel to contain the process while still capturing valuable signals from low-engagement customer feedback.

speaker: Yuriy Timen
text: The only thing that's worse than a channel or a tactic that you tried not working. The only thing that's worse now is when you didn't give it the appropriate shot, right?
keySentence: The only thing that's worse now is when you didn't give it the appropriate shot, right?
text_ko: 채널(channel)이나 전술(tactic)이 안 통하는 것만큼 안 좋은 건 없어요. 그런데 더 안 좋은 건 제대로 기회를 주지 않고 성급하게 '효과 없다'고 잘못 결론 내리는 거예요. 기업들 얘기를 들어보면 그런 경우가 정말 많더라고요. "유튜브요? 해봤는데 안 됐어요" 이렇게요.
text_zh: 有一件事比你试过的渠道或策略不奏效更糟糕。更糟糕的是，你根本没有给它足够的机会，对吧？你过早地就错误地下结论说它不行。我跟很多公司聊的时候，经常发现这种情况，特别常见。"哦，YouTube我们试过了，没用。"
text_es: Lo único que es peor que un canal o una táctica que probaste y no funcionó... lo único que es peor es cuando no le diste la oportunidad que merecía, ¿verdad? Y sacaste conclusiones apresuradas y equivocadas de que no sirve. Y es increíble qué tan seguido me encuentro con eso cuando hablo con empresas: "Ay, YouTube, ya lo probamos. No funciona."
fullContext: Lenny and Yuriy are discussing common failure modes in growth strategy. Yuriy explains a major mistake he sees companies make when testing new growth channels and tactics. He emphasizes that many companies conclude a growth channel doesn't work without giving it a proper chance to succeed, which is actually worse than trying something that legitimately fails after adequate testing.

speaker: Yuriy Timen
text: I hard count my week at about three to three and a half days a week worth of work, which is a personal choice.
keySentence: I hard count my week at about three to three and a half days a week worth of work.
text_ko: 저는 제 한 주를 대략 3~3.5일 분량의 일로 딱 제한해 놓고 있어요. 이건 개인적인 선택이에요. 그런 제약 안에서 제가 가장 잘할 수 있고 가장 즐겁고 보람을 느낄 수 있는 회사 수는 많아야 4~5곳인 것 같아요. 그걸 넘기면 문맥 전환(context switching) 비용 때문에 생기는 부담이 너무 커져서 감당이 안 돼요.
text_zh: 我仔细算了算，我一周大概就干三天到三天半的活儿，这是我个人的选择。在这个前提下，我觉得要想把工作做到最好，同时也是我最享受、最有成就感的状态，最多也就能同时管四到五家公司。如果再多的话，那种不断切换工作内容(context switching)带来的负担就太重了，根本受不了。
text_es: Calculando bien, yo trabajo unas tres a tres días y medio por semana, que es una decisión personal mía. Y dentro de esa limitación, también siento que para hacer mi mejor trabajo y el trabajo que más disfruto y me resulta más satisfactorio, cuatro o cinco empresas es probablemente lo máximo. Si trato de ir más allá de eso, la carga administrativa que crea en términos del costo del cambio de contexto (context switching) se vuelve abrumadora.

speaker: Yuriy Timen
text: If you have really healthy LTVs, and that usually means that you're attracting a proconsumer buyer, so they may be single player, but they're using it for work.
keySentence: you're attracting a proconsumer buyer
text_ko: 정말 고객 생애 가치(LTV)가 건전하다면, 보통 프로슈머(proconsumer) 고객을 끌어온다는 뜻이에요. 개인 사용자(single player)일 수 있지만 업무용으로 쓰는 경우가 많죠. 그래서 비용 처리(expensing)를 하거나, 단순히 체감 가치가 훨씬 높아서 연간 120~130달러짜리 구독료를 기꺼이 부담해요.
text_zh: 如果你的LTV(客户生命周期价值)真的很健康，那通常说明你吸引到的是专业消费者，他们可能是个人用户，但是用来工作的。所以可能他们会分摊费用，或者就是觉得价值很高，愿意承担每年120、130美元的订阅费用。
text_es: Si tienes LTVs realmente sanos, eso generalmente significa que estás atrayendo a un comprador "proconsumer" (proconsumer), o sea que tal vez sea un usuario individual, pero lo está usando para el trabajo. Entonces puede ser que lo esté distribuyendo o simplemente el valor percibido es mucho más alto y están dispuestos a pagar esa suscripción de $120 o $130 al año.
fullContext: Lenny asks Yuriy about different growth archetypes for consumer startups. Yuriy is explaining companies that can succeed with paid acquisition strategies. He describes 'proconsumer' products - those used by individual consumers but for professional purposes, which typically have higher lifetime values (LTVs) than typical consumer subscriptions. These higher LTVs make paid marketing more viable since companies can afford higher customer acquisition costs.

vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, healthy LTVs are crucial for assessing the long-term viability of customer acquisition strategies and overall business sustainability.

insight.nuance: The term 'healthy' implies that the LTV is significantly higher than the cost of acquiring the customer, suggesting effective marketing and customer engagement strategies.

vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding proconsumer behavior helps companies tailor their products and marketing strategies to meet the demands of discerning customers who value transparency and quality.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a positive alignment with consumer interests, which can enhance brand loyalty and customer satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: Paid acquisition strategies are marketing tactics that involve spending money to acquire new customers, typically through channels like paid advertising, social media promotions, or sponsored content.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, businesses often rely on paid acquisition strategies to quickly scale their customer base and enhance visibility in competitive markets.

insight.nuance: While effective for rapid growth, these strategies can be costly and require careful analysis to ensure a positive return on investment.

speaker: Yuriy Timen
text: I think it's very difficult to manufacture. You'd only study when... It's very hard to manufacture product network effects if they aren't there from the get go. So Airbnb from your days, obviously marketplace very strong product network effect dynamics.
keySentence: Manufacturing product network effects is difficult if they aren't there from the get go.
text_ko: 그건 인위적으로 만들어내기 굉장히 어렵다고 생각해요. 연구한다고 생기는 게 아니라, 처음부터 없던 프로덕트 네트워크 효과(product network effects)는 나중에 만들어내기 정말 힘들어요. 예를 들어 네가 있을 때의 에어비앤비는 마켓플레이스라서 프로덕트 네트워크 효과가 당연히 아주 강했죠. 협업 툴 쪽을 떠올리면 Airtable, monday.com, Whimsical 같은 서비스들은 우리 둘 다 알다시피 본질적으로 프로덕트 네트워크 효과가 강해요. 반면 Grammarly 같은 회사는 그런 게 그냥 없었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得这个很难人为制造出来。你只有在... 如果一开始就没有产品网络效应(product network effects)的话，后面想人为制造是非常困难的。像你那时候的Airbnb，很明显，marketplace模式天生就有很强的产品网络效应。再比如协作工具，像Airtable、monday.com、Whimsical这些我们都熟悉的公司，它们天生就有很强的产品网络效应，但你对比一下Grammarly这样的公司，它就是没有这种效应。
text_es: Creo que es muy difícil de crear artificialmente. Solo estudiarías cuando... Es súper complicado fabricar efectos de red del producto (product network effects) si no están ahí desde el primer día. Entonces Airbnb, de tu época, obviamente es un marketplace con dinámicas de efectos de red muy fuertes. Si piensas en herramientas de colaboración como Airtable, monday.com, Whimsical, que los dos conocemos, tienen efectos de red inherentes muy potentes. Contrasta eso con una empresa como Grammarly. Simplemente no los tenía.
fullContext: Lenny asks about when companies should invest in virality and referral programs. Yuriy explains that product network effects - where the product becomes more valuable as more people use it - are usually inherent to the product from the beginning and very difficult to add later. He contrasts companies like Airbnb and collaboration tools that naturally have network effects with Grammarly, which is primarily a single-user writing tool where network effects don't naturally exist.

speaker: Yuriy Timen
text: I think SEO is pretty specialized skill set. There are some basic principles that always hold like best content wins and don't do shady back linking and make sure that you're on page.
keySentence: best content wins and don't do shady back linking and make sure that you're on page.
text_ko: 저는 검색엔진최적화(SEO)가 꽤 전문적인 스킬셋이라고 생각해요. '좋은 콘텐츠가 이긴다' 같은 기본 원칙과 수상한 백링크(backlink)를 하지 말라는 것, 그리고 온페이지(on-page) 관리를 확실히 하라는 것들은 항상 유효해요. SEO를 잘하고 페이지가 크롤링(crawl)되기 쉽게 만드는 건 기본 중의 기본이고, 사실 다들 그 정도는 알고 있는 것 같아요. 진짜 승부는 결국 그 행간, 즉 작은 디테일들 사이에서 결정되는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得SEO是个很专业的技能。有些基本原则永远不会变，比如说好内容为王，别搞那些见不得人的反向链接(back linking)，还有确保你的页面SEO做得到位，让搜索引擎能轻松抓取(crawl)你的页面。不过我感觉这些大家都知道。真正拉开差距的，其实是那些细节上的功夫。
text_es: Creo que el SEO es una habilidad bastante especializada. Hay algunos principios básicos que siempre se mantienen como que el mejor contenido gana, no hacer enlaces sospechosos (shady back linking), y asegurarte de que tu SEO on-page esté bien y que tus páginas sean fáciles de rastrear (crawl). Pero siento que todo el mundo ya sabe eso. Y donde se determinan los ganadores es entre líneas.
fullContext: Lenny asks whether companies should work with SEO agencies or try to do SEO in-house. Yuriy explains that while basic SEO principles are well-known, success in SEO comes from more nuanced, specialized knowledge. He emphasizes that SEO requires staying current with algorithm changes and understanding subtle optimization techniques that differentiate successful companies from those that struggle with organic search.
